result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed L-functions share reflection symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source compares zeta, Dirichlet, Dedekind, modular, Maass, and higher-rank completions, exposing the common move of adjoining archimedean factors before reflecting s to 1-s.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler products assemble local prime-power factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It gives the reusable local-to-global representation across several L-function families and identifies higher-rank degree through local factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completion and recentering turn symmetry into evenness and real critical-line data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Completing zeta removes its pole, recentering gives an even Xi function, and the Hardy Z representation converts critical-line values into a real-valued function without changing their modulus.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product and reflection confine nontrivial zeros to the critical strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source derives the basic zero geometry by combining a zero-free Euler-product half-plane with functional-equation reflection, then distinguishes trivial gamma-factor zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three counting functions separate total, on-line, and right-of-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: N(T), N0(T), and N(sigma,T) encode distinct strengths of zero information and turn RH, partial on-line results, and density questions into comparable counting statements.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic L-functions link Dirichlet series, Euler products, and arithmetic sources
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span defines the broad arithmetic class and instantiates it with zeta, Dirichlet, Dedekind, and degree-two L-functions arising from cusp forms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke eigenform coefficients produce degree-two L-functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The transformation law, coefficient relations, Euler factors, coefficient normalization, and functional equation show how automorphic data is repackaged as an L-function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing oldforms isolates primitive newforms with Euler products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explains two mechanisms generating imprimitive forms, extracts the new subspace, and characterizes its Hecke basis through Euler products and functional equations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Point counts of elliptic curves become coefficients of modular L-functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This is a compact construction chain from reductions modulo primes to Hasse-Weil coefficients and then to weight-two modular forms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Selberg class packages analytic continuation, symmetry, locality, growth, and primitive factorization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It supplies a representation-independent candidate definition of arithmetic L-functions and records closure, unique primitive factorization, and the five governing axioms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient orthogonality organizes primitive Selberg-class factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selberg's conjectures turn primitive functions into an orthonormal-like system and connect coefficient correlations to uniqueness, holomorphy, and prime-number-theorem behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Periodic-orbit data constructs a zeta function whose zeros encode energy levels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source links chaotic spectral statistics to random matrices and builds a dynamical zeta function from a semiclassical spectral determinant and periodic orbits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH variants differ by L-function family and treatment of real zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It cleanly separates RH, GRH, ERH, Grand RH, and their modified forms, preventing family scope and real-axis exceptions from being collapsed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quasi, density-one, and density bounds retain different fragments of RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The three weakenings separate a fixed zero-free half-plane, almost-all zeros on the line, and quantitative control of off-line density, including the moment-estimation bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary nonvanishing becomes a prime number theorem through a Tauberian step
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The unit identifies both the semantic equivalence and the bridge mechanism: regularity of the logarithmic derivative on the boundary enables a Tauberian theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vertical zero questions are modeled by random-matrix statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It separates vertical spacing and correlations from RH's horizontal location question and records random matrix theory as the proposed descriptive framework.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The rightmost zero boundary controls the prime-counting error exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The von Mangoldt summatory function translates a zero-free half-plane into an error term, with the optimal square-root exponent equivalent to RH and an analogous GRH statement for progressions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CUE statistics and prime-sensitive long-range behavior motivate a self-adjoint spectral realization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source combines local random-matrix evidence, semiclassical chaotic systems, and prime/periodic-orbit analogies to specify features of a hypothetical operator whose spectrum would force RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Immutable v1 equivalence map
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Preserves the v1 unit ID and exact span, which crosses from prime-sensitive spectral statistics into the chapter's prime-zero duality and initial arithmetic-equivalence template.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Square-root cancellation in prime-weighted and Möbius sums encodes RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The two arithmetic functions expose complementary translations of RH into error control for prime powers and cancellation of multiplicative signs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robin and Lagarias turn RH into universal divisor-sum thresholds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The criteria compare the irregular divisor sum with asymptotically sharp smooth envelopes and show how equivalent formulations can be made finite-domain and elementary-looking.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Totient primorials and maximal permutation order encode RH through extremal growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span supplies two structurally different finite/combinatorial observables whose asymptotic inequalities are equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Farey discrepancy norms translate RH into quantitative equidistribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The unit shows that both quadratic and absolute aggregate deviations of ordered Farey fractions have RH-equivalent rates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cyclotomic-product height bounds encode zeta zero-free half-planes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Amoroso's criterion links growth of an averaged positive logarithmic height of a cyclotomic product to a specified zero-free region.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit formula converts prime-zero duality into a positivity criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's transform formula displays both prime and zero sides, while Bombieri's refinement reformulates RH as positivity over a test-function class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH is equivalent to positivity of coefficients derived from all zeros or derivatives of xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Li's criterion provides both a zero-sum representation and a local derivative representation, bridging global zero data to a sequence of scalar inequalities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros of zeta's derivative on the left half-strip characterize RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The criterion moves the question from zeros of zeta to critical points of zeta and notes its quantitative role in methods for counting critical-line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity of xi's logarithmic derivative on a half-plane characterizes RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This is a compact half-plane positivity reformulation that complements coefficient and test-function positivity criteria.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free half-planes become density of fractional-part spans in Lp
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The criterion turns analytic zero exclusion into approximation/completeness of an explicitly constrained function family and records the p-parametrized strengthening.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet polynomials approximating the reciprocal of zeta characterize RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The weighted L2 infimum expresses RH as the existence of increasingly effective finite mollifiers and records the direction previously known from Nyman-Beurling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dilates of a fixed kernel encode zero-free vertical lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Salem's criterion is a concise transform-style bridge from nonvanishing on a sigma-line to completeness in L1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Growth of an entire series built from reciprocal zeta values characterizes RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The M. Riesz criterion converts RH into a global growth bound for an explicitly defined series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A two-variable Fourier-kernel inequality characterizes real zeros of Xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The unit instantiates Polya's real-zero machinery as a universal positivity condition for a kernel constructed from Xi's Fourier data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A heat-like deformation turns RH into the sign of a real-zero threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The one-parameter family has only real zeros above a threshold Lambda, so RH becomes the boundary statement Lambda <= 0 and Newman's conjecture locates it at criticality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity of all Hankel-type determinants characterizes RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The logarithmic derivative coefficients are assembled into matrices, converting a zero-location problem into an infinite hierarchy of determinant inequalities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A divisibility matrix encodes RH in determinant growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Redheffer construction turns divisibility into a finite 0-1 matrix whose determinant bound is RH-equivalent, alongside unconditional and conditional spectral information.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta as a partition function with symmetry breaking at its pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source defines KMS equilibrium, symmetry, and spontaneous breaking, then poses and states solutions of zeta and Dedekind-zeta dynamical-system realization problems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite adeles and an ideal semigroup induce the endomorphism action underlying Bost-Connes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The exact sequence, strong-approximation quotient, finite solution fibers, and averaging endomorphisms construct the algebraic input for the crossed product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting the idele sequence converts inner symmetry into the Bost-Connes outer action
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The universal covariant representation and semigroup crossed product are followed by a splitting that restricts the semigroup and recovers the stated Bost-Connes algebra and outer symmetry group.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Immutable v1 catalogue of refuted sufficient-condition routes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Preserves the v1 unit ID and exact span: Turan's zero-free partial-sum hypothesis and a de Branges-space positivity hypothesis would imply RH, but the source records counter-results showing each proposed condition fails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replacing continuous dilation freedom by natural dilations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source sharpens a Hilbert-space closure criterion equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis: membership of the interval characteristic function in the span generated by all admissible real dilations can be replaced by membership in the much thinner span generated by natural-indexed dilations. This is the paper's central semantic change, turning a continuous approximation family into a discrete one without weakening the criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why direct natural Möbius approximants require regularization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The naive natural Möbius partial sums have useful pointwise and restricted L1 behavior yet diverge in the ambient Hilbert space. Proposed subsequences and logarithmic mollification do not remove a general lower bound showing that any bounded-scale Beurling approximation can approach the target only slowly. Together these facts motivate changing the summation mechanism rather than merely enlarging a cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An epsilon-weighted Möbius family as a reciprocal-zeta correction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introducing a complex exponent weights the entire natural dilation range in a single family. For fixed spatial input the family is described as meromorphic and as a finite correction of the reciprocal zeta function, which makes analytic information available to the approximation problem. The proof plan is explicitly split: under the Riemann hypothesis establish that each small positive-parameter limit remains in the natural span, then unconditionally let the parameter tend to zero in the Hilbert norm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free half-planes control truncated reciprocal-zeta sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The quoted Balazard-Saias estimate converts nonvanishing of zeta in a half-plane into uniform control of truncated Möbius Dirichlet sums relative to the reciprocal zeta function in an interior strip. This is the bridge later used to dominate the transformed finite natural approximants under the Riemann hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A functional-equation bound independent of the Riemann hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A second lemma bounds a zeta quotient along vertical lines uniformly over a small parameter range and explicitly does not assume the Riemann or Lindelöf hypotheses. Its proof route passes through the zeta functional equation and gamma asymptotics, furnishing the unconditional domination needed for the outer parameter limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted natural sums produce two nested pointwise limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof defines finite natural Beurling sums with an epsilon weight. Passing the cutoff to infinity uses the reciprocal-zeta term plus a finite correction to identify a pointwise limit, and then passing epsilon to zero uses the fundamental Möbius cancellation property to identify the target as the negative characteristic function. This exposes the two limits whose norm convergence must be proved separately.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier-Mellin isometry turns closure into transform-space domination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof changes representation from the original Hilbert space to an isometric Fourier-Mellin transform space. A Mellin identity for the basic Beurling function factors the transform of a weighted finite approximant into a zeta factor and a truncated Möbius Dirichlet sum, so Littlewood's theorem identifies the transformed pointwise limit. This is the structural move that makes analytic estimates usable as norm-convergence evidence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-hypothesis domination yields natural-space membership
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: With the zero-free parameter specialized to the critical boundary, the proof combines the truncated reciprocal-zeta estimate, the Lindelöf consequence of the Riemann hypothesis, and the unconditional quotient bound to produce an integrable transform-space majorant. Dominated convergence then gives norm convergence of weighted finite natural sums; separate control on the regions below and above one removes the auxiliary spatial weight, placing the limiting function in the closed natural Beurling space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The unconditional outer limit closes the strengthened criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After the Riemann hypothesis has supplied natural-space membership for each small positive parameter, the identified transform limit and the hypothesis-free quotient bound give Hilbert convergence as the parameter tends to zero. The previously established pointwise identification fixes the norm limit as the negative characteristic function, and closure then supplies the theorem's nontrivial implication.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A convergence criterion and a proposed Lp extension
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The author records that the proof also gives a route to the original Nyman-Beurling criterion without the cited Hardy-space machinery and states an exact corollary: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to Hilbert-norm convergence of the regularized finite sums for every sufficiently small positive parameter. An analogous Lp zero-free-half-plane criterion is explicitly presented as something to extend the proof to, not as an established theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Summability, subsequence criteria, and a possible rate-sensitive refinement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The construction is interpreted as a summability method applied to the old natural approximation. Convergence along special cutoff and regularization-parameter subsequences is said to remain necessary and sufficient, motivating comparison with other summability procedures. The unused cutoff dependence in the technical estimate is then suggested as potentially connected to the known slowness of approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros as absorption lines and the global trace boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes critical zeros appearing directly from noncritical zeros appearing through harmonic-potential resonances, locates both in an Adele-class trace formula, and states that the unproved global trace formula is equivalent to RH for all Grössencharakter L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Naturality criterion for a Hilbert–Polya realization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why selfadjointness or positivity could relocate RH, connects the proposal to Selberg and zero-spacing statistics, and insists that a genuine construction not smuggle the zeros or zeta function into its definition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Periodic-orbit constraints on a hypothetical Riemann flow
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Comparing semiclassical periodic-orbit and Euler-product oscillations forces primes as primitive orbits, logarithmic periods and instability exponents, absence of time reversal, while exposing the unresolved overall sign and finite-iterate denominator mismatches.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-field geometry turns the spectral sign into cohomology
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers zeros, functional equation, explicit formulas, and RH to Frobenius cohomology, duality, Lefschetz, and positivity; the alternating cohomological sign motivates a negative or absorption spectrum and the idele class group as the acting symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adele-class quotient and the two vanishing conditions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs X=A/k* as the noncommutative quotient, explains why quotient functions are formed through orbit sums, and derives f(0)=0 and integral f=0 as the conditions removing the fixed-origin and small-scale divergences before completion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Embedding into the regular representation and taking a cokernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The orbit-sum map E, with its square-root modular factor, embeds the Adele-class space equivariantly into a weighted regular representation; its invariant cokernel supplies the negative cohomological Polya–Hilbert space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical zeros as spectrum of the cokernel generator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes by compact characters, obtains a generator with imaginary spectrum, and states that its discrete spectral points are exactly critical-line L-function zeros with a delta-controlled multiplicity; the trace corollary and Jordan warning expose both value and limitation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Formal character from exact sequences and the need for regularization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the two exact sequences to express the Adele-class character as trivial and Tate terms minus the critical-zero spectrum, while explicitly identifying the divergent regular-representation trace and the need to regularize it by fixed-point methods.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Distributional Lefschetz trace from transverse fixed points
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how restricting an operator kernel to the diagonal turns transversality into isolated fixed-point contributions weighted by the inverse determinant, then recovers the alternating cohomological Lefschetz trace.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From fixed points to zeros and periodic orbits of a flow
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Generalizes the distributional trace to a one-parameter flow, separates fixed zeros from periodic orbits, and packages both using isotropy groups, covolume-normalized Haar measures, and transverse return maps.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier control of the local fixed-point denominator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For multiplication on an arbitrary local field, computes the fixed-point contribution |1−lambda|^{-1} and justifies the product of delta distributions by convolving their Fourier transforms, clarifying why the transverse case is well-defined.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dual cutoff and canonical local principal value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces infrared and Fourier-conjugate ultraviolet projections and states a trace asymptotic with a universal logarithmic divergence plus a principal value uniquely normalized by vanishing of its Fourier transform at one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symbol calculus converts cutoff trace to the principal value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the Schwartz kernel symbol, Parseval, the product variable x·xi, and the Fourier transform of −log|u| to split the cutoff trace into its logarithmic leading term and the canonical local distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Places as global fixed hyperplanes with local transverse actions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Solves the fixed-point equation on the Adele-class quotient: nontrivial stabilizers occur on place-indexed hyperplanes, each generic isotropy is the embedded local multiplicative group, and the transverse action is precisely local scaling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Formal global trace recovers Weil but remains nonrigorous
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Summing placewise fixed contributions yields Weil's explicit distribution, exposes the distinction between critical-only and all-zero spectral sides, and argues that positivity is Lefschetz/permutation-like rather than semiclassical quantization; cutoff and delta remain explicit obstacles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S-local non-type-I quotient with a unitary Fourier transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reduces the global problem to a finite set of places while retaining non-type-I orbit behavior, constructs L2(X_S) without delta, and proves that Fourier transformation is unitary by an exponentially convergent S-unit correlation sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rigorous S-local trace formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that the dual-cutoff trace on the S-local quotient equals the logarithmic identity contribution plus the sum of canonically normalized local Weil terms for every place in S.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg-style quotient trace decomposes into placewise logarithms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lifts the quotient test function to ideles, unfolds the trace over S-units, passes to symbols, and decomposes log|u| into local logarithms so the global quotient trace becomes a finite sum of local principal values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric summability and rapid decay of the cutoff error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a word metric on S-units, fractional-difference convolution norms, and Schwartz decay to prove geometric summability in the unit variable and faster-than-any-power decay in the cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cutoff replaces delta and admits all zeros canonically
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the weighted space gives artificial multiplicities and suppresses off-line zeros, then replaces it with the delta-zero Hilbert space and a cutoff whose spectral side contains critical zeros directly and noncritical zeros as resonances.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-field cutoff as an intersection of support and Fourier support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Analyzes the pair of projections by compact characters, computes their trace, constructs enough independent translated test vectors to identify their intersection, and obtains exact commutation and dimension control in positive characteristic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S-independent global cutoff and the remaining trace conjecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recasts the S-local result using the projection onto functions and Fourier transforms supported below the cutoff, explains stabilization as S grows, and isolates the unproved arbitrary-h global trace formula even in positive characteristic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global cutoff trace is equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Theorem 5 and proves the trace-to-RH direction by embedding the cutoff subspace into a regular-representation window; the positive operator difference converges to the Weil distribution, so trace validity forces its positive type.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Harmonic measure turns off-line zeros into resonances
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the limit of the positive cutoff-difference distributions from zero constraints: critical zeros give point masses on the spectral line, while off-line zeros contribute their Poisson/harmonic measures with full multiplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prolate spheroidal functions repair the Archimedean support obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why exact joint compact support fails at real places and replaces intersection by the near-one eigenspace of the time-frequency limiting operator, controlled by a commuting differential operator and a sharp transition near the phase-space dimension.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero counting appears as a deficit of cutoff states
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Counts the phase-space region for the scaling Hamiltonian under simultaneous position, momentum, and energy cutoffs, recovering the smooth zero-counting term with the negative sign appropriate to an absorption spectrum and interpreting it as failure of surjectivity of the orbit-sum map.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The cutoff angle spectrum also governs random-matrix gap probabilities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates eigenvalues of the projector-angle/time-frequency operator to the Fredholm-product description of large-matrix eigenvalue counts, linking the cutoff construction back to zero statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quotienting through the inner product as gauge removal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares the Adele-class completion with construction of physical Hilbert spaces in gauge theory: invariance directions disappear in the seminorm rather than by selecting representatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Noncommutative Adele classes as an Archimedean Frobenius setting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the idele connected component to type-III factor structure, emphasizes that quotienting destroys linear dimension products in favor of sums, and identifies the idele action on Adele classes as the class-field-theoretic analogue of Frobenius.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why state counting and imported positivity can miss absorption
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Critiques routes that obtain the sign by deleting regions or define an inner product directly from the Weil distribution, distinguishing explanation of the distribution from merely assuming its positivity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Proposed extension from GL(1) to matrix Adele classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Suggests replacing the Adele-class space by matrices modulo GL_n(k), reports only preliminary spectral evidence, and correctly leaves the higher-rank Lefschetz formula as the next unresolved step.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: L-functions normalize global homogeneous distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds local homogeneous distributions, normalizes unramified factors, forms their restricted tensor product, and shows that the Euler-product L-function is exactly the scalar relating the convergent global integral to the holomorphic normalized distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation gives inversion and rapid decay of the orbit sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses self-duality of the global-field lattice to derive E(f)(x)=E(f-hat)(1/x) on the two-vanishing-condition space, then proves rapid decay at both ends and extends the L-factor identity into the half-plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Band-limited approximate units in weighted regular representations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs uniformly bounded approximate identities with compact Fourier support in weighted translation spaces and transports them to the idele class group, allowing the cokernel analysis to reduce to compact spectral support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros characterize the annihilator of the orbit-sum range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the dual by compact characters, Mellin-transforms annihilators of Im(E), uses L(1/2+it) times the transformed distribution equals zero, and identifies the allowed delta derivatives with zero multiplicity and Sobolev order, yielding the cokernel generator's Jordan spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Schwartz convolution is trace class with zero sum trace
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses compact Fourier localization and zero-density growth to show Schwartz averages of the cokernel representation are trace class and computes their trace as the critical-zero sum with theorem-controlled multiplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weil distribution as global term minus local principal values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the zero sum and Weil distribution, decomposes it into discriminant, global, and placewise local terms, and records the normalized local principal values whose positivity is equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rewriting Weil's explicit formula in trace-test notation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Changes variables from radial F to the trace test function h, identifies Mellin transforms with character Fourier transforms, and rewrites the zero sum as trivial terms minus placewise fixed-point integrals, valid initially on the stated test class and unconditionally when h(1)=0.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local cutoff principal values agree with Weil's
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Checks non-Archimedean, real, and complex local fields separately, using normalized basic characters and Fourier transforms of −log|u| to show that the cutoff-selected principal value is exactly Weil's local prescription.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Changing the additive character shifts only the identity term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how rescaling the basic additive character changes the selfdual Fourier transform and adds log|lambda| at the identity; summing local differential-idele shifts cancels the discriminant term and yields the global explicit formula in the cutoff normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical Haar measure for modulated groups
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the unique Haar normalization from logarithmic growth of the module range, treats continuous and discrete ranges, and proves compatibility with quotienting by compact subgroups.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Densities, delta sections, and transverse pullback
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines generalized bundle sections, pushforward and pullback, states the wave-front transversality condition, and shows that a delta section on a submanifold pulls back to the delta section on its transverse inverse image.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A pullback operator has the graph delta as kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the Schwartz kernel theorem to a smooth map and canonically identifies the symbol of its graph-supported delta distribution, justifying the familiar kernel delta(y−f(x)) without coordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poincaré transversality yields periodic-orbit and zero contributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives that diagonal/graph transversality is invertibility of one minus the transverse return map, computes the pulled-back symbol, and pushes it to time to obtain covolume-weighted periodic-orbit terms and determinant-weighted fixed-zero terms in a single isotropy formula.

section_argument_map.label: Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the canonical critical/noncritical spectral split, the local-to-global trace plan, the open global boundary, and Hilbert–Polya/random-matrix motivation.

section_argument_map.label: I Quantum chaos and the hypothetical Riemann flow
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Compares periodic-orbit and Euler-product expansions to derive prime-orbit, period, instability, symmetry, and sign constraints.

section_argument_map.label: II Algebraic Geometry and global fields of nonzero characteristic
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses the function-field Frobenius/cohomology dictionary to motivate absorption, cohomological sign, and the idele-class acting group.

section_argument_map.label: III Spectral interpretation of critical zeros
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Constructs the Adele-class Hilbert space, embeds it into the regular representation, and identifies critical zeros in the cokernel spectrum.

section_argument_map.label: IV Distribution trace formula for flows
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Develops fixed-point and periodic-orbit distributional trace contributions for smooth flows.

section_argument_map.label: V Local-field multiplicative action
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Makes the local fixed-point denominator rigorous using distributions, dual cutoffs, symbols, and a canonically normalized principal value.

section_argument_map.label: VI Global formal trace computation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Identifies global fixed loci with place hyperplanes and formally recovers the Weil explicit distribution.

section_argument_map.label: VII S-local trace formula
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves a rigorous trace formula on non-type-I S-local Adele quotients and controls the cutoff error.

section_argument_map.label: VIII Global trace and elimination of delta
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines the delta-free cutoff, relates its trace formula to positivity and RH, treats resonances and the Archimedean cutoff, and returns to zero counting.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix I Proof of theorem 1
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Supplies homogeneous-distribution, Poisson-summation, Sobolev, and cokernel-annihilator machinery underlying the spectral theorem.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix II Explicit formulas
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Rewrites Weil's explicit formula in trace notation and proves agreement of local principal-value normalizations.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix III Distribution trace formulas
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Provides coordinate-free density, wave-front, kernel, transversality, and pushforward foundations for the flow trace formula.

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Equivalence does not supply the missing proof of the global trace, and the detailed construction is first established in positive characteristic.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: The cutoff makes RH a positivity statement about missing states

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: At real places, prolate-spheroidal concentration supplies an approximate joint cutoff whose effective dimension matches phase-space area; the deficit realizes the smooth zero count and the same angle spectrum connects to random-matrix gaps.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The semiclassical count does not by itself recover the oscillatory zero term or prove spectral convergence.

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Several constants are formula-layer sensitive and require scan verification before exact computational reuse.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Longer mollifier enabled by averaged Kloosterman control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper identifies the move from mollifier exponent one-half to four-sevenths as the new ingredient and decomposes the proof into mean-square reduction, arithmetic main-term evaluation, and Kloosterman error control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient and derivative-combination freedom deferred to optimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts a fixed Levinson mollifier with polynomially weighted coefficients chosen by calculus of variations and simultaneously enlarges the initial derivative combination, exposing two independent design freedoms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line and simple-zero proportion theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span defines the proportions being bounded, distinguishes simple critical-line zeros from all critical-line zeros, situates prior bounds, and states the quantitative 0.4077 and 0.401 conclusions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From derivative symmetry to zeros through change of argument
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Parity on the critical line is used to construct a derivative combination whose real-part zeros detect xi zeros, after which rotations of its argument supply a lower bound for those real-part zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compressing the derivative combination into a polynomial differential operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring off the functional-equation factor and using derivative asymptotics turns a finite derivative combination into V(s)=Q((1/L)d/ds)zeta(s), with a symmetry constraint on Q that preserves the critical-line real-part condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reducing zero density to a mollified second moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The argument principle counts zeros of the auxiliary function, a polynomial mollifier shifts the counting line, and Littlewood's lemma plus arithmetic-geometric mean bounds the zero count by the logarithm of a mollified mean square.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Specializing the auxiliary function to certify simple zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates auxiliary-function zeros on the half-line that are not eta zeros and shows that an additional identity forces them to correspond to simple xi zeros, yielding a parallel lower bound with Q restricted to degree one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-square asymptotic at mollifier length below four-sevenths
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper declares that, apart from numerical calculation, its main theorem follows from a mean-value asymptotic for the mollified differential transform V when the mollifier exponent is below four-sevenths.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Lagrange optimization of the mollifier profile
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After fixing the auxiliary polynomial data, the mean-square constant becomes a quadratic functional of P; Euler-Lagrange equations give a boundary-value ODE, and integration by parts reduces its value to boundary data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parameter choices converting the optimized mean into stated proportions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the simple-zero case the source restricts Q to a one-parameter form, evaluates the resulting integrals and variational constant, and records choices producing 0.4013, while a richer Q produces 0.4077.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted zeta integral as a generator for the target mean
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A two-shift proposition packages mollifier products and shifted zeta factors into an analytic function g; applying the proposition and Cauchy's formula in the shift variables recovers the derivative-weighted mean required by Theorem 2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factoring the shifted proposition into arithmetic and analytic lemmas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposition is split into an asymptotic for a mollifier coefficient sum and an analytic evaluation of g; an antisymmetry identity for the arithmetic main term then cancels the unwanted shifted contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian smoothing as an exact transform step
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A preparatory lemma converts the smoothed contour expression by a change of variables to a known integral identity, setting up the main-term analysis with controlled localization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Estermann functional equation and Mellin conversion of the off-diagonal sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The additive-twist Dirichlet series is continued and given a functional equation, then Mellin inversion and a contour move turn the exponentially smoothed double sum into dual Estermann terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform localization of the smoothing contour near its singular point
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After deforming to a real-axis contour with an indentation, rescaling around the singular point gives uniform convergence and a residue evaluation of the localized integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation, contour splitting, and residue extraction of the main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof shifts the defining contour, discards a localized residue, applies zeta's functional equation, splits into two rays, invokes the Estermann transform, and uses the localization lemma to show the two M terms reproduce the claimed main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dyadic off-diagonal reduction and the matched analytic/arithmetic bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remainder is organized by gcd and dyadic N,U,V ranges; the contour is chosen according to whether UV exceeds TN, and separate kernel and exponential-sum lemmas combine to make the total error negligible under the stated length restrictions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separability plus Vaughan's identity decomposes the Möbius-weighted sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The gcd variable and smooth weights are separated, Vaughan's identity rewrites the Möbius coefficient into three structured pieces, and each resulting sum is routed to a different estimation strategy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Averaged Kloosterman bound and exponent bookkeeping for the hard range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Deshouillers-Iwaniec lemma controls the multilinear Kloosterman family; the proof then reduces its bound to finitely many exponent tuples and checks the positive and negative exponent cases, exposing the length restriction needed for the longer mollifier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral average in one range, pointwise Weil bound in the complementary range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the third Vaughan piece the proof splits on the factor size: the large-factor range reuses the averaged lemma, while the small-factor range sums first and applies Weil's pointwise Kloosterman bound plus partial summation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Post-proof numerical improvement without a new analytic mechanism
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The note records a new auxiliary polynomial and parameter value that slightly improves the all-critical-line proportion to 0.4088, showing that the analytic framework admits later numerical retuning.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta function becomes a global analytic object
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Dirichlet series is introduced together with continuation beyond its convergence half-plane and a functional equation, separating the initial representation from the global object studied by RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completion exposes reflection symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplying zeta by gamma, power-of-pi, and polynomial factors packages the functional equation as xi(s)=xi(1-s), the symmetry that organizes the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product translates unique factorization into analysis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The product over primes turns arithmetic factorization into a zero-free analytic statement and motivates using zeta to study prime distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-counting fluctuations are encoded by complex zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The explicit formula for the Chebyshev function makes individual zeros contribute oscillatory terms of size controlled by their real parts, explaining why zero location governs the prime number theorem error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as square-root-scale prime-counting error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey states the direct operational equivalence between RH and a near-square-root error term for prime counting, then notes that direct control of pi(x) offers no evident new route to the zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius cancellation reframes RH but the sharp pointwise route fails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reciprocal Euler product converts RH into cancellation of the Möbius summatory function via Dirichlet-series convergence; the stronger Mertens conjecture would imply RH but was disproved, isolating a tempting yet invalid strengthening.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero counting supplies the natural local spacing scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The functional symmetry, zero-counting asymptotic, argument term, and resulting average gap 2pi/log T provide the normalization later used in random-matrix comparisons.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional symmetry yields convexity, arithmetic sums improve it
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The account separates a general complex-analytic growth bound from Weyl's sharper bound obtained through exponential-sum structure, illustrating how arithmetic input can beat symmetry-only control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Different evidence channels support RH with different force
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey distinguishes finite zero verification, concentration near the line, proved on-line proportions, derivative-zero evidence, random-sign heuristics, and expected prime regularity rather than treating them as a single proof signal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The completed zeta function appears as a Brownian-bridge moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A probabilistic identity represents xi as an expectation of a power of a Brownian-bridge range, supplying an unexpected alternative representation without itself resolving zero location.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Make RH automatic by realizing zero ordinates as a Hermitian spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hilbert-Polya reframes a zero-location theorem as construction of a natural self-adjoint operator, so reality follows structurally from spectral theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as density of fractional-part generators
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Nyman-Beurling replaces zero location by density in L2, and later reformulations make it a weighted approximation of 1 by zeta times finite Dirichlet polynomials, yielding a quantitative distance sequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier transform turns RH into membership in a real-zero class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The even real Xi function and its explicit Fourier transform motivate classifying kernels whose transforms have only real zeros; de Bruijn's theorem supplies a prototype sufficient-condition mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit-formula duality turns RH into positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's prime-zero explicit formula converts RH into positivity for an admissible class of test functions, while Li compresses this to positivity of a distinguished coefficient sequence whose missing geometric meaning is itself a strategic gap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Admissible test functions mediate prime-zero positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source gives the test-function hypotheses, Fourier transform, prime-side sum, and zero-side sum that make Weil's criterion an engineered positivity problem rather than a bare restatement of zero location.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trace formulas resemble explicit formulas without identifying zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selberg's trace formula offers a genuine spectral/geometric duality resembling the prime-zero explicit formula, but the apparent occurrence of zeta zeros in computed eigenvalue lists came from pseudo cusp forms, warning that formal resemblance and numerical coincidence are insufficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH survives translation into series decay, matrix determinants, and divisor inequalities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Three easy-to-state equivalences demonstrate that logically exact reformulations can occupy very different representational domains without automatically exposing a productive proof mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spurious spectral matches do not realize Hilbert-Polya
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computed coincidences between modular Laplacian eigenvalues and zeta or Dirichlet-L zero ordinates were artifacts of pseudo cusp forms; the episode isolates the difference between a legitimate spectral realization and a numerical false friend.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product plus functional equation defines the RH candidate template
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dirichlet, number-field, modular, and elliptic examples motivate a broader class of L-functions, while Langlands and Selberg's axioms frame classification by shared arithmetic and symmetry structures rather than by surface formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local point counts assemble an elliptic-curve L-function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey constructs coefficients from point counts modulo primes, builds an Euler product, and invokes modularity to obtain the functional equation, exemplifying how arithmetic geometry produces an RH-type analytic object.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modular transformation law generates an L-function with RH symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Ramanujan's product defines Fourier coefficients, modular invariance constrains their generating function, and the resulting Euler product and completed functional equation supply another arithmetic-to-analytic pipeline.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair correlation identifies the GUE universality class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Montgomery's normalized zero-pair statistic matches Dyson's Hermitian-matrix correlation function, extending Hilbert-Polya from individual reality to local statistics while explicitly leaving the operator unidentified.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High-zero computation tests statistical predictions, not RH universally
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A fast evaluation algorithm enabled millions of high zeros to be compared with GUE spacing predictions, giving strong finite statistical agreement at extreme height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Characteristic polynomials model zeta values and moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The random-matrix analogy is lifted from eigenvalue locations to characteristic-polynomial values, where exact Haar averages predict previously mysterious arithmetic-normalized zeta moment constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Families acquire unitary, orthogonal, or symplectic symmetry types
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Katz-Sarnak organize L-function families by monodromy/RMT symmetry, and finite-field proofs show how family geometry can control an individual zeta function, suggesting a family-level route unavailable from isolated-function analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Correct ensemble measure predicts moments, values, and central vanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Using Haar rather than physicists' circular measures produces family-specific moment formulas precise enough to predict value distributions and double-zero frequencies, making the analogy quantitatively falsifiable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Class numbers reduce to L-values and exclusion of near-one zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dirichlet's class-number formula transforms Gauss's problem into a lower bound for L(1,chi_d), which in turn becomes control of real zeros near 1; Deuring-Heilbronn results reveal that zeros of distinct L-functions constrain one another.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A hypothetical exceptional zero helps globally while causing ineffectivity locally
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A zero close to 1 forces useful lower bounds or repels zeros of other L-functions, yet assuming its possible existence makes Siegel's bound ineffective; the same obstruction simultaneously creates structure and blocks computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Any fixed improvement in a sieve constant would remove the exceptional zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Brun-Titchmarsh theorem sits exactly at constant 2, while lowering it by any absolute amount in a suitable range would force a quantitative exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros, exposing a sharp methodological bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An implausible half-integer gap model encodes the exceptional-zero obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The alternative hypothesis predicts normalized consecutive zero gaps near half-integers; disproving it, for example by crossing the half-average-spacing threshold, would eliminate Landau-Siegel zeros, but known methods stop essentially at that boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Forced central multiplicity is used to approximate Möbius by family coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Iwaniec proposes families with a forced multiple central zero whose coefficients linearly approximate Möbius, converting RH-style zero control into moment bounds and square-root cancellation for exponential sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exactly fifty percent nonvanishing is insufficient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Eliminating the Landau-Siegel zero would follow from proving a proportion strictly above one half of a modular L-function family is nonvanishing, while current work reaches exactly one half, making the missing epsilon structurally decisive.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A multiple central zero amplifies class-number lower bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Goldfeld's insight is that a simple central zero falls just short but higher multiplicity yields an effective diverging class-number bound; Gross-Zagier's triple-zero examples turn this into a solution of Gauss's problem and motivate extremal families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical analytic zero intuition does not transfer to L-functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conclusion contrasts regularly spaced zeros of differential-equation special functions with irregular and potentially high-multiplicity L-function zeros, diagnosing why familiar analytic techniques may miss arithmetic phenomena.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An RH route may require unexplored families and arithmetic geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conrey argues that families, moment theorems, modularity, exponential-sum estimates, and systematic construction of new L-functions may supply tools that isolated analytic study lacks.

section_argument_map.label: Front matter, motivation, and visual introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces RH and the zeta function amid publication metadata, workshop history, and plots whose visual content is not fully represented by the text layer.

section_argument_map.label: Analytic continuation, Euler product, and prime-zero bridge
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Presents the completed functional equation, Euler product, zero strip, and explicit formula connecting primes to zeros.

section_argument_map.label: Initial equivalent criteria and Möbius route
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Recasts RH as prime-counting and Möbius-sum bounds, then records why the strongest elementary-looking Mertens route fails.

section_argument_map.label: Subsequent analytic progress and evidence for RH
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Surveys approximate functional equations, moment and growth bounds, computational/density evidence, and probabilistic or regularity heuristics.

section_argument_map.label: Spectral, Fourier, probabilistic, and functional-analytic approaches
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces Hilbert-Polya, Polya's real-zero Fourier-transform program, a Brownian-bridge representation, and Nyman-Beurling approximation criteria.

section_argument_map.label: Weil explicit formula and positivity criteria
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Expresses prime-zero duality and turns RH into positivity of test-function sums, including Li's discrete coefficient criterion.

section_argument_map.label: Trace formula, false spectral identification, and elementary equivalences
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Continues Selberg's trace formula, diagnoses spurious computed eigenvalues, compares trace and explicit formulas, and lists cross-representation RH criteria.

section_argument_map.label: Other zeta and L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Generalizes the RH template through Euler products, functional equations, number fields, modular forms, elliptic curves, Langlands, and Selberg-style axioms.

section_argument_map.label: Random-matrix bridge and pair correlation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Connects zero spacings with GUE statistics while distinguishing statistical spectral evidence from an actual operator.

section_argument_map.label: Computations and moment models
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Reports high-zero numerical confirmation and transfers characteristic-polynomial moment calculations to conjectures for zeta values.

section_argument_map.label: Families and symmetry types
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses finite-field monodromy and Haar ensembles to organize L-function families and predict low zeros, moments, values, and central vanishing.

section_argument_map.label: Class numbers and the Landau-Siegel conspiracy
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Links exceptional real zeros to class numbers, repulsion, ineffectivity, sieve constants, and an alternative zero-spacing hypothesis.

section_argument_map.label: Threshold obstructions, multiplicity amplification, and Iwaniec's program
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Shows how tiny improvements in gaps or nonvanishing would remove exceptional zeros and how forced central multiplicity can tame Möbius through families.

section_argument_map.label: Conclusion and references
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Contrasts irregular L-function zeros with classical analytic zeros, argues for an arithmetic/family-based route, and closes with acknowledgements and references interleaved by the two-column extraction.

source_identity.title: The Riemann Hypothesis

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Explicit and trace formulas suggest a common duality pattern in which arithmetic primitives correspond to spectral data, but the pseudo-cusp episode shows that analogy must be backed by a legitimate operator and trace identity.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source provides resemblance and a cautionary failure, not a construction realizing zeta zeros spectrally.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Prime-zero and geodesic-spectrum dualities

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: RH can be transported among prime errors, Möbius cancellation, Hilbert-space approximation, series decay, determinants, and divisor inequalities, making selection of a fertile representation a separate problem from logical equivalence.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: No criterion is shown to be easier; the failed Mertens strengthening warns against confusing a sharper-looking proxy with a viable route.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Equivalent criteria as representation search

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The RMT correspondence coherently predicts zero spacings, value moments, family symmetry, and vanishing statistics across analytic, computational, and finite-field evidence.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source explicitly says this does not identify the Hilbert-Polya operator or directly lead to a proof of RH.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Random matrices: calibrated model, not proof

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Sieve constants, small zero gaps, family nonvanishing, and class-number effectiveness all meet at sharp thresholds whose slightest improvement would eliminate Landau-Siegel zeros.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These equivalences of obstruction do not show which threshold is tractable, and the numerical bounds are source-dated.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Exceptional-zero bottlenecks align across methods

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Rather than suppress exotic central zeros, one can choose structured families with forced multiplicity and exploit their coefficients, moments, and arithmetic geometry to amplify weak information into effective bounds.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Iwaniec's reduction still depends on unproved moment and exponential-sum estimates; the proposed extension to RH remains strategic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local zero statistics motivate characteristic-polynomial value transfer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects mean-spacing-scaled zeta zeros to CUE eigenphases and makes the reusable but explicitly local inference from spectral correlations to characteristic-polynomial value statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg Gaussian limit does not erase systematic finite-height deviations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs the independent Gaussian limiting law with the observed growth of finite-height moment deviations, establishing why a finite-size surrogate is a substantive target rather than a cosmetic approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta moments are normalized into an arithmetic factor and an unknown coefficient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the moment-coefficient problem in a form that later permits a clean separation between arithmetic Euler-product data and a universal random-matrix coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two exact CUE generators encode modulus and argument statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the finite-N gamma-product generators for absolute value and phase, and makes the logarithm branch convention and eigenphase jump explicit; these are the analytic engines for all later distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-density matching fixes matrix size and separates universal from arithmetic effects
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies N with log(T/2π), interprets finite-height zeta behavior through finite-degree CUE polynomials, and isolates random-matrix short-range effects from prime-driven long-range corrections in the moment conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Low-lying family statistics require the compact group selected by symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Limits naive CUE transfer by explaining that averaging low zeros across L-function families may select orthogonal or symplectic groups, so the correct characteristic-polynomial model depends on family symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Haar eigenphase integration becomes a Selberg integral for |Z| moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows the reusable derivation chain from a characteristic-polynomial eigenvalue product, through the CUE joint density and trigonometric coordinates, to a Selberg integral and exact gamma product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A branch-controlled sine series converts the phase generator to Selberg form
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the argument generator by fixing the logarithm branch, evaluating its sine series, and transforming the Haar integral into the second exact gamma product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One generator yields moments, cumulants, and the full density through three transforms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes explicit the reusable interface from Taylor coefficients of M_N to moments, derivatives of log M_N to cumulants, and Fourier inversion to the value density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Variance grows logarithmically while higher real-part cumulants stabilize
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the divergent second cumulant from bounded higher cumulants using integral representations and rescaling, which is the key scale separation behind Gaussian normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalized higher cumulants vanish and leave a Gaussian Fourier kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the conceptual proof of the real-part central limit: after variance normalization every cumulant above order two disappears, so Fourier inversion converges to the Gaussian density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Odd cumulants create asymmetric finite-N corrections before the Gaussian limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how retaining higher cumulants produces a correction expansion, identifies the leading (log N)^(-3/2) deviation, and traces finite-N asymmetry to odd powers, including an Airy resummation of the cubic term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponentiating the cumulant series recovers the Gaussian moment hierarchy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Closes the analytic loop by showing how cumulants reconstruct moments and why even moments have the Gaussian leading relation while odd moments are lower order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Argument cumulants have exact parity and equal eigenvalue-count fluctuations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the vanishing of all odd cumulants for Im log Z, relates even cumulants to the real-part calculation, and identifies Im log Z differences with fluctuations of eigenvalue counts in arcs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact evenness removes cubic corrections and accelerates Gaussian convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the identically zero odd cumulants to an even finite-N density and a (log N)^(-2) correction scale, asymptotically smaller than for the real part.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mixed cumulants vanish after scaling, yielding independent Gaussian components
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs the joint modulus-phase generator, evaluates it in Selberg form, and shows that normalized mixed terms vanish so the bivariate density factors into two Gaussian densities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Barnes G compresses the universal leading coefficient of modulus moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the N-normalized CUE modulus moment coefficient with a Barnes G ratio, extends it analytically, exposes its pole structure, and reduces integer values to factorial products matching known zeta coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The phase generator has a symmetric Barnes G leading coefficient and zero lattice
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carries the same compression method to the argument generator, where parity produces a symmetric Barnes G product and a structured set of zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Density-matched finite N explains deviations that the limiting Gaussian misses
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the mean-spacing map to select N≈42 and reports that exact finite-N CUE densities and moments track high-zero zeta data better than the asymptotic Gaussian, including the real/imaginary asymmetry contrast.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Long-range prime effects multiply the finite-N universal moment factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why local random-matrix information is incomplete, derives the need for an independent prime product under a truncated Euler-product heuristic, and combines it with the Barnes G CUE coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adding the arithmetic factor improves real-part moment predictions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines real-part moments by differentiating the product of the CUE and arithmetic generators and compares CUE-only versus CUE-plus-primes predictions against the same numerical data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A separate arithmetic product corrects phase moments and matches low-order checks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs the phase analogue of the multiplicative model, reports improved finite-height moments, and checks consistency with the second-moment formula and independent low-order heuristics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Saddle and pole regimes separate bulk lognormal behavior from near-zero mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourier inversion gives a large-N lognormal-type bulk approximation, while the nearest pole controls the fixed-N near-zero limit; the source explicitly diagnoses why exchanging the N and w limits invalidates the bulk approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Squaring and integrating the zero side creates a double-zero sum; tails outside the target height range are controlled by local zero counts, and a residue integral produces the weight w, identifying the result with F after x=T^alpha. Nonnegativity then supplies the theorem's lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantitative Parseval handles an infinite Dirichlet-series mean square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The prime side is evaluated with a quantitative Parseval identity whose coefficient-dependent error permits the infinite Dirichlet series; the author contrasts it with a weaker polynomial-only mean-square theorem and explains the methodological choice.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three x-ranges isolate the dominant term and prove the low-frequency asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Prime-number-theorem estimates, error-term mean squares, and Cauchy-Schwarz are organized into three x regimes. Their dominant terms combine with the zero-side identity after x=T^alpha to yield the theorem uniformly below alpha=1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Beyond unit frequency, off-diagonal shifted-prime correlations become main-order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For x>T, prior errors cease to be negligible and termwise integration leaves too many nondiagonal contributions. Regrouping exposes shifted von Mangoldt correlations; their conjectured mean gives the desired order for 1<=alpha<2, while additional independence of errors would extend the prediction through all larger alpha.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A character-average analogue supports stability past the proved boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A q-analogue replaces the continuous mean square by an average over characters and is shown in progressively wider parameter ranges, providing independent structural evidence that no new large-alpha transition is expected even though sharper error analysis is needed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier profiles are chosen to extract the first pair-sum corollaries

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The diagonal pair mass controls the second moment of zero multiplicities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Counting zeros with multiplicity identifies equal-ordinate pairs with the multiplicity second moment. Bounding that diagonal contribution by the nonnegative kernel sum and comparing it with the total zero count yields the stated positive proportion of simple zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A triangular Fourier kernel forces gaps below the mean
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A compactly supported triangular transform gives a computable lower bound for close pairs. After removing diagonal terms, positivity of C(A) for some A<1 guarantees a subaverage normalized gap; evaluating at 0.68 supplies the explicit stated constant and exposes kernel optimization as the route to improvement.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a Lehmer pair by multiplying the squared gap between consecutive simple positive zeros by an interaction sum over every other signed zero. The criterion compresses a global zero configuration into one local-gap-versus-background test.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Lehmer pair yields a quantitative lower bound for Λ
