result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The unit defines Pn, Vn, and its limiting value V, then records how bounds on this polynomial extremum transfer to permissible classical zero-free constants, including Stechkin's sharpening.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two-lever improvement program: better certificates and retained error information
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors frame their advance as the combination of randomized search for higher-degree certificates and a sharper use of the analytic error term, a reusable decomposition between representation search and proof-bound refinement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Improved zero-free and Landau bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states both its explicit zero-free theorem and the improved upper bound on the limiting polynomial extremum, connecting the analytic and optimization outputs while keeping them distinct.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bootstrap a known zero-free region against a hypothetical boundary zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Kadiri's method starts from an established constant R and a target lower parameter r, assumes a zero in the intervening strip, and seeks an intermediate R0 that rules it out; this exposes the logical bootstrap underlying the numerical iteration.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kernel monotonicity removes the unknown zero height from the R0 bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After defining normalized height variables, a compactly supported kernel, and admissible kappa/delta constraints, the method derives an R0 inequality and uses monotonicity of K and sign monotonicity of C to replace the unknown w and eta by endpoint data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nested replacement iteration converts a local improvement into a stable constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The algorithm repeatedly replaces the assumed region constant with the newly certified one while keeping r below it, uses inner and outer tolerances, and stops only when the improvement stabilizes, making the bootstrap computationally explicit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Split the eta range and balance complementary denominator bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introducing eta1 preserves useful negativity from C(eta): small eta uses a stronger lower bound on w, while larger eta retains -C(eta1). A minimax choice balances the two, and the source attributes most of the final gain to this retention plus the new polynomial.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: C1 and C2: sharpen a reusable exponential majorant with directed rounding
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The error is decomposed into four terms; for C2, precomputed moments replace repeated integration and a cubic exponential majorant sharpens the estimate, while direction-aware rounding preserves rigor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: C3: replace a global zero-counting error bound by an explicit tail sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Instead of inheriting an explicit N(T) error estimate, the authors express the needed contribution as a tail over zeta zeros, subtract a computable initial segment at t=0, and use Lehman's monotone-sum integral bound for positive t.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: C4: isolate numerically tractable middle ranges and analytically bound tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A piecewise majorant for U0 and symmetry reduce the integral; the domain is split at formula-change points and around its moving peak, middle pieces are evaluated numerically, and logarithmic tail inequalities yield explicit analytic bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Use a cheap Landau surrogate inside simulated annealing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explains why the true Kadiri objective is too expensive for repeated search and substitutes the fast Landau functional, while retaining annealing's controlled willingness to cross local barriers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Square-modulus coordinates make global nonnegativity automatic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Parametrizing f as the squared magnitude of a complex polynomial converts a global nonnegativity constraint into an invariant of the representation; feasibility then reduces to coefficient autocorrelations, nonnegativity checks, and a1>a0.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Incremental autocorrelation updates keep annealing inside the admissible set
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A one-coordinate move updates all affected autocorrelations in linear time, rejects infeasible states, applies the annealing rule to valid states, then combines cooling, greedy descent, shrinking step size, and diversified parallel runs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Refined annealing yields the degree-40 Landau certificate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Coarse searches followed by finer local passes produce F40 and a strictly improved upper bound for V40, illustrating how heuristic exploration becomes a checkable certificate once a concrete admissible polynomial is fixed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A good Landau polynomial need not optimize the true zero-free constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying Kadiri's calculation to record Landau polynomials reveals that their ranking for V does not determine their ranking for R0, explicitly diagnosing surrogate-objective mismatch.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rescore near-optimal surrogate candidates under the true objective
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors test hundreds of thousands of strong Landau candidates with Kadiri's objective, find many better R0 certificates, and refine the best degree-16 candidate; the eventual winner is not the degree-16 Landau record.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Increasing verified RH height has a diminishing asymptotic payoff in this method
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Holding the polynomial and other choices fixed while varying T0 yields an empirical formula approaching a limiting R0, which identifies finite verified height as a lever with bounded long-run benefit rather than an unlimited route to improvement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free width propagates to explicit prime-counting error bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The improved zero-free region is converted into sharper explicit bounds for theta, psi, and pi-li; the source also notes that a shifted-log zero-free form is asymptotically equivalent yet could further improve the finite explicit corollaries.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The functional equation and unit-modulus phase factor turn the geometric condition that zeta lies on eiφR into a root condition for Φ, while separating zeta zeros from roots of a rotating phase equation; this is the paper's reusable bridge from planar value distribution to discrete sampling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Counting and moment laws for directional critical-line intersections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the phase-root counting asymptotic and the first two discrete moments of zeta over intersections with eiφR, including the structural contrast that the leading second moment is direction-independent while the first varies as eiφ cos φ.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Directional means and arbitrarily large values on half-lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Translates the counting and moment laws into conditional directional means, an unconditional zero mean on the imaginary axis, positivity of real components, and unconditional arbitrarily large values on prescribed right-half-plane half-lines.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nonzero phase crossings and the missing imaginary-axis bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates phase roots that coincide with zeta zeros from genuine nonzero intersections, gives a directional lower bound away from φ=π/2, and identifies Fujii's proposed equidistribution of zero phases as a route to information in the exceptional direction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Monotone phase rotation converts root counts to a winding number
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the logarithmic derivative asymptotic to show that Δ rotates monotonically with increasing speed, identifies roots of a prescribed phase with a winding number, integrates the rotation rate, and removes a convenient endpoint assumption with a controlled error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residues sample zeta at phase roots under a separated endpoint choice
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a variation of the Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek method in which the logarithmic derivative of Δ-e^{2iφ} provides poles at the desired sampling ordinates, chooses an endpoint separated from them, and expresses the first discrete moment as four contour contributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Suppress three contour sides and reflect the main side
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses rapid geometric-series expansions and growth bounds to make the right, top, and bottom sides negligible, then reflects the left side through s↦1-s and the functional equation so its integrand becomes a tractable Dirichlet-series kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gonek's lemma isolates the two components of the first moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the reflected contour's two principal pieces: Gonek's lemma extracts the diagonal-scale term from ζ(s)Δ(1-s), while direct integration of ζ(s) supplies the phase-weighted companion; their combination yields 1+e^{2iφ}=2e^{iφ}cosφ.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The first-moment contour architecture lifts to the square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how the same phase-root residue kernel is reused for ζ(s)ζ(1-s), with one contour side now contributing a phase-dependent lower-order term and the reflected side producing ζ(s)^2Δ'(1-s).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A divisor-sum diagonal produces the second moment's leading square logarithm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies Gonek's lemma to ζ(s)^2Δ(1-s), converts the result to a divisor summatory asymptotic, and combines it with the phase-dependent companion term to obtain the second-moment expansion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditional and unconditional denominators yield different mean-value conclusions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes explicit that the same first-moment numerator becomes a full directional mean under RH through Nφ(T) asymptotics, while the imaginary-axis zero mean follows unconditionally because its main term vanishes and the phase-root count supplies a sufficient denominator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second-moment mass forces a large value in every dyadic interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares the number of phase samples in (T,2T] with their second-moment mass to rule out a uniform sub-square-root-log bound, then uses the signed first moment to force the desired half-line sign; the exceptional imaginary direction uses its zero-mean relation to obtain both signs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cauchy-Schwarz turns moments into a count of nonzero phase crossings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the squared first moment to the product of the nonzero-sample count and second moment, yielding the lower bound for genuine line crossings after inserting the two moment asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gram points recast real-axis intersections and expose failures of sign alternation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the phase roots to Gram points, introduces the real Hardy Z-function, relates sign changes to critical-line zeros, and interprets failures of Gram's law as negative real-axis intersections whose unbounded magnitude remains open.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Directional moments imply lower growth of fourth moments at Gram points
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Translates the paper's first and second moment asymptotics into sums over Gram points and combines the second moment with Cauchy-Schwarz to force a fourth-moment lower bound, complementing prior upper-bound work.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Averaging directional means suggests a small-versus-large intersection split
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Integrates the conditional means e^{iφ}cosφ over direction to obtain 1/2, relates that value to a separate a-point derivative phenomenon, and proposes the heuristic that each directional intersection set divides roughly equally between very small and large magnitudes around its mean.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The method extends to Dirichlet L-functions but encounters higher-degree factorization barriers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records that the mechanism transfers easily to Dirichlet L-functions but becomes difficult for higher-degree L-functions, with quadratic Dedekind zeta treated only by exploiting the factorization ζK=ζL and zero symmetry.

source_identity.title: On the value-distribution of the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: A unit-modulus functional-equation factor can discretize intersections of an analytic value curve with a chosen direction, after which winding counts and logarithmic-derivative residues provide matched cardinality and sampled-value statistics.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Established here only for the stated zeta/Δ setting; shared phase structure and suitable analytic control must be rechecked for any transfer.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Phase discretization as a bridge from curve geometry to analytic sampling

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The sample count normalizes a first moment into a directional mean, the second moment forces large samples, and the signed first moment or a zero-mean symmetry is separately needed to place those samples on a desired half-line.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: General directional normalization is conditional on RH or almost-all critical-line zeros, while the imaginary-axis branch has a distinct unconditional argument.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Moments become geometric information only after the correct count and sign controls

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Specializing the phase to the real axis makes negative intersections equivalent to failures of the normalized Gram sign rule, while the same discrete moments impose aggregate growth constraints on Hardy Z values at Gram points.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source does not determine whether negative real intersections have unbounded magnitude, and aggregate moments do not restore pointwise Gram interlacing.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Gram-law failure and Gram-point moments are two views of real-axis phase sampling

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The proof depends not merely on a functional equation but on phase-factor expansions and Dirichlet-series kernels whose main terms remain tractable; factorization supplies that tractability in the cited quadratic Dedekind case.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The paper states difficulty for higher degree and one successful factored case, not a necessary-and-sufficient transfer criterion.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: The contour method's portability is governed by structural factorization

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The family e^{iφ}cosφ traces a circle of conditional directional means and averages to 1/2, offering a geometric account of the positive-real tendency and a heuristic small/large split.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Neither the mean circle nor the heuristic split proves density of critical-line zeta values in the complex plane.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Directional means form a coherent planar picture but not a density theorem

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why unweighted moment inequalities do not yield positive-proportion nonvanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper distinguishes central-line nonvanishing from the better-understood near-one problem and explains that even conjectural raw moments combined with Cauchy-Schwarz do not supply the desired positive proportion, motivating a different detector.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fixed-point and real-segment nonvanishing targets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the positive-proportion fixed-point result and the stronger absence of real zeros on a segment beginning a logarithmic distance to the right of one half.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct counting through a mollified contour identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the reusable architecture: choose sieve-like weights with a coefficient gap, form a mollifier, represent a smoothed coefficient sum by a contour integral, use the functional equation and truncation to split it into LM, I, and J, then compare their mean squares and pass from points to circles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Barban-Vehov weights as a cancellation-producing mollifier kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the difference of two logarithmic Möbius weights, the divisor-sum coefficient a(n), and the mean-square/progression estimates that turn the designed cancellation into usable average control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted-convolution control for the cancellation coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 1.3 supplies the non-diagonal input later needed for the detector's second moment; its proof combines congruence compatibility, a bounded polynomial expansion, divisor reparametrization, and Graham's weight estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two-scale mollifier with an initial coefficient gap
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses Y and Z, forms M(s,chi), records a(1)=1 and a(n)=0 for 1<n<=Y, and uses the large sieve to bound the mollifier mean square; the gap is later decisive for the interval argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The basic equation S(s,chi)=L(s,chi)M(s,chi)+I(s,chi)+J(s,chi)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin inversion and a contour shift isolate LM; the functional equation and a length-Z truncation then divide the remaining integral into a principal polynomial piece I and tail J, making zeros testable by comparing independently estimable quantities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large-sieve control of the functional-equation tail J
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the truncated Dirichlet-series tail is small on average by combining Stirling decay, two Cauchy-Schwarz applications, the large sieve, and the mollifier bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Character orthogonality makes the detector's first moment explicit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The smoothed coefficient detector S has a first moment essentially equal to the number of characters because orthogonality selects the congruence-one terms while smoothing and coefficient bounds suppress the rest.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decomposing the S second moment into diagonal and congruence off-diagonal pieces
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the second moment by character orthogonality and partitions pairs into equality and two ordered congruence cases, exposing where shifted-convolution estimates are needed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted-convolution suppression of congruent unequal pairs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof rewrites congruent indices as n2=n1+jq, dyadically localizes them, invokes Proposition 1.3, and treats ranges crossing q by Cauchy-Schwarz, converting arithmetic cancellation into a small off-diagonal contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The coefficient gap determines the S diagonal main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On the equality diagonal the condition a(n)=0 for 1<n<=Y isolates the unit contribution, while Graham's mean-square estimate and partial summation evaluate the remaining Y-to-Z and Z-to-q ranges.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Mellin-gamma kernel representation for I
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites I as a finite arithmetic sum weighted by R_a(s,y), records the kernel symmetry, and obtains a residue expansion whose truncation can later separate main and error terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dual residue expansions for large and small kernel argument
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves the kernel contour to control its remainder for y>=1 and supplies the complementary expansion for y<=1, giving a uniform decay statement and coefficients for later Taylor-like diagonal analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parity-sensitive character orthogonality converts the I mean square to arithmetic congruences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding I and summing characters of fixed parity produces explicit equality, sign, and exceptional principal-character contributions, turning an analytic mean square into structured four-index sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The coupled four-index sums reveal the true diagonal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the positive and negative congruence sums, isolates the principal-character correction, and identifies simultaneous multiplicative equality and kernel-scale matching as the intended main contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounding the negative congruence by complementary-product geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because all indices are below sqrt(q), the negative congruence becomes an exact complementary relation m1 n2=q-m2 n1; splitting according to relative factor sizes limits residue-class choices and yields negligibility.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The principal-character correction is negligible
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separately bounds the term removed by character orthogonality using simple sums of the mollifier weights, closing a potential exceptional contribution before diagonal evaluation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting the diagonal kernel sum into main and tail regions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the diagonal arithmetic sum, separates the range according to the kernel argument, and substitutes the residue expansion so that a finite main series and a controlled contour remainder can be treated independently.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Choosing a deep residue truncation makes the kernel tail logarithmically negligible
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 8.1 converts multiplicative equality into a gcd-counting bound; applying it to the contour remainder and choosing K as a high power of log q drives the error below the main scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A refined gcd parametrization evaluates weighted diagonal powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 8.2 reparametrizes the equality m1 n2=m2 n1 using the gcd of m1,m2 and a shared multiple, then applies the Barban-Vehov correlation estimate to control complex powers of the kernel ratio.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reducing the I mean square to one arithmetic main sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the refined diagonal estimate to the residue series, controls single and double residue errors, handles the complementary diagonal range analogously, and summarizes all prior reductions in a single mean-square formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Encoding diagonal quadruples by a shared product and gcd data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines N(sigma), uses m1 n2=m2 n1 to remove the imaginary part, and rewrites each quadruple via a common product, gcd, coprime factors, and finite range constraints.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Expanding the two-scale weights exposes support and multiplicative error structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the inner coprime weight correlation into four cutoff combinations and proves it vanishes beyond the smaller cutoff while admitting a multiplicative main term plus controlled errors within support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Support cutoff collapses N(sigma) to a squarefree multiplicative sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the vanishing of cutoff combinations for i>Y, isolates the surviving term, interchanges ranges to control errors, and arrives at the squarefree arithmetic expression that Section 10 can evaluate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Asymptotic mean square of the principal integral I
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the culmination of Sections 5-10: a character mean-square asymptotic with an explicit arithmetic constant, a sigma-dependent analytic factor, and distinct error regimes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reducing Proposition 10.1 to evaluation of N(sigma)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects the non-diagonal, principal-character, kernel-tail, and diagonal-expansion errors, substitutes the Section 9 expression, and safely extends a finite arithmetic sum to an infinite multiplicative one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parity splitting and partial summation identify the main constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates even and odd squarefree factors, introduces a convolutional arithmetic function, derives its Euler product and mean value, and uses partial summation to evaluate N at and to the right of one half.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Final I mean-square formula with critical and off-critical error scales
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the evaluated arithmetic main term into the analytic reduction and records how the error changes at sigma=1/2, moderately right of it, and near one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First moment versus second moment counts nonzero central values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions characters according to whether L(s0,chi) vanishes, applies the basic equation on the zero set, bounds I+J in first moment, and uses Cauchy-Schwarz with the S second moment to obtain a positive nonvanishing proportion at the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extending the fixed-point count across the right half of the strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Discretizes the distance of sigma from one half, combines the appropriate S and I second-moment regimes, and produces an explicit positive lower-bound function depending on sigma.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Turning pointwise nonvanishing into a short-interval zero count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses the previously dormant cutoff Y=q^(1/4), divides the real segment into intervals of length 1/log q, associates a circle to each interval, and defines the count of characters with a zero there.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parameterized duality of the Riesz and Baez-Duarte criteria
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Places the continuous Riesz growth criterion and discrete Baez-Duarte decay criterion into the reusable paired form c_k=O(k^{-delta}) iff R(x)=O(x^{1-delta}), making the shift by one exponent explicit rather than relying only on transitivity through RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces a slowly convergent zeta-reciprocal power series by a Mobius-weighted exponential sum, a representation change that later makes comparison with the binomial formula for c_k possible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson transform from finite differences c_k to R(x)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that c_k is the first entry in iterated forward differences of f(k)=1/zeta(2k+2), then exponentiates the shift operator to obtain the exact identity sum c_k x^k/k!=e^x R(x)/x. This is the structural bridge behind the continuous-discrete duality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Forward growth transfer from c_k to R(x)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the general equivalence theorem and proves the c_k-to-R direction by combining the exact exponential transform with a coefficient-weight asymptotic for sum k^{-delta}x^k/k!, exposing Poisson smoothing as the source of the exponent shift.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recovering c_k decay from integer samples of R
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Completes the converse by combining R(k)=O(k^{1-delta}) with the appendix bound between c_k and R(k)/k; it also makes explicit why the available error restricts the proved transfer to delta<3/2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Binomial-to-exponential explanation of c_k approximately equal to R(k)/k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites c_k as a Mobius-weighted binomial-kernel sum and approximates (1-1/n^2)^k by exp(-k/n^2), directly matching the accelerated Riesz representation at x=k. This supplies an interpretable de-Poissonization heuristic later made quantitative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted generating family and the obstruction to formal unweighted summation
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: alternating sums and divergent total sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the alternating sum from the Mobius/binomial representation, embeds it in a parameterized generating identity with asymmetric convergence domains, and contrasts it with a formal shift-operator evaluation of sum c_k whose predicted value is defeated by growing oscillations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contrasting asymptotics for alternating and ordinary partial sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes a convergent alternating accumulation, conjectured to approach its limit at c_k-like rate, from an ordinary partial sum conjectured to oscillate with growing n^{1/4} scale. result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discrete self-entanglement constraint for the Riesz function

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Controls the difference between exponential and binomial kernels by removing Mobius signs, bounding a unimodal summand by its maximum plus an integral, and estimating that integral through Gaussian and beta-function asymptotics. result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sharp sixth moment as the decoupling target
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction identifies the essentially sharp A6 mean-value estimate as the paper's objective and states that it will be obtained from a curve-decoupling theorem, clarifying both the target quantity and the intended analytical bridge.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bombieri-Iwaniec first- and second-spacing architecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source decomposes the zeta-function route into short cubic-phase sums, a first-spacing distribution of (h,h^2,h^(3/2),h^(1/2)), a second-spacing distribution of interval-dependent phase vectors, and a double-large-sieve interface. It explicitly limits the paper's new input to the first spacing problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multilinear decoupling for even-dimensional nondegenerate curves
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 gives the central scale-sensitive decoupling inequality for separated arcs of an even-dimensional curve under a Wronskian nondegeneracy condition, reducing an L^(3d) multilinear quantity to L^6 pieces on N^(-1/2) parameter intervals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two gaps from bilinear decoupling to the A6 mean value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates two distinct obstacles between Theorem 1 and Theorem 2: replacing ball averages by a smaller anisotropic periodic region, and converting a bilinear estimate into a linear one. This is a reusable decomposition of the proof burden.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Planar L6 decoupling as the operative lower-dimensional input
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remarks identify planar nonzero-curvature L6 decoupling, including its discrete coefficient form, as the main analytical input for the higher-dimensional theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positioning the new inequality between multilinear endpoints
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Fourier-support reformulation relates the theorem to known d-linear and (d-1)-linear decouplings, and shows that the latter exponent pair is obtained by interpolation between the elementary Parseval endpoint and the new (3d,6) endpoint.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Preliminary interpolation bound and paired-tangent transversality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An L^d estimate derived by randomization and a trivial L-infinity bound are interpolated via wave packets to a preliminary L^(3d)-L6 inequality. The Wronskian condition is then converted into the wedge-product transversality of paired first and second derivatives needed for factorization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bootstrap by quadratic normal forms and product factorization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof partitions the large ball into K-cubes, Taylor-expands each separated arc to quadratic order, uses transversality to turn the ambient integral into a product of planar factors, applies planar decoupling after rescaling, and obtains b(N) bounded by b(N^(2/3)) up to N^epsilon.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Specializing decoupling to d=4 and an anisotropic intermediate box
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Section 2 specializes the curve, imposes the derivative condition needed by the application, enlarges the averaging domain to an anisotropic box, partitions it into N-cubes, and transfers Theorem 1 to a bilinear discrete estimate prepared for a second decoupling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Taylor-periodicity normal form for separated short intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For two separated length-N^(1/2) intervals, Taylor expansion plus periodic changes of variables converts the coupled phases into independent planar quadratic phases. Planar decoupling then refines the interval scale to N^(1/4), with an explanation of why a residual term can be absorbed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Aggregation over translated boxes and final bilinear estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The argument tiles the larger Huxley box by translated intermediate boxes, carries the phase translation into coefficients, and repeats the periodic/Taylor normalization at the N^(1/4) scale. Planar L6 control then yields the decisive bilinear L12 estimate on the full anisotropic domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Essentially sharp A6 mean value theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 states the twelfth-moment bound N^(6+epsilon) for the four-coordinate exponential sum that supplies the optimal first-spacing input.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Encoding moment solutions by a normalized nondegenerate curve
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof interprets a localized bilinear moment as a solution count, expands the fractional powers around a base point, uses the first two exact moment equations to cancel low-order terms, and packages the remaining constraints into a curve satisfying the earlier derivative condition. The bilinear estimate then bounds the localized count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bilinear-to-linear conversion by recursive interval decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Bourgain-Guth style broad/narrow decomposition recursively partitions the summation interval, controls separated pairs with the localized bilinear estimate, and derives a contraction recurrence for the linear twelfth moment.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Anisotropically rescaled first-spacing estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Corollary 3 converts Theorem 2 into Huxley's A6(N,delta,Delta) notation and supplies the delta*Delta*N^(9+epsilon) bound later inserted directly into the large sieve.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduction of smooth exponential sums to interval phase vectors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The application fixes derivative nondegeneracy, introduces the intermediate scales N and R, and cites the established Bombieri-Iwaniec reduction that bounds the original sum using short sums indexed by minor-arc intervals and four-dimensional phase vectors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Holder reduction to a sixfold first-spacing distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An interval-count estimate, the preliminary sum bound, and sixth-power Holder produce a dichotomy: either a direct bound holds or the problem reduces to a bilinear sum coupling interval phase vectors with a sixfold convolution of the first-spacing curve.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Double large sieve separates the two spacing problems
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The double large sieve bounds the coupled phase sum by the geometric mean of a first-spacing count A and a second-spacing count B1, times coordinate-volume factors, cleanly isolating what the new mean-value theorem can control from what must be imported.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First-spacing count identified with A6
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourier localization turns the first-spacing count A into a scaled A6 integral with delta=Q^2/(H^2R^2), after which Corollary 3 yields A bounded by delta^2 H^(10+epsilon). This is the direct causal interface from decoupling to the large sieve.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Combining first and baseline second spacing bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An imported second-spacing estimate for B1 is combined with the new A bound and the large-sieve reduction; choosing N=M*T^(-2/7) yields the exponential-sum estimate with exponent 13/84 over its initial M range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resonance-curve tightening of the second-spacing window
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source introduces a tunable factor V that narrows one coordinate window in the second-spacing count while enlarging the adjacent volume factor, allowing Huxley's resonance-curve estimate for BV to replace the baseline B1 bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Optimizing the resonance bound across scale regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combining the refined large-sieve and second-spacing bounds produces a minimum of competing terms. Optimizing N, then switching to N comparable to R^2 when the first optimizer violates a scale constraint, yields piecewise bounds that extend the desired estimate down to M>=T^(17/42).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform exponential-sum estimate in the large-alpha range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4 packages the preceding parameter analysis into the estimate |S| bounded by M^(1/2)T^(13/84+epsilon) for log M/log T between 17/42 and 1/2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Covering complementary scales and transferring to zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two external exponential-sum bounds cover the alpha range below Theorem 4, with an overlap calculation ensuring full coverage. For the logarithmic phase relevant to zeta, the approximate functional equation, partial summation, and dyadic dissection then transfer the uniform short-sum estimate to the critical-line bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moment order and the doubling of the critical-line saving
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remark compares essentially optimal A4, A5, and A6 inputs and interprets the 13/84 exponent as exactly doubling the original Bombieri-Iwaniec saving over 1/6.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From the paper's estimate to an exponent pair
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source reformulates the result as the exponent pair (13/84,55/84), handles scales with M above the square root by renormalizing T or applying the B-process after Poisson summation, and notes the fixed-point relation of the relevant pair under B.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extending partial-interval phases to use exponent-pair theory
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: To remove the full-interval assumption, the source constructs a smooth extension of the phase from [a,b] to [M/2,M] using a monomial derivative model plus a correcting polynomial, argues that derivative conditions persist, and then invokes an interval-restriction lemma at logarithmic cost.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From the analytic zeta setup to a fundamental-domain formulation of RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage assembles the series continuation, pole, real and nontrivial zeros, critical strip, Laurent expansion, and functional equation, then explicitly reframes the intended RH route in terms of conformal mappings of fundamental domains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fundamental domains near an essential singularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source defines the working role of fundamental regions as domains mapped conformally onto a slit plane and derives the proposed accumulation pattern: finitely many meet a compact set, while infinitely many occur outside it toward infinity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simultaneous continuation of real-axis pre-images and the red-black curve encoding
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This constructs pre-image arcs through zeros, continues them across derivative branch points, distinguishes the continuation stopped by the pole, and turns sign on the real image into a two-color encoding whose junctions mark zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quasi-lacunary value 1 and the infinite strip decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper identifies 1 as a quasi-lacunary value, obtains unbounded boundary curves from continuation over (1,+infinity), and states that consecutive curves bound doubly infinite strips mapped onto a slit plane; the proof uses the unique pole to rule out boundary intersection.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The j_k-strip inventory of zeros, one-points, and real-axis components
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Within each strip the source distinguishes one component mapping bijectively to (-infinity,1) from finitely many components mapping to the whole real axis, thereby tying the count of curves to nontrivial zeros and points where zeta equals 1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Color alternation constrains remote branches, derivative zeros, and circle pre-images
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 imposes a common left-half-plane direction on both sign branches, and the source then applies color alternation to claim unique derivative zeros between consecutive trivial zeros and unbounded alternating components of circle pre-images.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unique unbounded component of the unit-disc pre-image in each strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem links uniqueness of the distinguished real-axis component in a strip to uniqueness of an unbounded component over the unit disc by taking pre-images of rays as their angle tends to zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pulling back an orthogonal polar net as a conformal-coordinate visualization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source replaces isolated real-axis curves with the pre-image of rays and concentric circles, using color, saturation, brightness, and conformal modulus to compare image quadrilaterals with their pre-images and to visualize repeating strip geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Expanding zero loops, fusion at branch points, and fundamental-domain boundaries
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starting from small disjoint pre-image circles around zeros, the passage increases the radius until loops fuse at derivative branch points, then combines pre-images of branch-value segments and (1,+infinity) to bound sub-strips that are declared fundamental domains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adjacent-strip case: incompatible tangent half-planes in two configurations

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate strip width and decreasing average zero spacing

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three-part analytic-to-computational decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof is factored into an asymptotic theorem, a nearby-prime lemma, and a two-prime computation; this is the source's central modular interface and explains how the conditional conclusion is assembled.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted representation count turns existence into a positivity comparison
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source encodes prime triples with von Mangoldt weights, expresses the count through a truncated integral, and reduces existence to proving that a leading term dominates an explicitly bounded remainder above 10^20.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Narrowed major arcs isolate a GRH-controlled remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The main analytic refinement is to shrink the major-arc intervals, split the integral into a leading part and a complementary remainder, and use a GRH zero-sum estimate for the exponential sum on that remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A theta-function error bound produces a nearby prime and a bounded even remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under GRH, a bound for the Chebyshev theta function rules out an excessively long prime-free interval and yields a prime p for which n-p lies between 4 and 1.615 times 10^12. This is the analytic bridge that compresses every remaining odd case into the range of the two-prime computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A better asymptotic log factor can lose to a smaller explicit constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors explain that a GRH estimate with one log factor was not used because its derived constant made it numerically worse at the operative scale than Schoenfeld's two-log estimate. This is a reusable warning that finite-range optimization can reverse an asymptotic preference.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtracting the nearby prime reduces the residual task to finite Goldbach verification
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explicitly composes the intermediate lemma with the theorem that every even number through 10^13 is a sum of two primes: for an odd n below 10^20, n-p is even and small enough for the verified range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conventional Goldbach verification as cumulative translated-set coverage
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The usual computation builds primes in a target interval and cumulatively unions their translations by small odd primes until every even target is covered. The passage isolates prime generation as the bottleneck and records how the auxiliary interval margin depends on the largest small prime used.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Search near the interval endpoint and precompute the small difference primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The optimized approach reverses which prime set is expensive: it takes consecutive primes near the interval start, precomputes odd primes only up to roughly the interval width, and covers targets by translated copies of that fixed small-prime set. A density calculation motivates a finite candidate count without serving as the certification itself.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The optimized covering method trades one reusable sieve for cheap per-interval prime discovery
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper directly compares resource profiles: the older method sieves all primes in every high interval, while the new method sieves a larger low prime table once and then locates only a bounded list of primes near each interval. It also states the semantic cost: the witness prime is not extremal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded-base strong-pseudoprime tests certify the needed nearby primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The generation of primes near each interval start relies on quoted size thresholds under which passing strong-pseudoprime tests to specified initial prime bases implies primality, turning a probabilistic-looking filter into a bounded deterministic certificate for this range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bitset shifts realize coverage and the completed range is reported with a worst witness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each small-prime translate is implemented as an OR with a shifted primality bit array, making set coverage vectorizable. The authors report exhaustive coverage from 4 times 10^11 through 10^13, timing evidence, and the largest observed number of nearby-prime trials, which together describe both certification scope and workload behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate p-adic SUSY inverse eigenvalue system
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the Hilbert-Polya wish for a Hermitian spectrum into a concrete inverse problem: choose an antisymmetric prime-harmonic SUSY potential and solve quantization plus turning-point constraints for amplitudes and orbit endpoints from prescribed zeta-zero ordinates. The source also marks the decisive limitation that the phase-integral condition is exact only for shape-invariant potentials, so the recovered amplitudes are merely approximate here.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scale-covariant first-order operator generated by a theta-series potential
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a non-self-adjoint first-order operator with explicit eigenfunctions, a partner operator, and a potential chosen so its exponential is a Jacobi theta series. This is the representation change that makes a spectral-looking state construction analytically connect to zeta through Mellin integration.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin pairing converts state pairs into the completed zeta function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the completed-zeta functional equation, the scale-invariant measure, the theta Mellin representation, and a change of variables to express a two-state pairing as a transformed completed zeta value. The discrete parameter transformation and relation between k and l expose how zeta reflection symmetry is encoded in the operator family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-strip normalization and replacement of the scalar product by a complex map
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives that the proposed norm depends only on the real part, fixes a sign convention on the critical line, then directly confronts the failure of the Hilbert-space scalar-product interpretation. Replacing the integral by a map from two complex labels to a completed-zeta value is a crucial semantic downgrade that prevents orthogonality language from silently carrying positivity or Hermiticity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reference-state reduction of zeta zeros to orthogonality-like relations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After disclaiming a rigorous scalar-product interpretation, specializes the complex map and proves algebraic orthogonality relations for symmetric state labels. It then shows that every pairwise map evaluation can be rewritten against the reference state, yielding an exact equivalence between a zeta zero and vanishing of that reference-state map.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros as destructive interference for reflected state labels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Forms a superposition of labels s and 1-s and observes that cross terms vanish exactly at critical-line zero ordinates, giving a Pythagorean-style additivity of the map-defined norm. This supplies a distinct physical interpretation of the same vanishing relation and explicitly locates the destructive-interference lines.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Permutation audit fails to exclude generic off-critical zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Systematically compares the four reflected zero locations with four reference-state orthogonality arguments. It rejects permutations that smuggle in the RH through s*=1-s, classifies generic and degenerate mappings, and concludes that generic off-critical orthogonal states cannot be discarded. This negative result is the paper's clearest protection against a circular symmetry proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Double-reflection covariance criterion for affine zeta maps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Isolates an exact affine constraint, 2b+a=1, under which the map from state labels to zeta arguments commutes with both conjugation and reflection. It makes explicit that the claimed RH consequence assumes the orthogonal states possess the double-reflection symmetry; the theorem does not establish that assumption.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continuous operator-family deformation turns RH into parameter-independent orthogonality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Parametrizes a family of operators satisfying the reflection constraint, reformulates RH as independence of reference-state orthogonality from the family parameter, and argues that a continuously moving real part is incompatible with a discrete zero set unless the fixed point is one half. This exposes both the intended deformation mechanism and its unproved premise.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractal-string frequency spectrum factors through the Riemann zeta function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates a string's geometric length counting function from the integer harmonics of each length and derives the reusable factorization ZF=ZL times zeta. It also explains why poles of the geometric factor encode complex dimensions and why collisions with zeta zeros affect spectral visibility.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cantor-string poles generate complex dimensions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Works from length multiplicities and scaling ratios to a geometric counting series whose poles have a real part equal to Cantor dimension and periodically spaced imaginary parts. This is the concrete model motivating pole-defined complex dimensions in the proposed Riemann fractal string.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continuum fractal-string duality encodes zeta as a ratio of counting integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces discrete lengths and frequencies by complex-valued continuum maps and measures for a string and its dual, proposes their counting-integral ratio as zeta, and defines a Riemann fractal string by poles of its geometric counting function at zeta zeros. It is the source's explicit attempt to realize the functional equation as duality between representations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From infinitude to asymptotic prime counting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts a contradiction proof and Euler's divergent prime harmonic sum with Gauss's shift to a smooth asymptotic model for an erratic counting function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product turns unique factorization into an analytic object
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how geometric-series expansion plus unique prime factorization identifies a Dirichlet series with a product and converts absence of vanishing factors into a zero-free half-plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic continuation changes the domain of the zeta problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the Euler product's convergence region from the continued function's nearly global domain and records gamma-function singularities as part of that extension.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime powers and Mobius inversion recover prime counts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a weighted prime-power staircase, recovers the prime-counting function by Mobius inversion, and relates the reciprocal Euler product to square-free parity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros collectively reconstruct the prime-power staircase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The exact formula replaces direct prime input by a sum over zeta zeros and explains their collective role in turning a smooth term into discontinuous arithmetic structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional symmetry organizes trivial and nontrivial zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the critical-strip localization and fourfold symmetry pattern from the functional equation and gamma singularities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit prime formulas require a natural ordering of zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Refines the explicit formula, separates trivial-zero terms, and explains that conditional convergence makes the pairing and ordering of nontrivial zeros mathematically consequential.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH controls oscillatory corrections to prime counting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Links the computational utility of explicit formulas, diminishing trivial-zero contributions, and RH's placement of every nontrivial zero on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Under RH, zeta zeros become waves whose derivative localizes primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the explicit formula as oscillatory modes and differentiates the reconstructed staircase to obtain prime-centered delta-like spikes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic zero-free control proves PNT while finite zero checks only test RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts the proof-relevant zero-free line that yields PNT with large finite computations and positive-proportion results that do not establish all-zero criticality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard factorization represents zeta through its zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the complementary global product in which zero locations determine the function, contrasting it with the prime Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The de Bruijn-Newman deformation makes RH a boundary question
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carries the frozen v1 unit linking prime-counting error criteria to a heat-like deformation whose real-zero threshold frames RH as barely true if true.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Equivalent integral and divisor-sum tests expose RH's delicacy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carries the frozen v1 survey of integral equalities and elementary divisor-sum inequalities equivalent to RH, including near-threshold computations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert-Polya reframes RH as spectral reality and Montgomery links gaps to random matrices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carries the frozen v1 unit from the proposed self-adjoint spectral explanation of real zero ordinates to Montgomery's repulsion law and Dyson's random-matrix recognition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unfolding reveals symmetry-class level repulsion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the random-matrix model, explains unfolding away the mean spectral trend, and organizes level statistics by Hamiltonian symmetry classes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Odlyzko gap statistics infer broken time-reversal symmetry and quantum chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses progressively higher zero computations to support GUE behavior and then infers constraints on any candidate spectral system: broken time reversal and chaotic classical dynamics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The xp Hamiltonian matches the leading zero count but fails as the required operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows both the appeal of matching the spectral counting asymptotic and why that match is insufficient: special regularization, wrong subleading behavior in analogues, continuous spectrum, and integrability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random-matrix characteristic polynomials predict zeta moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers a theorem about GUE characteristic polynomials to conjectural asymptotics for all moments of zeta, recovering previously known low moments and predicting higher ones.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A prescribed spectrum does not identify a unique or chaotic classical system
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An inverse-spectrum existence result supplies infinitely many integrable Hamiltonians for broad spectral sequences, warning that spectral matching alone underdetermines the desired mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Connes and Okubo relocate rather than resolve the missing proof obligation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares a construction accounting only for critical-line zeros but leaving a trace-formula obstacle with a boundary-condition construction whose eigenfunctions are not normalizable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial zeros admit a harmonic-oscillator operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs an explicit differential operator whose evenly spaced eigenvalues reproduce the trivial zeros, contrasting an easy regular spectrum with the unresolved nontrivial spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum verification proposals can merely repackage classical RH criteria
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes constructing unitary encodings of assumed critical-line zeros from an allegedly verifying circuit that only quantum-counts primes against an existing bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partition-function zeros motivate a statistical-mechanical RH route
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Frames phase transitions through analytically continued partition-function zeros and notes that functional symmetries and restricted zero loci resemble zeta's structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic energies turn unique factorization into a zeta partition function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assigns prime-labeled energy levels so many-particle composition mirrors prime factorization, making the canonical partition sum equal to zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Duality and a conformal map translate critical-line localization into a circle problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares zeta's functional equation to Ising duality, maps the critical line to the unit circle, and proposes using Lee-Yang or Fisher zero-locus theorems after realizing zeta as a suitable partition function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zeta-valued spin model falls outside the proven circle-theorem class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records a concrete spin-chain realization and the decisive gap: its interactions do not satisfy the hypotheses under which the circle theorem is established.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Mobius random-walk heuristic suggests a bound that is too strong for RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects Mobius signs to a symmetric walk, derives how a square-root Mertens bound would imply RH, reports its disproof, and preserves the weaker epsilon-relaxed condition equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Riemann-Mobius walk locates zeros but tolerates off-line behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a jump distribution directly from Mobius values and shows that general probability laws recover only limited zero localization, not the needed boundary exclusion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Billiard survival asymptotics provide a physically measurable RH condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates escape probability in open billiards to zeta and gives an RH-equivalent limiting law whose violation could in principle refute RH experimentally.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A shaped optical signal physically computes a zeta Fourier transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Describes van der Pol's electro-mechanical realization of an integral representation as a paper-disc signal, optical transduction, and analog Fourier transform locating early zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Electrostatic fields and quasicrystals offer incomplete geometric encodings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Juxtaposes an electrostatic vector field built from zeta's real and imaginary parts with the proposal that zero locations form a one-dimensional quasicrystal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Voronin universality makes local zeta behavior approximate arbitrary nonvanishing analytic functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the approximation theorem and derives a self-similarity interpretation by applying the universality perspective to zeta itself.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reconstructing a potential from zero ordinates yields fractal structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reports a numerically constructed one-dimensional potential whose eigenvalues reproduce known zeros and whose graph is fractal or multifractal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Newton iteration turns zeta's many roots into convergence-basin geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers Newton's method from a finite-root polynomial to zeta and visualizes initial points by iterations required to approach a root.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eventually false inequalities defeat huge ranges of finite confirmation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses sign changes in prime-counting error and the false Mertens bound to show that counterexamples may lie beyond conceivable computation, undercutting extrapolation from extensive checks.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Strip counting versus critical-line counting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Sets up the central semantic distinction N(T) versus N0(T) and the proposed saturation criterion: a line-restricted count matching the strip count would exclude additional off-line zeros in that range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Individual-root equations are not counting formulas

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed-zeta functional symmetry becomes amplitude and phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the functional equation for the completed zeta function into a polar amplitude-phase representation, creating the phase variable from which the indexed conditions are later extracted.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary phase prescription and selected cosine branch
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines arg zeta at a zero by a one-sided horizontal limit, factors the symmetric completed-zeta combination, selects theta=theta-prime with cos(theta)=0, and obtains an integer-indexed transcendental equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unique indexed solutions imply asymptotic counting saturation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how a well-defined monotone left side with one solution per index yields N0(T), then compares it with the strip-wide asymptotic count to claim saturation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact Riemann-Siegel phase equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces the asymptotic gamma phase by the exact Riemann-Siegel theta function and states the exact indexed equation, with the asymptotic formula recovered by Stirling expansion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniqueness of the exact equation is the RH bottleneck
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes the logical bottleneck explicit: monotonicity and a unique solution for every index would turn the exact critical-line count into the full strip count and hence imply RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros as regularized phase-sign discontinuities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reframes a simple zero as a sign jump of normalized completed zeta and uses positive delta to smooth the discontinuity so cos(theta)=0 can be assigned at the zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric multiplicative factors and spurious zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tests whether multiplying zeta by an auxiliary symmetric factor could manufacture off-line zeros and argues that the symmetric combination factors it out, clarifying what the phase construction is intended to detect.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why dependence on arg zeta is not merely circular
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates an indexed equation with an intended unique solution from the undifferentiated equation zeta(z)=0 and notes that the phase term can be computed through independent representations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive delta turns phase jumps into a zero-counting staircase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that the small positive shift regularizes a discontinuous oscillatory phase and that adding it to the smooth count yields unit jumps at line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lambert-W inversion of the mean zero equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Drops the mean-zero fluctuating phase, chooses the real principal Lambert-W branch, and converts an implicit average equation into an explicit index-to-ordinate predictor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High-index scale and shrinking mean spacing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the explicit Lambert-W predictor to arbitrarily high indices and derives the familiar leading scale and shrinking consecutive spacing from W's logarithmic asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lambert predictor versus Gram-point search
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes an index-specific approximate ordinate from Gram points used as search brackets and explains how the proposed solver starts from the former without relying on Gram's law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The fluctuating phase displaces the smooth predictor to a zero

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text contrasts integrable torus quantization with the Green-function/Gutzwiller route for nonintegrable systems, decomposing density into a smooth phase-space term and periodic-orbit fluctuations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arbitrary spectral realizability weakens bare Hilbert-Polya existence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An existence theorem supplies infinitely many integrable Hamiltonians for bounded sequences, including the zero sequence, but is nonconstructive; spectrum matching alone therefore does not identify a natural RH mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum ergodicity separates universal averages from exceptional scars
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Almost-all eigenstate averages may approach the classical microcanonical value while system-specific deviations and scars remain; this qualifies random-matrix universality as a scale-limited description.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Specific heat determines phonon density and a physical zero-free strip

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta poles encode the dimensional threshold for ideal Bose condensation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Integrating the Bose occupation over a D-dimensional continuum produces a zeta value; negativity in one dimension and the pole at one in two dimensions obstruct a finite positive particle count, translating analytic singularities into phase-transition constraints.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral-zeta poles organize Bose fluctuations and partition asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A contour integral makes the leading pole control thermodynamic growth and subsequent poles finite-size corrections; the same calculation becomes a statement about integer partitions and exposes ensemble-dependent fluctuation behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partition combinatorics yields persistent statistical-ensemble inequivalence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Counting partitions by number of summands gives non-Gaussian limits and shows microcanonical, canonical, and grand-canonical predictions for ground-state fluctuations need not agree, even where textbook equivalence is often assumed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime energies turn unique factorization into the Riemann-gas partition function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assigning logarithmic energies to prime-labelled modes makes many-body occupation vectors identical to integer factorizations, so the bosonic partition function is ζ(s), its pole becomes a Hagedorn boundary, and fermionic exclusion selects square-free integers with ζ(s)/ζ(2s).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet and twisted convolutions model parafermion mixing and transmutation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Occupation caps interpolate between fermionic and bosonic gases, while Dirichlet/unitary convolutions encode free or interacting mixing and factor a coupled boson system into decoupled boson/fermion components.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A uniquely occupied Riemann gas keeps zero microcanonical fluctuations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unique factorization permits only one excited configuration at each logarithmic integer energy, giving zero microcanonical state fluctuations while canonical and grand-canonical predictions remain nonzero or divergent, even in the thermodynamic limit; an explicit logarithmic potential addresses realizability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: LeClair's thermodynamic zero-free argument depends on its decisive assumption
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A scattering-kernel formalism makes physical thermodynamic quantities finite in a strip and argues that an off-line zero would violate an assumed interaction effect; the source explicitly identifies that assumption as why the claimed RH conclusion is not a proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Möbius random walk explains why a strong RH-sufficient bound can fail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partial sums of the Möbius function define a walk; the Mertens square-root bound would imply RH but is known to fail at an enormous unknown location, showing both that a sufficient criterion need not be necessary and that vast computation can miss eventual counterexamples.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-factor walks yield an Erdős-Kac Gaussian limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mapping distinct-prime-factor counts to a corrected random walk transfers Brownian/central-limit intuition into a limiting distribution for an arithmetic function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High verified zeros do not exclude a still-higher RH counterexample
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source juxtaposes large-scale verification and statistical evidence with the possibility of an inaccessible off-line zero, explicitly separating computational success from proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Removes a zero-free boundary ratio from the asymmetric amplitude so its argument is exactly twice the critical-line zeta argument, yielding the Volchkov–Veneziano if-and-only-if integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs the entire xi function, its canonical product and logarithmic derivative, then applies functional symmetry to set up a zero-sum invariant.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns functional symmetry into the constant zero sum −B and compares it with a Stieltjes-weighted zero-counting sum; strict equality in the paired convexity bound occurs exactly on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decomposing zero count yields the Volchkov integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the smooth Gamma and average contributions in the zero-counting identity so the remaining oscillatory critical-line phase integral equals the fixed constant exactly when the zero-sum equality holds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Volchkov is the first Li-coefficient integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the zero-counting integration kernel to Li's coefficients and identifies the Volchkov sum and integral as the n=1 case of the Li hierarchy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Chebyshev kernels extend the Volchkov construction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Designs a family Gn whose derivatives match Li's Chebyshev kernels, with a convergence constant that also makes positivity visible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the generalized zero-height sum is equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts an unconditional Li zero sum that sees full zeros with a height-only Chebyshev sum, argues equality forces real part one-half, and verifies the Stieltjes integration boundary term vanishes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Average zero-count contribution from the Chebyshev generating function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the generalized integral into average and oscillatory pieces and uses the Chebyshev generating function to evaluate the first average contribution uniformly in n.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Controls the endpoint term, converts the Gamma contribution through a digamma series, and extracts a closed coefficient formula using a generating function and Pochhammer simplification.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages the preceding construction into RH-equivalent equality and positivity statements for all Li coefficients, explicitly recovering Volchkov at n=1.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the rational kernel is unusually tractable and rewrites it via a Fourier transform, turning the criterion into a weighted moment of the transformed amplitude phase.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectrum sees trivial zeros while phase carries the criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the central representational distinction: the usual string spectrum reflects trivial zeros, whereas the scattering phase supports the RH-equivalent sum rule.
