result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditional-bound landscape and the S(t) extremal analogy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction distinguishes improvement of constants from improvement of asymptotic form and presents the explicit-formula plus optimal-majorant/minorant treatment of S(t) as the methodological benchmark for a zeta-value bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounding zeta becomes bandlimited minorization of a logarithmic kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors explicitly reframe the value-bound problem as minorizing a specific logarithmic function by functions with prescribed Fourier support, link the route to an optimal extremal construction, state the resulting theorem, and contrast it with conjectural and known extreme-value scales.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard factorization converts a zeta value into a statistic of zero displacements
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Taking a ratio of two values of the completed zeta function, using RH to write zeros on the critical line, and then applying the functional equation and Stirling transforms log absolute zeta into a deterministic term minus a sum of a logarithmic kernel over t minus each zero ordinate. This is the bridge that makes a pointwise value accessible to the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The minorant is specified by order, spectral support, and exact approximation loss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 2.1 packages precisely the properties later consumed by the proof: pointwise minorization with real-axis lower control and complex growth, compact Fourier support with bounded transform, and an explicit L1 deficit. It separates the analytic approximation problem from the number-theoretic transfer.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit formula trades the minorized zero sum for a short prime expression
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After replacing the zero kernel by the minorant, the explicit formula moves the problem from zeros to primes. Fourier support truncates the arithmetic side, the L1 deficit controls the archimedean contribution, and the bandwidth is chosen to balance the main loss, the prime sum, and the growth error, yielding the theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A measure representation generates an optimal entire minorant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The cited extremal framework starts from a nonnegative measure satisfying an integrability condition, represents a real function as a mixture of exponential kernels, and supplies an interpolation-series entire minorant of exponential type that minimizes L1 distance. This is a reusable construction principle rather than a source-specific calculation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A tailored measure realizes the scaled logarithmic kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors choose a concrete nonnegative measure, identify its exponential-mixture integral with a scaled and shifted version of the target logarithmic kernel, and thereby obtain the corresponding optimal Carneiro-Vaaler function. This connects the abstract extremal theorem to the zeta kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Interpolation and Poisson summation give the required complex-plane bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A cardinal-interpolation identity obtained via Poisson summation rewrites the extremal function so elementary decay estimates on the target kernel and its derivative yield the exponential-type growth bound needed by the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pairing symmetric interpolation nodes yields sufficient real-axis lower control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Although global nonnegativity of the shifted extremizer is only expected, the proof pairs positive and reflected interpolation terms, uses positivity and oddness of the derivative, and derives the weaker decaying lower bound actually needed. This is a useful example of proving only the structural estimate the downstream argument consumes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The extremal theorem certifies Fourier support and exact L1 loss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Carneiro-Vaaler transform formula makes the shifted extremizer integrable, supported in the desired base frequency interval, and uniformly controlled; subtracting it from the scaled kernel then yields the exact L1 approximation error. These are the two certificates that determine arithmetic truncation and analytic loss.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dilation turns the base extremizer into the bandwidth-Delta minorant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defining the final minorant by dilating the Carneiro-Vaaler function and adding the offset transports pointwise minorization, doubles the exponential-type scale to the requested bandwidth, rescales the Fourier transform, and assembles the three proposition clauses from the preceding estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The remaining obstruction is estimating the prime sum, not constructing the minorant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The discussion compares the new inequality with an earlier proposition, states that good pointwise estimates of the prime sum are difficult and block better zeta bounds, and notes that frequency information about large prime sums can instead support moment estimates. This separates an analytic approximation gain from the surviving arithmetic bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A nonoptimal convolution minorant sacrifices sharpness for a wider kernel class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An integral kernel with compactly supported Fourier transform is assembled into another minorant. The authors identify it with the construction underlying the earlier proposition, explicitly note that it is not optimal, and emphasize that it applies to related shifted logarithmic kernels outside the Carneiro-Vaaler framework. This exposes a sharpness-versus-generality tradeoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The minorant-explicit-formula pipeline extends to general L-functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper specifies a standard Dirichlet-series, Euler-product, completed-function, functional-equation, GRH, and analytic-conductor setting, then states the analogous minorant bound. Trivial estimation gives a stronger conductor-scale constant under Ramanujan-type coefficient control and a weaker one using only absolute Euler-product convergence, showing exactly where coefficient information enters the method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li coefficients encode the Riemann Hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction states that positivity of a derivative-defined sequence is equivalent to RH and rewrites the same coefficients as a symmetrically interpreted sum over nontrivial zeros, establishing the two representations studied in the paper.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separating the general inequality mechanism from zeta-specific arithmetic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors contrast Li's use of zeta-integral positivity with their plan: first a criterion for arbitrary multisets, then an explicit-formula arithmetic expression and comparison with Weil's criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric convergence makes multiset zero sums well defined
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper defines a multiplicity-aware symmetric limiting convention and gives summability hypotheses under which the transformed sums are absolutely or symmetrically convergent; conjugation invariance makes the limiting value real.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-sided transformed sums characterize multiset containment in a half-plane
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem equates half-plane containment with positivity and subexponential one-sided bounds for a sequence of transformed multiset sums. If containment fails, finitely many maximal-modulus offenders dominate and simultaneous Diophantine approximation aligns their phases, forcing exponentially large negative values infinitely often.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation symmetry upgrades the half-plane test to a critical-line test
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For a multiset invariant under conjugation and reflection across the functional-equation center, applying the general theorem to the multiset and its reflection makes the transformed sums real and equates coefficient positivity with every element lying on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Guinand self-reciprocity versus Weil arithmetic in explicit formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes an earlier self-reciprocal-transform viewpoint from Weil's arithmetic emphasis and explains why it restates the explicit formula in Mellin-transform language.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin test functions translate zero sums into prime and archimedean terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Regularity and decay conditions define a test-function class with an involution and Mellin transform; the explicit formula then represents a symmetric sum over zeros by arithmetic prime-power terms and continuous correction terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li's transformed summand has a concrete inverse-Mellin test function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors identify an inverse Mellin transform supported on one side of the multiplicative identity and express it through an explicit polynomial, producing the test function later inserted into the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncating the Li test function exposes an arithmetic coefficient formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the raw inverse-Mellin function violates the decay hypothesis, the proof truncates it, applies the explicit formula to the admissible approximation, and sends the cutoff to zero after evaluating prime and continuous terms, yielding an arithmetic expression for the Li coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-number estimates justify removal of the test-function cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remaining zero-side limit is controlled using the prime number theorem with error term and a classical zero-free region, which make the discarded contributions decay faster than any negative power of the logarithmic cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li positivity is an explicit test-function slice of Weil positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplicative convolution turns into product under Mellin transform; self-convolution therefore gives a transform positive on the critical line. A source-stated identity shows the Li test functions fit this pattern, so their positivity has Weil's meaning while requiring only a simple explicit family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stieltjes-type constants give a second route to the Li coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The arithmetic constants from the explicit-formula expression are compared with Stieltjes constants, related through generating-series expansions, and said to yield coefficient formulas directly after the same conformal change of variable, without invoking the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta large-value and frequency target
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States both the pointwise extreme-value lower bound and the uniform lower bound for the measure of a large-value set, fixing the two outputs the resonance construction must deliver.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian-value heuristic and the unresolved extreme scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects Selberg's approximately Gaussian law for log absolute zeta to a predicted tail measure and much larger extreme scale, while contrasting that heuristic with known conditional upper bounds in different deviation ranges.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resonance as a mixed-moment quotient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a Dirichlet-polynomial resonator, defines its norm and its mixed moment with zeta, bounds the maximum by their ratio, and observes that evaluation turns coefficient choice into optimization of two quadratic forms. This is the paper's transferable conceptual core.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large and small quadratic Dirichlet central values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States matched large- and small-value conclusions in a quadratic-character family and explains that very small nonzero central values remain possible despite positivity and nonvanishing questions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cusp-form central values and the functional-equation parity obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the Hecke eigenform family and its L-functions, identifies the parity class in which the functional equation forces central vanishing, and states large and small central-value results in the non-forced-zero class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Optimization depth versus portability of resonance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the optimized zeta application from deliberately simplified family applications and records that longer resonators could improve constants; it also identifies resonance as portable to character sums, zeta derivatives at zeros, and eigenfunction norms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier diagonalization of smoothed zeta resonance moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the resonator norm and zeta-mixed moment, uses rapid Fourier decay plus the length condition to suppress off-diagonal frequencies, and reduces the analytic problem to an explicit coefficient quotient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sparse multiplicative resonator for the lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the extremal quotient scale and constructs a squarefree-supported multiplicative resonator concentrated on a prime window. Rankin's trick turns the finite cutoff into a negligible Euler-product tail, leaving a product whose linear prime terms generate the large exponential gain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplicative majorant limiting every resonator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a multiplicative weight g and applies a two-term quadratic inequality to dominate every numerator by the coefficient norm times two tractable divisor sums, establishing that arbitrary coefficients cannot beat the stated resonance scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From the optimized quotient to a zeta maximum and moderate-value frequency
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the optimization theorem into the resonant quotient for the maximum, then uses the second and fourth moments of zeta with Cauchy-Schwarz to force a nontrivial measure of moderately large values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High-threshold frequency from a resonator and fourth-moment control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns a mixed moment exceeding twice the thresholded norm into a lower bound for the large-value set via two Cauchy applications, then chooses a shorter prime-supported resonator so its fourth moment diagonalizes and tunes its scale parameter to the desired threshold.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-character resonator and square detection
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines family moments over squarefree discriminants and a character-valued resonator. Expanding its norm shows that character orthogonality is replaced by a square/non-square dichotomy, with perfect-square products supplying the main term and character-sum estimates controlling the rest.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate functional equation and the quadratic-family mixed moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a smoothed approximate functional equation to expose an extra character variable, then applies the same square detector to derive an asymptotic mixed moment whose main term is supported exactly when the product of three indices is an odd square.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One multiplicative profile selects either small or large quadratic central values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States asymptotics for the resonator norm and mixed moment in which using mu times f produces negative linear Euler factors and an exponentially small quotient, while removing mu reverses the effect and gives large values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rankin control of the quadratic resonator norm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extends a truncated squarefree multiplicative sum to an Euler product and uses a small Rankin exponent to prove that the omitted tail and character-sum error remain negligible in the permitted length range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parametrizing the square constraint and extracting the quadratic mixed-moment residue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the two resonator indices into their gcd and coprime parts, parametrizes the square-condition variable accordingly, Mellin-inverts its weighted sum, and moves contour to extract the zeta pole. This converts an opaque square constraint into a multiplicative main term with an explicit logarithmic factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler factorization and tail completion of the quadratic mixed moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extends the constrained coprime sums to all indices, factors the extension prime by prime, simplifies harmless local weights, and applies Rankin's trick to show that the extension tails are exponentially smaller than the main product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Harmonic Petersson weights turn the cusp-form family into a diagonal norm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces harmonic weights, applies Petersson's trace formula, and uses a small-argument Bessel bound plus a resonator-length restriction to make off-diagonal Kloosterman contributions exponentially small, leaving the coefficient square norm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate functional equation for cusp-form central values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the central-value expansion by contour shifting and the functional equation, including the parity factor that annihilates the forced-zero class, and records weight estimates that make the Dirichlet series effectively short.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke multiplication and Petersson averaging yield a gcd kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the approximate functional equation with Hecke relations and Petersson orthogonality to reduce the central-value-weighted resonator average to a finite quadratic form with kernel sigma of the gcd divided by the geometric mean.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mobius twisting switches large to small cusp-form central values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the norm and gcd-kernel quadratic form with the same multiplicative profile used in the zeta optimization; positive coefficients create reinforcing linear Euler factors for large values, while multiplying by mu reverses them to produce small values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH-conditional bounds and the two-route program
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces S and S1, states the improved extremal bound for S1 and the resulting factor-two improvement for S, and situates the use of exponential-type extremals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Representing S1 as an even statistic of zero ordinates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 3 turns an integral of log zeta into a constant term minus a sum of the even kernel f1(t-gamma), creating the interface to one-sided approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transferring an S1 increment bound to a pointwise S bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Captures the averaging mechanism that uses short integrals of S and a tunable h to convert the S1 estimate into a pointwise estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct odd-extremal proof for S(t)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Presents the direct route: one-sided bandlimited approximants for the odd kernel bound the zero sum, whose explicit-formula image separates an L1 main term from a truncated prime-power contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the indirect and direct extremal routes agree
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why a difference bound need not be the pointwise limit, motivates short S1 increments, introduces direct odd approximation, and identifies f as minus the derivative of f1 in parallel with S being the derivative of S1 almost everywhere.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-number sums as the present-method bottleneck
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the proved RH-conditional bound from the conjecturally smaller scale and attributes the limitation to trivial estimation of prime sums generated by the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalize before interchanging the zero sum and integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Completes Lemma 3 by integrating a nonnegative absolutely convergent zero sum and records the reusable trick of dividing xi-values, or subtracting a reference logarithmic derivative, before exchanging limits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Representing S as a rapidly decaying odd statistic of zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 4 subtracts a reference logarithmic derivative to obtain an absolutely convergent zero sum for S with odd kernel f, whose cubic decay permits dominated convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bandlimiting converts zero sums to prime-power sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the core architecture: replace the natural kernel by an exponential-type majorant or minorant, invoke Paley-Wiener compact support, and apply Guinand-Weil to trade zero ordinates for finitely supported prime-power data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Even majorants and minorants for the S1 kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 6 packages exactly the properties needed downstream: pointwise order, exponential type, compact Fourier support and uniform transform control, plus asymmetric exact L1 costs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Propagating one-sided approximation error into Theorem 1
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Translates pointwise extremal order into two inequalities for S1, bounds gamma and prime-power contributions, evaluates the L1 costs, and selects bandwidth so approximation error and exponential prime support yield the stated asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-count monotonicity controls S by neighboring averages
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 7 derives upper and lower comparisons of S(t) with forward and backward averages using only nonnegativity of zero-count increments and the main term of N(t).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Choosing the averaging scale and diagnosing constant loss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the S1 increment estimate with Lemma 7, chooses h at reciprocal log-log scale to balance average error and smoothing penalty, proves both signs, and compares the result with weaker asymmetric S1 inputs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The one-sided Beurling-Selberg design pattern
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines extremal entire approximation, distinguishes one-sided majorants/minorants, and explains why compact Fourier support is decisive for analytic-number-theory applications while no universal construction exists.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Realizing f1 as a positive Gaussian mixture and rescaling its extremals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the even S1 kernel belongs to a positive Gaussian-mixture class, constructs the finite measure, invokes the solved extremal problem, and rescales type-2pi interpolants to bandwidth Delta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Controlling entire growth and pointwise order for the even extremals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses decay bounds for f1 and its derivative inside interpolation series, then pairs symmetric lattice terms and splits sums by scale to prove the growth and real-axis envelope required by Lemma 6.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completing the even extremal certificate
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: spectral support and exact approximation cost
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies Paley-Wiener to obtain compact Fourier support and derives exact upper/lower L1 errors from the subordinating measure, including the nonnegative-integrand justification for exchanging integrals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Building odd extremals from a positive truncated-Gaussian mixture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Embeds the odd S kernel into a finite nonnegative Gaussian-subordination measure, rescales unique odd extremals, and uses reflection symmetry to reduce the two-sided verification to the majorant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parity pairing proves growth and real-axis order for odd extremals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines interpolation-series decay with odd/even parity, pairs positive and negative indices, and bounds the residual odd term to establish the complex growth and pointwise envelope in Lemma 8.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Oddness isolates the exact L1 excess and Paley-Wiener gives support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the majorant into an odd term plus a squared sinc correction, so integration kills the odd part and yields the exact pi/(2 Delta) error; exponential type and integrability then imply compact support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transforming the candidate measure into the odd kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Verifies the Gaussian-mixture identity by Fubini and successive substitutions, reducing the inner integral to an elementary Gaussian integral with the desired exponential kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reducing measure positivity to monotonicity of a scalar remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns nonnegativity of the oscillatory-looking density into a one-variable inequality, then proves it from h(0)=0 and an explicitly nonnegative derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Total mass from monotone convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the established representation and monotone convergence as x approaches zero to compute finite total mass, completing the measure hypotheses.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Characteristic-polynomial moments model zeta moments after matrix-size scaling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source replaces critical-line values by characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices, computes their moment growth, and then transfers the matrix-size exponent and Barnes-G factor to a zeta-moment conjecture with a separate arithmetic factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted moments split into coalesced, critical-scale, and separated regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The multishift moment definition makes relative shifts the semantic variables, and Conjecture 1 predicts a change from fully correlated growth to separated growth when the relative displacement crosses the inverse logarithmic scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A shifted-moment upper bound is reduced to a joint log-zeta tail set
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1.1 encodes pairwise shift interactions through capped inverse separations, then generalizes Soundararajan's tail-distribution method from one log-zeta value to a weighted sum of shifted log-zeta values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The unconditional lower bound reproduces the pairwise separation factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1.2 shows that, for integer weights and controlled shifts, the same capped inverse-separation structure appearing in the conditional upper bound is also forced from below.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A short Dirichlet-polynomial proxy turns a moment lower bound into an energy quotient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The zeta-product is approximated by a short coefficient polynomial A(t); a smoothed correlation S1 and its quadratic energy S2 are combined by Cauchy-Schwarz so the desired moment is bounded below by S1 squared over S2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Matching bounds identify the inverse-logarithmic correlation transition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source compares the two-shift upper and lower orders in the finite and infinite scaled-separation cases, interpreting their change as a transition from correlated to asymptotically independent value distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The shifted unitary integral exhibits the same three separation regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Translation invariance reduces two matrix arguments to their difference, and Proposition 2.1 separates coincident, finite scaled, and widely separated shifts, supplying the random-matrix model for Conjecture 1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coalescing shifts merge two insertions into a higher moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A contour identity is rescaled by the matrix size; when the shift is smaller than the inverse matrix scale, both pole families coalesce and the normalized shifted integral becomes the ordinary moment with doubled multiplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separated pole families are dominated by balanced contour allocations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For separation larger than the inverse matrix scale, each contour is split around two pole families. Power counting shows that only allocations with equal numbers assigned to each family survive at leading order, causing factorization into two ordinary moments times a separation factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite scaled separation is encoded by a continuous determinant limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At nonzero finite matrix-scaled separation, the same rescaling leads to a sine-kernel determinant divided by a Vandermonde factor; continuous extension defines the interpolation constant between the two extreme regimes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A covariance parameter controls Gaussian and large-deviation tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The moment is written as an integral of joint-tail measure, and Theorem 3.1 packages all shift interaction into W, giving Gaussian-like decay through the moderate range and stronger exponential decay for extreme values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The joint log-zeta tail is reduced to two prime ranges
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An RH upper bound for log-zeta and high moments of prime polynomials are applied to every shift. Prime powers are discarded, and the prime sum is split at a scale chosen so an exceptional value must occur in either a short covariance-bearing block or a longer sparse block.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Oscillation caps prime covariance at the inverse shift scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 3.5 bounds the prime cosine covariance by the logarithm of the smaller of the prime cutoff and inverse displacement, explaining directly why nearby shifts correlate and separated shifts stop accumulating covariance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adaptive moment orders convert prime covariance into exceptional-set decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: High-moment estimates bound the long and short prime blocks differently; choosing moment order according to V and W yields the Gaussian core and very-large-value tail needed for the shifted moment bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The short polynomial's mean square already contains the full shift-correlation product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 4.1 identifies the mean square of A(t) with the same pairwise capped inverse-separation factors as the target moment, reducing the analytic lower bound to understanding a multiplicative coefficient norm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted coefficient energy becomes a product of displaced zeta singularities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplicativity turns the coefficient-square Dirichlet series into one central zeta factor and one conjugate pair for every shift difference, with a holomorphic Euler factor. This exposes correlation as the geometry of clustered singularities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shifting separates critical-scale pole clusters from remote residues
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A truncated Perron integral is moved into a zero-free region. The main pole at zero and poles whose shift differences lie within the inverse-logarithmic scale are retained, while residues at more distant displacement poles are isolated as a negligible term to be proved later.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One small contour captures a whole critical-scale singularity cluster
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The residues at zero and all inverse-logarithmically close shift poles are enclosed by one shrinking circle. Laurent expansions show that analytic or lower-pole-order terms integrate away or are lower order, leaving the product of the principal singular parts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient and analyticity bounds suppress every correction to the main clustered residue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The principal cluster integral is expanded into separation coefficients and Taylor coefficients of an analytic remainder. Bounds from combinatorial coefficient growth and radius of convergence show that only the first series contributes at leading order, recovering the pairwise min-factor asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin inversion gives a uniform smoothed Dirichlet approximation to the shifted zeta product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The full product is represented by a smoothed coefficient series; shifting the Mellin contour leaves the value at zero plus clustered pole residues, while gamma decay and a partition of near-coincident shifts make all extra terms uniformly negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier localization kills off-diagonal correlations and preserves coefficient energy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substituting the smoothed approximation into S1 converts it to a double coefficient sum weighted by the Fourier transform of a compactly supported cutoff. Rapid decay makes off-diagonal terms negligible, while the positive diagonal is exactly the coefficient energy from Lemma 4.1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repeated divided differences cancel the Vandermonde singularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Appendix 5.1 proves existence of the critical-scale constant by expressing the sine kernel through an even analytic function and repeatedly subtracting/dividing rows and columns, extracting exactly the squared Vandermonde factors before points coalesce.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Remote residue bounds require a partition by relative shift geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: To prove remote poles negligible, the appendix groups poles near a chosen remote difference and divides every other pair into close, dominant-scale, separated-scale, or near-parallel-difference cases, producing a target exponent inequality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A signed bipartite graph turns residue exponent positivity into component squares
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first exponent inequality is encoded by a bipartite graph on positive and negative weights. Structural properties forbid sign-paired cycles and force a singleton component, so a sum of squared component weights is strictly positive and dominates the required exponent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nested shift scales extend graph positivity to all near-parallel differences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remaining near-parallel shift differences are organized into asymptotic equivalence classes. A nested family of graphs repeats the positivity argument at each scale, and induction across their strict hierarchy proves the final negligible-residue estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Computer refutation through finitely detectable failure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes computer proof from the plausibility of numerical refutation, then uses Polya, Mertens, Lagarias, and Robin-type examples to show how one counterexample or a near-violated equivalent condition can organize a search for failure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Near-boundary criteria motivate a dual-representation falsification test
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates near-boundary equivalent criteria to the broader pattern that elementary quantities also admit zero-explicit representations, then states the experiment's key asymmetry: compute once without zero data and once through a finite high-precision zero sum, with a certified disagreement serving as a possible refutation signal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maslanka continuation coefficients induce the Baez-Duarte decay criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects a globally convergent representation of zeta to the finite-difference coefficients c_k and states the equivalence between RH and c_k=O(k^{-3/4+epsilon}), supplying the semantic bridge from a representation change to an asymptotic criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial-zero trend versus nontrivial-zero oscillation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates c_k into a rapidly decreasing trend from trivial zeros and an oscillatory contribution from nontrivial zeros, showing that the k^{-3/4} behavior relevant to RH is carried by the oscillatory part rather than the k^{-2} trend.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residues and Pochhammer asymptotics turn zero data into a fast oscillatory formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the nontrivial-zero contribution from residues through Pochhammer and gamma functions, pairs conjugate zeros, uses the Pochhammer asymptotic, and under RH exposes exponential gamma decay and first-zero dominance; it also defines the generic and explicit computational routes compared later.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH failure becomes escape of the rescaled sequence from a fixed strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the asymptotic criterion into a geometric diagnostic: if RH holds, k^{3/4}c_k remains bounded, while a violating contribution must eventually force escape; it also fixes the simple-zero setting used for the subsequent mechanism analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An off-critical-line zero changes a k exponent but may surface only astronomically late
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that zeta-derivative size changes constants rather than the decisive exponent, while a zero with real displacement delta contributes k^{-3/4+delta/2}; exponential suppression in its height makes the crossover index enormous and makes a truncated explicit zero sum unable to expose it at feasible k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Catastrophic cancellation makes the generic finite sum a precision-certification problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The generic c_100000 computation sums enormous intermediate terms to a tiny result; rerunning at substantially higher working precision and comparing outputs provides a bounded accuracy claim, while the explicit route must retain exact k+1 terms at thousand-digit scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gamma-tail decay converts a decimal target into a required zero cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses exponential decay of the zero terms to estimate how many zeros are needed for 1000-digit accuracy, separately checks that the zeros themselves satisfy zeta to roughly the target precision, and records an 87-digit mismatch that must still be treated as a numerical failure candidate rather than an RH refutation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative accuracy, not zero accuracy, controls the apparent discrepancy

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta-state normalization inherits Dirichlet convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines finite and infinite photon-number zeta states and shows that normalization of the infinite state is the reciprocal of the real Dirichlet sum, so existence of the state inherits the condition that the real part exceed one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Polynomial zeta weights as a logarithmic reparameterization of thermal weights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts exponential thermal photon statistics with polynomial zeta-state statistics and isolates the substitution of photon number by its logarithm as the structural change.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic evolution and atom-conditioned opposite phases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the logarithmic number Hamiltonian and its two-level conditional extension, mapping real part to initial occupation weights and imaginary part to evolution time while replacing the usual linear number coupling by a logarithm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet zeta as a return amplitude and classical interference law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the normalized zeta function as the overlap between initial and logarithmically evolved zeta states, then shows that the same mechanism is classical interference and interprets Dirichlet convergence as conservation of total intensity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann–Siegel continuation as oppositely phased truncated branches
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the lowest-order Riemann–Siegel formula as two truncated Dirichlet-like sums with opposite logarithmic phases and relates that paired structure to atom-conditioned forward/backward evolution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Entangled branch state plus tuned reference projection produces the Riemann–Siegel amplitude
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs the equal-weight atom-field branch state, evolves it into opposite zeta phases, and chooses a parameter-dependent reference state whose overlap reproduces the two-sum Riemann–Siegel expression up to normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The tuned reference state disentangles on the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that although the evolved branch state is entangled, the reference state becomes a field–atom product specifically at real part one-half because its coefficient reduces to a pure phase.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wigner and Moyal components expose state interference
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Motivates experimentally accessible phase-space reconstruction and expands the zeta-state Wigner function into diagonal photon-number terms plus off-diagonal Moyal interference terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic phase shear breaks and curls the Wigner wedge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains phase-space deformation through a velocity inversely proportional to photon number: low-index components move faster, causing a wedge to shear, curl, and develop interference negativity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wigner overlap retains only the zeta magnitude squared
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps the return probability to an integral of the initial and evolved Wigner functions, making phase-space cancellation compute the normalized absolute square rather than the complex zeta value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wigner matrices retain diagonal branches and off-diagonal coherence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the Wigner matrix of a bipartite state and separates branch Wigner functions from cross-branch Moyal functions, preparing a phase-space account of entanglement and overlap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Opposite branch rotation and stationary off-diagonal interference
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Analyzes the Riemann–Siegel Wigner matrix: diagonal branch functions rotate in opposite directions and shear, while off-diagonal terms remain spatially unrotated and change through complex scaling, localizing a distinct role for coherence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line product structure makes every reference Wigner-matrix entry share one shape
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tracks how the tuned reference state's diagonal and off-diagonal components vary with real part, then shows that at one-half all entries reduce to the same Wigner shape scaled only by constants and conjugate phases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Wigner-matrix overlap kernel turns a zero into signed phase-space cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the Riemann–Siegel return probability through a kernel containing diagonal and off-diagonal products, and interprets small values near a chosen zero as cancellation of positive and negative phase-space regions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moyal integration restores the complex scalar product lost by Wigner overlap
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the complex cross-state Moyal function whose phase-space integral returns a scalar product including phase, resolving the Wigner representation's magnitude-only limitation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet zeta as an integral of a complex zeta-state Moyal function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the Moyal identity to the initial/evolved zeta-state pair so a complex phase-space distribution integrates to the normalized complex zeta value, and contrasts its dynamics with the Wigner function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A sum of branch Moyal functions represents the complex Riemann–Siegel value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recasts the two weighted branch overlaps as a sum of cross-state Moyal functions whose integral yields the complex Riemann–Siegel approximation, and records the exceptional symmetry of its magnitude at real part one-half.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A smoother first correction is implemented by redesigning the reference state
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves beyond the discontinuous lowest-order Riemann–Siegel truncation to a complementary-error-function representation and shows that the first correction can be incorporated by changing the reference state while retaining the evolved branch state.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why a single-system phase-conjugate revival does not remove the two-system requirement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tests the construction against a particle-in-a-box counterexample and argues that its conjugate superposition is already encoded by periodic boundary-induced initial conditions rather than generated from one generic system's evolution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moyal functions turn cross-state operators into scalar products and overlap products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines cross-state Moyal functions, establishes conjugation and normalization identities, and derives the phase-space product identity whose equal-state specialization gives ordinary Wigner normalization and fidelity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Off-diagonal Wigner-matrix entries carry entanglement information erased by partial trace
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Generalizes Moyal integration to bipartite scalar products, shows that tracing out a subsystem retains only diagonal Wigner entries, and identifies off-diagonal entries as the entanglement-bearing contributions that still enter full-state overlaps.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Photon-number expansions separate populations from interference Moyal terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands arbitrary single-system and bipartite states in the photon-number basis and decomposes their Wigner objects into diagonal population terms and off-diagonal interference terms, supplying the reusable calculation behind the paper's phase-space formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Accurate overlap can survive an inaccurate pointwise Hamiltonian approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives a second-order effective Jaynes–Cummings-like generator and explains three reasons its aggregate zeta overlap can be accurate without matching each logarithmic phase: phases need only agree modulo a cycle, high-index errors are downweighted, and summed errors can compensate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Polynomial coupling reduces logarithmic simulation to coefficient optimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Restricts the field coupling to an even polynomial, gives a small illustrative coefficient choice, and shows output-level agreement despite poor exponent matching, while correctly leaving systematic optimization unresolved.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite critical-line verification as a bounded computational claim
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper sharply separates a finite numerical result from the unrestricted hypothesis: the first 10,000 zeros are reported simple and on the critical line, yielding verification only through a stated height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gram intervals, Gram's law, and adjacent compensation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This span defines the interval-based prediction used to organize the search, states why universal validity would imply RH, and immediately shows that individual failures can be locally compensated by double-root neighboring intervals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global zero count plus critical-line sign changes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hutchinson's strategy combines an independent count of all zeros in a rectangle with at least as many critical-line roots detected by sign changes, excluding off-line zeros in the bounded region; the span also identifies the term-count bottleneck of the Euler-Maclaurin implementation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel compression of critical-line evaluation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts the earlier order-of-t workload with an expansion requiring only about the square root of the height in terms, then links that reduction to a substantially larger verified range and an explicit count of Gram-law failures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Machine access as a boundary on numerical evidence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Aborted differential-analyzer and ENIAC plans, followed by Turing's bounded Manchester runs, show that the extent and continuity of verification depended materially on available computing architecture and time rather than only on mathematical formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Iterative generation of Gram points
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first stage of the SWAC pipeline converts the implicit Gram-point condition into an iterative computation over the first 5,000 indices, establishing the sampling grid on which later sign screening operates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Remainder-aware screening and local refinement of exceptional intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The computation does not treat a small approximate value as a sign: it compares magnitude with a remainder estimate, emits distinct uncertainty and proven-failure flags, then subdivides neighboring intervals to resolve exceptional behavior, exposing one case beyond the approximation's certifying power.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Branching from broad screening to a smaller-remainder local computation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: One program extends broad screening while a second switches formulas for minute investigation of selected neighborhoods; the latter resolves two formerly ambiguous intervals in a way consistent with RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local and second-neighbor displacement of missing roots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source classifies almost all Gram-law failures as compensation in an adjacent interval and isolates a smaller class where the missing root is displaced one interval farther, replacing a binary pass/fail view with spatial structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Increasing failure frequency with nearly balanced displacement direction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The cumulative table supports the stated rise in Gram-law failure frequency through the first 10,000 intervals, while the final counts show no large imbalance between rightward and leftward displacement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coupled Gram-law failures and three-root intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The failure events are not purely isolated: the source identifies clusters in which a three-root interval is flanked by empty intervals and gives a longer alternating root-count pattern.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repeated neighboring-failure configurations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The prose reports that configurations like the preceding cluster recur at multiple locations and tabulates how often neighboring intervals fail together, establishing that the pattern is not unique.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From frequency anomalies to low-amplitude extrema and close roots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explicitly changes the diagnostic target from local modulation in oscillation frequency to unusually low maxima, high minima, and nearly coincident roots, then identifies cases where ordinary sampling was insufficient and fine-mesh computation was required.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Escalating precision to certify a nearly merged root pair
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For cases whose extrema could not clear the Riemann-Siegel remainder bound, the computation switches to many terms of the more accurate expansion, evaluates both real and imaginary parts on a local mesh, and reports a very low maximum between two distinct roots.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-logarithm phase cancellation as a delicate RH stress point
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: In explicitly informal concluding comments, the author interprets the lowest observed maximum as a delicate balance among early rising and later descending terms, invokes Kronecker recurrence for repeated occurrences, and proposes targeted searches far up the strip as a possible attack.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Additional 15,000-root computation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof addendum extends the reported experiment and distinguishes increasingly irregular Gram behavior from the still-observed critical-line location of all examined roots.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Equidistribution and Euler products as the two initial value-distribution mechanisms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction separates the classical mean-motion route for trigonometric polynomials from the Euler-product and prime-logarithm independence route for zeta, then identifies generalized almost periodicity as latent structure not used by the older proofs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier density regularity versus Jensen zero-frequency control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source juxtaposes Fourier-transform proofs of smooth value densities with convex Jensen functions whose slopes encode mean motion and strip zero frequencies, motivating a bridge between value distribution and zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Program and target conclusions for zeta and log zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors state the need to extend Jensen theory to generalized almost periodic functions and preview twice differentiable Jensen functions, density-valued second derivatives, mean motions, strip zero frequencies, smoothness, analyticity, and analogous results for zeta itself.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ordinary Jensen functions convert convex slopes into mean motions and zero frequencies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Definitions of one-sided argument variation support the core package: the mean of log|f| is convex, its one-sided derivatives bound mean motions, derivative differences bound zero frequencies, and differentiability yields exact Jensen formulas; uniform function convergence also gives uniform Jensen convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weak convergence and Fourier decay certify smooth value densities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper fixes the distribution-function convergence notion, parameter continuity, integration over parameters, Fourier-transform uniqueness and convergence, inversion, derivative criteria, and exponential-decay criteria for real-analytic or entire densities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vertical means produce unweighted and derivative-weighted value distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Almost periodicity makes Fourier transforms of empirical value measures converge uniformly on bounded frequency sets, yielding asymptotic distributions both for values and for values weighted by |f'|^2, continuously in the vertical-line parameter.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Jensen function is the logarithmic potential of the value distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Truncated logarithms permit passage from empirical value measures to the identity expressing the Jensen function of f-x as the integral of log|u-x| against the asymptotic value distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Area counting turns weighted value density into Jensen curvature
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The area theorem and Fubini identify an integrated derivative-weighted value distribution with normalized zeros of f-x; convex one-sided derivative inequalities then show that a continuous weighted density forces twice differentiability of the Jensen function, with curvature equal to the density up to the stated constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Half-strip Besicovitch-type mean convergence replaces uniform moving-interval means
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: To treat zeta below the ordinary almost-periodic region, the source replaces two-sided uniform interval means by fixed-origin half-line means and defines analytic convergence in mean with arbitrary positive index on reduced half-strips.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generalized limits retain Jensen convexity, mean-motion bounds, zero-frequency bounds, and value distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 1 and 2 assert that uniform convergence in an inner ordinary strip plus mean convergence on a half-strip yields a uniform Jensen limit, convexity, motion and zero-frequency inequalities, convergence of approximating Jensen functions, and convergence of asymptotic value distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nested rectangles turn mean approximation into local analytic control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof localizes half-strip convergence using nested rectangles: mean convergence controls local sup differences, local maxima have mean values and sublinear growth, and ordinary almost periodicity supplies a uniform nonvanishing point in each window.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero, argument-variation, and logarithmic-singularity estimates from one nonvanishing point
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Jensen, Carathéodory, and harmonic estimates bound local zero counts, factorized residual size, argument variation, a well-chosen horizontal derivative, and the error from truncating log|F|, all in terms of local growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncated logarithms and corrected convex approximants prove the generalized Jensen theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uniform control of truncated logarithms first transfers log means from approximants to the limit; local argument bounds make horizontal boundary contributions sublinear, and a small correction makes finite-window Jensen means convex so one-sided derivative limits give motion and zero-frequency bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean convergence transfers asymptotic value distributions through Fourier transforms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Hölder-type bound on exponential characters converts mean convergence of analytic functions into uniform convergence of empirical Fourier transforms on bounded frequency sets, and hence convergence of asymptotic distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cut-aware one-sided argument variation for branches of log f
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source constructs a branch domain by horizontal cuts from zeros and defines left/right variation across cut endpoints and zero endpoints by continuation and limits, preserving the one-sided continuity needed for Jensen arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Branches of logarithms inherit generalized Jensen and value-distribution limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 3 and 4 extend Jensen convexity, motion/zero-frequency bounds, uniform approximation, and asymptotic distributions to branches g=log f under exponential approximants; constancy of the exponential approximants' Jensen functions forces zero frequency of f itself to vanish.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rare cut windows and good logarithmic approximations isolate branch instability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zero-frequency zero for f makes windows intersecting branch cuts density-zero; on most remaining windows uniform approximation of f by zero-free exponentials forces the chosen logarithm branch to match the approximating logarithm, while large-log windows also have vanishing density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Backlund-style variation bounds control log f despite cuts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zero counts for G=log F, real/pure-imaginary crossing counts, horizontal and vertical argument bounds, a good transversal segment, and a bounded log|G| integral provide local control even when branch cuts divide paths.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Good/bad-window truncation proves convergence of logarithmic Jensen means
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof combines truncated-log comparison on good windows with global growth bounds on bad windows, then chooses the large-log threshold, truncation level, and approximation error in sequence to make the Jensen means of g and g_n converge uniformly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Loop corrections restore an argument-principle proof across logarithmic cuts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each cut contributes a loop variation term; adding its integral to the finite-window Jensen function restores one-sided derivative identities, while the aggregate correction vanishes in mean because cut windows have density zero. Cauchy's theorem then yields the logarithmic motion and zero-frequency bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rare branch failures still permit asymptotic distributions of logarithms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On good windows logarithmic branches are uniformly close, and the exceptional windows have vanishing mean density; this controls characteristic functions and transfers asymptotic distributions from almost-periodic logarithmic approximants to the limit branch.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial Euler products satisfy the generalized hypotheses for zeta and log zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler products and chosen branch domain define finite approximants; ordinary almost periodicity, uniform convergence to the right, and mean-square convergence in Re(s)>1/2 allow Theorems 1–4 to reduce zeta and log-zeta means, zeros, and distributions to finite products followed by a limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Independent circular summands yield smooth unweighted and derivative-weighted densities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 5 formulates two coupled distributions on finite tori—values of sums of analytic circular components and the same values weighted by a derivative-like sum—and gives eventual absolute continuity, arbitrary smoothness, convergence, and uniform convergence of densities under square-summability conditions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factorized characteristic functions turn small circular summands into density regularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Independence factors the unweighted Fourier transform and expands the weighted transform into products with one or two marked factors; local oscillatory estimates give enough inverse-power decay, while summability yields Cauchy convergence uniformly on bounded frequency sets.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Limit characteristic functions retain explicit convergent product expansions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite factorizations pass to absolutely convergent infinite products and marked-factor series for the limiting unweighted and weighted distributions, making later decay and analyticity estimates possible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Convolution tails give Gaussian-type spatial majorants for densities and derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splitting head and tail variables expresses finite densities as convolutions; exponential moment bounds for tail sums make translated tail probabilities rapidly small, yielding Gaussian-type majorants uniformly for densities and their derivatives and passing them to the limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Divergent step lengths make the unweighted limiting density positive everywhere
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When the component radii are summable the value support is bounded; when they diverge, polygonal selection of tail phases reaches every target neighborhood, tail concentration transfers positive mass through convolution, and continuity then forces the limiting density F to be positive at every point.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A nondegenerate double representation transfers positivity to the derivative-weighted density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two small circular summands are chosen so the same value has two regular phase preimages with distinct derivative weights; inverse-coordinate maps and a Jacobian lower bound prevent cancellation, reducing positivity of the weighted density G to the already-established positivity of an unweighted tail density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rate of radius decay controls real analyticity versus entire density extension
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Allocating successive small-radius factors in the characteristic-function products produces exponential Fourier decay; geometric-rate radius decay yields local real analyticity, while supergeometric decay permits arbitrarily strong exponential decay and entire extension in the two real coordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform tail control upgrades distribution convergence to joint parameter regularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 9 shows that uniform decay and uniform summable majorants in a parameter give continuous measure dependence, joint continuity of densities and derivatives, uniform convergence in value and parameter, and uniform spatial majorants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diverging variance forces the limiting density and all derivatives to vanish uniformly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When the square-sum diverges at a boundary parameter while remaining convergent inside, the characteristic function tends to zero away from frequency zero under an integrable uniform majorant, so Fourier inversion and dominated convergence give uniform vanishing of the density and its derivatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic Euler factors instantiate the abstract smooth-density theory
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Choosing l(z)=-log(1-z), its derivative-weight companion, prime radii, and log-prime frequencies verifies the abstract hypotheses and yields smooth, positive, analytic, parameter-continuous log-Euler-product densities with uniform decay and boundary vanishing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponentiation transports log-value distributions to zeta-value distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The exponential map sends log-value measures to value measures and transforms densities by summing over all logarithms with the Jacobian factor; Gaussian decay makes these periodized sums and all derivatives converge, giving smoothness, positivity away from zero, analyticity after composition, and boundary-weighted vanishing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-log independence identifies torus distributions with vertical asymptotic distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Linear independence of log primes makes long vertical averages of continuous functions equal Haar averages on the finite torus; hence the torus measures are exactly the asymptotic value and derivative-weighted distributions of partial Euler products, and their densities give second derivatives of finite-product Jensen functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Log-zeta value density is Jensen curvature and determines motions and zero frequencies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 13 identifies the asymptotic distribution of log zeta, expresses the Jensen function of log zeta minus x as a logarithmic potential, proves twice differentiability with curvature 2π times the weighted density, and derives exact mean motions and strip zero frequencies by integrating that density; it also records boundary divergence and the conjugate negative-height version.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta-value density is Jensen curvature and determines motions and zero frequencies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 14 gives the parallel statements for zeta minus x: asymptotic distribution, logarithmic-potential Jensen formula, curvature from the weighted zeta-value density, mean motions, and density-integral zero frequencies; its proof uses the exponential pushforward and relates zeta Jensen functions to all logarithmic preimages.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros of zeta-minus-value and log-zeta-minus-value have unbounded normalized totals over the half-plane
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 15 condenses the boundary growth of Jensen slopes into the conclusion that the normalized number of relevant zeros in Re(s)>1/2 tends to infinity for log zeta minus arbitrary x and zeta minus nonzero x.

source_identity.title: Mean motions and values of the Riemann zeta function

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Convex logarithmic means preserve enough structure under generalized mean approximation that their slopes remain the interface to argument motion and strip-zero density even when ordinary almost periodicity fails.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This is proved only under the source's half-strip analytic continuation, inner-strip uniform convergence, and mean-convergence hypotheses.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Jensen slope as a universal interface from approximation to zero frequency

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The logarithmic potential of the value distribution becomes twice differentiable because area counting identifies its curvature with a derivative-weighted value density, whose integral across real parts equals zero frequency.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Exact constants and applicability require the continuous-density and differentiability conditions stated in the source.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Derivative-weighted value density is the local curvature behind zero counts

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Logarithmic cuts need not destroy Jensen/argument-principle reasoning when cut-intersecting windows have zero mean density and each cut's lost variation is restored by a loop correction whose aggregate vanishes asymptotically.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The mechanism depends on zero-frequency zero for the exponentiated function and the source's controlled cut geometry.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Branch defects can be neutralized by sparse-exception and loop-correction mechanisms

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Partial Euler products first supply ordinary almost-periodic objects whose torus laws are exact by equidistribution, then generalized convergence theorems transfer their Jensen functions and distributions to zeta and log zeta.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The transfer is conditional on the stated mean convergence and branch-domain hypotheses and does not extend automatically beyond Re(s)>1/2.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Finite Euler products form a two-stage transfer scaffold

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Independence factorizes characteristic functions; allocating enough small factors yields polynomial decay and arbitrary smoothness, while quantitative radius decay upgrades this to exponential decay and analytic or entire density extension.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The weighted law requires additional marked-factor summability, and exact decay rates depend on the radius sequence.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Fourier factor allocation yields a hierarchy from smoothness to entire density

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Unweighted positivity comes from phase-polygon reachability plus convolution, whereas derivative-weighted positivity additionally needs two regular representations of one value with separated weights to prevent the weight from degenerating.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The arguments use small analytic circular components and divergence of their effective radii; they are not generic positivity theorems for arbitrary sums.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Full support and weighted positivity require distinct mechanisms

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Zeta-value densities are periodized, Jacobian-adjusted pushforwards of log-zeta densities, allowing regularity and curvature results to transfer while creating a distinguished behavior at value zero and multiple logarithmic preimages.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Boundary statements need the explicit |x|-weights recorded in Theorem 12; unweighted uniform vanishing is false.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Exponentiation preserves the distribution program but changes singular behavior

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: As the log-Euler variance diverges at Re(s)=1/2, pointwise density flattens while the logarithmic-potential/Jensen quantities grow, producing increasing zero frequencies across the full half-plane.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source establishes asymptotic distribution and zero-frequency consequences in Re(s)>1/2, not any assertion about the location of zeta zeros on the critical line.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Boundary variance collapse drives Jensen growth near the critical-line edge
