result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed Eisenstein series, continuation, and two symmetries
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates two series representations to meromorphic continuation, the s↦1−s functional equation, and modular invariance, supplying the structural symmetries used by every later integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier decomposition isolates an exceptional constant term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the Eisenstein series into entire nonconstant coefficients built from divisor sums and K-Bessel functions versus a meromorphic constant term built from two completed-zeta terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Measures turn Eisenstein symmetry into an RH test family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines F_mu as integration over the modular surface, explains inheritance of the functional equation, realizes Fourier coefficients through horocycle measures, and states the nonnegative-measure RH objective.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semistable-lattice integral produces Weng's rank-two zeta function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects Mellin integration over semistable-lattice moduli to an Eisenstein integral, states its continuation and functional equation, and gives the rank-two RH theorem while noting the absence of an Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncation converts geometric integration to a shifted zeta combination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Horizontal integration deletes nonconstant Fourier modes, yielding an explicit two-term expression I(T,s); Theorem 2 gives its sharp T≥1 RH range and the T=1 partition identifies it with Weng's zeta function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the constant Fourier coefficient is the difficult case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that nonconstant coefficients inherit imaginary-axis zeros from two factors, whereas the meromorphic constant coefficient requires a modified RH and Maass-Selberg input.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact exceptional-zero bifurcation for the constant term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 identifies the cutoff y*=4πe^{-γ}, distinguishes the no-exception and two-real-zero regimes, describes monotone escape toward 1, and contrasts this behavior with Epstein zeta functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two proof mechanisms and a polynomially weighted extension
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the Hadamard block-inequality route from the Maass-Selberg route and records a less elegant numerical extension that bounds off-line zeros for polynomially weighted combinations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Distinct routes to line-zero results for Eisenstein-derived functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps Taylor's differencing result, Vinogradov-Takhtajan heuristics, Zagier's representation at zeta zeros, Ki's finite Fourier truncations, and three proof approaches to Theorem 3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-strip hypothesis forces shifted sums to vanish on one line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4 abstracts the core mechanism: an entire genus-zero/one function with real and functional-equation symmetries and a bounded zero strip yields a strict shifted-modulus inequality and line zeros for every phased sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry blocks remove Hadamard convergence factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions zeros into functional-equation/conjugation orbits, proves block convergence from the strip bound, removes exponential factors, and uses the functional equation to force the remaining linear exponential to vanish.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pairing rho with 1−conjugate(rho) creates a half-plane modulus separator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reduces the shifted-function ratio to independent zero-block factors and shows each paired distance ratio lies strictly above or below one according to the side of the critical line, excluding zeros off it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: What survives without real-axis symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies constant modulus on the critical line as sufficient for the local pairing argument, explains why global Hadamard blocks then need extra hypotheses, and indicates the extension to general automorphic L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scaled xi shifts prove the truncation-integral RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses F(s)=xi(2s−1/2) so the known critical-strip containment matches c=1/4, converts I(T,s) to an entire antisymmetric H(T,s), and uses T≥1 to amplify the strict ratio beyond one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An antisymmetric entire transform makes both constant-term summands entire
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the natural entire multiple G is replaced by H with an extra central zero: the alternative representation makes both summands entire and separates the proof into nonreal and real-zero problems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maass-Selberg positivity excludes nonreal off-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At a zero of the constant term, reflection kills the boundary side of the Maass-Selberg relation while the integral side cannot vanish off the relevant symmetry lines, forcing every nonreal zero onto the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity confines real constant-term zeros to (0,1)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses positivity of the Eisenstein series and the horocycle-average identity to exclude real zeros above 1, then reflects the conclusion below 0 by the functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real zeros become a positive scalar level-set equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites H(y,σ)=0 as F(y,σ)=y^{2σ−1}f(σ)=1 and obtains positivity of f from the symmetry-grouped xi product, reducing zero location to one-variable shape analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The central derivative determines the exceptional-zero threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiates the scalar level-set function, shows the central derivative changes sign once, and evaluates the unique transition parameter through xi'(0)/xi(0) as 4πe^{-γ}.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-block derivatives enforce unimodality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiates −f'/f into an elementary term and blockwise xi logarithmic derivatives, then uses the known height of xi zeros to make every derivative contribution positive on (1/2,1).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unimodality yields zero-free and two-exception regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the monotone logarithmic derivative to show F decreases below the threshold and has a single interior return to level one above it, producing exactly one real zero on each side by symmetry and motion toward the poles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simplicity, zero density, and monotone motion for I(T,s)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that all truncation-integral zeros are simple, gives their count as the xi count plus a parameter-dependent linear term, and asserts strictly decreasing positive ordinates as T grows.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line zeros become phase crossings of xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents H(T,1/2+it) as a sine of θ(2t)+t log T, turning zeros into phase congruences, and imports a differenced-xi theorem to establish the T=1 simple-zero base case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phase monotonicity controls simplicity, count, and parameter motion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adds log T to the phase derivative, invokes nonnegative xi phase rotation, derives simple crossings and the asymptotic count, then reads decreasing zero ordinates directly from monotonicity in both variables.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A wrong-way phase contribution obstructs monotone zero motion for a0
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the analogous zero count, identifies the multiple-zero migration to the real axis, and explains why a factor whose argument turns oppositely prevents the I(T,s) monotonicity proof from transferring directly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct verification leaves the Fourier-coefficient RH mechanism unexplained
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates proof of a line-zero property from conceptual explanation, asks why the constant term needs y≥1 and admits exceptional zeros, and proposes truncation as a representation in which the zero-th coefficient regains RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrated Fourier coefficients reduce to an integrated K-Bessel zero problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines twisted hyperbolic integrals J_n and isolates a special-function condition whose imaginary-axis zeros would imply RH for the whole family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Laplacian structure kills only the zero-mode full-surface integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts Zagier's identically vanishing K_0, explained by a Laplacian eigenfunction property, with potentially nontrivial full-surface integrals for other Fourier modes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smooth parameterized zeros are predicted not to exhibit GUE spacing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes a falsifiable zero-statistics prediction from the behavior of related differenced L-functions, explicitly contrasting it with a tempting random-matrix analogy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Averaging Epstein zeta functions sharpens an approximate real-zero cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the nearly identical Bateman-Grosswald threshold for individual Epstein zeta functions to the exact cutoff for their x-average, the Eisenstein constant term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sublattice covolumes form a canonical convex polygon
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines lattice covolume, rankwise minimal slopes, and the convex envelope controlled by the sublattice intersection/sum inequality, creating the representation used to define stability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical polygon vertices induce a unique filtration and stability test
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains increasing-slope canonical vertices, their unique nested sublattices, the Harder-Narasimhan analogy, and the stable/semistable/unstable distinctions with an example.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rank-two semistability becomes the geometric region D_ss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quotients lattice bases by integer changes, rotations, and homotheties, identifies rank-two lattices with the modular upper half-plane, and converts the canonical-polygon test into y≤1 in the fundamental domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weng's lattice zeta specializes to the Eisenstein integral at rank two
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the rank-r zeta as integration of Epstein zeta sums over determinant-one semistable lattices and identifies the rank-two inner sum and domain with the paper's Eisenstein-series construction.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Proof of Theorem 3

source_identity.title: The Riemann hypothesis for certain integrals of Eisenstein series

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Horocycle/truncation integration selects the constant Fourier mode, the resulting two shifted completed-zeta terms admit a symmetry-blocked product comparison, and T≥1 turns that comparison into a strict half-plane modulus barrier.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This mechanism proves RH only for the specified integrated/truncated combinations; it neither proves RH for zeta itself nor conceptually explains every Eisenstein coefficient.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: From Fourier projection to a shifted-xi modulus barrier

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Canonical-polygon semistability selects D_ss in rank two, Weng's lattice Mellin integral becomes an Eisenstein integral over that region, and the fundamental-domain partition converts it to the T=1 truncation integral whose zeros are controlled by Theorem 2.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The rank-two identification does not extend the proved RH result to Weng's higher-rank zeta functions, which have different groups and no asserted Euler product.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Semistability geometry identifies Weng's rank-two zeta with the T=1 theorem

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Maass-Selberg first confines nonreal zeros to the critical line; positivity and symmetry isolate real zeros in (0,1); the scalar level-set representation then turns the central derivative sign at y* and strict log-derivative monotonicity into creation of one symmetric exceptional pair.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The proof is specific to this completed-zeta combination and depends on delicate formula-level inequalities; the Landau-Siegel language is analogy, not identity of arithmetic mechanism.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Exceptional zeros as a one-parameter level-set bifurcation

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Writing critical-line values as a sine of a rotating xi phase unifies zero detection, simplicity, an asymptotic counting correction, and monotone motion under T; the failed transfer to a0 pinpoints an oppositely rotating factor and the real-zero escape.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: For a0 the analogous motion and simplicity statements are partly conjectural/numerical and need additional analytic estimates.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Phase rotation links zero density, simplicity, and motion

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The paper itself separates several successful direct verification technologies from the unresolved question of why Eisenstein Fourier coefficients should display RH behavior, then proposes truncation, integrated Bessel functions, full-surface modes, and zero-motion statistics as tests of possible mechanisms.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These proposals are not established unifications; some are conditional or heuristic and must not be promoted to proved explanations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero counts, Speiser equivalence, and derivative-zero concentration
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the count of zeta-prime zeros left of the critical line to the zeta zero count, records the RH equivalence, and places higher-derivative zeros in a shrinking neighborhood of the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Signed first moment of higher-derivative zero displacement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 packages the aggregate horizontal displacement of zeros of the kth derivative over a height interval into an explicit asymptotic, a stronger semantic statistic than a raw count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Left-right displacement comparison and right-side mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 4 and 5 compare the total leftward displacement of zeta-prime zeros with rightward displacement of zeta zeros and then determine the right-side first moment, exposing a transfer mechanism across the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantitative left tail for zeros of zeta prime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 6 bounds the weighted population of derivative zeros well left of the critical line and states a local comparison with right-side zeta zeros, yielding the qualitative conclusion that almost all complex zeta-prime zeros lie just to the right of the line at a slowly shrinking scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Differentiation inheritance and RH-conditional higher-derivative moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 7 says finiteness of nonreal zeros left of the critical line propagates to every later derivative; its corollary and Theorem 8 turn RH into a higher-derivative location statement and explicit moment formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary sign of the logarithmic derivative controls zero-count equality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs functional-equation zeros, shows the real part of zeta-prime over zeta is negative on an indented half-strip boundary, and converts zero-count comparison into an argument-principle statement; failure of a favorable top boundary itself forces many left-side zeta zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: All negative-half-plane zeros of zeta prime are real and interlace trivially
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 9 combines known existence between consecutive trivial zeros, Rolle's theorem, and a boundary argument variation to prove uniqueness in each interval and exclude other derivative zeros for negative real part.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reflected auxiliary function J for locating off-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces zeros of zeta prime by zeros of an auxiliary function built from zeta, zeta prime, and gamma-factor logarithmic derivatives, so right-half-plane counts can be read from argument variation on the critical line and computed with a differentiated Riemann-Siegel expansion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalize zeta derivatives and encode horizontal zero positions by Littlewood's lemma
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a derivative normalization tending to one in the far-right half-plane, fixes the argument branch, applies Littlewood's lemma on a wide rectangle, and uses the functional equation plus Stirling asymptotics to prepare evaluation of the far-left boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Far-left functional-equation asymptotics yield the higher-derivative zero count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the Littlewood boundary integral by separating Stirling, reflected-zeta, and correction-factor terms; subtracting two rectangle widths removes the horizontal moment and produces the asymptotic total number of nonreal zeros of the kth derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-square control converts horizontal moments into concentration near the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses an approximate formula and mean-square bound on the critical line to control the total absolute displacement of derivative zeros, then combines it with the far-left weighted count to bound zeros on both sides beyond a fixed offset; a short-interval approximate functional equation extends the result to windows longer than square-root height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtract total counts to isolate signed horizontal displacement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 10 is obtained by subtracting the known total zero count from the weighted Littlewood identity, and elementary interval differencing then turns the global formula into Theorem 3's local signed moment.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A reflected auxiliary function compares left derivative zeros with right zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The functional equation makes zeros of zeta prime correspond to zeros of a reflected auxiliary J; Littlewood's lemma expresses the difference of left derivative-zero and right zeta-zero displacement sums as a logarithmic integral, which is bounded using local partial fractions and a fractional-moment estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional moments of positive-residue pole sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves the auxiliary inequality by embedding a finite pole sum in the upper half-plane, using positivity of its real part to control its argument, integrating a fractional power around a rectangle, and taking a boundary limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Right-side derivative displacement from signed moment plus left-tail control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the signed moment to the first derivative and uses Theorem 4's corollary to show the left contribution is lower order, leaving the asymptotic rightward displacement asserted in Theorem 5.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Chains of zero-centered boxes localize the left tail of zeta-prime zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the logarithmic-derivative sign in terms of right-side zeta zeros, surrounds them by boxes, chains overlapping protruding boxes, chooses chain-free endpoints through a density estimate, and applies Littlewood's lemma on chain rectangles to bound derivative zeros reflected far left.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second chain estimate and shrinking-strip majority corollary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces the high-moment estimate on the rectangles' left sides by an L2 bound, obtains the second comparison in Theorem 6, and chooses a slowly growing displacement scale to show that almost all complex zeta-prime zeros lie to the right of the corresponding shrinking line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic-derivative negativity propagates left-side zero finiteness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands a derivative's logarithmic derivative over real and nonreal zeros, observes that only finitely many left-side nonreal terms are bounded while the real-zero sum becomes logarithmically negative, excludes new far-left nonreal zeros of the next derivative, and iterates; under RH this closes the higher-derivative moment formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta second moment as a divisor-problem analogue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source identifies the structural target: refine the classical mean-value asymptotic in the way Voronoi refinement improves the divisor summatory formula, rather than merely sharpen an undifferentiated error term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An approximate formula with two distinct oscillatory groups
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem organizes the mean-value remainder into two finite oscillatory families, one asymptotic to low-index Voronoi terms and another formally associated with the functional-equation product. This is the paper's central representational claim.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classify off-diagonal pairs by their difference
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reindexing the product by m-n turns the mean-value problem into a shifted double series. Poisson summation, continuation by Voronoi summation, integration on the critical line, and saddle analysis then form a composable proof route.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Expose polar pieces before continuing the shifted series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Euler summation separates explicit zeta/polar contributions from a bounded-periodic remainder, showing how an initially convergent off-diagonal series becomes meromorphic in a larger region without conflating poles with the regular part.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation produces a divisor-weighted analytic continuation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poisson summation converts the shift sum into cosine-transform integrals weighted by divisor-power sums, with an explicit uniform decay argument supporting absolute convergence and analytic continuation. Continuity then resolves the exceptional boundary u+v=1 in the zeta-product identity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continue the boundary function by splitting divisor summation into smooth and oscillatory parts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source truncates the divisor-weighted kernel, applies the divisor summation formula D+J to the tail, and decomposes the continuation into four pieces with different analytic roles. This is the decisive bridge from the shifted series to Voronoi-type oscillation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Use derivative decay and contour rearrangement to reach the critical boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Atkinson controls the derivative kernel against the divisor-error bound and rearranges the remaining oscillatory integrals to prove uniform convergence at the critical boundary. The move separates a formal continuation from an actually convergent boundary representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Convert the continued product identity into four mean-value integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Integrating the boundary identity and using Stirling isolates the classical main term and partitions the remaining contribution into I1-I4, assigning subsequent saddle and error analysis to distinct analytic components. The truncation parameter N is explicitly restricted to be comparable with T.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A uniform complex saddle-point estimate with endpoint control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The lemma packages analyticity, local scale, curvature, and amplitude hypotheses into a stationary contribution plus endpoint and uniform error terms. Its proof deforms the contour through the saddle, obtains exponential decay away from it, and uses Gaussian symmetry to discard odd local terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Specialize the saddle lemma to the logarithmic mean-value phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The specialization solves the stationary equation explicitly through variables U and V, separates positive and negative frequency behavior, and derives different remainder regimes for k below or above T. This turns a general contour lemma into the phase calculus used by the theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The first saddle contribution yields the Voronoi-like oscillatory family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the specialized lemma uniformly and letting auxiliary integration limits tend to their endpoints produces the I1 finite oscillatory sum for N comparable with T, while I2 is reduced to a smaller divisor-error contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Range splitting isolates the nonoscillatory contribution of I3
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source splits the kernel at its natural scale and again at y=1, using monotonicity plus the second mean-value theorem on the smallest range, the saddle lemma on the tail, and contour estimates on the remaining terms. The pieces combine to a constant contribution with a controlled error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Insert the Voronoi expansion after evaluating the I4 inner kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A first saddle estimate simplifies the inner kernel, after which the oscillatory divisor-error expansion is inserted and the variable is changed to produce a family of one-dimensional phase integrals J_n. This composes two asymptotic representations rather than attacking I4 directly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A second saddle criterion selects when the dual phase contributes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The second lemma applies the general saddle machinery to J_n, records inequalities under which a stationary point exists, and omits the main term when the sign or index conditions fail. Thus the finite dual sum is selected by geometry of the phase rather than an arbitrary cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transition-range estimates complete the second oscillatory family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After applying the second saddle lemma, Atkinson splits the residual divisor sums around the transition index, uses partial summation and the divisor asymptotic to control near and far ranges, replaces the cutoff by an equivalent explicit one, and recombines I1-I4 to prove the theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-power recursion controls G_k, P_k, and f_k

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generating function F_k isolates universal zeta singularities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages f_k(dx,d) into a Dirichlet generating function, factors its local terms, and separates four zeta-function singular factors from an analytic residual Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The residual Euler product at the origin equals a_k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reduces the local factors at (0,0,0) using divisor identities and identifies their Euler product exactly with the arithmetic moment factor a_k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric truncation separates diagonal and shifted off-diagonal terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the mean square is centered on [-T,T], recovers the desired interval by differencing, and rewrites the off-diagonal using shifts h.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Correlation replacement and cancellation of the T-independent off-diagonal term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lists the controlled approximations replacing coefficients by the conjectural correlation density, transforms the h-sum through f_k, and isolates a large but T-independent term that vanishes under J(2T)-J(T).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncating d and y leaves the leading small-y contribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the proved f_k bound to show the large-d and large-y ranges are lower order, reducing the off-diagonal main term to a bounded integral suited to the generating function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Laurent extraction and scaling produce the M_k profile integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inserts F_k, retains the leading Laurent data, rescales contour variables, and converts N=T^{1+eta} into a dimensionless profile integral M_k with a decay bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residue coefficients gamma_k(n) yield w_k(eta)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the profile integral, evaluates its residue coefficients combinatorially, integrates the scale parameter, and combines diagonal and off-diagonal pieces into Conjecture 4.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Alternative finite local-factor expression for a_k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a_{k}=a_{1-k} and the generalized divisor identity to rewrite the infinite local sum as a finite binomial-square sum, the form used in the stated moment conjectures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sixth- and eighth-moment constants from the w_k profile
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that w_3(eta)+w_3(1-eta)=42 for every split and that w_4(1)=12012, producing the conjectural constants 42 and 24024.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-range split proves the large-k asymptotic for a_k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the Euler product at 2k^2, applies Mertens-type behavior to small primes and elementary product bounds to large primes, and obtains matching upper and lower estimates for log a_k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A bidirectional spectral-dynamical-prime analogy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Frames the zeros as putative wave eigenvalues of an unknown chaotic dynamics and stresses that even without identifying the system, inferred properties transmit useful information between spectral physics and prime-number theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime density as oscillations indexed by complex zero heights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves from the prime staircase through prime powers and the explicit formula to oscillatory density contributions indexed by zeta zeros, exposing how zero location controls frequency and damping.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic reparameterization turns RH into discreteness of a prime spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The substitution u=log x removes slowing oscillations; under RH the prime-derived signal has discrete Fourier support, motivating the Hilbert-Polya question of which self-adjoint system has these frequencies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smooth and fluctuating parts of the zero counting function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates N(t) into a secular mean governed by the functional equation and a zero-mean fluctuation from the argument of zeta, while defining the asymptotically local averaging scale used throughout.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A divergent prime-power orbit-like expansion can resolve zeros when truncated
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Formally inserts the Euler product in the critical strip to express Nfl as prime-power oscillations, identifies periods 2π/log p, and links resolution of individual zeros to a t-dependent prime cutoff despite divergence of the full series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Chaotic periodic orbits determine semiclassical spectral fluctuations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces Hamiltonian wave quantization, isolated unstable periodic orbits, and the trace formula in which actions, periods, stability matrices, repetitions, and Maslov phases generate counting fluctuations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime powers map to repetitions of uniformly unstable, non-time-reversal-symmetric orbits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches actions, periods, stabilities, and asymptotic parameters term by term, inferring prime-labelled primitive orbits of period log p, unit instability exponent, scaling dynamics, and absence of time-reversal symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two discordances constrain any literal trace-formula realization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recasts the analogy in density form and isolates two nontrivial mismatches: exponential stability is approximate for generic long orbits but exact arithmetically, and the required negative sign conflicts with repetition behavior of Maslov phases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Heisenberg time sets the orbit length needed to resolve individual levels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines Weyl cell counting, orbit-induced energy wavelengths, and mean spacing to show that level resolution requires orbits through the Heisenberg time, corresponding on the Riemann side to primes up to t/2π.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orbit proliferation cancels amplitude decay to produce a universal sum rule
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how exponential proliferation and squared-amplitude decay balance in the Hannay-Ozorio rule, relates it to ergodicity, Perron-Frobenius invariance and a dynamical-zeta pole, and transfers the resulting microscopic universality expectation to the zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Within-spectrum GUE universality is nonuniform and breaks at the shortest-orbit scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Clarifies how statistics arise from local spectral averaging without an ensemble, identifies GUE for chaotic systems lacking time reversal, and predicts loss of universality at separations controlled by the shortest orbit, log 2 for the zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair correlation, form factor, and number variance are interchangeable bilinear views
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines local unfolding and three linked spectral statistics, with Fourier duality between pair correlation and form factor and an integral relation to number variance, establishing the observables used to separate universal and nonuniversal structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The diagonal approximation yields GUE only before the Heisenberg time
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitution of the trace formula creates a double orbit sum; diagonal terms plus the universal sum rule give K=|τ| and match GUE for |τ|<1, while discreteness forces coherent off-diagonal cancellation for longer times.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair correlations supply the missing off-diagonal coherence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows why uncorrelated prime-orbit phases would kill off-diagonal terms and how the arithmetic deviation of the prime-pair factor from randomness yields the cancellation required by the GUE form factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short orbits restore system-specific statistics beyond the universal window
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splices direct short-orbit contributions into the universal form factor, producing a nonuniform correction that accurately tracks the transition from random-matrix behavior to long-range Riemann-zero statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High-zero correlations contain low zeros as nonuniversal resonances
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the diagonal correction using the zeta function near 1, separating primitive and repeated contributions and revealing low Riemann zeros as resonances in pair correlations and number variance high in the spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Perron-Frobenius resonances are the dynamical analogue of low-zero resurgence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers the zeta correction to generic chaotic dynamics: the invariant dynamical-zeta pole cancels the local singularity, while other singularities, equivalently subdominant Perron-Frobenius eigenvalues, cause nonuniversal resonances.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unsmoothed prime-pair arithmetic produces the small off-diagonal oscillation correction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that using the full Hardy-Littlewood factor rather than its average adds a convergent Euler-product correction that recovers tiny observed oscillations, while emphasizing why the same derivation cannot simply be copied to unknown generic orbit correlations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A truncated trace formula defines an approximate spectrum whose correlations can be computed
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses orbits shorter than the Heisenberg time to reconstruct approximate eigenvalues and treats their contributions as effectively uncorrelated, yielding generic diagonal and off-diagonal corrections and a heuristic route back to Hardy-Littlewood-type orbit correlations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GUE universality and nonuniversal zeta structure extend to n-point correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extends the two-point picture to determinant-form n-point GUE limits, separating proved diagonal results, conjecture-dependent off-diagonal calculations, and zeta-near-one corrections for higher correlations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stationary truncation and tail resurgence repair the formal critical-line series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the real Hardy Z-function, diagnoses nonconvergence and hidden reality in the naive Dirichlet series, then truncates at the stationary term so the resummed tail becomes the conjugate of the early terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel correction terms smooth truncation discontinuities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why abrupt stationary truncation breaks analyticity and constructs an inverse-a asymptotic series whose coefficient functions derive from derivatives of a base function and a Bernoulli-driven recurrence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factorial late terms determine an exponentially small optimal error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compresses high-order coefficients into a decorated factorial asymptotic, identifies divergence after a least term, and uses Borel-supported optimal truncation to obtain an exp(-πt) error scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum spectral determinants turn primitive orbits into pseudo-orbit Dirichlet terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a real spectral determinant, expands the trace formula into composite pseudo-orbits analogous to integers built from primes, and derives a stationary cutoff at half the Heisenberg time.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Long pseudo-orbits resurge from short ones, but proliferation limits computation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs groups around the half-Heisenberg cutoff so the long tail is approximately the conjugate of the short pseudo-orbit sum, producing a real finite Riemann-Siegel lookalike while exposing exponential term proliferation and remaining discontinuities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Error-function smoothing gives a transferable completion of abrupt resummation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces the hard cutoff by a complementary-error-function window, improves the attainable zeta accuracy, and transfers the analytic-continuation construction to quantum spectral determinants with reported near-degenerate-level resolution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The exponentially small Riemann-Siegel remainder suggests imaginary-period orbits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets exp(-πt) as a semiclassical phase with imaginary action, inferring complex periodic orbits with periods that are multiples of iπ in addition to the real prime-log periods.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trace and statistical analogies impose a detailed Riemann-dynamics checklist
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects required properties: Hamiltonian or symplectic origin, bounded chaos, broken time reversal, homogeneous instability, prime-log periodic orbits, anomalous phases, complex orbits, exact leading semiclassics, quasi-one-dimensional growth, and a functional-equation/hermiticity parallel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical XP matches instability and mean counting only after an ad hoc cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The flow of XP is uniformly hyperbolic and non-time-reversible, and Planck-cell area under a truncated energy hyperbola reproduces the smoothed zero count including its constant term, but the unbounded phase space prevents a discrete spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric quantization of XP places its power-law eigenfunctions on the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The formally Hermitian dilation generator has monomial eigenfunctions X^{-1/2+iE}, echoing n^{-s} and p^{-s}; symmetrization supplies the one-half real part, and canonical rotation links the model to the inverted oscillator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier duality recovers the theta phase but leaves compactification unresolved
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: With even continuation across X=0, the Fourier-transformed momentum eigenfunction is the time reverse of the position eigenfunction and carries the zeta functional-equation phase, while the required self-adjoint discrete boundary condition remains equivalent to closing phase space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sign identification and dilation symmetry offer hints but not a boundary condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifying X with -X halves the complex XP period to the desired iπ, while continuous dilation symmetry makes time evolution logarithmic; restricting to integer dilations can insert zeta into a superposition but neither forces its vanishing nor forms a group.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modular dilation characters suggest L-functions as self-adjoint extensions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces non-group integer dilations by multiplicative residue-class groups and interprets their characters as discrete extension phases, potentially assigning different Dirichlet L-functions to different self-adjoint extensions of XP.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical position-momentum exchange yields an almost-correct zero condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposes closing XP motion by reinjecting asymptotic position flow through momentum, derives an XP-preserving exchange and a functional-equation identity, then exposes a decisive sign mismatch that prevents it from generating the zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: XP satisfies many inferred constraints but misses boundedness, primes, and phase structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Performs a concise property-by-property audit: XP has the right instability, symmetry breaking, scaling-related features and several analytic parallels, yet remains unbounded and offers no clear primitive-prime mechanism or explanation of the anomalous Maslov phases.

section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds the formal dictionary between the Riemann counting formula and chaotic trace formula, including scaling, stability, symmetry, phase, smooth density, and Heisenberg-time consequences.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Long Orbits and Universality

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-versus-two-hole escape as a probe of internal dynamics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The abstract proposes a directly comparable experimental observable whose exact circle-billiard formulas are sums over zeta zeros, establishing the paper's bridge from escape dynamics to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Escape-law contrast and the short-time masking confound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts power-law survival in an integrable billiard with exponential survival in a strongly chaotic one and warns that a transient exponential contribution can mask the integrable asymptotic in simulations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Circle map, orbit dichotomy, invariant measure, and hole observable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The unit-radius circle map preserves the collision angle, rational angle choices give equally spaced periodic collisions, irrational choices are uniformly distributed around the boundary, and holes convert these dynamics into a survival-time observable under an invariant boundary measure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramanujan compression of the periodic-orbit escape sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After defining the positive-part square function, the source rewrites trigonometric orbit contributions as exponentials and applies the Ramanujan identity, replacing a sum over coprime phases by Möbius and totient weights in the long-time coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Near-periodic trajectories control long-time survival
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source argues that exact non-escape is confined to certain short periodic orbits and that very long finite survival comes from slow precession near them; it parameterizes the angular deviation, describes the surviving boundary intervals, and integrates their invariant measure to obtain the leading 1/t contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin inversion converts small-hole behavior into a residue problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite, piecewise-smooth long-time coefficient is Mellin transformed in hole width, the orbit sum is interchanged with the integral in a convergence half-plane, and inverse Mellin integration makes the small-hole expansion a sum of residues.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rational hole separation becomes residue-class harmonic analysis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For rational theta, the orbit-period sum splits by congruence classes modulo q; dividing by the class gcd produces coprime reduced data, and Dirichlet-character orthogonality acts as the projector selecting a residue class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler products turn the congruence sum into Dirichlet L-function ratios
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inserting character orthogonality permits a sum over all integers; prime factorization then separates the totient and Möbius contributions into Euler factors, yielding a character sum involving L(s,chi) over L(s+1,chi). The trivial character recovers zeta with factors at primes dividing the modulus removed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact rational two-hole escape as residues of an L-function integrand
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first main result expresses the long-time two-hole survival coefficient as residues of a Mellin integrand assembled from congruence data and Dirichlet L-functions, and justifies shifting the contour left by controlling large negative real and imaginary parts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as a small-hole escape asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states that RH is equivalent to two families of nested limits: one compares one-hole survival with its leading 2/epsilon term, and the other compares one-hole survival with twice the symmetric two-hole survival, with errors tested against every positive delta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rational GRH corrections versus the irrational-angle analytic barrier
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For rational two-hole separation, the source relates correction size to generalized RH for the participating L-functions; for irrational separation it says the residue-class analysis breaks down and proposes that dense critical-line poles obstruct analytic continuation, while retaining a theta-independent leading term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-field averaging for irrational hole separation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uniform distribution of the fractional parts for irrational theta permits averaging the hole-overlap weight, while mean values for the totient and Möbius functions replace the remaining arithmetic factors; the resulting integral gives the leading tP(t) approximately equal to 1/epsilon.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residue hierarchy separates hole geometry from zeta-zero corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source identifies the leading inverse-hole-width residue with total hole size, explains the vanishing candidate constant term, records special logarithmic and simple integer-pole terms, and places the next-order contributions at nontrivial zeros of zeta, yielding its RH condition on their real parts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complex poles are required for the survival function's step structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The numerical discussion observes that retaining only real poles would produce an analytic integer-power series, whereas complex poles are essential to reconstruct the nonanalytic step structure of the exact finite orbit sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scaled survival collapse tests the irrational leading asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Figure 3 varies the hole width with fixed irrational separation and reports that epsilon times tP(t) approaches a limiting curve in the scaled time epsilon t, converging to one at large scaled time as predicted by equation (18).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole truncation separates smooth convergence from visible steps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Figure 4 varies the number of critical-line poles in the residue computation and reports convergence of the second derivative, with more real poles needed in one inverse-width regime and more critical poles needed in another for the steps to become visible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residue extraction plus Riemann-Lebesgue decay proves baseline convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin inversion expresses m_y(f) on a vertical line; moving the contour crosses the pole at s=1, whose residue is the limiting functional, while the remaining vertical integral decays by Riemann-Lebesgue.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH is equivalent to a universal smooth-test contour shift
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH the zeta bounds permit shifting the Mellin inversion line and yield the advertised error rate. Conversely, a universal rate analytically continues every M_f into the corresponding half-plane; choosing f whose entire Mellin factor does not vanish at a candidate zero prevents cancellation and forces the zeta quotient to be holomorphic there.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The rightmost zeta zero sets the attainable convergence exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Writing beta for the supremum of real parts of zeta zeros, the source derives a convergence rate from vertical-line integrability and reverses the implication: a rate with exponent a rules out zeros in Re(s)>2(1-a).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-step jumps obstruct overfast convergence for interval tests
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof rewrites interval-test error through the summatory totient function and shows that an assumed overfast remainder would force a bounded expression; evaluating its discrete recurrence at integers whose successor is prime instead makes it unbounded.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A non-Paley-Wiener test has poles only at zeta-zero locations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the designated function F, its Mellin transform has no other poles in Re(s)>0 than those contributed by zeros of zeta(2s). Although the transform lacks rapid Paley-Wiener decay, it decays sufficiently to shift inversion to a line determined by the rightmost zeta zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residual Fourier decay makes the special probe rule out beta below one
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming the supremum beta of zero real parts is below one, the paper bounds the shifted-line integrand and its derivative, obtains a contour representation, and identifies the remainder with a Fourier transform in log y. Integration by parts and Riemann-Lebesgue force that remainder to decay, contradicting the probe's hypothesized large normalized error.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It maps ground-state divergence to a critical fugacity, turns the critical density into zeta(d/2), and interprets the pole at one as the disappearance of finite-temperature condensation in two dimensions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fermionic exclusion extends the thermal integral through the critical strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The alternating fermionic polylogarithm relation remains convergent at unit fugacity for 0<Re(nu)<1, providing the statistical mechanism the later RH model requires.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Leading Fermi energy is interaction-independent while free energy is not
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It distinguishes a representation-defined Fermi surface observable from pressure/free-energy sensitivity, sharpening why the later heuristic selects pressure as its interaction witness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two-dimensional bosonic thermodynamics becomes an algebraic Rogers-dilogarithm system
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It exhibits a representation change from an integral saddle equation to an algebraic fugacity equation, then connects pressure to Rogers dilogarithm identities and rational special points.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fermionic statistics remove the bosonic real-axis branch obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It compares solution existence and dilogarithm branch structure under attractive interactions, making exclusion statistics an analytic stability mechanism rather than a label.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coupled algebraic thermodynamics for multiple particle species
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It generalizes a single-species saddle to a matrix of scattering couplings and shows how mixed statistics combine into a total pressure coefficient, including a boson-fermion example.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A complex-power fermionic kernel turns zeta zeros into vanishing leading pressure corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It derives the central candidate mechanism and explicitly separates three required premises: leading-order adequacy, Hamiltonian realizability, and the claim that nonzero interactions modify pressure over temperatures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A log-quasi-periodic real-space potential realizes the kernel only inside an open convergence strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It maps the hypothesized kernel back to a second-quantized potential and shows that convergence requires 1/2<Re(nu)<3/2, with the critical line itself needing additional regularization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The proposed RH argument lacks control of its formalism and leading-order approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conclusion explicitly identifies the gap between a physical conditional argument and a rigorous proof: the filling-fraction framework needs a firm foundation and the selected contributions need justified dominance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-temperature/finite-size channel exchange yields the completed-zeta functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It reframes the zeta functional equation as consistency between a thermal free energy and a Casimir ground-state energy after exchanging compact Euclidean directions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative-zero exclusion as an RH criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source makes derivative zeros a structural diagnostic: RH is equivalent to excluding zeros of zeta prime left of the critical line, while a quantitative refinement localizes a positive proportion near that line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Horizontal zeta-prime distance versus radial characteristic-polynomial distance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This is the paper's central representation change: local zeta statistics at height T are modeled by CUE characteristic polynomials with N approximately log(T/2pi), turning horizontal derivative-zero location into radial derivative-root location.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Near-critical derivative zeros as an inherent Levinson-method loss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage explains operationally why the horizontal distribution matters: derivative zeros in a thin strip are an unavoidable loss term, and lower bounds there could improve critical-line zero estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Close zeta-zero gaps create nearby derivative zeros, but density forces missing matches
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The example records both sides of the local correspondence: close zeta zeros accompany a derivative zero near the critical line, yet unequal global densities prevent a one-per-gap matching and force missing derivative zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Soundararajan's limiting frequency functions for zeta-prime proximity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The liminf/limsup functions compress horizontal derivative-zero distribution into a family of testable proximity frequencies, together with continuity, positivity, and mass-at-infinity conjectures and a small-gap conditional result.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local root collision controls a derivative root near the unit circle
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gauss-Lucas, continuity, and locality combine into a reusable mechanism: a close pair of unit-circle roots creates a nearby derivative root whose leading displacement depends on the gap and the background configuration.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Heavy radial tail reproduces the Levinson-Montgomery scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The 1/s-squared radial tail has no finite mean but has a logarithmically growing truncation, which places a positive proportion of derivative roots within log N/N of the circle and matches the zeta scale after density normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Translation-invariant CUE spacing and its small-gap expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source normalizes eigenangles to unit mean spacing, derives index independence from translation invariance, and supplies the small-s nearest-neighbor expansion that later drives the derivative-root density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Perturb a double root and expand the scaled derivative-root displacement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A degenerate root anchors an analytically moving derivative root; centering the close pair and expanding its scaled displacement yields the stated small-s density through the s-to-the-three-halves term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small radial derivative distance is not exclusively a close-gap phenomenon
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explicitly blocks a tempting converse by citing separated-root families that still produce near-circle derivative roots, then explains why close pairs nevertheless determine the leading square-root density and records the unresolved normalization problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bimodality persists across correlated and independent root ensembles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Numerics support the asymptotic tail yet expose an unexplained second bump that appears for CUE, COE, independent uniform roots, and zeta-prime data, suggesting a mechanism more general than one ensemble's correlations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic derivative separates a close pair from its background
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring the polynomial into the close pair and the remaining roots turns the derivative-root equation into a sum of two singular pair terms plus the background logarithmic derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-spacing and radial-displacement rescaling for a nontrivial CUE limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rotation invariance reduces the distribution to radial position, and the paired rescalings identify the variables that remain meaningful as matrix size grows.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Even analytic root branch and coefficient expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The implicit-function argument, convergence domain, logarithmic-derivative Taylor coefficients, and close-pair expansion combine to show that the scaled displacement is an even analytic function of gap size with explicit first two coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Push nearest-neighbor spacing through the root map with controlled dependence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source converts the complex root displacement to radial distance, pushes the spacing density through the local inverse map, and isolates why the second coefficient may be averaged despite finite-gap dependence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A double eigenvalue induces fourth-power characteristic-polynomial reweighting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because exact repeated eigenvalues form a measure-zero event, the source defines collision conditioning by a shrinking-neighborhood limit and shows that expectations of the remaining roots equal Haar expectations reweighted by the fourth power of the characteristic polynomial.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ratio averages reduce random root coefficients to computable expectations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A generating ratio of characteristic polynomials converts the needed collision-conditioned coefficient moments into derivatives of a known Haar average; computer algebra then supplies the expected second coefficient and closes Theorem 3.1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta logarithmic derivative reproduces the CUE close-gap expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separating two close zeta zeros in the partial-fraction expansion, rescaling by local zero density, and expanding yields the same implicit equation and leading coefficients as the unitary characteristic-polynomial calculation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Observed zeta-prime radial analogue matches the CUE distribution shape
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Approximately one hundred thousand derivative zeros in a stated height interval give an empirical distribution with the same striking overall shape as derivative roots of unitary characteristic polynomials.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-level density for a unitary ensemble with endpoint multiplicities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The lemma gives the limiting rescaled one-level density for a circular ensemble weighted by fixed powers at plus and minus one, identifies its Bessel form, and notes the local density near plus one is independent of the opposite-end multiplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaudin-Mehta and Szego reduce the conditioned density to local OPUC asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The weighted eigenvalue process becomes determinantal through the orthogonal-polynomial projection kernel, so its one-level measure is the kernel diagonal and its microscopic limit reduces to orthogonal-polynomial asymptotics near the conditioned point.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Jacobi asymptotics produce the microscopic Bessel kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explicit OPUC-to-Jacobi formulas plus microscopic rescaling and Jacobi-to-Bessel asymptotics yield the limiting kernel, its diagonal one-level density, and access to higher correlations and spacings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A close pair has a unique analytic derivative root in its diameter disk
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix states a uniform theorem that turns the informal close-pair picture into a unique local derivative root with analytic dependence throughout a truncated configuration domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Argument principle turns root uniqueness into stability of a winding number
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof deforms the close-pair disk around possible boundary multiplicities, decomposes the logarithmic derivative into a dominant pair term and a background term, and reduces uniqueness to preserving index one under perturbation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Half-plane localization controls the background logarithmic derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The model image curve has index one, while boundary-arc localization, a sharp real-part maximization, and elementary trigonometric remainder bounds keep the perturbed image in the required half-planes uniformly for gaps below one over pi.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eliminate inaccessible constants, then enforce sign control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The prose identifies the reusable move from a Hadamard-factorization identity, through elimination of hard constants and differentiated combinations, to explicit formulas whose sign constraints expose both the power and limitations of discriminant bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unconditional discriminant bounds as a positive-kernel extremal problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The explicit formula becomes a lower-bound instrument by choosing a test function whose prime and zero contributions are nonnegative, converting analytic estimation into constrained Fourier-kernel optimization with a sharp main term and an unresolved remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GRH weakens the positivity domain but not the main-term ceiling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under GRH, positivity is required only through a nonnegative Fourier transform on the critical line, enlarging the admissible kernel class; nevertheless the best main term is unchanged and optimization moves to the remainder term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poles obstruct transferring conductor bounds without Artin holomorphy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The explicit-formula method transfers from discriminants to Artin conductors only if uncontrolled pole contributions are excluded, cleanly isolating the analytic assumption that blocks an otherwise parallel argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prescribed local completions unify discriminant and curve-genus minimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Serre's local-to-global viewpoint reframes root-discriminant minimization as a problem conditioned by local completions and shows the same template turning into minimal-genus questions for curves over finite fields.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Root-discriminant invariance turns lower bounds into class-number certificates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Passing to the Hilbert class field preserves root discriminant while multiplying degree, so a degree-sensitive lower bound can rule out a nontrivial extension and certify class number one; weaker versions bound the class number before algebraic refinement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infinite class-field towers defeat divergence of minimal root discriminants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The old conjecture that minimal root discriminants grow with degree would force all Hilbert class field towers to terminate; Golod-Shafarevich towers and Martinet sequences provide the structural obstruction and replace that expectation with bounded-root-discriminant families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small-discriminant data challenge degree monotonicity and expose prime-degree ignorance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Near-contact between analytic lower bounds and known minima supplies a calibration signal, while the degree-seven anomaly challenges monotonicity and the tower constructions' small-prime-power degrees isolate prime degree as a distinct unresolved regime.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Field discriminants do not generally reduce to polynomial discriminants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Analytic field-discriminant methods do not address bounded polynomial discriminants, and equality of polynomial and field discriminants requires a power basis, a representation property expected to fail in higher degree.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elkies recovers a GRH-scale bound by Taylor positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiated Landau-Stark identities have alternating signs under GRH; high-order Taylor truncation suppresses an unwanted pole term while preserving positivity uniformly in zero height, yielding the discriminant bound without invoking the full explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tailor kernels to known, absent, or targeted small prime ideals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rapidly decaying general-purpose kernels can underuse known prime data; an alternative explicit-formula kernel admits termwise estimates, improves when an ideal norm is excluded, and can be redesigned to emphasize selected ideals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ideal-class norm bounds retain more structure than discriminant bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Geometry-of-numbers product estimates imply a small-norm representative in every ideal class and hence a discriminant bound, but the implication loses ideal-class information that remains useful for other problems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ideal-class zeta functions improve Minkowski constants but resist GRH import
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zimmert's analytic use of ideal-class zeta functions strengthens small-ideal representatives and recovers an unconditional discriminant bound, yet the lack of Euler products and failure of GRH for these functions blocks a naive conditional upgrade.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic regulator bounds extend the zeta-function strategy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zimmert's ideal-class analytic machinery also yields regulator lower bounds, with Friedman variants improving small-degree behavior and later reformulation suggesting a path to stronger general estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discriminant-bound deficiency splits into small-prime and low-zero contributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the explicit formula is an identity, excess discriminant over a baseline bound must be supplied by prime ideals or zeros; decay localizes the relevant terms, and zeros can be inferred by subtracting computable prime-ideal contributions when direct zero computation is unavailable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Use the same kernel to compare prime and zero shares, then test kernel sensitivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey fixes the discriminant-bound kernel, defines deficiency and prime-ideal columns, obtains the zero share by subtraction, and warns that the apparent balance shifts materially under the unconditional optimal kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Low-zero pressure and why GRH bounds might survive some off-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text contrasts the lack of an algebraic small-prime guarantee with asymptotic low-zero results, then reframes the GRH gap as positivity of a kernel on different regions and sketches mixtures that tolerate broad classes of off-line zeros while exposing unusual zero distributions as the remaining obstruction.
