result_and_mechanism_map.title: Invert xp before quantizing it
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates the failure point of the formal Berry–Keating proposal and makes the central representation move: quantize 1/(xp) on a lattice, where the inverse momentum has a tractable Green kernel, rather than impose an unestablished direct quantization of xp.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cyclic RG suggests a Russian-doll bridge, but exponent and energy roles must be repaired
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares scale-related RD bound states and Dirichlet-like wavefunctions with Berry–Keating dilation eigenfunctions, identifies two mismatches, and proposes the inverse Hamiltonian as the mechanism that resolves them rather than treating surface resemblance as an equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: BK→I→RD as a regularization, RG, and threshold-state pipeline
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the roles of the three models: BK supplies the dilation target, I supplies a finite-dimensional regularization with a running boundary coupling, and RD supplies cyclic RG and threshold states corresponding to I eigenstates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Berry–Keating phase-space truncation recovers only the smooth counting asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how a Planck-cell phase-space cutoff produces the leading smooth Riemann counting formula, explicitly separates smooth and oscillatory terms, and records that this is heuristic rather than a spectrum obtained from a consistent quantized xp operator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Connes cutoff reverses emission into missing states
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts a large phase-space cutoff with Berry–Keating's Planck cell: the divergent continuum count contains the Riemann smooth term with the opposite sign, motivating zeros as absences in a continuum rather than emitted eigenlines; it also ties the formal xp eigenfunctions to scale generation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace x by a velocity profile v(x) without losing adapted plane-wave structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Generalizes xp to v(x)p and gives both its cutoff count and formal eigenfunction in the integrated coordinate ∫dx/v(x), anticipating the later coordinate that turns the inverse-model spectrum into free motion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite lattice Green kernel regularizes the inverse Berry–Keating operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the one-dimensional Green function for p⁻¹ to define a finite Hermitian matrix with weights f_n and an additional coupling g_I, then defines the regularized BK Hamiltonian by matrix inversion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite matrices violate the canonical commutator yet recover it spectrally in the continuum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes the finite-dimensional obstruction explicit through the trace of [X,P], then uses convergence of most commutator eigenvalues to justify continuum recovery; it also clarifies that the RG coupling is classically invisible but quantum-mechanically fixes boundary conditions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An inverse-model eigenstate is a zero-energy RD threshold state
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After defining the RD Hamiltonian, a nonunitary wavefunction rescaling converts each I eigenproblem into an RD problem at zero energy, with the BK energy determining the time-reversal-breaking RD coupling and the velocity levels becoming RD energies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Differentiating the inverse integral equation recovers generalized BK eigenfunctions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the continuum integral equation into a first-order differential equation whose solution, after undoing the RD rescaling, exactly matches the formal generalized Berry–Keating eigenfunction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary quantization becomes a twisted free particle in an adapted coordinate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Boundary ratios yield the energy quantization condition; for uniform levels the spectrum becomes continuous as the cutoff grows, while q=log n—and more generally q=∫dn/ε(n)—turns the states into plane waves in a box with coupling-controlled twist.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gauss elimination closes exactly only after retaining the boundary coupling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Eliminating the highest component reproduces the same Hamiltonian family: h_I and level weights remain invariant while g_I flows. Reparameterizing by the associated RD threshold state exposes the exact state-conditioned RG rule.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The spectral coordinate and RG scale are complementary, yielding energy-dependent cycles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The continuum flow is a tangent trajectory; the scaling coordinate s equals total adapted length minus q, and the I-model RG period is 2πℏ/E, unlike the energy-independent period of a fixed RD model.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One RG cycle lowers the state label, separating gapless I scaling from gapped RD scaling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splitting the quantization integral at one cycle proves an energy/state relabeling identity. Its state-dependent contraction gives algebraic, gapless inverse-model levels, whereas the fixed RD cycle produces exponentially scaled bound states.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The quantum number counts completed RG cycles to leading order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the finite number of cycles to system-size contraction and shows that the state label approximately equals the number of cycles needed to reach one site, while flagging finite-size corrections as potentially important.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discrete recursion produces a product quantization condition and a complete spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Subtracting neighboring RD threshold equations yields an exact recursion; one boundary condition closes it into a product equation whose phase is monotone and spans exactly N integer labels, establishing completeness of the finite regularized BK spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact momentum spectrum diagnoses which term survives the continuum limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A constant-level special case gives the exact finite momentum spectrum, and expansion of the general phase count shows that only the harmonic-like sum ∑1/ε_n diverges for uniform levels, explaining why the first continuum term controls large N.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The smooth Riemann term is a finite spectral deficit, but its linear term is cutoff-scheme dependent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Taking the continuum limit of the exact phase count reproduces Connes's finite smooth term up to a regulator-dependent linear contribution; incompatible naive cutoff identifications prevent a conclusive equivalence and motivate a blueshift interpretation of missing states in a fixed energy window.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform levels turn the finite count into the Gamma phase of the smooth Riemann formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Renormalizing the exact finite product gives a Gamma-function phase. Choosing the zero-point shift a=−3/4 aligns its Gamma term with the smooth Riemann count, while the remaining linear and constant pieces expose boundary and regulator choices.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta regularization converts the missing linear term into a scale choice
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Regularizing the infinite product assigns the disputed linear contribution to the regulator μ; choosing μ=1/π restores the Riemann linear term while leaving a separate half-unit boundary mismatch.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A half-cycle offset improves smooth zero locations but leaves random fluctuations unexplained
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite numerical check compares the smooth count at known zeros and finds a half-unit offset consistent with completed RG cycles; the remaining deviations track the oscillatory zeta contribution, so the uniform model is explicitly limited to the smooth component.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Level perturbations and prime deletion cannot synthesize zero-scale randomness from smooth phase steps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records two negative routes—algebraic corrections to levels and deleting prime-indexed levels—and explains their common obstruction: sums of smoothly varying arctangent contributions resist producing the irregular interpolant required by the zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Only two level-dependent coupling patterns preserve the simple antisymmetric interaction under RG
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Promotes the scalar g coupling to a structured matrix and identifies max-index and min-index patterns I+ and I− as the two choices that keep the h interaction invariant. Their elimination directions are opposite, and the exact I↔RD threshold-state map survives levelwise.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The I+ continuum equation becomes scattering from the derivative of the running coupling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introducing an integrated wavefunction converts the nonlocal threshold equation into a second-order ODE; an adapted coordinate and gauge transformation expose an effective Schrödinger Hamiltonian with potential V+=(1/2)dg_D/dq and explicit boundary conditions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: I− supplies the opposite derivative potential and a constrained route to oscillatory scattering data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The companion construction gives V−=−(1/2)dg_D/dq with reversed boundary placement. The source then proposes, without claiming success, that scattering from these potentials or discrete couplings might carry the oscillatory count and perhaps connect RG-time asymmetry to GUE behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Statewise solvability does not automatically extend to many-body integrability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Limits the exact correspondence: multiple rapidities obstruct a direct many-body I→RD map, and level-dependent boundary couplings suggest a more complicated transfer-matrix structure rather than an established integrable theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as closure and totality of periodic sequences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This is the source's most discrete criterion: a constant vector lies in the closed span of simple fractional-part sequences exactly when those sequences are total, and both conditions are equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Harmonic approximation meaning and robustness to equivalent weights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text interprets totality as approximation of arbitrary mildly growing sequences by simple periodic ones and shows that the criterion is invariant under any quadratically comparable weight through an invertible identity map.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free RH formulation inside a Hardy space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It reframes RH as analyticity of reciprocal zeta on the right half of the critical strip and places the later closure argument in a functional Hilbert space whose norm is controlled by critical-line boundary values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parameterized zeta functions encode the Hardy-space closure criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The family F_lambda and discrete subfamily G_l package a zeta factor with a pole-cancelling coefficient, yielding equivalent continuous-parameter and discrete closed-span formulations of RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform Mobius Dirichlet bounds under RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof requires more than pointwise reciprocal-zeta convergence: a quantitative Littlewood lemma supplies uniform control of finite Mobius sums on shifted half-planes, enabling later dominated convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two-stage construction of an approximate inverse
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mobius-weighted finite combinations first converge in Hardy norm to shifted reciprocal-zeta approximants H_epsilon, after which the shift tends to zero toward E; this exposes the constructive core of the closure implication.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero geometry yields the domination needed for norm convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH, pairing zeros in the Hadamard product gives monotonic control of the completed zeta function under a real shift; gamma asymptotics then yield an integrable bound for H_epsilon and complete the constructive implication.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero in Omega forces the entire generating family into a proper kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reverse implication is a concise functional-analytic obstruction: any off-line zeta zero annihilates every F_lambda, so their closed span lies in a proper evaluation kernel and cannot contain the nonvanishing target E.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The discrete generating family can be thinned to square-free indices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because Mobius coefficients vanish off square-free integers, the same construction proves the closure criterion using a strictly thinner family, separating the essential support of the approximants from the full indexing set.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional-part functions give the original L2 closure and totality criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem realizes RH as approximation of the constant function and, equivalently, totality of a parameterized family of fractional-part functions in L2((0,1]).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An isometric Mellin transform transports the L2 problem to Hardy space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The transform supplies the structural bridge between interval functions and analytic functions, with indicator functions furnishing a total family that establishes isometry on the whole source space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional-part generators map to the analytic zeta family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The calculation identifies the Mellin image of each f_lambda with minus F_lambda, making the two closure problems genuinely equivalent rather than merely analogous.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semigroup invariance promotes one-vector containment to totality

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime logarithms as periodic-orbit data for the zero spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text maps the oscillatory density of zeta zeros to a Gutzwiller-like orbit sum whose actions are logarithms of prime powers, making a precise structural analogy between arithmetic and spectral representations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Correlated zeros interfere to locate nearly uncorrelated prime powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reverse direction is conceptually nontrivial: an infinite oscillatory series indexed by highly correlated zeros reconstructs the locally irregular prime-power sequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the inverse oscillatory formula need not be a dynamical trace formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It distinguishes formal oscillatory resemblance from dynamical origin and explains what a separate trace formula for primes would and would not imply.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncation turns exact spikes into lines with unknown shape and resolution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It identifies the central finite-information problem: conditional convergence to delta spikes does not guarantee that a truncated sum has correct widths, shapes, or relative intensities, motivating both numerical and analytic controls.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product to the oscillatory prime-power density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler product is logarithmically expanded, inverse-Laplace transformed into a weighted prime-power count, differentiated, and rewritten under RH as a smooth density plus cosine terms indexed by zeros; the text identifies interference of those terms as the source of prime-power spikes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted prime-power counts versus prime-only counts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The step function assigns reciprocal-power weights and Möbius inversion recovers the prime-counting function, clarifying why the density of all prime powers retains more direct information than a prime-only density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditional convergence selects increasing-zero order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite computation is not permutation invariant: summing zeros in increasing imaginary part is the required natural order, while other selection rules can drive incorrect finite values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian convolution makes line heights comparable while exposing a resolution limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Convolving the truncated density with an unnormalized Gaussian replaces sufficiently narrow peaks by nearly uniform Gaussian responses whose heights encode pre-convolution areas, avoiding oscillatory-tail integration errors and yielding an explicit width-versus-spacing resolution criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Convolved line heights recover reciprocal prime-power multiplicities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The checked caption states that prime powers p^n appear at height 1/n after convolution, directly validating the relative-intensity semantics rather than mere peak location.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian smoothing converts the conditional explicit formula into a damped sum rule
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source reframes convergence control as reproduction of a coarse-grained density, convolves each oscillatory term, locally freezes the slow amplitude and linearizes phase, and obtains an exponential damping factor in zero height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential damping translates a zero cutoff into a controlled x range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Absolute convergence of the smoothed rule permits a threshold epsilon that relates alpha_max, sigma, and x_max; omitted terms are largest near the boundary and exponentially smaller below it, making resolution and truncation error tunable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The phase of zeta links zero locations and prime density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The phase jumps at zeros, its derivative contributes the oscillatory zero density, and a contour integral of log zeta yields the prime-power density, locating the bridge in a shared representation rather than in statistical similarity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resolution at large x requires increasingly high zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Logarithmic phase makes fixed terms oscillate more slowly and decay as x grows, so constructive interference at larger prime powers requires higher-frequency zeros; conditional convergence prevents replacing the natural initial segment by high zeros alone, leading to impractical scaling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moving zeros off the critical line separates peak location from intensity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source changes the real parts of zeros while retaining imaginary parts and reports that prime-power peak locations persist but relative intensities fail, distinguishing frequency/phase control from amplitude control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Missing repetitions and orbit-dependent amplitudes block a dynamical trace-formula reading
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposed orbit identification fails because there are no repetition indices, the implied trajectories are not periodic, amplitudes lack zero-index dependence, and a single Hamiltonian is unlikely to reproduce both oscillatory and smooth energy dependence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small-x behavior refines the inflection-point upper bound

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The article begins from the equivalence between RH and approximation of the indicator of [1,+infinity) by fractional-part functions, then announces the sharper target of approximating E1 by e_q={qt}-{t} inside an explicitly manageable subspace. result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coordinate convergence plus square-summable domination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates the decisive proof architecture: compute basis coordinates, show each tends to the target coordinate, and seek a subsequence with a uniform square-summable envelope so dominated convergence yields norm convergence. The three later criteria differ mainly in where this envelope is still needed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sine-difference orthonormal family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defining E_n as consecutive differences of sine waves turns the integral kernel min(p,q) into Kronecker orthogonality. The construction is reusable because a covariance-like min kernel is diagonalized by discrete differences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry characterization and Fourier model of H_P
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The closed span of the E_n is exactly the weighted-L2 functions that are one-periodic and antisymmetric under x maps to 1-x. A weighted rescaling maps this space isometrically to a subspace of L2(0,1) where the E_n become the standard odd-frequency cosine basis, making completeness and coefficient reasoning transparent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dilation orbit of E1 is dense in the ambient Hilbert space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A compactly supported function is encoded into a periodic antisymmetric g_T, expanded in H_P, and then rescaled back to approximate the original function with an explicit vanishing error. This constructively proves density of the dilation span of E1 and contrasts it with a nonconstructive Mellin-Wiener criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as density of e_q in H_P with a coefficient-sum repair
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 transports the standard Nyman-Beurling condition through an isometry to approximation of E1 by {qt} in H, then proves that the common {t} component can be removed. Reflection of the residual controls the sum of coefficients, so adding that small multiple of {t} converts the approximants into finite combinations of e_q without losing convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact E_p-coordinate of a fractional-part difference
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 2 converts each generator e_q into the explicit coefficient log q minus a short reciprocal sum indexed by p/q <= k < p. This is the computational bridge from functional approximation to arithmetic coordinate estimates used in every subsequent scheme.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generator Gram matrix via Vassiounine sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The pairwise inner product of e_p and e_q is expressed through logarithmic terms and Vassiounine cotangent sums, providing an alternative route for norm computations and exposing arithmetic structure beyond individual basis coordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Common domination framework and Möbius-sum inputs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper makes the remaining task explicit: coordinatewise convergence must be supplemented by a uniform square-summable majorant, with only a bounded index window left after far-tail estimates. Rapid logarithmic decay of partial Möbius sums and convergence of their logarithmic weighting to -1 supply the common analytic inputs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Triangular approximation with an exact residual tail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The coefficients lambda_{q,n} retain Möbius weights through n-1 and choose two boundary corrections by a two-equation system. The resulting error with E1 has coordinates -1 at p=1, zero for 2<=p<=n before adding E1, and hence vanishes through the first n coordinates, while all residual coefficients p>=n+1 receive an explicit harmonic-sum formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Remote-tail bound for the triangular residual
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Euler-Maclaurin control and the Möbius-sum estimates give x_{n,p}=O(n^2/(p log n)), hence a square-summable p-dependent bound once p is at least n^4. This confines the unresolved domination problem to the finite moving interval immediately above the matched coordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Triangular square-summable-window criterion for RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Criterion 1 states that a uniform square-summable envelope only on p in [n+1,n^4] for infinitely many n closes the triangular approximation argument and implies RH. It precisely identifies the scheme's remaining burden after exact low-coordinate cancellation and automatic far-tail control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Natural Möbius approximation: coordinate limits and tail control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dropping the two boundary corrections gives the natural coefficients mu(q)/q. Divisor cancellation plus Möbius-sum asymptotics yields coordinatewise convergence to -E1, while a direct generator-coordinate estimate gives y_{n,p}=O(n/p) and automatic domination beyond n^2 log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Natural-approximation domination criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Criterion 2 reduces RH for the natural approximants to a square-summable uniform coordinate envelope on p up to n^2 log n for infinitely many n. Compared with the triangular scheme the unresolved range is shorter at the top but includes all low coordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact low-coordinate energy exposes restrictive Möbius conditions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An exact formula for the sum of y_{n,p}^2 over 2<=p<=n+1 converts success of Criterion 2 into simultaneous smallness conditions on two Möbius partial-sum combinations. The source argues these are quite restrictive and contrasts them with known square-root-scale oscillation, diagnosing why coordinatewise convergence alone is inadequate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponent-smoothed Möbius approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing mu(q)/q by mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), with epsilon_n tending to zero no faster than the stated logarithmic threshold, preserves coordinatewise convergence to -E1 and the O(n/p) far-tail estimate. The proof rewrites divisor sums by Euler products and controls zeta-tail errors directly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothed domination criterion and conditional calibration
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Criterion 3 gives the smoothed analogue of Criterion 2: a square-summable envelope through n^2 log n along infinitely many n implies RH. The source reports that under RH prior work verifies the criterion for a particular logarithmic smoothing scale and even bounds the approximation distance, making this scheme a conditional calibration rather than an unconditional proof.

section_argument_map.label: Front matter and abstract
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Identifies the Nyman-Beurling density problem, the symmetry-adapted orthonormal family, and the three approximation programs.

section_argument_map.label: 1. Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the closure formulations equivalent to RH and previews the coordinatewise-plus-domination strategy.

section_argument_map.label: 2. Orthonormality
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Constructs the sine-difference family, proves orthonormality, characterizes its closed span by periodicity and reflection antisymmetry, and identifies it with an odd-cosine Fourier subspace.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Density results and the Riemann hypothesis
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves dilation completeness and transfers the Nyman-Beurling criterion to density of the generators e_q in the symmetry subspace.

section_argument_map.label: 4. Computational lemmas
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Computes generator coordinates and pairwise scalar products, then isolates the Möbius-sum inputs used by all later approximations.

section_argument_map.label: 5. The triangular approximation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Solves a finite triangular coordinate-matching problem, gives its exact residual tail, proves a remote-tail estimate, and states the remaining square-summable domination criterion.

section_argument_map.label: 6. The natural approximation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Studies the uncorrected Möbius-weighted approximant, derives coordinate limits and tail control, and quantifies a low-coordinate mass obstruction.

section_argument_map.label: 7. Smooth approximations and acknowledgements
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces exponent smoothing, proves its coordinate limits and tail estimate under a decay window, and states the corresponding RH criterion and conditional comparison.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The source turns a weighted functional closure statement into an explicit l2 coefficient problem by selecting the symmetry class naturally containing the fractional-part differences, diagonalizing that class with a Fourier-equivalent basis, and computing each generator's arithmetic coordinates.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The closure-to-RH link uses cited Nyman-Beurling and Baez-Duarte results, and the transformation does not itself supply the missing uniform coordinate envelope.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Triangular correction, raw Möbius weighting, and exponent smoothing all solve fixed-coordinate convergence and admit automatic remote-tail control; they differ in exact low-coordinate cancellation and in the moving interval on which a common square-summable majorant remains necessary.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: All three RH conclusions are conditional on an unproved domination hypothesis for infinitely many n; coordinatewise limits and big-O tails alone do not give Hilbert-norm convergence.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Three approximation schemes isolate moving domination windows

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The natural scheme's exact low-coordinate energy forces simultaneous cancellation in Möbius partial sums, revealing a concrete obstruction that the smoothed weights are designed to soften while preserving the same target coordinates.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source does not prove that smoothing removes the unconditional obstruction; its strongest positive efficiency statement assumes RH and cites prior work.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The article pairs two representation mechanisms: symmetry reduction identifies an explicit Fourier basis for H_P, while periodic folding and dilation reconstruct arbitrary compactly supported functions in H; a Mellin-Wiener criterion supplies a parallel transform explanation of dilation completeness.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Only the periodic-folding proof supplies an explicit approximation rate in the source, and neither completeness result by itself resolves the RH-specific restricted-generator closure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From Atkinson's diagonal split to automorphic spectral decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the reusable strategic replacement: a diagonal/off-diagonal split that Poisson summation handles for a double sum becomes a determinant split of matrix-indexed quadruple sums, with the SL(2,Z) spectral decomposition replacing Poisson summation. It also previews the full proof pipeline and its analytic-continuation bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maass spectrum, Hecke coefficients, and multiplicative L-function factorization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects the non-holomorphic spectral objects later used to turn Kloosterman sums into separated variables: Laplace eigenvalues, parity, Hecke eigenvalues, Fourier normalization, spectral weights, Hecke L-functions, coefficient bounds, the divisor-twist factorization, functional equation, and polynomial growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Holomorphic cusp-form counterpart of the Maass spectral data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the holomorphic branch parallel to the Maass branch: Petersson bases, Hecke eigenvalues and L-series, divisor-twist factorization, analytic continuation, growth, Fourier weights, and the aggregate weight bound later needed for absolute convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit fourth-moment formula as a three-part spectral expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that the Gaussian-smoothed fourth moment decomposes into an explicit main term, a continuous spectral integral, a Maass discrete sum, and a holomorphic cusp-form sum, and explains why every spectral expression converges absolutely and why the Gaussian weight is operationally preferred.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-square analogy, Voronoi transformation, and the missing spectral analogue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares the fourth-moment spectral formula with an explicit mean-square formula, explains how Voronoi summation recovers Atkinson's result, identifies the absence of a comparable transform for spectral sums as a genuine obstruction, and motivates asymptotic evaluation as an alternate route.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Asymptotic spectral wave formula and its conceptual interpretation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the simplified asymptotic regime, interprets fourth-moment values as coupled to the full non-Euclidean Laplace spectrum, and distinguishes the method from a prior smoothing/reflection route that does not preserve full explicitness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Four-variable meromorphic family encoding the smoothed moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a four-complex-variable zeta integral, recovers the target moment at a special point after explicit residue terms, expands it into a quadruple Dirichlet sum, and splits it into diagonal and two off-diagonal pieces. This is the central deformation that makes later continuation possible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Additive-character and Mellin separation of the shifted divisor correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rejects an insufficiently explicit appeal to general Eisenstein convolution theory, expands a divisor sum through Ramanujan additive characters, then Mellin-inverts the smooth weight to separate the remaining variables. It also records meromorphy and rapid vertical decay of the Mellin transform and the functional equation of the additive-twist Dirichlet series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shift converts additive twists into Kloosterman-sum kernels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines an overlapping domain where the Mellin contour may be shifted, extracts pole residues, applies the additive-twist functional equation, and reorganizes the remainder into positive- and negative-sign Kloosterman sums. Lemma 1 packages the result and shows only trivial Kloosterman bounds are needed at this stage.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twisted diagonal decomposition as a completion of van der Corput's method
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records an alternate derivation: twist the diagonal/off-diagonal split by coprime parameters, average with weights while exploiting invariance of the left side, and obtain Kloosterman sums for smooth inputs. The source presents this as a general route to exponential-sum bounds using SL(2,Z) theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Corrected opposite-sign Kuznetsov trace formula via K-Bessel inversion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the trace formula for opposite-sign Kloosterman sums, flags corrections to earlier statements, and sketches its proof by changing the Poincare-series inner product and using Kontorovich-Lebedev inversion. This is the mechanism that produces Maass and continuous spectra for the negative-sign kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rapid-decay transform and spectral expansion of the negative-sign kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the corrected trace formula to the constructed kernel, computes its Bessel transform, proves rapid decay uniformly on compact parameter sets by contour deformation and Stirling estimates, and uses Hecke factorization to obtain Lemma 3's separated continuous and Maass contributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kloosterman-sum zeta function exposes Maass, holomorphic, continuous, and diagonal terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the Kloosterman-sum zeta function and its four-part Kuznetsov expansion, proves convergence in an enlarged half-plane, and invokes Petersson's identity to identify the holomorphic spectral weights and derive their aggregate bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive-sign kernel expansion and cancellation of the diagonal auxiliary term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin-inverts the positive-sign Kloosterman kernel against the zeta-function spectral decomposition, obtains Maass, continuous, holomorphic, and diagonal pieces, proves rapid decay permitting reordering, and shows an auxiliary diagonal series telescopes/cancels before reassembly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lemma 5 assembles the full positive-sign spectral expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the positive-sign kernel calculation with Hecke identities to give continuous, Maass, and holomorphic separated-variable contributions and defines generalized Mellin-Barnes kernels suitable for continuation beyond the initial domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduce all kernel continuation to one Mellin-Barnes function

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hypergeometric residue extraction gives global meromorphy and rapid decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Converts the Mellin-Barnes kernel into a hypergeometric integral, expands it into finitely many explicit residues plus a controlled remainder, and lets the number of extracted poles grow to continue the kernel over all five variables. Lemma 6 adds rapid decay, which then propagates to the discrete spectral series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shifting across arithmetic poles completes global continuation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the two continuous-spectrum integrals, rewrites them using the master kernel, shifts the spectral contour, accounts separately for parameter poles and poles indexed by zeta zeros, and uses an arbitrarily wide bounded-parameter box to prove global meromorphy of the off-diagonal family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Specialize the continued family and isolate regular spectral contributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the global decomposition at the fourth-moment point, proves that discrete spectral kernels may be evaluated there without modification, cancels odd Maass parity through the functional equation, moves the continuous contour back to the imaginary axis, and separates polar main terms from a regular integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regular main term recovered from cancellation of eleven meromorphic pieces
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes polar contributions, rewrites the main term as eleven explicit meromorphic summands, and extracts its finite value by perturbing along a generic direction so individual Laurent singularities avoid collision while their aggregate singular parts cancel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Split a singular kernel into its residue and a regular contour remainder

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hypergeometric representation closes the explicit-formula proof

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Suppress the holomorphic range and establish uniform real-spectral kernel bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Begins asymptotic analysis by deriving rapid decay for integral spectral parameters, sharpens the Mellin-transform bound with exponential dependence on the imaginary coordinate, and shifts contours to obtain uniform decay when the real spectral parameter exceeds the T scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complex path deformation localizes the moderate spectral range

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-twist family targets: nonvanishing and average analytic rank
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects arithmetic questions about twisted elliptic curves to central vanishing of their L-functions and states the two family-level outcomes whose proof mechanisms organize the paper.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large-sieve loss controls the strength of both conclusions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes an explicit sensitivity claim: replacing the D-epsilon loss in the family estimates by logarithmic loss would simultaneously sharpen nonvanishing density and average rank.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moment and zero-density reductions for the two average results
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carried v1 unit linking a second moment plus a first moment to nonvanishing and linking average zero density to a general average-rank theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet-series and functional-equation data for the twist family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects exactly the coefficient control, analytic continuation, and reflection symmetry that enable smoothing, large-sieve estimation, contour shifting, and zero symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin truncation plus the real-character large sieve
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how an analytic family moment is converted into smoothed character polynomials, truncated dyadically, and bounded by a large-sieve input while a reflected moment is retained for bootstrapping.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation exponent bootstrap and derivative control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses different reflected lines on the two sigma ranges to force the moment-loss exponent to zero, then turns a neighborhood bound for L into a central derivative bound using Cauchy's integral formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Carried zero-detection argument through its first alternative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carried v1 unit preserving the transition from the mean-square theorem into a mollified zero detector and the Cauchy-Schwarz estimate for its first alternative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mollified zero detector and its two alternatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns a zero in a small box into one of two detectable large quantities: a mollified L-integral or a dyadic tail polynomial, creating complementary analytic routes to bound the same zero count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Balancing the two zero-detection alternatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds the integral alternative by the family moment and mollifier large sieve, bounds the polynomial alternative directly, and chooses X and Y so neither case dominates before summing zero boxes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transition from the second detector case to explicit-formula kernel requirements
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carried v1 unit preserving the original span that reaches from the second zero-detector case into the stated decay and positivity requirements for the explicit-formula kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A nonclassical kernel matched to decay, symmetry, and positivity needs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why classical test functions are unsuitable and specifies a smooth compactly supported kernel whose transform decays off center, has nonnegative real part in a strip, and is symmetric about the central point after scaling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric contour formula with controlled horizontal tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a zero-avoiding rectangle, log-derivative bounds, functional-equation antisymmetry, and kernel symmetry to replace a finite contour by an infinite vertical integral plus a tunable small error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit formula, averaged prime term, and pre-density rank bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carried v1 unit connecting the weighted zero identity to conductor and prime terms, averaging the latter over discriminants, and reaching the inequality where off-center zeros are the remaining obstruction to an average-rank bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fundamental-discriminant structure controls the explicit-formula prime term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates higher prime powers, rewrites the prime coefficient average as a quadratic character sum, parametrizes fundamental discriminants by square-free progression conditions, and applies Polya-Vinogradov to close the average.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Average zero density converted into an average-rank bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses kernel positivity to isolate central multiplicity, partitions off-center zeros by horizontal distance and height, inserts the density hypothesis, and optimizes the scale lambda as log D divided by log L(D).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infinite convolution gives compact support and subexponential transform decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs a smooth even nonnegative compactly supported function from scaled tents, derives factorial-logarithmic derivative bounds, and optimizes repeated integration by parts to obtain the required transform decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Strip positivity obtained through a transform convolution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents the final kernel transform as a convolution with the hyperbolic-secant transform and uses positivity of the first Fourier factor plus the sign of the real part of the second to prove the strip condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies Littlewood's lemma and then Jensen's inequality to replace a derivative-zero counting problem by an upper bound involving the mean square of the mollified auxiliary function J_k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Differential-polynomial proxy for J_k and import of the mollified mean square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs V_k using Q_k(x)=(1-x)^k, replaces the J_k mean square asymptotically by the V_k mean square through chi asymptotics and integration by parts, then invokes Conrey's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolic-sine trial mollifier and balancing-parameter optimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relaxes the polynomial infimum to a continuous hyperbolic-sine trial function, balances two integral contributions by choosing a parameter, and estimates the Q_k integrals to obtain a large-order constant bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conversion of the optimized mean-square constant into derivative-zero abundance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the optimized constant with the zero-count inequality and the total derivative-zero count to obtain the stated positive proportion and its large-order behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed-zeta auxiliary function tuned to multiplicity loss
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines an auxiliary linear combination of the completed zeta function and its derivative, normalized by the gamma factor, so that its zeros encode repeated rather than simple zeta zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplicity and symmetry turn Littlewood's lemma into a distinct-zero deficit bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the auxiliary function's behavior at simple and multiple zeros plus symmetry about the critical line to lower-bound its weighted zero sum by the gap between total and distinct zero counts, then applies Jensen.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rewrite of the multiplicity detector as a differential polynomial in zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the logarithmic derivative of the completion factor and integration by parts to express the auxiliary function through a linear differential polynomial Q, placing its mean square under Conrey's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalized parameter choice certifying the distinct-zero proportion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Imposes the normalization needed by Littlewood's lemma, specializes the affine polynomial and mollifier parameters, and reports the evaluated constant that yields the final distinct-zero lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Artin holomorphy as a positive certification problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes falsifying Artin's conjecture by finding a pole from certifying holomorphy when the only critical-strip representation is a Brauer ratio, where a denominator zero and a tiny nearby pole-zero cancellation cannot be resolved naively.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coupling Artin holomorphy, bounded RH, and complementary zero locators
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It explains why Turing's method alone normally presupposes holomorphic irreducible factors, how the new criterion can remove that circularity, and why explicit-formula estimates and rigorous many-value evaluation play different roles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generic analytic contract for the L-functions under computation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler product, completed function, functional equation, analytic conductor, possible-pole polynomial, and Ramanujan-type bound specify exactly which later zero-count and numerical arguments are reusable beyond Artin L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Net-zero counts cannot by themselves certify local holomorphy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Argument-principle counts for numerator and denominator reveal only zeros minus poles in a neighborhood, so finite numerical uncertainty cannot rule out a pole masked by a nearby zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Heilbronn characters convert analytic orders into monomial inequalities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring Dedekind zeta and monomial Artin L-functions turns every possible local order pattern into a virtual character nonnegative on monomial representations, and confines individual zeros and poles to zeros of the Dedekind zeta function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Runtime simplicity hypothesis becomes character indecomposability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming distinct simple irreducible zero patterns only as a checked runtime hypothesis, an observed net zero for one representation is certified when its character cannot split into two nonzero virtual characters nonnegative on all monomial representations; the central point requires a parity-aware variant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Almost monomiality as cone proximity and indecomposability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source reframes the criterion geometrically: the dual nonnegative region cut out by monomial characters must leave irreducible character rays indecomposable. It also identifies central multiplicity as a distinct practical limitation of sign-change counting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Almost monomiality survives quotients and products with monomial groups
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposition and proof show how the certification property transports through common group constructions using lift/descent, Frobenius reciprocity, and tensor-product inner products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lattice enumeration certifies A5, S5, and SL2(F3)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source reduces almost monomiality to a finite integral-basis search: enumerate bounded inner-product vectors, invert the monomial Gram matrix, and test the remaining inequalities; the same finite audit handles the central parity condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Induced information can be insufficient to expose a hidden pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: GL2(F3) and SL2(F5) defeat the optimistic generalization: even after adding known non-monomial induced cases, certain virtual-character decompositions allow a pole to hide at a zero of the six-dimensional factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adjoint-square bridge and a weaker route to bounded RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Passing an icosahedral representation to its three-dimensional adjoint square suggests an effective converse-theorem route, while the local character condition for RH allows bounded verification even when full Artin holomorphy is unavailable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compactly supported coefficient data probes the zero spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's explicit formula converts finitely many Euler/Dirichlet coefficients into weighted zero sums; under RH, nonnegative band-limited test functions turn this identity into a localized spectral probe.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero exclusion as constrained quadratic minimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A finite trigonometric-square family makes the positive zero sum a positive-definite quadratic form; minimizing it subject to h(t0)=1 gives a computable quantity below one only when t0 is not a zero ordinate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resolution cost, close-zero sensitivity, and diagnostic use of the explicit formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The uncertainty principle ties coefficient range to local zero density, exceptionally small gaps can increase cost, and the RH-dependent method is positioned as a fast low-zero locator and cross-check rather than the final unconditional certificate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generalized Turing counting from phase plus argument
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The functional equation folds an argument-principle contour onto the critical half-plane, decomposing the net zero count into a computable gamma phase Phi and the argument term S; simple critical-line zeros are then observed by sign changes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrated step-function bounds recover the missing zero-count offset
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Left- and right-endpoint brackets around observed sign changes give one-sided counting functions; integrating them and bounding the mean of S isolates the integer N(t0), so only endpoint neighborhoods need precise zeros while the interior needs sign changes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation plus pole clearing yields a uniform strip bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A symmetric auxiliary function and the Phragmen-Lindelof principle propagate boundary bounds across the strip; multiplying by shifted pole polynomials repairs holomorphy when L has poles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform gamma, conductor, and pole logarithmic-derivative control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under a separation condition at height t, explicit Stirling estimates bound the logarithmic derivatives of the gamma factor, analytic conductor, and pole polynomial uniformly in the spectral parameters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Paired-zero comparison controls the lower logarithmic integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A strip inequality for an integrated logarithmic ratio, proved by asymptotics, maximum principle, real-axis calculus, and a bounded computation, supplies the device that controls nearby-zero contributions in the lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramanujan bounds sandwich L and its logarithmic derivative by zeta envelopes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairing Euler factors produces explicit upper and lower zeta-based envelopes for both |L| and the real logarithmic derivative, converting local coefficient bounds into global computable constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit two-sided bound for the integrated argument term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4.5 combines the strip bound, gamma estimates, zeta envelopes, a Hadamard product over functional-equation-paired zeros, and Lemma 4.3 to bound the integral of S with an explicit conductor main term and controlled error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One Mellin transform enables many rigorous critical-line values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Instead of evaluating a two-parameter Cauchy-integral family pointwise, the source Fourier-transforms the damped completed L-function, expands its Dirichlet series through a single kernel G, and uses Poisson summation to obtain an FFT pair.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reality symmetry reduces transform sampling to a half-grid with certified tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjugate symmetry reduces the FFT input range, while large-shift asymptotics and a separate critical-line bound account for transform aliasing and time-domain wraparound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shifting gives a computable residue series for the kernel G
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Mellin kernel becomes a sum over gamma-factor poles; grouping equivalent shifts and propagating polar coefficients by recurrence yields a tail bounded by the last computed pole block and eventual factorial decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative recurrences and Taylor caches turn G into reusable family infrastructure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A shift in one gamma parameter computes derivatives of G, enabling certified local Taylor models that are reusable across every L-function with the same archimedean parameters; binning Dirichlet coefficients then converts evaluation at all samples into convolutions handled by another FFT.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Damping trades precision against coefficient range at square-root conductor scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Choosing eta near one slows decay enough to reach height T but raises coefficient/precision demands; after this tradeoff, the dominant coefficient count is of square-root analytic-conductor size and the FFT supplies many values at near-linear mean cost.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Effective large-u control of G from stationary phase and contour shifting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states the stationary-phase shape of G and derives a less sharp but fully effective contour-shift bound using Holder and explicit gamma estimates, making the large-shift FFT terms certifiable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient growth plus kernel decay certifies Dirichlet-series truncation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A polynomial coefficient bound and the effective G estimate make the omitted tail monotone after an explicit threshold, so an incomplete-gamma-style integral bounds every term beyond M.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two tail lemmas close both sides of FFT discretization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 5.4 sums shifted transform samples using kernel decay and pole residues; Lemma 5.5 sums shifted critical-line values using the functional-equation strip bound, together certifying aliasing in both Fourier domains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S5 character relations reduce global conjectures to selected nonvanishing checks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the worked S5 field, monomiality and explicit direct-sum relations identify which Artin factors are already holomorphic and reduce the remaining Artin/RH certification to zero isolation and nonvanishing of a small collection of compound L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parameter selection balances coefficient availability, damping, and interval precision
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The worked computation chooses eta by comparing the largest truncation error with the expected function size, determines how far beyond the target height Turing bounds require evaluation, and assigns interval arithmetic to the rigorous downstream stages.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dedekind-zeta ratios handle ramification while Frobenius classes scale coefficient generation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Brauer-style zeta ratios provide local factors at exceptional primes, while unramified Frobenius conjugacy classes are recovered from low-degree factorization data modulo p, yielding essentially linear-time coefficient generation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit-formula zero spikes cross-check coefficients and expose conductor-dependent density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The low-zero estimator yields unit-height spikes at plausible ordinates, agrees with the known zeta zero quoted by the source, and visibly tracks conductor/degree; because the explicit formula is coefficient-sensitive, this supplies an independent integrity check before the rigorous FFT/Turing pass.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Certified local G models feed the main FFT evaluation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The implementation precomputes high-precision Taylor models of G with a stated remainder, spends most effort on binned coefficient moments, and then makes the actual L-value FFT fast while choosing A and B so the sampling-tail bound is negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Agreement of independent zero locators precedes Turing closure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source compares zeros of the rigorously computed critical-line function with explicit-formula spikes, then applies Turing's method while simultaneously checking the runtime zero-isolation working hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free geometry as an explicit prime-counting error control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction makes the causal bridge from excluding zeros near one to an exponential error estimate for prime counting, then identifies which proof components are being changed and which numerical result is imported.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trigonometric averaging converts the Euler side into a nonnegative constraint
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The logarithmic derivative and Hadamard-product representation are combined with a nonnegative cosine polynomial so a chosen zero can be isolated while the prime-side weighted sum remains nonnegative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stechkin symmetrization makes paired zero contributions discardable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The zero symmetries ρ̄ and 1−ρ̄ are paired with a shifted logarithmic derivative so all nonexceptional contributions have a controlled sign, improving the constant available from the raw positivity argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A compactly supported test function turns Weil's formula into four controllable contribution classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source introduces an admissible test function and Laplace transform, then forms a shifted difference that decomposes the positive prime sum into archimedean, pole, zero, and remainder terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity parameters are rescaled around a candidate zero and anchored by verified low zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The method wraps the explicit formula in a positive trigonometric polynomial, parameterizes distance from the line Re(s)=1, and uses a finite verified-height boundary so the remaining analytic argument only addresses higher zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exceptional-zero isolation and geometric partition reduce the proof to signed error budgets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The candidate zero is separated, the remaining zeros are partitioned into a sign-discardable class and a density-controlled class, and four auxiliary estimates are assembled into one master inequality with a single correction term C(η).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kernel rescaling converts the master inequality into an iterative bound on the zero-free constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Scaling f by η collapses the proof to a kernel functional K(ω,θ); negativity of the correction and monotonicity in ω yield a scalar inequality that can be iterated to improve R.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Test-function and trigonometric families define a constrained representation search
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors vary both the smoothing kernel and the positive cosine polynomial while preserving the same proof interface, reject empirically worse polynomial forms, and update the verified-height cutoff before optimization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Four admissible kernels are compared under the same certification pipeline
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Propositions 6-9 hold the analytic framework fixed while changing kernel representations, numerically maximizing their objective, rechecking admissibility, correction negativity, and monotonicity, and comparing the resulting constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Autocorrelation builds an admissible kernel whose optimization gives the best bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A compactly supported nonnegative even function is convolved with itself, automatically satisfying the needed endpoint and transform-positivity constraints; the same numerical certification pipeline then yields the best reported constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parameter nonuniqueness and a structurally different kernel family test representation sensitivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remarks show that nearby parameterizations reproduce the best constant while a different hyperbolic-trigonometric construction performs slightly worse, providing both robustness evidence and a negative comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li positivity converts RH into a coefficient-sign problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text identifies analyticity after the map s=1/(1-z) and nonnegativity of every real Li coefficient as the necessary-and-sufficient RH interface used throughout the paper.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li coefficients as derivatives and sums over zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The same sequence is presented through logarithmic derivatives at one and zero and through reciprocal-power expressions over nontrivial zeros, connecting local analytic data to global zero geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eta decomposition of each Li coefficient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 decomposes lambda_n into an eta-binomial sum, an explicit alternating zeta-binomial sum, and elementary terms, while deriving eta from the Laurent expansion of zeta'/zeta and from von Mangoldt limits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Equivalent discrete forms of the explicit S1 sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reordering the zeta Dirichlet series turns the finite binomial sum into sums of elementary kernels, creating monotone functions suitable for integral comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integral comparison gives an n log n lower bound for S1
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 compares a decreasing summand with an integral, changes variables, integrates by parts, evaluates with the digamma function, and transfers the result into lower and upper bounds for lambda_n modulo S2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The explicit-sum estimates port to generalized Li formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper maps parity-dependent Dirichlet and elliptic gamma-factor sums to S0, S1, and S3, explaining which already-estimated components can be reused for generalized hypotheses.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stieltjes-to-eta recursion from logarithmic differentiation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Equating (zeta'/zeta)zeta with zeta' yields a recursive bridge between familiar Stieltjes constants and the eta coefficients targeted by the Li decomposition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eta coefficients equal zero-power sums plus an explicit tail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 connects sigma_k, the reciprocal-power sum over nontrivial zeros, to eta_{k-1} and an explicit zeta term; reordering and a generating identity evaluate the intervening zeta sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic evaluations constrain eta signs and moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluating and differentiating the Laurent series at several points produces sums, alternating sums, weighted moments, logarithmic sums, and a beta-weighted integral, ruling out a one-sign eta sequence and constraining decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial-zero scale versus nontrivial-zero scale predicts eta alternation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjecture 1 separates four claims about sigma decay and eta alternation/size; the argument compares the first nontrivial-zero contribution with the explicit odd-integer tail and proves the stated triangle-inequality bound while leaving global magnitude control conjectural.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stieltjes bounds induce a recursive eta majorant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Known bounds for Stieltjes constants are inserted into the eta recursion to produce a possible inductive control, illustrating both a route and its weakness relative to Theorem 5.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S2 cancellation is the unresolved bridge from eta behavior to Li positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source conjectures square-root-scale growth for the eta-binomial sum S2 and combines it with the proved S1 bound to obtain an eventual positive lower bound for lambda_n, leaving only finitely many direct checks.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Program summary isolates exponential cancellation and magnitude correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The discussion cleanly separates explicit sign alternation in S1, established or asserted eta sign alternation in S2, and the still-needed control relating consecutive eta magnitudes; it also states the proposed transfer to generalized L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Appendix A strengthens the S1 integral comparison
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A second integral form, integration by parts, hypergeometric reduction, binomial expansion, and elementary inequalities sharpen the lower estimate for S1 beyond the main-text comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same comparison method bounds S0
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Changing the kernel from odd denominators to all positive integers yields S0 and an exact comparison integral, showing the reusable part of the S1 estimation strategy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S3 comparison exposes parity-sensitive digamma structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A weighted zeta sum is converted to an integral whose evaluation changes form with parity, furnishing the S3 term required by the elliptic-curve Li formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Binet's formula yields a two-sided digamma remainder bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating Binet's representation isolates a positive-kernel remainder and produces a reusable two-sided correction to log z.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite alternating sums as contour integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source presents a Rice-type contour representation and explains asymptotic evaluation by contour displacement and residues, contrasting it with the paper's demand for non-asymptotic information.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integral evaluation of the zeta sum in Theorem 3
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substituting the Mellin integral for zeta, changing variables, and subtracting the unit contribution independently evaluates the summation that links eta and sigma.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coefficient comparison rederives the eta-sigma identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding xi'/xi, the digamma term, and zeta'/zeta around one and equating coefficients gives a second, conceptually different proof of Theorem 3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet Li coefficients split into gamma growth and an arithmetic character sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For primitive characters, the generalized Li coefficient is decomposed into an arithmetic von-Mangoldt/Laguerre sum and parity-dependent explicit terms, then bounded using S0 and S1; cancellation in character phases is explicitly conjectural.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elliptic Li coefficients expose a signed prime-power residual
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The elliptic xi product yields a Li decomposition with an arithmetic b(k) sum and explicit S0/S3 terms; possible sign changes in local coefficients motivate, but do not establish, cancellation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hurwitz-zeta identities become polygamma integral kernels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix rewrites the half-integer reciprocal-power sum as a Hurwitz-zeta relation and then as polygamma values and positive integral kernels useful in explicit zero formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet generalized Li formula from logarithmic derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starting from the xi product, repeated logarithmic differentiation separates conductor, gamma-factor, and prime-power contributions and recovers the explicit Dirichlet Li formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elliptic generalized Li formula from logarithmic derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The same product-to-derivative template applied to the elliptic xi function separates conductor, gamma, and local arithmetic components and recovers the elliptic explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dedekind Li explicit-formula framework and convergence gate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Dedekind completion is decomposed into discriminant, archimedean, and prime-ideal terms; differentiating supplies the candidate Li representation while explicitly leaving convergence justification as a gate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A hypergeometric family unifies alternating zeta-sum bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introducing a shift and multiplier turns several special sums into terminating 2F1 forms, whose comparison integrals become 3F2 expressions and reduce to digamma/harmonic forms at special parameters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtracting trivial-zero poles enlarges the eta expansion radius
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explicitly removing six trivial-zero contributions moves the nearest remaining singularity outward, yields faster-decaying modified eta coefficients, and changes the Li representation by known exponential terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial-zero derivatives calibrate the modified eta sequence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Taylor expansion at each trivial zero and functional-equation derivative identities provide modified coefficient data, including eta_0, and refine the lower-bound decomposition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation formulas relate zeta derivatives across the critical reflection
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating the zeta functional equation relates negative-integer derivatives to positive-side values and Bernoulli series, supplying explicit data for modified eta moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin integrals generate logarithmic-derivative moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating the Mellin representation of zeta produces formulas for zeta derivatives and successive derivatives of zeta'/zeta, directly targeting the weighted eta moments from the main text.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li's polynomial as a Laguerre derivative and Mellin-Laplace kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite binomial polynomial is identified with a terminating confluent hypergeometric series and an associated Laguerre polynomial, converting its Mellin transform into a Laplace transform with a simple closed form.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero counting bounds an RH-conditional tail of sigma
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A unit-interval zero-count estimate is combined with integral comparison to bound a reciprocal-ordinate tail, giving a concrete route from zero density to sigma decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Dedekind xi integral forces real-axis derivative positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For an imaginary quadratic field, a positive integral kernel and the functional symmetry imply positivity of xi on the real axis, nonnegativity of derivatives on the right half-axis, and strict positivity for even orders.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Special-function series evaluate Dedekind xi derivative inputs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theta-integral pieces are rewritten using incomplete gamma, error, and exponential-integral functions, and special derivative values are identified as inputs to Dedekind Li logarithmic derivatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Maclaurin expansion refines S1 with a divergent correction series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explicit summand derivatives are inserted into Euler-Maclaurin to refine the n log n contribution and suggest alternating upper/lower approximations while warning that the correction series is generally divergent.

within_source_synthesis_map.title: Zero-power sums mediate local Laurent data and Li coefficients

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Portability of the explicit component does not control the separate prime-weighted arithmetic residuals.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Integral comparison is the portable deterministic component

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Character phases or local sign changes are only plausibility for cancellation, and the Dedekind formula still carries an explicit convergence-justification gate.

within_source_synthesis_map.title: Alternative derivations test representation robustness

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Asymptotic corrections can tighten S1's linear term and suggest alternating approximations, but further refinement of S1 leaves S2 magnitude control as the decisive missing ingredient.
