result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elliptic point-count bound reduced to positivity of a quadratic form
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states the analogue as |N-q| bounded by 2 square-root q, contrasts characteristic-restricted elementary proofs with a valuation-theoretic proof for all finite characteristics, and identifies positive semidefiniteness of a quadratic form as the stronger intermediate target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-divisor valuations and the additive product formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The construction expands the prime divisors of k(x) to K, normalizes their discrete valuations, records the sharp ultrametric rule and finite support, and invokes the additive product formula with residue-degree multiplicities; these are the local-to-global ingredients later used to prove quadraticity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Self-composite curve and its K-rational point group
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The article passes from the original curve over k to the same elliptic equation over K as constant field, making its K-rational points into an abelian group whose coordinate addition formulas can be analyzed valuation by valuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole-weighted function and the parallelogram target
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source defines d(P) as a residue-degree-weighted sum over primes where x_P has a pole, uses finite support to make it well-defined, and identifies the parallelogram identity as the condition that makes d a quadratic form on the rational-point group.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole behavior under elliptic-curve addition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 1 shows that adding two points with negative x-valuations preserves a pole and controls its valuation, while adding a pole point to a non-pole point yields a non-pole; the proof uses the sharp ultrametric rule, the addition formula, and decompositions such as P=(P+Q)-Q.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Valuations of P-Q and P+Q tied to coordinate separation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 2 separates the non-pole and pole cases for P and Q and relates the x-valuations of P-Q and P+Q to the valuation of x_P-x_Q, providing the local equality that later converts the sum defining d into a parallelogram identity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nonzero constant discriminant forces local equalities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After deriving valuation inequalities from coordinate identities and the addition law, the proof represents the curve discriminant as a polynomial combination of the two partial derivatives. Because that nonzero discriminant lies in the constant field and has valuation zero, the possible strict inequalities would force a contradiction, upgrading the local estimates to the equalities in Lemma 2(a).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Closing the equal-pole case in characteristic 2 and non-2
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remaining part of Lemma 2 is reduced to unequal pole orders by Lemma 1, then treats equal pole orders through three possible valuations of P-Q and P+Q, using different coordinate identities in characteristic 2 and in other characteristics to obtain the missing equality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Product-formula globalization of the parallelogram identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof combines the mixed-sign case from Lemma 1, the local separation identities from Lemma 2, and the residue-degree-weighted product formula to show d(P-Q)+d(P+Q)=2d(P)+2d(Q), with the equal or opposite point cases supplied by doubling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integer-lattice nonnegativity forces nonpositive discriminant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source reduces positive semidefiniteness of each two-point restriction of d to a general lemma: if a real binary quadratic form is nonnegative on a scaled integer lattice, a positive discriminant would make the separation of its real roots grow with the lattice parameter while lattice nonnegativity bounds that separation, a contradiction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Frobenius height matrix encodes the point-count error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For P0=(x,y) and its coordinatewise q-th-power Frobenius image Q0, Lemma 4 targets d(P0)=1, d(Q0)=q, and the cross term q-N; substituting these values into the nonpositive discriminant inequality is stated to be equivalent to the theorem's point-count bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The unique infinite prime gives the diagonal height values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof identifies the unique extension of the infinite prime to K through ramification degree two, computes the pole order of x there, and obtains d(P0)=1; Frobenius scaling similarly gives d(Q0)=q.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rational solutions detected by primes dividing x-x^q
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The addition formula shows that finite primes can create poles in x(P0+Q0) exactly when they divide x-x^q. The source then gives a bijection between k-solutions of the curve and degree-one primes with those residue coordinates, using the factorization of x^q-x to fix the positive valuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramified degree-one primes contribute poles of order two
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Among primes above factors of x^q-x, the ramified degree-one case uses the nonzero discriminant identity to keep one partial derivative a unit, determines the valuation of y-y^q, and hence obtains valuation -2 for the x-coordinate of P0+Q0; these primes account for M rational solutions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decomposed degree-one primes versus inert degree-two primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The decomposed degree-one primes correspond to rational solutions but yield no negative x-valuation for P0+Q0, whereas inert degree-two primes yield no k-solution and contribute valuation -2; the source counts the two sets as 2L and q-L-M respectively.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-type counts produce the Frobenius cross term q-N
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The classification gives N=2L+M. Adding the finite-prime contributions to the infinite-prime contribution in the definition of d yields the stated identity d(P0+Q0)-d(P0)-d(Q0)=q-N, completing Lemma 4 and therefore the theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Montgomery's formula turns pair counts into weighted bandlimited approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the normalized statistic and shows that admissible majorants and minorants of an interval give conditional upper and lower bounds, with the lower bound's simplicity requirement explicit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three complementary routes separate optimality, explicitness, and asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors distinguish an explicit reproducing-kernel solution, a general de Branges extremal solution, and non-extremal Beurling-Selberg bounds whose asymptotics remain tractable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Translated Beurling functions approximate an arbitrary symmetric interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A sign-function extremizer is synthesized into interval majorants and minorants for every beta, yielding explicit weighted bounds and large-beta behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The two-delta gap becomes a reproducing-kernel evaluation problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The minimal possible separation between interval upper and lower bounds is encoded by a nonnegative bandlimited function constrained at two points, then solved using the explicit kernel of the weighted Paley-Wiener space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hermite-Biehler data generate a de Branges reproducing-kernel space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Supplies the semantic bridge among bounded type, mean/exponential type, the H(E) norm, companion functions A and B, and kernel evaluations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The pair-correlation Hilbert space is realized as a de Branges space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructing E from the explicit kernel yields an isometric identity between the pair-correlation measure norm and a de Branges norm, enabling interpolation theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Interval approximation in de Branges spaces has three node regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The optimal majorant/minorant values are discrete quadrature sums over zeros of A, B, or auxiliary companions, with endpoint membership determining the qualitative regime.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Interval-width loss equals the two-delta extremum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The difference of optimal interval majorant and minorant is itself optimal for the two-point constraint, identifying the sharp attainable pair-correlation bound gap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive pair-count lower bounds imply small normalized gaps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how minorant positivity forces many close pairs and why the conclusion on consecutive gaps survives whether the simplicity assumption holds or fails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bandlimited comparison remains valid for slowly growing intervals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 8 tracks diagonal multiplicity explicitly and quantifies how Fourier-transform regularity limits growth of beta; a multiplicity bound then yields an RH-only corollary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Montgomery's nonnegative correlation function is the transfer channel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines F(alpha), proves positivity through a squared exponential sum, gives the convolution identity, and states the known asymptotic on the accessible support interval.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit transforms expose support and regularity of the interval approximants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the transforms of the building blocks and r_beta plus/minus, making compact support, beta oscillation, and the Lipschitz growth used in error control explicit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Plancherel plus diagonal separation proves the variable-beta bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the admissible test sum spectrally, controls the growing-beta error via transform bounds, and separates diagonal multiplicities from off-diagonal pairs to obtain both inequalities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted Beurling-Selberg error is evaluated at general bandwidth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Scaling to support [-Delta,Delta] and decomposing the transform integral into A, B, and C yields a convergent series formula that specializes to Theorem 2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Fourier-sum term is constant in beta, revealing the large-beta correction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Summation by parts, analytic continuation, termwise differentiation, and the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma show an auxiliary function is constant, converting the exact series into the asymptotic weighted error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uncertainty prevents the pair-correlation weight from losing a bandlimited function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An uncertainty principle supplies a uniform lower norm bound away from the weight's zero, proving equality of the weighted and ordinary Paley-Wiener sets and equivalence of norms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A convolution equation determines the explicit reproducing kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourier expansions and cancellation of the interior convolution defect prove the proposed kernel reproduces evaluation; a differential heuristic explains how its ansatz and two free parameters arise.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two equal-norm evaluation constraints reduce to a two-vector minimizer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Hilbert-space lemma gives both the minimum norm and all equality cases according to whether the representing vectors are orthogonal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Krein factorization converts the two-delta function problem into kernel geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A nonnegative entire function factors as an absolute square in the Hilbert space, so pointwise constraints become kernel inner-product constraints and Lemma 13 yields the sharp extremum and extremizers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The one-delta extremum is reciprocal kernel mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Cauchy-Schwarz at one evaluation gives the exact optimal majorant and connects its value to an improved bound on zero multiplicities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orthogonal kernel bases turn integrals into node sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Auxiliary E_beta spaces preserve the required de Branges properties, position beta among zeros, and yield quadrature identities for nonnegative entire functions via Krein factorization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generic extremizers are certified by interpolation at quadrature nodes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Laguerre-Polya interpolation constructs interval majorants/minorants and the node-sum formula proves optimality immediately in the generic regimes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Root endpoints recover Beurling-Selberg-type extremizers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When beta is a zero of A or B, sign-function extremizers combine into interval approximants at exactly the quadrature nodes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Below the first node, zero is the optimal minorant and a squared quotient is the majorant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interlacing rules out interior quadrature nodes, while Laguerre-Polya monotonicity makes a normalized quotient dominate the interval; quadrature then certifies both extrema.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtracting interval extremizers recovers the unique two-delta optimizer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shared interpolation nodes make the difference majorize the two-point set and attain the quadrature lower bound; the off-diagonal kernel value determines generic uniqueness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A triangular test bounds the unknown mass of Montgomery's function beyond one
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Positivity and a sinc-squared test combine known F(alpha) behavior on [0,1] with diagonal multiplicity to lower-bound a weighted integral on [1,xi].

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A second use of Montgomery's formula improves the small-gap threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A positive-transform interval minorant produces a pair-count inequality, while two integrations by parts let Lemma 17 control the otherwise unknown spectral tail and make the final numerical expression positive.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primitive Dirichlet families provide a wider-support pair-correlation analogue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines smoothed q-aspect counts and their spectral function, states the conditional upper/lower bounds, and identifies support up to nearly two as the source of stronger constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An asymptotic large-sieve window upgrades the extremal bandwidth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 19 controls the q-aspect correlation function to support 2-epsilon, and the same convolution comparison with scaled Beurling-Selberg functions reduces Theorem 18 to the earlier general-bandwidth asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reproducing-kernel symmetries construct the Hermite-Biehler generator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Positivity, conjugation symmetry, and the kernel identity produce E from a fixed nonreal evaluation and verify both the Hermite-Biehler inequality and de Branges kernel representation.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: A zero-pair counting problem is modularized into a spectral transfer theorem plus an approximation problem; explicitness, optimality, and asymptotic transparency can then be supplied by different approximant families.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The transfer is conditional on the stated RH/multiplicity hypotheses and on the Fourier support where Montgomery's formula is controlled.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Pair correlation as weighted bandlimited approximation

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: After norm equivalence and nonnegative factorization, a function constrained at two points becomes a minimum-norm vector constrained by two kernel evaluations, so the sharp value depends only on a diagonal kernel mass and one off-diagonal correlation.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This reduction applies to the specified bandlimited nonnegative class and inherits the exact weighted space and kernel normalization.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Two-delta optimization is evaluation geometry

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: A de Branges representation turns continuous weighted optimization into interpolation at orthogonal kernel nodes; endpoint position selects the node family, and subtracting the two interval extremizers recovers the two-point extremizer.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The theorem requires properties P1-P4 and changes construction across root, generic, and below-first-root regimes.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Quadrature unifies interval and two-point extremizers

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: When the main pair-correlation asymptotic is only known up to frequency one, an independent positive triangular test constrains the spectral tail, and integrating that constraint against a second minorant improves the small-gap conclusion.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The final threshold is a conditional, numerically evaluated consequence for this formal worker and does not establish pair correlation beyond the known interval.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: A second positive test unlocks unknown spectral mass

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The general-bandwidth extremal calculation can be reused unchanged when a different family supplies a wider correlation window; the q-aspect support near two directly sharpens the leading constants relative to zeta support one.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The zeta and primitive-Dirichlet settings use different averaging, smoothing, and hypotheses, so the improvement is a structural comparison rather than an unconditional transfer between families.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Spectral window width controls the strength of transferred bounds

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The one-delta optimum is governed by reciprocal diagonal kernel mass, while the two-delta optimum adds the magnitude of the off-diagonal kernel interaction; interval-bound width realizes the latter quantity.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The hierarchy concerns nonnegative entire functions of the fixed exponential type and weighted norm, not arbitrary zero-spacing statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moment constants split into arithmetic and universal factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The continuous zeta moment problem is organized as an arithmetic Euler-product factor times a still-mysterious coefficient, making clear which part a random-matrix model is intended to predict.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Matrix size is matched to zero density and fixes the universal moment factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The characteristic polynomial of a Haar unitary matrix is matched to zeta at height T by setting matrix dimension to the local logarithmic density, and its Barnes-G asymptotic supplies the previously unknown universal coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative moments arise from sampling characteristic-polynomial derivatives at eigenangles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It extends the same density matching from ordinary zeta moments to discrete derivative moments at zeros, with a shifted admissible moment range and exponent, and records agreement with known special cases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A microscopic offset family is proposed to unify value and derivative moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rather than treating zeta and derivative moments separately, the paper inserts an offset of one local-spacing scale and predicts that a single profile has the ordinary-value and derivative conjectures as opposite offset limits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Microscopic eigenangle offsets have a Bessel-profile moment asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 identifies the leading Haar-unitary moment near an eigenangle as a Barnes-G scale times an explicit spherical-Bessel profile, uniformly out to offsets proportional to dimension below the angular boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditioning on an eigenangle reduces the target to a two-point mixed moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring out the selected eigenvalue and absorbing Vandermonde terms converts an eigenangle-centered characteristic-polynomial moment in dimension N into a mixed moment at two points in dimension N-1; this is the key structural reduction behind Theorem 3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The profile series resums into Bessel functions and normalizes at separated points
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matching Taylor expansions converts the coefficient series into a compact Bessel expression, while fixed angular separation and large-argument Bessel asymptotics show F_k tends to 1 and extend the leading term across a macroscopic offset range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integer moments yield explicit crossover profiles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For integer k the derivative representation of spherical Bessel functions turns the abstract profile into elementary trigonometric rational expressions, including the k=2 profile used in the later number-theoretic comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-N mixed characteristic-polynomial moment admits an explicit double sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4 supplies the exact finite-dimensional two-point moment representation needed by the conditioning reduction, separating powers of the point distance from a finite inner sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A constant-term representation opens the mixed moment to Selberg evaluation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For integer k, the Haar integral is algebraically recast as a multivariate constant term, converted to a generalized Selberg integral evaluated by Kaneko, and expanded into an exact gamma-function sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry controls parity and Carlson continuation removes the integer restriction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Invariance of the inner summand under index reversal explains why only even offset powers occur, and analyticity plus growth bounds and agreement at positive integers permit continuation to complex k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hypergeometric transformations expose the coefficientwise microscopic limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite inner sum is recognized as a Gauss hypergeometric polynomial, transformed quadratically, reorganized as a finite double sum, and asymptotically scaled to a double power series whose coefficients converge one by one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wilf-Zeilberger telescoping collapses the double series to the profile series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Coefficient comparison reduces equality of the double and single profile series to a finite identity; a generated WZ pair makes the difference telescope, proves independence from the coefficient index, and fixes the constant at the base case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted discrete zeta moments inherit the random-matrix crossover profile
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjecture 5 transfers F_k to values of zeta displaced from its zeros by alpha local spacings, preserving the arithmetic factor and Barnes-G factor and demanding uniformity over a growing alpha range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zero-offset limit recovers derivative moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dividing the shifted value by the offset and using the small-alpha leading term of F_k converts Conjecture 5 into the derivative-moment conjecture with the correct Barnes-G shift and logarithmic exponent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The large-offset limit recovers an ordinary moment sampled discretely
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Large-argument Bessel asymptotics force F_k to 1; setting alpha equal to a fixed physical displacement times the local density then yields the usual moment scale and explains why values sufficiently far from a zero behave like generic critical-line samples.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The k=1 crossover matches a proved zeta formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A theorem of Gonek gives the shifted discrete second moment uniformly in alpha and its sine-kernel-shaped factor agrees with Conjecture 5 at k=1, providing a direct number-theoretic calibration point.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A mollified k=2 theorem matches the profile only after an unproved endpoint extrapolation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The available number-theoretic theorem controls a zeta value multiplied by a short Dirichlet polynomial for eta below one half; formally setting eta=1 turns the polynomial into zeta and the resulting series simplifies exactly to the predicted F_2 profile.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The extrapolated k=2 profile reproduces the fourth derivative moment constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the same small-offset argument to the conditional k=2 profile yields the eighth-logarithmic-scale fourth moment of zeta prime and agrees with the earlier derivative conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cahen-Mellin plus Tauberian transfer to prime-number-theorem equivalents
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction identifies a reusable architecture: convert a generalized Dirichlet series by Mellin inversion, then use one-sided Tauberian hypotheses to recover coefficient-sum asymptotics and several elementarily equivalent forms of the prime number theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothed Möbius explicit formula and RH-conditioned oscillation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the exponentially smoothed arithmetic error, forecasts an explicit zero formula, and separates an RH-sized upper bound and two-sided oscillation from the stronger estimates the method cannot reach.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tschebyschef prime-bias assertion through a Dirichlet L-function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Frames a prime-residue bias as a transform governed by zeros of a Dirichlet L-function and explicitly distinguishes the proved implication under the critical-line hypothesis from the unproved converse intuition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted exponential sums over zero ordinates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how Landau's zero-power-sum method is adapted to damped oscillatory sums and highlights a potentially artificial parameter dependence in the proved order estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From special-function proofs to short-interval sign changes on the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tracks how an existence proof using Mellin and theta-function behavior was simplified and then replaced by a different sign-change argument yielding a zero in every sufficiently long short interval, while recording an unsuccessful stronger density target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why persistent empirical prime-counting bias must eventually reverse
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts a slowly varying fixed-sign contribution with a larger oscillatory zero contribution and previews Kronecker-style simultaneous phase alignment, explaining both long empirical bias and inevitable reversals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin inversion, Fourier decay, and one-sided Tauberian recovery
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages three reusable steps: exponential-kernel Mellin inversion, decay of an integrable vertical-line transform, and recovery of partial sums from small-parameter exponential asymptotics under controlled coefficient increments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic continuation and vertical growth imply small exponential sums and partial sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how contour displacement turns continuation and vertical growth of a generalized Dirichlet series into an o(y^{-c}) exponential-sum bound, then invokes the Tauberian lemma to obtain o(lambda_n^c) partial sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The c=0 boundary yields convergence at the analytic value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Modifies the shifted contour at the boundary c=0 by indenting around the origin, converting regularity there into ordinary convergence of coefficients and deriving a Möbius-series consequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A simple pole becomes the main coefficient-sum term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces boundary regularity by a simple pole and shows that its residue becomes the leading asymptotic after Mellin inversion and Tauberian recovery, with the prime number theorem as the principal instance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing an artificial vertical-growth restriction by changing the kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates genuine hypotheses from proof artifacts, notes a failure for rapidly spaced exponents, and removes the restrictive growth exponent by replacing the exponential kernel with a fractional-power kernel and transferring back to the original scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour displacement and complete residue taxonomy for a smoothed Möbius sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds an explicit formula by moving the Mellin contour and classifying contributions from the main pole, the origin, nontrivial zeros, trivial zeros, and double poles, including an explicit warning about the delicate limiting justification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtracting the Bernoulli expansion isolates the zero sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a second Mellin representation for the unweighted exponential sum and subtracts it from the Möbius formula, leaving a zero-driven term plus controlled analytic power-series remainders.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Crude local zero counts suffice to control the RH zero tail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH, reorganizes positive zero ordinates and shows that a deliberately crude zero-count bound is enough to make the discarded tail smaller than the leading pair of zero terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First zero pair forces two-sided square-root oscillation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the explicit formula and tail estimate to obtain an RH-sized upper bound and infinitely recurring positive and negative values, then transfers this to the sharp Chebyshev error and records why an off-line zero does not yet yield the analogous smoothed statement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riesz/Cesaro means restore regularity lost by the sharp sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that the exponential smoothing behaves as regularly as the zeros allow whereas the sharp sum does not, then derives comparable bounds for every positive-order Riesz/Cesaro mean and distinguishes Abelian implications in each direction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-residue bias expressed as a sum over Dirichlet L-zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the logarithmic derivative of the relevant Dirichlet L-function, applies Mellin inversion, and shifts the contour to express the weighted bias through its complex zeros plus analytic remainders.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed L-function product bounds the aggregate zero contribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the functional equation to form a real even completed function, factors it over real zero ordinates, and extracts a coefficient identity giving both a global reciprocal-square sum and a lower bound on the first zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separating prime, prime-square, and higher-power terms exposes one-sided bias
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds the total zero contribution, decomposes the logarithmic-derivative coefficients by prime-power multiplicity, and shows the prime-square main term dominates the higher-power remainder, forcing the prime contribution negative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional coefficient weighting preserves a one-sided lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces an integral transform that turns a lower bound for an exponential generating function into a lower bound after multiplying coefficients by n^{-s}, with an explicit restriction on the exponent range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A logarithmic convergence factor proves Tschebyschef's assertion under the L-hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents 1/log n by an integral kernel, transfers the one-sided bound to the prime series, and obtains the claimed divergence rate; it also states the compelling but unproved reason the assertion should fail if the L-zero hypothesis fails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First-order Riesz/Cesaro means yield a stronger averaged prime bias
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recasts the bias in Riesz means, isolates prime, square, and higher-power contributions again, and obtains a first-order mean tending to negative infinity, from which the earlier exponential assertions follow Abelianly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bessel-Mellin and integral Tauberian lemmas for the zeta mean square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the missing critical-line mean-square asymptotic and assembles a Mellin-square identity, a sectorial Bessel asymptotic, and an integral Tauberian theorem that will convert a damped transform into cumulative mean behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Divisor-weighted Bessel transform localizes the zeta mean square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Sums the Mellin-Bessel kernel with divisor coefficients, moves the contour through a double pole, uses the functional equation, and chooses a near-boundary angle so the resulting series has a tractable localized asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Damped mean-square asymptotics imply the undamped critical-line mean square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the integral Tauberian lemma to the localized transform, then uses a change of variables and integration by parts to recover the asymptotic for the cumulative square modulus of zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramanujan-inspired reciprocal formula from a non-rigorous contour shift
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives a striking reciprocity between a Möbius-Gaussian series at reciprocal parameters by Mellin inversion and a proposed contour shift across zeta zeros, then checks the symmetry constraint on the residue series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The missing horizontal-boundary estimate and reciprocal-function generalization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies a concrete sufficient zeta bound along a sequence of heights or curves that would justify the contour shift, admits the inability to prove it even under RH, and generalizes the reciprocal structure through paired cosine transforms and Mellin factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equations propagate reciprocal identities and conditional growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines reciprocal-transform functional equations with the zeta and Gamma functional equations to produce a broader family of candidate identities, then shows how RH plus absolute convergence would impose square-root-scale growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riesz-function growth as a necessary and sufficient criterion for RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a Mellin integral for the Riesz function to motivate a growth criterion, explains why analytic continuation would imply RH, then proves the converse estimate from a known RH consequence for Möbius partial sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted damped exponential sums over zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starts from Landau's resonance formula, converts it under RH to an exponential sum in zero ordinates, and states uniform bounds and convergence regimes for a damped and rotated generalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial summation reduces the rotation parameter to the base case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that proving the theorem at zero rotation suffices, using partial summation to transfer a uniform base bound to the general oscillatory factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A rectangular zero-residue contour isolates a difficult top edge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs a large rectangle for the logarithmic derivative, lets the far-left edge recede, decomposes the top edge into far-zero and near-zero pieces, and proves all but the main vertical integral negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The main contour integral becomes a Dirichlet-series oscillatory integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reduces the surviving vertical integral to a Dirichlet series whose coefficient terms are oscillatory integrals, then partitions indices according to whether the phase has an interior stationary point.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Monotone-phase integration controls both tails uniformly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves an integration lemma after the change of variable w=t log(t/xi), then applies it symmetrically to indices below and above the stationary range to bound both nonstationary tails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local quadratic expansion at the phase critical point
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Locates the stationary point, rescales around it, separates central and outer pieces with careful endpoint conventions, and obtains the main Gaussian/Fresnel-scale estimate from a quadratic phase expansion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Five error sums close the weighted zero-sum estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the stationary-phase bounds into the coefficient sum, estimates five distinct error families, and recombines them with the contour reduction and RH parameterization to prove the section's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line zeros from sign changes of a real auxiliary function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a real-valued critical-line auxiliary function and reduces the existence of an odd-order zero in each short interval to two integral estimates, explicitly separating the easy contradiction stage from the hard cancellation stage.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Constant sign conflicts with the functional-equation main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming the auxiliary function keeps one sign, converts its absolute integral into a zeta integral and uses a rectangle plus the functional equation to expose a main term too large for the previously asserted cancellation bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounding side edges reduces critical-line cancellation to one short vertical integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses another rectangle and uniform zeta/Gamma bounds to dismiss two sides, leaving a single short vertical integral as the only remaining estimate needed for sign changes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: At most one resonant Dirichlet term controls the short-interval integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies Stirling's formula, freezes slow factors, expands into oscillatory Dirichlet terms, and splits around the unique possible stationary index; nonresonant terms are bounded by the earlier phase lemma and the central finite block is controlled directly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Odd-order critical-line zero in every prescribed short interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records the source's final local sign-change theorem and its global lower bound for the number of critical-line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-error oscillation reduced to a sine series over zero ordinates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the target two-sided Omega bounds, notes why RH may be assumed without loss for this lower-bound goal, and uses the zero-counting inverse plus the explicit formula to express the normalized prime error as a convergent sine series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A damped zero series has a logarithmically large boundary profile
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces an analytic damping parameter, approximates zero ordinates through the inverse counting function, converts the sum into a tractable integral, and obtains an explicit large asymptotic along a shrinking interior path.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tail control plus simultaneous approximation moves the large value deep into the strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Controls the high-zero tail uniformly, uses Dirichlet/Kronecker-style simultaneous approximation to align finitely many zero phases with the seed configuration, and obtains arbitrarily high strip points carrying logarithmically large imaginary part.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A modified Lindelof lemma handles discontinuous boundary data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the standard theorem cannot be applied to the boundary zero series, formulates a strip maximum-principle variant with only pointwise boundary limits plus local boundedness, and proves it by damping with an auxiliary entire factor and splitting the rectangle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Interior Omega behavior forces boundary Omega behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the modified Lindelof lemma to an exponential of the zero series, verifies local boundary control from the explicit formula and partial summation, establishes the interior growth condition, and contradicts the strip Omega theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From Chebyshev oscillations to prime-counting oscillations using smoothed control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the main Chebyshev-error oscillation theorem and then shows why ordinary partial summation is insufficient for one-sided Omega relations; a prime-power aggregate and the earlier Riesz/Cesaro bound control the extra term, yielding oscillations of Pi(x)-Li(x).

section_argument_map.label: Front matter and introduction/summary
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the paper's problem families, previews the transform/Tauberian, zero-sum, critical-line, and prime-oscillation mechanisms, and records limitations and unsuccessful strengthenings.

section_argument_map.label: 2.1 The prime number theorem and allied theorems
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Develops Cahen-Mellin plus Tauberian transfer from analytic continuation and growth of generalized Dirichlet series to coefficient-sum asymptotics, including prime-number-theorem applications.

section_argument_map.label: 2.2 The function sum (mu(n)-1)e^{-ny}
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives an explicit residue formula, controls its zero contribution under RH, proves two-sided oscillation, and compares exponential smoothing with Riesz/Cesaro means.

section_argument_map.label: 2.3 On an assertion of Tschebyschef
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Transforms a prime-residue bias into a Dirichlet L-zero formula, obtains a conditional one-sided divergence, and studies its first-order means.

section_argument_map.label: 2.4 Mean value of |zeta(1/2+it)|^2
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses Mellin-Bessel transforms, divisor sums, asymptotic localization, and an integral Tauberian lemma to derive the critical-line mean square.

section_argument_map.label: 2.5 Ramanujan-Riesz reciprocal series and RH criterion
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Presents conjectural reciprocal-transform identities, isolates the missing contour estimate, generalizes through reciprocal functions, and derives a Riesz-function growth criterion for RH.

section_argument_map.label: 3 Weighted exponential series over zeta zeros
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Adapts Landau's contour method and stationary-phase analysis to weighted oscillatory sums over zero ordinates, with uniformity and convergence regimes.

section_argument_map.label: 4 Zeros of zeta on the critical line
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves sign changes of a real critical-line auxiliary function in short intervals and obtains a lower bound for the number of critical-line zeros.

section_argument_map.label: 5 Order of psi(x)-x and Pi(x)-Li(x)
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Combines an explicit zero formula, phase alignment, a boundary maximum-principle lemma, and smoothed-to-sharp transfer to prove large oscillations in prime-counting errors.

section_argument_map.label: Additional note and erratum
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Records independent later work overlapping Section 4 and an unrelated correction; contains no new proof mechanism for this source plan.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From central nonvanishing to real-zero freedom in a quadratic family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes forced or arithmetic central vanishing from the stronger absence of zeros on the real segment, identifies what earlier density and nonvanishing results did not rule out, and fixes the negative-discriminant family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive proportion with positivity on the full real interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the main positive-proportion conclusion and strengthens it to a thin zero-free rectangle and a quantitative bound for discriminants with a zero near one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg kernel turns a real zero into a positive weighted boundary integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives a cut-domain argument-principle identity whose kernel has chosen reality properties, applies it to a mollified L-function in a microscopic box, and uses functional-equation pairing to give every real zero a fixed positive cost.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Average boundary size becomes a shifted mollified second-moment problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the weighted bad-family count and normalized shifted second moment, applies arithmetic-mean versus geometric-mean control to log size, and chooses a coefficient gap in the mollifier to oppose exponential kernel growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted moment propositions isolate tail, main term, and near-central specialization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Organizes the analytic burden into an off-center estimate, an approximate functional equation for paired completed values, a square-free truncation, an explicit principal-plus-remainder formula, and the near-central specialization actually needed for the zero count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit mollifier parameters close the positive-proportion inequality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the near-central moment into the two boundary integrals, reduces the bad-family proportion to explicit integrals of V, and records the parameter choice whose computer evaluation gives 0.79, below the real-zero threshold one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kernel geometry and mollifier length impose a box-size tradeoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the Selberg kernel avoids the hard boundary argument, why its exponential horizontal growth forces a long coefficient-annihilating mollifier, and why the box height, mollifier length, and unresolved coefficient optimization are coupled.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symplectic repulsion predicts why the weighted zero count is small
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the rigorous 0.79 bound from a GRH-and-symmetry heuristic, interprets the symplectic one-level density's quadratic vanishing at the center as zero repulsion, and proposes transfer to other odd-sign families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour symmetry gives an exact smoothed representation of paired completed values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Establishes small- and large-argument behavior of the smoothing kernel, then shifts the paired-completed-L integral so the functional equation makes the remainder equal the negative original series, yielding an exact representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-power Gauss sums encode multiplicativity and frequency support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the exact local rules that decide which Poisson frequencies survive and how square and nonsquare prime powers contribute, enabling later Euler-factor and support calculations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real-character large sieve and shifted L-moments control averaged errors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages character-sum and second/fourth-moment estimates that repeatedly convert long arithmetic expressions into controlled family averages.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation dualizes the square-free quadratic-character average
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the original discriminant average into a sum over dual integer frequencies weighted by Gauss sums, exposing a zero-frequency diagonal and structured nonzero frequencies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourth moments of the mollifier follow from square-sensitive character large sieve
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Repackages the squared mollifier coefficients, applies the real-character large sieve, and produces global and square-divisor-conditioned fourth-moment bounds used in both Propositions 2.1 and 2.2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A smoothed contour splits the mollifier error into near and Dirichlet-series pieces
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Writes the normalized mollified product as one plus an error, represents that error by a gamma-smoothed contour integral, shifts across the target value, and isolates a boundary piece controlled by L- and mollifier moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The mollifier's initial coefficient gap yields decay away from the center
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the mollified product in its convergence region, uses vanishing of coefficients below the designed threshold and on small squares, truncates exponentially, and applies the character large sieve to obtain the decisive shifted mean-square decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin inversion separates square principal terms and proves the zero-free boundary estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the first contour piece by Mellin inversion of square-free character averages, identifies a pole only when the index is a square, exploits the mollifier's square cancellation, and combines the estimates to keep the product nonzero on the right boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large square divisors are removed by moment bounds before main-term analysis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the support structure of the square-free remainder, repeated Cauchy inequalities, a shifted integral for the approximate-functional-equation sum, and fourth moments to bound the discarded large-square-divisor contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation splits the moment into zero-frequency principal and nonzero-frequency terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inserts the approximate functional equation into the truncated square-free average, applies Poisson summation termwise, and explicitly separates k equals zero from all nonzero dual frequencies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Square support turns the zero frequency into an Euler product and four residues
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the zero-frequency Gauss-sum rule to impose that l times n is a square, parametrizes that diagonal, Mellin-transforms its weight, factors the resulting series, and shifts contour to residues at plus/minus delta and plus/minus tau.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Square dual frequencies inside the nonzero modes create a secondary principal term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin-transforms the nonzero-frequency weight, factors its Gauss-sum Dirichlet series into two L-functions and a controlled Euler product, shifts contour, and observes that poles occur only when the dual frequency is a square.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local factor analysis continues the secondary term and controls truncation extension
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a Dirichlet series over square frequencies, factors it into zeta functions and a holomorphic local product, moves the Mellin line using that continuation, and extends the square-divisor cutoff to infinity with an explicit error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An even auxiliary integral collapses the secondary main term to residues
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the completed local product K, combines zeta and gamma functional equations into an even J-function, shifts from plus kappa to minus kappa, and uses evenness to express the integral entirely through residue data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decay plus character moments give individual and averaged off-diagonal control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: First bounds each remainder using transform decay and L-moments, then gains a dyadic-average improvement by Cauchy and a bilinear estimate, matching the error form required in Proposition 2.3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local Gauss support converts the bilinear remainder into a large-sieve sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves the second remainder bound by rewriting the transform, reducing to a mean square of the local Euler factor, characterizing when that factor vanishes, and reorganizing divisibility so the real-character large sieve applies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primary and secondary delta-poles cancel, leaving only tau main terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the two independently extracted principal contributions and observes exact cancellation of their plus/minus delta residues, yielding the regular four-term expression asserted earlier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The near-central moment is assembled with a tuned square-divisor cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses W through the exact paired-value sum, inserts the tail and main-term propositions, chooses Y to balance errors, and separates the surviving M1 and M2 residue families for tractable evaluation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Square-free mollifier pairs reorganize into a one-variable convolution of two factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites r and s by their common square-free part, factors the arithmetic weight multiplicatively, removes the coprimality condition by Möbius inversion, and groups by a single combined variable gamma so the two mollifier sums decouple.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-free-region contour evaluates polynomial mollifier convolutions uniformly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factors a generic mollifier convolution by two reciprocal zeta functions, uses the polynomial's double zero at the endpoint, shifts within a zeta zero-free region, and expresses the result as a local residue plus exponentially decaying error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The short gamma range collapses to a single tau pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the convolution lemma twice below the mollifier breakpoint, extends the gamma sum with controlled error, shows the apparent minus-tau pole is killed by reciprocal-zeta zeros, and evaluates the remaining pole through an Euler-product asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative data of the taper controls the long gamma contribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the convolution residue beyond the breakpoint, expands the local analytic factor, converts the gamma sum to an integral involving Q, Q-prime, and Q-double-prime, and uses contour residues plus integration by parts to obtain the explicit long-range term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The conjugate residue family completes the explicit near-central moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records the analogous M2 contribution and combines it with M1 to recover Proposition 2.4, including the second symmetry quotient in the final moment.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primitive factors and the local-scale zero-statistics question
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The article treats cuspidal GL_m L-functions as irreducible building blocks for general L-functions, then normalizes zero ordinates to unit mean spacing so that Poisson behavior can be contrasted with structured local statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GUE level repulsion as the target local law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Montgomery's pair correlation and Odlyzko's computations motivate the GUE spacing law, whose quadratic vanishing at zero encodes repulsion rather than Poisson independence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: n-level correlations as translation-invariant cluster statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source replaces consecutive-spacing questions by all n-level correlation functions and explains how symmetry, diagonal-translation invariance, and rapid decay make a test function count localized clusters of normalized zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GUE determinant density and the coefficient hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The sine-kernel determinant is the comparison density, while the square-summability condition on higher prime-power coefficients isolates the arithmetic assumption needed to make that universal target accessible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Restricted-support GUE correlation theorems
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 state the smoothed result without RH and the unsmoothed correlation result with RH, both under a Fourier-support restriction and with a universal GUE limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Support saturation, primitivity, and second-moment universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remarks separate three mechanisms: diagonal saturation at the Fourier boundary, failure of GUE for products through multiplicity or independent superposition, and universality across primitive L-functions arising from a common Rankin-Selberg second moment despite nonuniversal prime coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Proof architecture from zeros to primes to determinant cycles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The integrated explicit formula converts zero correlations to tractable prime sums, unique factorization selects diagonal pairings, and the pairing structure is matched to cycles in the GUE determinant by combinatorial identities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Principal local factors and Ramanujan-type parameter control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler product is organized uniformly across unramified and ramified primes through local parameters, then finite and archimedean bounds delimit the analytic region available to contour and coefficient arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation, nontrivial zeros, and the density scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Completion by the archimedean factor yields analytic continuation and a contragredient functional equation; its gamma factors determine the leading zero count and hence the normalization used in correlations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smooth explicit formula as a zeros-to-prime-coefficients bridge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The logarithmic derivative packages prime powers into coefficients c_pi(n), and contour shifting plus the functional equation expresses a smooth sum over zeros in terms of conductor/gamma contributions and Fourier-localized prime sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rankin-Selberg convolution as second-moment access
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The self-convolution encodes squared local coefficients, has a simple pole at one and a controlled completed functional equation, and supplies the analytic continuation and growth properties needed for Tauberian and contour arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universal coefficient mean square from the Rankin-Selberg pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating the Rankin-Selberg logarithmic derivative and applying Tauberian/contour arguments turns its simple pole into a universal quadratic-log asymptotic for the weighted mean square of c_pi(n), with a sharpened error under Hypothesis H.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Verification of Hypothesis H in degrees at most three
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Ordering the three Satake parameters, using determinant/contragredient symmetry, the global parameter bound, and Rankin-Selberg convergence controls every fixed higher prime power, proving the technical hypothesis for m <= 3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unrestricted smoothed correlations as the analytic surrogate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The distinct-index statistic is replaced temporarily by an unrestricted sum, smoothed at height T and Fourier represented; Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 predict a measure consisting exactly of disjoint pair contributions, with distinctness deferred to a later sieve.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Applying the explicit formula coordinatewise and localizing prime products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourier inversion lets the explicit formula act on each zero coordinate, expanding the correlation into signed prime-sum terms; compact Fourier support bounds individual prime powers and the total product below T^(2-delta).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplicative equality forced by Fourier support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Once neutral Fourier coordinates are truncated, the zero-sum constraint makes the logarithm of the ratio of the positive and negative prime products too small for two distinct integers of the allowed size, forcing exact diagonal equality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncation and off-diagonal suppression without a large sieve
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tail bounds for the gamma kernels, divisor-convolution estimates, dyadic decomposition, and Cauchy-Schwarz show that removing the truncated region and retaining unequal prime products contributes below the main T log T scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Evaluating diagonal integrals by rescaling and Parseval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After exact product matching, a change to localized Fourier variables freezes the test function at logarithmic prime coordinates; Parseval and Stirling evaluate the remaining gamma-kernel integral and expose the correct T and log powers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Only prime pairings survive at main order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Higher prime-power coincidences and unmatched numbers are bounded, while equal numbers with the same number of factors reduce by unique factorization to permutations of distinct primes; repeated use of the universal second moment then produces the disjoint-pair integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Fourier-support boundary is a method-sensitive saturation threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For zeta, the pole and nonnegative prime coefficients make the boundary where diagonal dominance fails visible; for higher degree, expected cancellation suggests a wider natural range than the proven 2/m range, while Dirichlet characters behave differently.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing smooth cutoffs and reconciling zero normalizations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH, approximation by admissible majorants/minorants extends the smooth limit to interval indicators, and a mean-value estimate shows that local log-gamma normalization agrees at main order with the initial unit-spacing normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partition-lattice Möbius sieve for distinct zero indices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Coincidence patterns of unrestricted index tuples are encoded as set partitions; embeddings identify lower-order correlations, and Möbius inversion subtracts every diagonal pattern to recover the distinct-index statistic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pushing correlation measures through partition embeddings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Delta constraints describe the Fourier subspace induced by each partition, allowing Theorem 3.2's pairing measure to be pushed forward and Möbius-combined; the remaining goal is precisely equality with the Fourier transform of the sine-kernel determinant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reducing the GUE identification to a subset identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Möbius side factors into subset functions X_S, the determinant Fourier transform factors into cycle-overlap functions Y_S, and equality reduces to a local identity for every zero-sum subset under the support bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Marked partitions and permutation cycles produce the two factorizations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Marking paired blocks makes the Möbius-side factorization explicit, while decomposing determinant permutations into disjoint cycles and applying Parseval yields the Fourier-side interval-overlap factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spitzer random-walk identity closes the arithmetic-to-GUE bridge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Cycle overlap is reinterpreted as one minus the range of a zero-sum walk; Spitzer's unique rotation below a chord and upper-convex-envelope decomposition count that range by set partitions, proving the subset identity needed for the GUE determinant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Langlands quotients organize general local factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A non-tempered generic local representation is decomposed into tempered blocks with ordered real parameters, tempered blocks into square-integrable constituents, and principal L-factors multiply along both stages.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: p-adic twist classes factor the self Rankin-Selberg local term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Square-integrable p-adic representations are built from supercuspidals, Rankin-Selberg factors vanish outside matching twist classes, and regrouping matched blocks into explicit positive-factor products locates the first pole and bounds local Langlands parameters below one half.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local factorization yields nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Taking logarithms of the twist-class product writes each relevant coefficient as sums of squared magnitudes, giving a lower bound that implies nonnegativity of the global Rankin-Selberg Dirichlet coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Archimedean factor classification and a global proof of the half-bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Real Langlands quotients reduce to characters and discrete series, whose gamma factors give the completed local term; comparing the first local pole with global Rankin-Selberg holomorphy proves the archimedean parameter half-bound and avoids a more complicated local classification proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Landau positivity sharpens finite-place parameter bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients plus meromorphic continuation let Landau's theorem bound coefficient growth; taking high powers isolates each local parameter and yields the exponent 1/2 minus 1/(m^2+1), with an analogous spherical archimedean estimate cited.

section_argument_map.label: 1. Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Frames primitive principal L-functions as building blocks, defines normalized zero correlations, states the restricted-support GUE results, and previews the explicit-formula/diagonal/combinatorial proof mechanism.

section_argument_map.label: 2. Background on L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds local and global L-function data, functional equations, the smooth explicit formula, Rankin-Selberg analytic input, coefficient mean-square asymptotics, and Hypothesis H.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Sums over primes
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Transforms smoothed unrestricted zero sums into prime sums, isolates multiplicative diagonals, suppresses off-diagonals, evaluates pairings, analyzes the support barrier, and removes smoothing under RH.

section_argument_map.label: 4. Combinatorial Sieving
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses partition-lattice Möbius inversion to restore distinct indices and proves that the resulting Fourier-side distribution is the GUE determinant via marked partitions, cycles, and Spitzer's walk identity.

section_argument_map.label: 5. Appendix
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Describes Langlands-quotient local factors at finite and archimedean places, derives Rankin-Selberg coefficient positivity, and proves finite-place and archimedean parameter bounds used in the main argument.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Nonuniversal prime-coefficient laws can yield universal local zero correlations because the diagonal main term retains only the Rankin-Selberg-controlled second moment and its induced pairings.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This explains the leading term in the proved restricted-support regime; it does not establish unrestricted universality or universality for nonprimitive products.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Universality through a compressed second moment

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The Fourier cutoff controls prime-product size and diagonal dominance; the source's own heuristics show that the proven 2/m range can reflect available off-diagonal control rather than the conjectured final law.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Primitivity is structurally aligned with a single GUE-type process: products create repeated or independently superposed zero sets, whereas a primitive factor's diagonal main term is internally paired through its own coefficients.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The superposition discussion is a natural conjectural interpretation, not a complete classification theorem for every nonprimitive L-function.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Primitivity prevents superposed zero processes

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Local representation structure makes Rankin-Selberg coefficients positive and locates local poles, while global continuation, holomorphy, and Landau estimates feed back to sharpen local parameter bounds used in the global prime-sum analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function spaces, dilation spans, and Mellin coordinates for the closure problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Establishes the shared language in which the criterion is posed: vanishing and compactly supported function classes, the fractional-part kernel, bounded dilations K_lambda, the generated space B(g), and the Mellin transform analytic on the critical strip under the stated Lp hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Muntz operator measures a sum-integral discrepancy and commutes with dilation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines P f as the difference between an extended sum of dilates and a scaled integral, then identifies dilation commutation as the structural property used to move generated spans through P and related operators.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The strong Nyman-Beurling criterion becomes a Muntz-generated closure problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the classical L2 closure equivalence, identifies direct Gramian computation as a stalled Hilbert-geometry route, uses P chi=-rho_1 to re-express the theorem, and formulates the search for kernels satisfying the analogous closure equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Strong kernels form a dilation-stable cone whose additive closure is unknown
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explores the generalized kernel family: step functions with zero-free Mellin transform provide examples, scalar multiplication and dilation preserve strength, addition is not known to do so, and this failure motivates restricting attention to a differentiable subspace with potentially tractable scalar products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted derivative control forces decay and all-Lp integrability of good kernels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the good-kernel class and proves from integration by parts that t f(t) tends to zero, ruling out a nonzero limiting constant by L1 integrability; this supplies the decay and integrability prerequisites used throughout the Muntz analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Good kernels yield universal necessity but only compact-support sufficiency with a Mellin zero condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the paper's central asymmetry: RH sends every good kernel into the closure of dilates of P f, while compactly supported good kernels satisfying that closure can only force zeta zeros in the right half of the strip to be zeros of f-hat; a zero-free f-hat upgrades this to an equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Burnol's weighted sum bound makes the Muntz series well defined almost everywhere
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses two monotone-convergence rearrangements and a counting-function bound to control the sum of |f(nx)| with dx/x, yielding almost-everywhere existence and local integrability of P f for good kernels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Multiplicative convolution imports Young's inequality and factors every good kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the invariant operator T_F, proves its Lp norm bound by rewriting it as ordinary convolution on the multiplicative group with Haar measure dt/t, and records f=-T_{f'} chi, the identity later used to transfer Nyman-Beurling approximants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: P f is pseudo-convolution of f-prime with rho_1, with an Lp bound and a sharp endpoint warning
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives an alternative definition P f=T_{f'}rho_1, derives Lp control for p>1, explains why P is not continuous in the ordinary Lp norm because the derivative remains exposed, and identifies rho_1 not in L1 as the endpoint obstruction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integration by parts and Burnol convergence identify the sum-integral operator with pseudo-convolution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands T_{f'}rho_1 through P chi, controls the integral term using t f(t) to zero, converts the indicator sum into truncated samples f(nx), invokes Burnol's lemma for absolute convergence, and recovers the defining sum-integral expression for P f.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Muntz's formula turns P into multiplication by zeta under the Mellin transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the transform identity (P f)-hat=zeta times f-hat, shows that the nonsmooth characteristic kernel already realizes the proto-Muntz formula, and links this identity to the functional equation and Nyman-Beurling criteria before extending it to all good kernels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pseudo-convolution factorization proves Muntz's formula with an explicit Fubini certificate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes P f=T_{f'}rho_1 into the Mellin integral, separates variables using the proto-Muntz identity, integrates by parts to obtain f-hat, and repeats the calculation with absolute values to justify the interchange for every point in the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The necessity route tests RH without requiring a nonvanishing kernel Mellin transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The author frames the generalized necessity condition as a possible disproof test using analytically tractable kernels and stresses that, unlike the earlier proof for chi, it requires no Mellin-transform condition on the chosen kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A bounded dilation-invariant operator transports classical approximants to every good kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starts from RH-conditioned approximants to -chi in B(rho_1), applies T_{f'} to them, uses commutation with dilations and P f=T_{f'}rho_1 to land in B(P f), and uses f=-T_{f'}chi plus L2 boundedness to preserve convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compact support blocks analytic kernels, while the expected Lp extension lacks matching necessity theory
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies removal of compact support as the immediate open improvement needed to admit analytically promising kernels, and records the expected Lp half-plane analogue together with the precise reason it is not claimed: neither necessity direction has been worked out in that setting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean cancellation and compact support convert L2 closure into pointwise Mellin vanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At a zeta zero in the right half of the strip, applies V=I-2K_2 to the approximating family, creating a compactly supported mean-zero F whose P F and generated approximants vanish beyond a common bound; Muntz's formula kills their Mellin values, and Cauchy-Schwarz on the bounded interval passes the zero to F-hat and hence f-hat.
