result_and_mechanism_map.title: Heat-deformed entire functions and the threshold constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Fourier-cosine family H_t converts the real-zero question into a monotone parameter threshold: all zeros are real exactly at and above the de Bruijn–Newman constant, while the Riemann Hypothesis is the assertion that the t=0 member lies on the real-zero side. This supplies the parameter geometry used by every later collision argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Laguerre–Pólya membership and zero-product representation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper recasts the real-zero threshold as membership in the Laguerre–Pólya class and represents each H_t by a Hadamard product over square-summable reciprocal zeros. This bridges a global zero-location property to local derivative inequalities and convergent zero interactions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lehmer pairs require a close gap relative to the entire zero environment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The definition improves on a raw close-pair heuristic: a consecutive simple gap is qualified only when its squared size is small relative to a convergent sum measuring interaction with all other zeros. The discussion explicitly explains that arbitrarily small gaps alone do not suffice.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Lehmer pair yields an explicit lower bound and an infinite cascade forces nonnegative threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The main statement maps a local pair statistic to a source-defined negative lower bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant, handles the case of a negative environmental sum by forcing nonreal zeros at t=0, and shows that infinitely many increasingly close Lehmer pairs would force the threshold to be nonnegative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local zero velocity predicts pair collision under backward heat flow
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Implicit differentiation gives a local velocity for a simple real zero in terms of derivatives of H_t. For two close zeros separated from their neighbors, derivative signs make them approach as t decreases, motivating collision time as a lower-bound witness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A multiple real zero cannot occur above the threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A coalesced zero at parameter t_0 implies t_0 is at or below the de Bruijn–Newman threshold. The proof perturbs backward in heat time and violates a necessary Laguerre inequality; higher multiplicity is reduced by differentiation and closure of the Laguerre–Pólya class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Forward perturbation splits a double zero and all above-threshold zeros are simple
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The local expansions show that a double real zero with nonzero second derivative splits into two simple real zeros for a small forward parameter change. Coupled with threshold membership, this yields the global simplicity statement for every t above the threshold.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero motion as an inverse-square interaction and a gap ODE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring out a simple zero and differentiating the Hadamard product replaces direct evaluation of H_t derivatives by a convergent sum over all other zeros. Subtracting velocities produces an ODE for a neighboring gap with a singular attraction term plus a positive environmental correction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The environmental interaction obeys a Riccati-type lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating the comparison sum and reorganizing single and double interactions isolates a nonnegative remainder, producing a lower differential bound for g_k. Integration then gives the upper control needed on the backward interval toward collision.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrating the squared-gap equation forces the threshold lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming the threshold lies below the pair-derived bound keeps both zeros real and simple throughout an interval. An integrating factor and the environmental estimate then force the squared gap to become negative at the proposed endpoint, contradicting simplicity and proving the lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infinitely many shrinking Lehmer gaps force a nonnegative threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The pair-derived lower bound is rewritten using the dimensionless product of squared gap and environmental term. Monotonicity shows the bound tends to zero exactly when the certified gaps do, so a sequence of lower bounds approaching zero forces the threshold to be nonnegative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A moment ratio fixes the total reciprocal-square zero mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Comparing the Hadamard product with the Taylor expansion expresses the total reciprocal-square sum over zeros through low-order moments of the Fourier kernel, allowing a rigorously controlled global constant to enter later tail estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite zero sums can be completed by an explicit tail bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The full environmental interaction g_k(0) is decomposed into a finite partial sum and a remainder. Evenness, zero ordering, reciprocal-square mass, and a bound on possible imaginary parts control the omitted tail and prove convergence, creating a reusable numerical certification pattern.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The historic Lehmer pair is certified and converted into a threshold bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A close pair whose neighboring zeros are relatively distant is tested by summing 14,999 zero contributions and bounding the remainder with the global reciprocal-square constant. The resulting strict Lehmer inequality feeds Theorem 1 to produce a numerical lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The pair-derived bound is dominated by the squared gap
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Order-of-magnitude changes to the upper estimate for the environmental term barely affect the first significant digits of the threshold bound. A series expansion explains this stability: the leading contribution depends on minus one eighth of the squared gap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Record-small consecutive gaps prioritize candidate Lehmer pairs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Among record-setting consecutive zero gaps, early entries need not satisfy the stronger Lehmer condition, but the dominance of the squared-gap term makes the smallest available gap a rational candidate for the best lower bound. This distinguishes candidate retrieval from certification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A high-index pair is certified by a local window plus two tail controls
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The environmental sum for the selected high pair is partitioned into 5,000 nearby zeros on each side, a finite remote block, and the far tail. Crude but explicit bounds on both omitted regions suffice to establish the strict Lehmer inequality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A much smaller certified gap sharpens the lower bound and motivates an infinite-pair route
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the general theorem to the high-index certificate yields the paper's sharper numerical lower bound. result_and_mechanism_map.title: Xi as an entire completion with reflection symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage relates zeta's nonreal-zero problem to an entire function: the added factors cancel the pole and real zeros, so xi retains precisely the nonreal zeta zeros, while xi(1-s)=xi(s) supplies the symmetry used later.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free half-planes force horizontal monotonicity of xi modulus
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem converts absence of xi zeros in an open right or left half-plane into strict increase or decrease of modulus on every contained horizontal half-line, with the region outside the critical strip given as an immediate instance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as two-sided horizontal monotonicity about the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The corollary gives an operational equivalence: strict horizontal monotonicity on either side excludes zeros there, and the functional equation supplies the reflected side; conversely RH makes both open half-planes zero-free so the theorem applies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduce monotonicity to factors in the Hadamard product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof reduces the left-half-plane statement by the functional equation, fixes a horizontal line inside a zero-free right half-plane, and changes representation to xi's Hadamard product, isolating the negative real exponential constant B from zero-indexed factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero exclusion turns each linear factor into increasing distance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because every zero lies on or left of the half-plane boundary while the moving point stays to its right, horizontal motion increases its distance from each zero and hence increases the modulus of each linear Hadamard factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard exponential factors are non-decreasing along the half-line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Writing a zero as beta+i gamma makes the modulus exponent affine in the horizontal coordinate with nonnegative coefficient beta, so each exponential zero factor is non-decreasing; strict increase is noted as unnecessary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regroup the negative exponential prefactor through zero partial sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The sole obstruction is the decreasing factor from B<0. An alternate series for -B yields partial sums S_N with -(B+S_N)>0 tending to zero; combining exponential factors then rewrites xi as a finite zero product, an infinite increasing tail, and a residual factor whose decay can be made arbitrarily small.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A vanishing residual decay yields strict local growth at every point
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After the finite and infinite zero products are known to increase, the remaining factor f_N has positive derivative when a positive distance ratio exceeds -(B+S_N). At any chosen point, zero exclusion makes that ratio positive and the residual tends to zero, so some N gives positivity on a neighborhood; arbitrariness of the point and horizontal line proves the theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The first lower-order Ratios term appears only when support reaches frequency one

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Perron representation identifies the universal residue and zeta logarithmic derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the prime-power sum through Perron’s formula, shifts to a contour indented around the zeta pole, extracts the half-residue g(0)/2, and identifies the remaining integral with the zeta logarithmic derivative after rescaling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime divisibility frequencies become the derivative of the arithmetic Euler factor

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothing prepares long quadratic-character sums for Poisson shortening

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squarefree decomposition and Poisson summation turn the odd sum into a balanced error budget

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A dyadic partition transfers interval-family bounds to the initial segment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how a result for discriminants in (X,2X] extends to (0,X] without changing the decisive support condition: rescale interval-dependent parameters, retain the global normalization and test-function scale, and sum only error terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation and contour shifting derive the zero-to-prime-powers identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the completed quadratic Dirichlet L-function, extends the test function using compact Fourier support, shifts a logarithmic-derivative contour across zeros, uses functional-equation symmetry, and expands L′/L into prime powers to obtain the family explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius inversion counts fundamental discriminants and their prime-divisible subfamilies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the family size with square-root error, modifies the count under p|d, and obtains the local proportion 1/(p+1), including a separate explanation for p=2. These counts justify the arithmetic correction in the even contribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial summation evaluates the oscillatory conductor average uniformly on shifted contours
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the discriminant counting asymptotic inside partial summation to replace a conductor phase average by an explicit rational factor with logarithmic error, uniformly when the contour has sufficient imaginary shift.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Splitting the Poisson dual variable saves the missing smoothing power
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Repairs an insufficient nonsquare-frequency bound by splitting the dual variable at a very large cutoff, using a second-derivative transform bound for the finite range and a third-derivative bound for the tail. The recombined estimate saves a power of the smoothing parameter and closes the Poisson error budget.

Its reusable insight is that a structurally correct final answer may arise from a deliberately incomplete detector only through conjectured cancellations that remain unexplained.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primitive L-function structure, Z-normalization, log conductor, and approximate functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This span assembles the semantic invariants later reused by every moment calculation: analytic continuation, functional-equation symmetry, Euler-product locality, primitive factorization, the critical point, zero density, a derivative-defined log conductor, and a two-piece approximate functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Characteristic-polynomial dictionary and conductor matching
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The characteristic polynomial mirrors Dirichlet expansion, functional equation, critical locus, zero density, critical value, conductor, and a two-piece coefficient decomposition. Matching matrix size to L-function log conductor gives a concrete representation bridge, while the missing Euler product isolates arithmetic information.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moment-polynomial degree laws across unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The examples expose a stable structural classification: moment degrees k squared, k(k+1)/2, and k(k-1)/2 accompany unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families, with leading coefficients split into arithmetic and compact-group factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted moments expose structure and regularize coincident poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing an unshifted power by a product at independently shifted arguments makes the full mean-value structure visible and allows the original moment to be recovered by coalescing shifts. The same deformation has direct compact-group analogues.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Full unitary moment conjecture as arithmetic deformation of an exact matrix integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The contour-residue formula isolates matching pole geometry in zeta factors and characteristic-polynomial averages, with an additional analytic Euler product carrying arithmetic. Vandermonde cancellation explains polynomial degree, and equating zero densities explains the matrix-size/log-conductor substitution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symplectic shifted moments and the refined conductor hidden in gamma factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The quadratic-character conjecture and symplectic matrix theorem share sign-sum/contour structure. Re-expanding the functional-equation factor yields a refined conductor for which the first three leading polynomial terms become independent of residual gamma corrections, showing how a representation choice reorganizes lower-order terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orthogonal cusp-form moments, root-number sectors, and conductor normalization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The cusp-form conjecture pairs with SO and negative-determinant orthogonal averages, and the discussion shows how the functional-equation factor can be written as an exponential in a refined conductor times a cubic-order correction. Separate root-number sectors change the sign-weighted contour sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second-moment calibration and a residual constant beyond the integrated main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The k=1 residue recovers Ingham's shifted and unshifted second moment, while exponential smoothing leaves an explicit constant after subtracting the integrated conjectural main expression. This distinguishes asymptotic main-term agreement from exact finite residual behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Motohashi's fourth-moment decomposition matches the recipe's six balanced terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An exact spectral formula decomposes the shifted fourth moment into a residual main term plus discrete, continuous, and holomorphic spectral pieces. After gamma-ratio asymptotics, its six residual terms match the recipe's balanced permutation terms, and a two-contour reformulation suggests nonminimality of the general four-contour representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Six-step t-aspect moment recipe with explicit non-rigorous failure modes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The procedure expands shifted approximate functional equations, retains nonoscillatory balanced terms, keeps diagonals, completes sums, and conjectures equality of averages. Crucially, the authors say the steps can discard and add terms of main-term size and are not individually justifiable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Balanced phase selection produces the zeta permutation sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the shifted zeta product, Stirling phase analysis keeps exactly terms with equal numbers of opposing functional-equation factors. Diagonal extraction defines a multiple Dirichlet series, and symmetry compresses the survivors into choices of k shifts or ordered block permutations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transfer from zeta to a general primitive L-function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under stated local-factor and gamma-factor assumptions, Stirling asymptotics again force an equal split between the two approximate-functional-equation pieces. The same diagonal and permutation architecture survives, with degree and gamma data entering only through the scale factor and arithmetic coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal Dirichlet series separates into universal zeta poles and an analytic arithmetic factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplicativity converts the constrained diagonal sum to an Euler product. Fourier integration enforces equality of exponent totals locally, the first-order local terms identify a product of zeta poles, and the remainder is analytic near the critical point, separating universal singular geometry from source-specific arithmetic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour residues regularize singular permutation and sign sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The lemmas turn sums over block permutations or all sign choices into Vandermonde-weighted contour integrals. Although individual summands have poles, the contour representation makes their cancellation and the regularity of the total transparent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit arithmetic factors, low-moment zeta products, and local polynomial symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Residue evaluation gives closed local factors for degree-one Euler factors, identifies simple formulas for the first low moments, and marks a structural boundary: for k at least three the arithmetic factor cannot be a finite product of zeta-functions. A reversal symmetry shows each local factor is polynomial in both positive and negative shift monomials.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recovering the arithmetic leading constant from the full-moment Euler product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Scaling the contour variables isolates the highest power of log height. Evaluating the arithmetic factor at zero and reducing its local integral by residues and binomial identities reproduces the independently conjectured arithmetic constant a_k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recovering the random-matrix combinatorial constant by determinant transformations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding Vandermonde determinants, exploiting block symmetry, converting contour coefficients to gamma reciprocals, and applying triangular determinant transformations reduces the remaining leading coefficient to the Keating-Snaith product g_k.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Families as conductor-ordered coefficient systems with multiplicative expectations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A family is abstracted as arithmetic coefficient functions whose twists are primitive L-functions, ordered by a refined conductor, with limiting coefficient expectations required to exist and be multiplicative. This converts averaging into an Euler-product-producing orthogonality operator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: t-twist and primitive-character averages collapse to exact diagonals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Continuous phase averaging yields equality of products as the surviving diagonal. Primitive-character averaging initially gives congruence modulo q, but with fixed inputs and q tending to infinity only exact equality persists, with a ramification coprimality condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-character orthogonality in restricted discriminant progressions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The average of a quadratic character vanishes unless the argument is a square up to primes constrained by the modulus, and the nonzero value is a product of local density corrections. Counting fundamental discriminants in progressions explains how sign, powers of two, common factors, and coprimality alter the local weights.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Petersson weighting changes newform orthogonality and simplifies the moment detector
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hecke relations reduce products of eigenvalues to linear combinations. Unweighted and Petersson-weighted family averages select different coefficients; under Petersson weighting only the identity coefficient survives, and prime-power expectations become a Chebyshev/Sato-Tate integral whose multiplicativity feeds the Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Building L-function families by Rankin-Selberg twisting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A fixed primitive L-function is convolved locally with a family of character Euler factors, producing twisted coefficients and a required functional equation. Monotonic gamma data and separate treatment of finitely different archimedean types ensure that the resulting collection is coherent under conductor ordering.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: General family moment recipe and root-number symmetry selector
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The t-aspect recipe is lifted to arbitrary families: expand two-piece functional equations, average root-number products, average coefficients, and complete sums. Expected root-number phases select balanced subsets differently for unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic families, while multiplicative coefficient expectations supply the surviving arithmetic series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From multiplicative family averages to symmetry-revealing polar products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplicativity turns the completed average into local series. The first nonzero degree-two local terms determine whether zeta poles range over strict pairs or include diagonal pairs, leaving an analytic remainder and exposing the orthogonal-versus-symplectic degree pattern.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: t-aspect moments are a unitary family average
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Viewing n to the negative it as a character identifies a single L-function along the critical line with a family of twists. Averaging root-number phases becomes the nonoscillation rule, and averaging coefficients becomes diagonal selection, unifying the earlier recipe with the general family formalism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primitive Dirichlet families inherit the unitary moment architecture with ramified-prime repairs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uniform root-number phases select balanced terms, while character orthogonality imposes product equality and coprimality to q. The resulting formulas match t-aspect unitary moments after omitting ramified Euler factors and retaining the appropriate archimedean X-factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-twist symmetry is detected by the pole of the symmetric-square channel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quadratic-character averaging forces products to be squares up to controlled ramified factors. Local expansion then always gives pairwise poles, while an additional diagonal pole appears precisely when the symmetric-square-type prime coefficient series has a pole; strict-pair poles yield orthogonal symmetry and diagonal-inclusive poles yield symplectic symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orthogonal cusp-form moments from Petersson averages and root-number parity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For newform L-functions, random root-number signs keep only parity-compatible approximate-functional-equation terms, and Petersson-weighted coefficient averages produce the arithmetic Euler product. Sign-restricted sums then separate even and odd subfamilies and contour compression recovers the stated orthogonal conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Full zeta polynomials show lower-order dominance at accessible heights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explicit and numerical moment polynomials reveal that leading coefficients can be far smaller than lower-order coefficients and that coefficient signs eventually vary. Sharp-block and exponential-weight comparisons agree closely with the full polynomial, illustrating why leading-order-only validation would be misleading.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-family checks separate discriminant signs and expose rare-value skew
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moment polynomials are computed separately for positive and negative discriminants and compared under a frozen smooth cutoff. Similar fluctuations across moment orders are traced to rare large central values whose influence grows with k, identifying a concrete heavy-tail confound in moment validation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orthogonal GL(2) twist test via a half-integral-weight modular form
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the conductor-11 elliptic-curve L-function, residue classes select twists with even functional equation, the conjecture supplies a degree k(k-1)/2 moment polynomial, and a Kohnen-Zagier relation converts central values into squared coefficients of an explicit weight-3/2 form, enabling a large exact-data comparison.

section_argument_map.label: Front matter, abstract, and contents
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the full-main-term objective, the unitary/orthogonal/symplectic comparison, and the numerical-validation claim; the remainder is navigational front matter.

section_argument_map.label: 1. Introduction and Statement of Results
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Motivates full moment polynomials and isolates the central heuristic tension between diagonal input and uncomputed off-diagonal cancellation.

section_argument_map.label: 1.1. Properties of L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines the analytic, functional-equation, Euler-product, critical-line, conductor, and approximate-functional-equation structures used by the recipe.

section_argument_map.label: 1.2. Properties of characteristic polynomials
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds a representation-by-representation dictionary from L-functions to unitary characteristic polynomials and identifies matrix size with log conductor or local zero density.

section_argument_map.label: 1.3. Example families and moments of L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Classifies unitary, symplectic, and orthogonal families and exhibits their distinct moment-polynomial degree laws and arithmetic/geometric leading factors.

section_argument_map.label: 1.4. Shifted moments
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces shifted L/Z products and their random-matrix analogues as the representation in which pole structure and full moments become visible.

section_argument_map.label: 1.5. Main results and example conjectures
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Pairs full shifted L-function conjectures with exact compact-group formulas, using contour residues, Vandermonde factors, arithmetic Euler products, and refined conductors.

section_argument_map.label: 1.6. Second moment of the Riemann zeta-function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Checks the recipe against Ingham's shifted second moment and exposes a nonvanishing residual constant under exponential smoothing.

section_argument_map.label: 1.7. Fourth moment of the Riemann zeta-function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Matches the recipe's six shifted terms to Motohashi's residual main term and notes a lower-dimensional contour representation.

section_argument_map.label: 2 and 2.1. Moments in t-aspect and the recipe
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the six-step t-aspect recipe and explicitly records that discarded and restored main-sized terms are conjectured to cancel.

section_argument_map.label: 2.2. Moments of the Riemann zeta-function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives nonoscillatory selection, diagonal extraction, the shifted Dirichlet series, and the permutation sum for zeta moments.

section_argument_map.label: 2.3. Moments of a primitive L-function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Transfers the zeta derivation to a general primitive L-function by Stirling analysis of functional-equation factors.

section_argument_map.label: 2.4. The arithmetic factor in the conjectures
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Factors the diagonal multiple Dirichlet series into its leading zeta poles and an analytic arithmetic Euler product.

section_argument_map.label: 2.5. Concise form of permutation sums
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves residue identities that compress singular permutation or sign sums into regular contour integrals and applies them to the general conjecture.

section_argument_map.label: 2.6. Explicit versions of the arithmetic factor
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Computes local arithmetic factors, shows the finite-zeta-product boundary at low moments, and establishes polynomial symmetry of local factors.

section_argument_map.label: 2.7. Recovering the leading order for moments of zeta
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Recovers separately the arithmetic constant and random-matrix combinatorial constant in the previously conjectured leading coefficient.

section_argument_map.label: 3 and 3.1. Families of primitive characters
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines families through conductor ordering and multiplicative coefficient expectations, then derives orthogonality laws for t-twists, Dirichlet characters, quadratic characters, and newforms.

section_argument_map.label: 3.2. Families of L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Constructs L-function families by Rankin-Selberg twisting and records the functional-equation regularity needed for a coherent family average.

section_argument_map.label: 4 and 4.1. General family recipe
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Generalizes the moment recipe to discrete families, with root-number expectations selecting terms and multiplicative coefficient averages producing Euler products and polar parts.

section_argument_map.label: 4.2. Unitary moments of a primitive L-function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Shows t-aspect moments are a special case of the family formalism: phase averaging selects balanced terms and coefficient averaging selects diagonals.

section_argument_map.label: 4.3. Unitary family of primitive Dirichlet L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives the unitary family analogue, with equality rather than congruence surviving in the limiting orthogonality relation and ramified primes omitted.

section_argument_map.label: 4.4. Quadratic twists of a real L-function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives quadratic-twist moment terms and distinguishes symplectic from orthogonal symmetry by whether diagonal local coefficients contribute extra square factors and poles.

section_argument_map.label: 4.5. Cusp-form L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses Petersson-weighted coefficient averages and root-number parity to conjecture orthogonal moments, including separate even/odd subfamilies.

section_argument_map.label: 5 and 5.1. Numerical zeta calculations
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Computes full zeta moment polynomials and compares sharp and smoothed moments, demonstrating substantial lower-order contributions.

section_argument_map.label: 5.2. Quadratic Dirichlet calculations
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Tests symplectic moment polynomials for both discriminant signs and explains shared fluctuations through rare large central values.

section_argument_map.label: 5.3. Orthogonal GL(2) twists
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Instantiates the orthogonal conjecture for conductor-11 elliptic-curve twists and uses a half-integral-weight modular-form identity as a computational bridge for central values.

section_argument_map.label: References, coefficient tables, and extracted figures
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Provides bibliography and numerical evidence tables; the final figure coordinate text is extraction-defective but its captions preserve the intended comparison.

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The matrix correspondence is heuristic on the L-function side, and exact conductor normalizations are family-specific.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Log conductor as the invariant bridge between analytic and matrix representations

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Independent shifts avoid coincident higher-order poles, label the balanced functional-equation choices, expose singular factors, and permit contour identities whose regular coalescing limit recovers the unshifted moment.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Analytic continuation and cancellation justify the representation only formally within the conjectural recipe; coalescing limits need exact pole control.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Shifts turn singular moment powers into a tractable deformation calculus

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Phase or root-number averaging selects balanced approximate-functional-equation pieces and coefficient averaging selects diagonals, producing the observed compact formula even though rigorous analyses contain main-sized off-diagonal terms; the recipe therefore encodes a structural cancellation conjecture, not a proof heuristic.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Agreement in known cases and numerics does not identify or prove the missing cancellation mechanism.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: A deliberately lossy detector can predict a full answer only through a cancellation hypothesis

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The analytic remainder and prime-coefficient bounds rely on stated or conjectural assumptions, and higher-moment arithmetic factors no longer reduce to finite zeta products.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Universal pole geometry and arithmetic local data are separable layers

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Root-number distributions determine which functional-equation pieces survive, while coefficient orthogonality determines whether polar factors run over strict pairs or include diagonal pairs; together these mechanisms produce unitary, orthogonal, or symplectic moment geometry.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The paper's family definition and coefficient expectations are restrictive, and exceptional symmetric-square poles or changed averaging weights can alter the classification.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Family symmetry is an output of averaging laws, not merely a root-number label

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: At accessible conductors the leading coefficient can be much smaller than lower-order coefficients, smoothing can reveal residual constants, and rare large central values can dominate high moments, so validation must compare the full source-specific polynomial under a declared weighting and range.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The reported numerical agreement is not proof, coefficient precision degrades in harder families, and famous examples may reflect preexisting arithmetic familiarity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robin inequality, RH criterion, and the finite exception baseline
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the central inequality and set R, records Robin's equivalence threshold and infinite-failure consequence, and identifies the checked exceptions below 5041 that anchor later reductions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squarefree and odd subfamilies reduce the RH check to even non-squarefree integers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 1 and 2 eliminate all but small exceptions in two broad families, and Theorem 3 converts them into a lower-density conditional test class for Robin's criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squarefull and 5-free exclusions yield a fifth-power formulation of Robin's criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 4 and 5 eliminate squarefull and 5-free candidates, while Theorem 6 packages the result as an RH-equivalent test on integers divisible by a prime fifth power and contrasts it with Lagarias's harmonic formulation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elementary reciprocal-prime estimate sufficient for the squarefree proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 1 supplies a deliberately elementary upper bound for the reciprocal-prime sum, with an explicit computation-to-asymptotic cutoff that later closes the small-largest-prime case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adjoining a sufficiently large prime repairs the finite Robin exceptions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 2 and its corollary turn finitely checked seed values into an infinite closure step by monotonicity in the adjoined prime, isolating three exceptional products at q=7.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squarefree induction split by the largest prime relative to log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof of Theorem 1 uses two complementary mechanisms: induction transfers Robin's inequality when the largest prime is large, while the reciprocal-prime bound controls the product when that prime is below log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Totient strengthening and squarefree-kernel invariance prove the odd case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 7 replaces the divisor ratio by the stronger n/phi(n) bound, observes that this ratio depends only on the squarefree kernel, and compares an odd squarefree n to a smaller even squarefree n1 so Theorem 1 and a finite fallback apply.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primorial totient behavior blocks extension of the odd-number strengthening
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explicitly tests its proof route against even integers and uses the RH-dependent sign behavior of n/phi(n) on primorials to show that Theorem 7's stronger inequality cannot supply such an extension.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squarefull violations have bounded prime support and size
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Rosser-Schoenfeld product bound forces at most four distinct prime factors for a squarefull totient violation, which then bounds n and reduces Theorem 8 to finite verification; the a^2 b^3 representation supplies an enumeration method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Limsup constants across unrestricted, squarefree, odd, and squarefull families
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 9 compares how structural restrictions change the maximal normalized divisor and totient ratios, and identifies Mertens's product asymptotic as the shared analytic input.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: t-free limsup via large-prime suppression and a matching prime-power construction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 6 proves the upper bound by separating primes above log n and truncating the Euler product, then proves sharpness on products of primes with exponent t-1 using Mertens and the prime number theorem; it also gives the odd analogue.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robin counterexamples would require unbounded prime exponents
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combining Robin's infinite-counterexample consequence under false RH with the fixed-t limsup bound shows that the maximum exponent along such counterexamples must tend to infinity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The ratio landscape follows by varying t and choosing squarefull extremizers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof of Theorem 9 derives unrestricted, squarefree, and odd constants as limits or special cases of Lemma 6, and realizes the squarefull lower bounds with uniform prime-power products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Testing Hardy-Ramanujan integers suffices up to any finite bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 1 states a sparse canonical test set for Robin's inequality and quantifies its asymptotic count, setting up a representation-level reduction rather than a new criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Swapping exponents favors larger powers on smaller primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Monotonicity of a rational function yields Lemma 8's exchange inequality, the local move that orders exponent assignments to maximize sigma(n)/n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponent patterns map every possible violation to a least canonical representative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source defines exponent patterns and m(e-bar), proves that this smallest Hardy-Ramanujan representative maximizes sigma(n)/n within the pattern, and transfers any Robin failure to that representative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A least t-free counterexample must have largest prime below log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 11 removes a largest prime factor, uses minimality and the finite exception structure to force the remainder into R, then shows q at least log n would preserve Robin's inequality by submultiplicativity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded Hardy-Ramanujan verification for 5-free candidates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 12 records the finite enumeration and verification counts for 5-free canonical integers with largest prime at most 73 and also gives an alternative route using a prior lower bound on counterexamples.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-product tail estimates used to bound 5-free divisor ratios
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemmas 13 and 14 state the explicit truncated-product and tail bounds that convert a largest-prime restriction into a numerical cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tail control plus the explicit prime-product estimate proves the truncation bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source factors the truncated t-free Euler product into the zeta value and tail, applies Lemma 14, and combines the result with Lemma 4 to obtain Lemma 13.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cascading numerical bounds reduce a 5-free counterexample to largest prime at most 73
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 15 repeatedly feeds an upper bound for the truncated Euler product back into a bound on log m, shrinking the admissible prime cutoff from 193 through a finite cascade to 73.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Minimality, canonicalization, and finite verification prove all 5-free integers satisfy Robin
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 5 assembles Lemmas 11, 15, 10, and 12: a least counterexample has small largest prime, must equal its canonical exponent-pattern representative except for a separately bounded case, and both routes contradict its failure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The proof method does not presently extend from 5-free to 6-free integers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors identify substantial computational cost as the barrier to the immediate extension and point to a different, less self-contained proposed approach as future work.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic resonance produces the lower-order density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates uniform distribution from its first systematic lower-order correction: g_alpha vanishes except when alpha is a rational multiple of log p/(2 pi), where an Euler-prime resonance creates a periodic bias. Conjecture 1 sharpens the smooth-test-function result to interval indicators.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discrepancy as the sharp manifestation of the bias
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the density correction into a supremal interval discrepancy and distinguishes a conjectured asymptotic from unconditional lower and RH-conditional upper information. This is the target sharp statistic to which later smoothing arguments return.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential-sum cancellation is the central sharpness criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies sums of x^{i gamma} over zeros as the Fourier data controlling interval counts. Under RH, uniform o(T) cancellation on a specified x-range implies both sharp distribution conjectures; the Landau formula also explains why prime-power resonance governs small x and why unconditional control survives only in a narrower range.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short-interval prime fluctuations and zero-sum cancellation constrain each other
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 gives a two-way, though quantitatively asymmetric, bridge: sufficiently small prime-counting errors in short intervals imply the zero exponential-sum conjecture, while that conjecture forces a weaker short-interval estimate. The normal-fluctuation heuristic supplies scale context without being used as proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Strong pair correlation implies the needed exponential cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the weighted pair-correlation statistic and makes a strengthened, error-sensitive pair-correlation conjecture sufficient for Conjecture 3 and hence sharp fractional-part distribution. The comparison with Montgomery and Chan clarifies that main-term asymptotics alone are not enough for this use.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mollification transfers a smooth bias law into a sharp discrepancy lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Convolves an extremizing interval indicator with a narrow smooth nonnegative kernel, applies the established smooth asymptotic, and uses boundedness of g_alpha plus averaging to recover a nearby interval with the desired discrepancy. This is a reusable smooth-to-sharp lower-bound move.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extremal trigonometric brackets isolate resonance and control the unresolved Fourier tail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Majorizes and minorizes an interval indicator by optimal degree-J trigonometric polynomials, evaluates low Fourier modes through Landau's formula, isolates exactly the prime-power resonant modes as the g_alpha term, and leaves high modes to Conjecture 3. Choosing the cutoff differently yields the RH bound or the conjectural asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A band-limited interval cutoff converts zero sums into local prime variation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a Beurling-Selberg-type approximation to an interval with compact Fourier support, controls its endpoint error, then uses Fourier inversion, integration by parts, and the explicit formula to bound the zero exponential sum by the maximum local variation of G(x)=psi(x)-x. This supplies the forward half of the prime-to-zero bridge.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial summation sends zero-sum cancellation back to short-interval primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starts from the explicit formula for psi(x+y)-psi(x)-y, uses Conjecture 3 and partial summation for medium and large zero ordinates, and bounds small zeros directly. It demonstrates how a spectral cancellation statement becomes an arithmetic local-error estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair-correlation second differences control a first-moment zero sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a beta-smoothed pair-correlation statistic, bounds the linear exponential sum by its quadratic energy, and rewrites that energy as an exponentially weighted average of D(xe^u,t)-D(x,t). Symmetrization reveals that small multiplicative second differences of normalized pair correlation are the operative regularity signal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg-class transfer isolates degree and zero-density assumptions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specifies the analytic continuation, functional equation, Euler product, coefficient growth, intrinsic degree, zero-counting law, primitivity, RH_F, and a weaker zero-density hypothesis. These are precisely the structural inputs used to generalize the zeta mechanisms without conflating full RH with the weaker hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: General Euler coefficients determine the fractional-part bias for L-functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Generalizes Landau's formula with Lambda_F and uses it, together with the zero-density hypothesis, to define g_{F,alpha} and prove the smooth-test-function distribution law. It shows that the same resonance mechanism survives, with its shape now carrying local Euler-factor data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-factor phase predicts translated shortages of Dirichlet zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the generalized density to a Dirichlet character and interprets its complex phase as the location of shortages among fractional parts. The finite-height histograms are framed as an illustration of this analytic prediction rather than evidence establishing the asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sharp distribution and discrepancy bounds extend to primitive Selberg-class functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States interval and discrepancy conjectures for F and transfers the smooth-to-sharp lower-bound mechanism. The RH_F upper error explicitly depends on the coefficient-growth exponent, exposing how analytic complexity changes the usable Fourier cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: General zero sums and generalized prime sums retain the two-way bridge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adjusts the zero-sum x-range to the coefficient-growth exponent, gives an explicit formula for the generalized Chebyshev error G_F, and states the two directional implications between short-interval G_F control and exponential-sum cancellation. This distinguishes a structural transfer from a zeta-specific accident.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The pair-correlation transition zone obstructs higher-degree transfer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why a naive pair-correlation analog proves the needed zero-sum result for degree one but fails for degree at least two: the transition near x=T^{d_F} lies outside the effective explicit-formula range. The proposed repair is boundedness plus small multiplicative second variation through that zone, which restores the argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Baez-Duarte decay criterion and exponential generating identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The frozen v1 span states the equivalence between RH and the k^{-3/4+epsilon} decay threshold, notes the sharpness and simple-zero strengthening, and introduces the inversion/generating-function framing that makes the sequence analytically useful.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-difference sequence as an exponential transform of the Riesz function
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: representation bridge and equivalent growth criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage defines c_k, places it in a general binomial/exponential-transform identity, identifies its generating function with R(x)/x, and states the bidirectional correspondence R(x)=O(x^{delta+1}) iff c_k=O(k^delta). This is the source's main bridge from a discrete sequence to an analytic growth criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Catastrophic cancellation forces precision linear in the sequence index
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Direct evaluation combines enormous alternating partial sums to obtain tiny c_k values. The paper turns that instability into a concrete precision rule, requiring enough digits to distinguish 1 from 1+2^{-k}, and uses the generic formula as a slow computation that does not assume RH, hence as an independent check on fast zero-based formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separating a rapidly decaying trend from zero-driven oscillation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The explicit formulas recast c_k as a trend plus an oscillatory sum over nontrivial zeta zeros, state the simple-zero assumption, and contrast the fast assumption-dependent route with the generic formula. The unexpectedly good small-k agreement is used only as numerical evidence that omitted integrals decay rapidly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trend/oscillation representation and its asymptotic regime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The immutable v1 span contains the assumptions on the zero sum, identifies the beta-function representation, reports close agreement with the generic sequence, and begins the exact-to-asymptotic treatment of the trend. It preserves the conceptual split between smooth decay and spectral fluctuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The trend is asymptotically k^{-2}, below the criterion-scale wave
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source derives an exact trend series, a finite asymptotic expansion, and a leading k^{-2} simplification, then compares all three across increasing k. This establishes that the trend decays faster than the k^{-3/4} oscillatory scale relevant to the criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conjugate zeros generate logarithmic waves with exponentially damped coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming RH, conjugate zeros convert the oscillatory term into a k^{-3/4} envelope multiplying sines and cosines whose log(k) frequencies are set by zero ordinates. The Hadamard-product and gamma-identity discussion yields exponential coefficient decay, explaining why only the first few zeros materially shape the computed wave.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First-zero dominance turns the normalized sequence into a log-periodic sine
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first-zero truncation rewrites k^{3/4}c_k as a single phase-shifted sinusoid with constant wavelength on a logarithmic k-axis. Consecutive sign changes then estimate the first zero's ordinate, while a Mobius-sum transform supplies the independent c_k calculation required for that check.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Off-critical zeros may be invisible because spectral damping overwhelms asymptotic growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The immutable v1 span separates on-line and hypothetical off-line zero contributions and argues that a very high off-line zero could have an exponentially tiny coefficient, requiring an enormous k before its slower-decaying contribution becomes visible. This directly limits what finite nonviolation of the decay bound can establish.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fast arbitrary-index evaluation is not visibly destabilized by the first Lehmer pair
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The final remarks state that the low-zero explicit formula enables evaluation at arbitrary large indices and contrast the Baez-Duarte bound with criteria sensitive to Lehmer pairs. The checked first pair has derivative values comparable for its two zeros, so the author finds no mechanism there for violating the bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed-function symmetry reframes the Riemann hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The prose converts the hypothesis into a real-zero statement for an even entire function and equivalently into a critical-line statement for nonreal zeta zeros, then uses conjugation symmetry to restrict attention to positive height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel evaluation replaces the earlier Euler-Maclaurin computational regime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes hand or desk-calculator work based on Euler-Maclaurin summation from later electronic computation based on the Riemann-Siegel formula, tying representation choice to a large change in reachable zero counts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite zero verification becomes costed sign-change separation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper states that verification over a finite range is performed by separating zeros of the real function Z(t), equivalently by finding enough sign changes, and identifies Z-evaluation as the dominant cost. It then compares evaluation counts and gives a source-specific lower bound for methods evaluating every Gram point.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduce a Gram block to locating two missing sign changes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Once a block of length L has implicitly supplied L-2 sign changes, the search is reduced to two remaining changes that must share a Gram interval. The program ranks the two outer intervals by endpoint-value evidence, applies parabolic interpolation, then searches the other outer interval and finally the interior or full length-two block.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Escalate unresolved blocks to preserved plots and manual inspection
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The automated routine records unresolved blocks instead of silently treating its heuristic as conclusive: it emits a message and plot, continues provisionally, and subjects the exceptional cases to later inspection, including adjacent blocks. Extending beyond the target range and invoking the cited theorem then closes the finite-zero claim.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conservative two-method error control certifies signs of Z(t)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The computation combines a Riemann-Siegel approximation, analytic remainder control, interpolation and machine-error accounting, then uses fixed bounds more conservative than the derived upper bounds. A higher-precision method is available when the fast method is inconclusive, and the source reports that it always determined the sign rigorously in the run described.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small argument shifts reduce expensive fallbacks but break strict count accumulation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When method A cannot rigorously determine a sign, the program tries small shifts before invoking method B. This optimization means some evaluations occur near rather than exactly at Gram points, so its statistics are not strictly accumulable with Brent's even though the paper presents them together.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted sampling can change the observed class of a Rosser-rule exception
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source warns that shifted Gram-point evaluation may miss or reclassify exceptions, gives a concrete zero-pattern mechanism for such reclassification, and distinguishes six exception types while noting that one type had not been observed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selected subranges can efficiently screen for Rosser-rule exceptions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A different method searches only selected small ranges inside a height interval and nevertheless recovers all exceptions in one comparison range and most in another, showing that rare-event detection need not exhaustively scan the whole interval in the same way.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Independent programs closely agree on Gram-block counts despite shifted sampling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On an overlapping range the two programs give extremely close counts for short blocks and identical counts for longer blocks. The surrounding summaries record a stable empirical distribution of block lengths and of zeros per Gram interval, while explicitly retaining the possibility that shifts obscured some first occurrences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The outer-interval heuristic is conditional on Gram-block length
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The counted block types support the outer-first search for lengths two through five, but for lengths at least six the missing zeros increasingly move one interval inward; only one length-seven block places them in an outer interval. Thus an efficiency heuristic validated in common short blocks does not extrapolate uniformly to rarer long blocks.

This is the mechanism that makes the closure theorem inductive rather than a black-box assertion.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remaining contribution is handled through a second Riesz mean expressed using characters and a line integral, after which smoothing and character estimates are routed by conductor size: the relevant hypothesis treats small conductor, while a large-sieve argument combined with Chen's integrand division treats large conductor. result_and_mechanism_map.title: Single-value zeta computation with exponent 4/13
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the target accuracy, arithmetic and storage model, precomputation allowance, bit-size control, and independence from the precise Riemann-Siegel remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From prior zeta algorithms to normalized Poisson descent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates Euler-Maclaurin, Riemann-Siegel, Schoenhage, and Heath-Brown approaches to the reusable goal of shortening polynomial-phase sums, and explains why normalization between Poisson steps prevents trivial cycling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Block size controls phase degree and global complexity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how Taylor expansion on common Riemann-Siegel blocks converts logarithmic phases into quadratic, cubic, or higher polynomial phases; the block exponent simultaneously determines phase degree, coefficient scale, and number of blocks.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lattice overlap and cost balancing in quadratic sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains Taylor recovery from a coefficient lattice, how overlap among block queries creates reuse, and why balancing lattice precomputation against block count yields the 3/8 FFT and 2/5 direct regimes while motivating a polylogarithmic quadratic-sum algorithm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small-cubic-coefficient evaluator and its precomputation budget
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2.2 isolates the exact cubic coefficient range, pointwise polylogarithmic evaluation cost, and K^(4 mu) precomputation that drive the main zeta algorithm; the following discussion identifies coefficient-range growth and phase degree as the barriers to faster methods.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel main sum to bounded polynomial-phase queries
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carries the block idea through weights, truncation errors, coefficient computation, and a critical evaluator assumption, giving a reusable reduction from the entire main sum to many normalized polynomial exponential sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic and cubic specializations yield exponents 1/3 and 4/13
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the generic reduction and, for cubic blocks, splits at K=t^(1/13) so either direct lattice FFT or Theorem 2.2 has the same t^(4/13) precomputation scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: What must change to beat 4/13
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies lower cubic precomputation cost or control of larger cubic coefficients as the improvement lever, notes possible amortization, and separates the 1/3 method from reliance on Riemann-Siegel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic van der Corput descent as the model mechanism
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects Poisson summation to van der Corput stationary contributions, explains Gaussian self-similarity and coefficient normalization, and shows how repeated length halving plus inexpensive nonstationary remainders gives a polylogarithmic quadratic evaluator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small cubic coefficient restores approximate self-similarity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Diagnoses the square-root phase created by cubic stationary points, then uses a small-coefficient expansion to absorb quartic and higher terms and recover a short linear combination of cubic sums with controlled error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Iterate while self-similar, then route boundary cases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates inexpensive nonstationary remainders, small-length direct evaluation, Euler-Maclaurin handling when the quadratic coefficient is small, and a final precomputed high-degree sum when cubic self-similarity fails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reuse quadratic machinery through integral factorization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A prototypical cost count explains four parameter dimensions, then the author deliberately replaces a literal cubic iteration by a factorization that reuses an existing quadratic-sum algorithm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decouple, descend quadratically, extract saddles, then precompute
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the whole implemented pipeline: express a cubic sum as an integral of quadratic and cubic factors, weaken their coupling, apply quadratic descent, extract stationary contributions as constrained higher-degree sums, and evaluate them from an FFT grid.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complexity conventions and easy coefficient regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes informal reductions precise in the paper's cost model and removes small K, negative mu, and moderately large cubic coefficients by direct evaluation, quadratic reduction, or lattice precomputation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parity descent to the cubic-integral transition scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the Fourier integral into stationary and nonstationary x-regions, reduces the nonstationary pieces to quadratic sums, and repeatedly separates even and odd cubic terms until cN^2 reaches a controlled scale while the coupling coefficient remains small.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalize coefficients while trading quadratic length for coupling growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies periodic normalization and the quadratic transformation repeatedly; each step halves the quadratic length while amplifying the coupling parameter, with explicit invariants and three stopping conditions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduce every second-phase stopping route to controlled integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Handles short-length and small-quadratic-coefficient exits, decomposes inherited remainders into explicit function families, and uses interval localization, contour changes, and Taylor expansions to reach a single terminal double-integral interface.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stationary contributions turn the terminal integral into a phase sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates computable tails, extends the bulk contour, evaluates the Gaussian x-integral, centers at each y-stationary point, and reduces the result to one nonquadratic phase sum plus quadratic sums already handled by Theorem 2.1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded analytic tail becomes a finite polynomial-phase family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses coefficient decay and the relation between N and M to truncate the stationary phase series at degree 3+floor(log N/log M), expanding the remaining bounded tail outside the exponent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dyadic approximation and FFT grids for the large-M regime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes arbitrary lengths into powers of two, tracks how phase coefficients transform, discretizes them at derivative-controlled resolutions, and proves an FFT cost bounded by the desired fourth power when M is not too small relative to N.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exploit coefficient dependence when the polynomial degree grows
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows why treating higher coefficients independently is too costly for small M, reparameterizes all of them through six linked variables, derives analytic interpolation radii, and obtains a sparse FFT grid within the K^(4 mu) budget.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Maclaurin decomposition with explicit remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the discrete-to-integral conversion and remainder inequality used at algorithmic boundary points.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recursive derivative bounds make few Euler-Maclaurin corrections sufficient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents derivatives by recursively generated polynomials, controls their coefficient norm, and turns small cK^2 into logarithmically many accurate correction terms with bounded precision.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Maclaurin correction integrals reduce to quadratic sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits terms according to whether a linear frequency is small, uses local Taylor expansion in the small region and explicit integration in the large region, and controls cancellation by shifting the summation index before binomial expansion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Move nonstationary cubic contours into exponentially decaying directions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Cauchy deformation and small cK^2 to create exponential decay, truncate long contours to logarithmic length, and reduce the resulting integrals to the quadratic-sum interface.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partition by stationary geometry and reduce to Airy-type integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Handles a broad cubic-quadratic double integral by separating small and large quadratic curvature, then partitions y by stationary-point location, deforms contours for decay, and reduces all cases to controlled Airy variants and incomplete Gamma functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: External contour tails collapse back to quadratic exponential sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves that the extended x-contours used in saddle extraction are cheap by rotating the y-contour, exploiting uniform decay, separating a full Gaussian integral from a decaying half-line correction, and reducing both to quadratic sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The de Bruijn-Newman real-zero threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage organizes the problem around a parameter threshold: above it the entire functions have only real zeros, below it some zeros are non-real; it states the implications and conjectural relation to the Riemann hypothesis and frames improvement of a lower bound as the goal.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Jensen-polynomial witness for a lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Taylor expansion supplies moments and associated finite-degree Jensen polynomials, and the cited criterion says that a non-real zero of one such polynomial at a chosen parameter witnesses that the parameter lies below the de Bruijn-Newman constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Earlier coefficient-error certification by full root computation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This passage records the prior constructive certificate: compute moments with known precision, find every polynomial zero, and use an Ostrowski error bound to transfer a numerically observed complex zero from approximate to exact coefficients. It also identifies coefficient sensitivity as the driver of very high precision.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Count real roots instead of finding all roots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Anticipated growth in the first complex-root degree makes repeated computation of all zeros expensive; the paper reframes the needed decision as detecting whether any zeros are non-real and selects Sturm sequences as a cheaper route.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sturm sequence and sign-variation root count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage constructs a decreasing-degree polynomial sequence by Euclidean division and states that the difference of endpoint sign-variation counts equals the number of real zeros on an interval.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continuation search from a known complex zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starting from a known parameter and minimal degree, the algorithm moves to larger parameters, computes successive Jensen polynomials, counts their real zeros on a chosen interval, and then uses a tracked local extremum and the previous imaginary part to initialize Newton's method as a check. It reports minimal degrees with two missing real roots and increasingly small imaginary parts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Chaotic sign patterns diagnose insufficient precision
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A sudden chaotic departure of the Sturm endpoint-sign sequence from the preceding degree's pattern is used as an operational warning that working precision is inadequate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Minimal degree and precision grow sharply toward minus five
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The table reports minimal degrees rising from 16 at parameter -50 to 406 at -5, together with complex-zero approximations and working precision, concretely supporting the paper's claim that improvement becomes much more expensive.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tail-bound selection for moment integration
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The moment integral is split at a cutoff, an analytic upper bound controls the omitted tail, and the cutoff is chosen so that this contribution is negligible relative to both the moments and the working precision; the parameter -5 computation is used as the concrete check.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Precision-aware truncation of the kernel series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A remainder inequality for truncating the kernel series is used to choose the number of terms as a function of the evaluation point, requested decimal precision, and the scale of the leading term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Evenness makes trapezoidal refinement preferable to Romberg extrapolation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inspection of the Romberg table showed extrapolation reducing rather than increasing accuracy, while the first-column trapezoidal estimates converged rapidly. The paper connects this to exponential convergence for an even integrand and therefore uses repeated composite-trapezoid halving with reusable precomputed values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct recurrence for the Sturm polynomial coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage turns the abstract Sturm definition into a coefficient computation: initialize with the Jensen polynomial and its derivative, obtain initial coefficients from the moments, and apply linear-quotient remainder relations through the decreasing-degree sequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adaptive root interval, precision escalation, and explicit-zero cross-check
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The real-root count is performed on an interval enlarged when necessary; abrupt implausible count drops are attributed to insufficient precision and resolved by increasing accuracy. A separately computed complex zero, located through a local extremum, is retained as an extra check.
