result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two spectral pictures from quantum chaos and Connes's sign objection
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects self-adjoint spectral realization, Selberg-style classical/quantum duality, GUE time-reversal breaking, prime-labelled periodic orbits, and Connes's minus-sign objection to the alternative picture of zeros as missing continuum levels; this frames the paper's embedded-state reconciliation target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Planck-cell regularization reproduces the smooth Riemann zero count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how bounding the unbounded xp flow by position and momentum cutoffs makes the subenergy phase-space area finite and yields the leading smooth zero-count asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-orbit analogy and its two mismatches
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the smooth count from the zeta-dependent fluctuation, compares its formal prime expansion to a periodic-orbit trace expression, and records the period, instability, time-reversal, sign, and finite-winding mismatches that any quantum-chaos model must confront.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Deforming the xp phase-space boundaries while preserving exchange symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces positive curved position and momentum boundaries as carriers of spectral fluctuations and formulates the scaled exchange symmetry that links them.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary geometry determines the fluctuation density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the allowed area for general boundaries, isolates the correction to Berry-Keating counting, and shows that under exchange symmetry the logarithmic boundary displacement is fixed by the derivative of the fluctuation count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Monotonic inverse reconstruction versus multivalued boundaries
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns a prescribed fluctuation density into a boundary function when the energy-position map remains monotone and identifies strong curvature of the fluctuation count as the condition producing multivalued, discontinuous boundary branches.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-rank antisymmetric interaction as the quantum boundary model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quantizes xp on the positive half-line and adds an interaction built from two real boundary states; Hermiticity and antisymmetry yield a real paired spectrum and connect the two wavefunctions to the classical boundary roles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary transport closes allowed trajectories and opens forbidden ones
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets the rank-two interaction as projection-and-transfer between boundary states, with an inverse supplied by Hermiticity; classically the transfer closes allowed xp trajectories while the inverse channel yields unbounded forbidden-region trajectories, anticipating embedded bound states in a continuum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reconciling Berry-Keating levels with Connes missing lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts lower-cutoff discrete counting with Connes's upper-cutoff continuum and proposes embedded discrete states as a single quantum structure capable of realizing both spectral interpretations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic-coordinate solution and the shuffle identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the Schroedinger problem into a first-order equation in log position, expresses the solution through boundary overlaps and endpoint amplitudes, and derives paired ordered-integral representations whose change of integration order gives a shuffle relation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Jost determinant separates scattering states from embedded bound states
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the determinant F from the overlap system, derives its reality symmetry, and shows that nonzero F leaves nonnormalizable endpoint amplitudes while real zeros cancel both endpoints and can produce normalizable bound states embedded in a full real scattering continuum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum trap: fine tuning converts resonances into confined embedded states
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses delta-localized boundary states to show concretely that a coupling-product condition creates periodic or antiperiodic embedded levels, confines their wavefunctions to a finite interval, and turns them into resonances when the tuning is relaxed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cauchy representation imposes Jost analyticity and zero location
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the ordered overlap as a Cauchy transform, linking causal ordering to analyticity in the upper energy half-plane and restricting zeros of F to the real axis or lower half-plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier-dual hard boundaries generate completed-L-function phases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Associates the position cutoff with a delta boundary state and the momentum cutoff with cosine or sine states, then uses Mellin transforms to show that their exchange duality contributes the gamma-factor phases of even and odd Dirichlet L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole subtraction converts the gamma phase into the Berry-Keating Jost function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the completed-zeta phase into upper-half-plane analytic and pole parts, evaluates the required Hilbert transforms, and obtains a Jost function whose leading high-energy form is one plus a phase factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coupling choice turns smooth zero counts into resonances
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that a tuned coupling product makes real-axis zeros of the asymptotic Jost function track either the average Riemann count or a shifted cosine-phase count, and interprets these smooth locations as asymptotic bound states or, more accurately, resonances.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantized fluctuation constraint solves the position-boundary state
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Promotes the semiclassical logarithmic boundary relation to an operator equation, diagonalizes the free xp generator, and solves the resulting first-order energy equation so that the Mellin transform of one boundary state acquires the prescribed fluctuation phase.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Half-line momentum extensions solve the dual boundary state
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines log absolute momentum through self-adjoint extensions of squared momentum on the half-line, uses cosine and sine bases to solve the second boundary equation, and recovers the Fourier duality between both boundary wavefunctions for arbitrary fluctuations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An analyticity assumption collapses the Jost function to a counting phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the fluctuating boundary transforms, assumes the total counting phase is analytic and decaying in the upper half-plane, and conditionally reduces F to a simple phase expression whose zero count matches the semiclassical fluctuation formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dual boundary data factor the critical-line zeta function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the exchange transformation of the two boundary amplitudes and the zeta functional relation to propose a duality-invariant sum, yielding a factorization of the Riemann-Siegel Z function into an amplitude and cosine of the candidate counting phase.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel truncation supplies a candidate fluctuation phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches cosine and sine components of the Riemann-Siegel main sum to define a finite Dirichlet sum f, extracts its argument as the fluctuation function, and distinguishes its smooth interpolation and truncation-induced jumps from the exact step count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncated Dirichlet sum versus truncated Euler product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explicitly notes that the critical-line Euler product is invalid, then compares the finite Riemann-Siegel sum with a finite prime product and reports only qualitative alignment of extrema and phases, isolating a possible but unproved prime-information channel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Berry-Keating smoothing gives an exact dual decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces the discontinuous main-sum cutoff by contour-defined smooth weights, obtains a smooth exact f and the dual decomposition of zeta, and identifies the error-function leading approximation for improved numerical evaluation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Approximate functional relation as phase-space splitting beyond the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets the two sums in the Hardy-Littlewood approximate functional relation as position and momentum lattice contributions along the xp energy hyperbola and suggests that moving off the critical line corresponds to an imaginary non-Hermitian shift of the xp Hamiltonian.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the construction does not prove RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the unproved upper-half-plane analyticity and decay of the counting phase, the needed nonvanishing of f on the real axis, the merely partial zeta-as-Jost factorization, and the missing classical interpretation of the interaction and primes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bound-state wavefunctions, orthogonality, and density-of-states norm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reexpresses eigenfunctions in the free-energy basis, separates distributionally normalized scattering states from localized zero-of-F states, and uses Jost analyticity to derive orthogonality and a norm proportional to the derivative of the counting function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residue construction for smooth-zero wavefunctions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the boundary phases to the smooth Riemann count, evaluates the bound-state integral by residues, and relates decay at infinity to the smooth phase-zero condition while contrasting forbidden-region and oscillatory components.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncated integral for exact-zero candidate wavefunctions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains that no analytic exact-zero wavefunction is obtained and instead truncates the boundary-state integral numerically, reporting both shared structure with the smooth states and additional irregular behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hardy Z turns critical-line zero geometry into a real-variable moment problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The phase-adjusted Hardy function is real on the real axis, preserves the critical-line modulus, and has zeros exactly at critical-line zeta zeros; defining moments of Z and Z' then makes zero spacing accessible to real endpoint inequalities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mixed RMT moments expose a coefficient-availability bottleneck
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source connects zeta moments to random-matrix constants and explains that the mixed-moment route requires rational functions H(h,k) whose unavailable values beyond the known range block higher-k gap estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separate derivative moments replace unavailable mixed-moment coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Characteristic-polynomial derivative moments motivate a conjecture for M_k with constants c_k, offering a separate derivative/function moment ratio that can be inserted into gap inequalities without computing H(h,k).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair correlation is a distributional spacing lens distinct from extremal gaps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separates the large-gap objective from pair correlation, while relating the latter to essential simplicity and unitary eigenvalue statistics; this prevents treating all zero-spacing evidence as the same target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalized gaps define separate limsup and liminf extremal statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dividing consecutive ordinate gaps by 2pi/log(gamma_n) creates a scale-free sequence with average one, after which lambda and mu isolate asymptotically large and small gaps.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line gap Lambda dominates the all-zero gap statistic and coincides with it under RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defining Lambda using distinct positive critical-line zeros clarifies what the real Hardy-function argument can measure; Lambda is at least lambda unconditionally at the definitional level described here, and the distinction disappears under RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moment information and stronger variational Wirtinger inequalities successively sharpen gap bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The historical progression shows two independent levers in the same proof family: richer mixed moments and stronger endpoint inequalities, including a variational inequality whose optimization can be recast algebraically through Jacobi-Schur functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global-versus-local averages yield positive-proportion multi-zero gap statements
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This route compares a continuous global average with a discrete local average and targets r-step gaps for a positive proportion of zeros, rather than only an extremal limsup.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The paper reframes higher-k gap extension around separately available b_k and c_k
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After recording the prior mixed-moment ceiling, the source proposes using ordinary Hardy moments and derivative moments with explicit b_k and c_k to continue from k=7 through k=15.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Agarwal-Pang endpoint inequality converts a uniform gap cap into a moment-ratio lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof scales an endpoint Wirtinger inequality to each consecutive Hardy-Z zero interval, replaces every interval length by a hypothetical common cap, sums, and compares conjectural Z and Z' moments to force the explicit Lambda(k) bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Brnetic-Pecaric endpoint constant slots into the same moment-to-gap proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem replaces the prior endpoint constant by I(k), then reuses the interval argument to derive a second explicit b_k/c_k gap formula and its finite numerical specialization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Beesack's endpoint inequality gives the strongest listed finite-k bounds and reveals the c_k ceiling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A third endpoint inequality yields a closed Lambda(k) bound, produces the source's strongest k=15 value, and makes clear that extending the computation requires new derivative-moment constants c_k rather than difficult b_k values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation phases turn critical-line zeta values into real data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source relates xi, Phi, Lambda, theta, Z, and Gram points so that phase normalization makes Z real and identifies Gram ordinates as locations where zeta is real. This is the representation layer used by every later contour and averaging claim.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A compensating functional-equation term extends the Gram-point mean across sigma > 0
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 identifies the sigma-dependent main term that must be subtracted from Re zeta at Gram ordinates, gives a uniform error, and explains both geometric robustness of the sampling path and the unproved numerical suggestion of extension left of the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity on a Gram line would rigidify an argument-principle zero count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source turns positivity of Re zeta along a horizontal boundary segment into a single-valued logarithm and a bounded argument variation, forcing the zero count to be the nearest integer to the theta main term. It then isolates infinitely many Gram lines with this positivity as the motivating target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lambda-real contours pair by reflection and classify critical-line crossings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The functional identity Lambda(s)Lambda(1-s)=1 forces reflection symmetry of real-Lambda contours and values ±1 on their critical-line crossings. Those signs distinguish real from imaginary zeta values and center from node behavior at simple zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lambda-real contours are asymptotically horizontal Gram lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Stirling expansion converts the implicit reality condition for Lambda into contour equations, showing O(1/t) departure from horizontal intervals and an even/odd split between Gram and imaginary-zeta crossings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Magnitude of Lambda varies monotonically along its real contours
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring Re Lambda into a positive exponential amplitude and a cosine phase shows that on a real-Lambda contour the phase is asymptotically pinned to an integer multiple of pi while the amplitude grows with sigma. This yields strict monotonicity and an explicit signed asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reflected off-critical zeros cannot have equal derivative magnitude
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating the functional equation to the zero multiplicity transfers derivatives between reflected zeros with multiplier Lambda. The contour magnitude estimate then makes the derivative magnitude strictly asymmetric on opposite sides of the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phi-real contours meet Gram points with a small nonhorizontal angle
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts the two functional-equation multipliers: Phi-real contours cross the same Gram points as Lambda-real contours but have asymptotic slope -pi/(2 log t), with O(1/t) deviation from the corresponding tilted intervals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modified Gram-point means expose cosine sums as the analytic bottleneck
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The modified averages numerically approach one across sampled sigma values, and the text immediately isolates a uniform cosine-sum estimate over Gram ordinates as the needed analytic control. This links empirical normalization to the proof mechanism without treating the plot as proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phase curvature at Gram ordinates yields square-root cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extending the Gram index continuously turns the oscillation into a phase phi(nu). Theta asymptotics give a positive lower bound for -phi'', allowing a van der Corput-type estimate and hence an O(N^(1/2) log N) cosine-sum bound with absolute constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Dirichlet-series regime controls modified means to the right of one
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first regime of Theorem 1 expands zeta where sigma exceeds a tunable threshold and applies the Gram-ordinate cosine estimate termwise, producing a bound controlled by the distance of that threshold from one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The approximate functional equation reduces the left regime to two cosine sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For 0 < sigma below the transition, the approximate functional equation and the Gram-line asymptotics for chi separate the modified real zeta value into two truncated cosine sums F1 and F2 plus a controlled aggregate error. The functional-equation correction appears naturally as the second main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reordering and partial summation transfer the cosine bound to F1 and F2
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof reorders the moving truncation using a threshold tau to bound F1 directly, then applies weighted partial summation through t(x)=x/log x to control F2. This demonstrates how one oscillatory estimate survives two differently weighted pieces of the functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Optimizing the transition parameter makes the average estimate uniform in sigma
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source packages competing error terms into g_N(x), chooses the unique minimizing transition sigma_N, and splits the sigma range so that the high- and low-sigma estimates combine into the theorem's uniform bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Average positivity gives infinitely many positive Gram-point values, but leftward extension remains conjectural
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proved error estimate yields convergence of the modified average, a linear lower bound for the sum of real parts, and therefore infinitely many positive values at Gram ordinates for each fixed 0 < sigma < 1. The authors separately mark sigma = 0 and further-left extension as numerical conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines vacuum energy and signed states, distinguishes physical from unphysical tachyons, and explains why finite level-matched energy alone is insufficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the graded sum as a mass-supertrace generator and derives dimension-dependent vanishing below a threshold order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Robin normalization and record-sequence counterexample sieve
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the pointwise Robin inequality with Gronwall's limiting upper envelope and explains why a least violation can be sought among superabundant record setters, while contrasting other divisor-function formulations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extremely abundant records and an infinitude criterion for RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines XA as successive records of f above a fixed baseline, proves XA is contained in SA, places any least Robin counterexample in XA, and proves RH iff XA is infinite by combining record behavior with Gronwall's limsup.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Inverting relative logarithmic perturbations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides a reusable mechanism for converting a two-sided relative bound on y around x into a two-sided relative bound on x around y with controlled logarithmic error constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Controlling changes in x log log x
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages monotonicity of a normalized secant ratio for x log log x and a square-root comparison for log-log growth, later enabling consecutive-record monotonicity arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Effective Chebyshev and prime-counting bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Collects explicit two-sided estimates for theta and psi and bounds for pi, including how cited estimates plus finite computation produce constants usable in later largest-prime arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Oscillation, prime steps, and Mertens-product control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Supplies sign-changing theta/psi oscillation, a short-interval prime input, a bound on consecutive primes, and explicit Euler-product estimates that drive later CA separation and XA monotonicity arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dense SA records force lower bounds on prime exponents
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows consecutive SA numbers differ by at most a factor of two and uses a replacement competitor to force each prime exponent to be at least the floor of log p divided by log q.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-power balance in SA factorizations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates exponents at different primes and derives two-sided scale control of the power of two by p log p, exposing the compressed exponent profile of superabundant integers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From the exponent profile to p asymptotic to log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the two-adic scale, the known SA relation p asymptotic to log n, and Chebyshev sums to sandwich log n relative to theta(p), clarifying how factorization geometry controls the ambient size.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Effective approach of SA divisor sums to the Gronwall constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses explicit p-versus-log n bounds, a comparison of sigma(n)/n with n/phi(n), and an Euler product to prove f(n) tends to e^gamma along SA with a quantitative lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Additive excess sigma(n) minus n increases along SA
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extracts an additive monotonic quantity directly from the defining multiplicative record property of SA, illustrating a reusable conversion from ratio growth to difference growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponentiating record growth preserves an SA monotone
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines SA ratio growth with the additive excess monotonicity to prove increase of a nonlinear sigma(n)-exponent expression.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Monotonicity after subtracting n log log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses bounded spacing of consecutive SA numbers, log-log secant control, and the asymptotic lower bound for sigma to show an adjusted additive excess increases, then lifts that result to a nonlinear normalized expression.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transferring SA growth through phi and Psi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how monotone prime support controls n/phi(n) and combines that support change with SA growth to derive further monotonic arithmetic-function expressions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Threshold coordinates for CA prime exponents
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents a CA number through a parameter epsilon and threshold values x_k, turning the global extremal inequality into local exponent intervals and explaining uniqueness or finite multiplicity at boundary parameters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CA endpoints capture maxima of the Robin normalization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that between successive CA numbers the normalized divisor sum cannot exceed both endpoint values, reducing the search for Robin violations to CA endpoints.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transferring XA records to CA endpoints and exploiting theta oscillation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that an XA point between successive CA numbers forces the upper CA endpoint into XA, derives infinitely many CA∩XA under RH, and then constructs infinitely many CA numbers with largest prime exceeding log N from Chebyshev oscillation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: XA records force p below log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares an XA number with n/p and converts the record inequality through a logarithmic bound to prove its largest prime factor is strictly below log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-scale incompatibility yields infinitely many CA outside XA
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts the XA prime bound with the preceding infinite CA family having p greater than log N, yielding an unconditional infinite separation of the two extremal classes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A spacing condition makes (sigma+phi)/n increase along XA
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines XA record growth, explicit product estimates, a prime-gap bound, and a lower spacing assumption to prove monotonicity of a mixed divisor-totient statistic for consecutive XA numbers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Observed local rigidity of XA exponent vectors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records finite-range relations among adjacent prime-power blocks, one-step exponent changes between consecutive XA numbers, monotone largest-prime and divisor-count observations, and counterexamples showing these patterns do not automatically characterize highly composite or SA behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Empirical overlap of XA and CA below a fixed SA cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Quantifies that neither XA nor CA contains the other in the inspected finite domain and measures the substantial but non-identical overlap.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the minimal Weierstrass-product and generalized-Stirling hypotheses needed to turn a sequence into a Delta function and associated zeta function, while explaining why the framework minimizes order and pole complexity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One Mellin transform converts asymptotics and Taylor data into complementary meromorphic continuations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how the large-argument expansion controls poles on one side, the origin Taylor series controls positive-integer behavior on the other, and sine-factor cancellations produce trace identities and finite values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional-equation pairing lowers the effective sequence order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs functional-equation-related zeros and rewrites the completed zeta product as an even Delta product in a squared variable, replacing an awkward order-one zero sequence with a simpler order-one-half setting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stirling expansion of the Delta product fixes the half-integer pole ladder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the inverse quadratic branch into the completed-zeta asymptotics to obtain arbitrary-order Delta coefficients, double half-integer poles, values at zero, and the regularized determinant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two Taylor expansions yield finite identities among zero sums, zeta derivatives, and Stieltjes cumulants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches the Delta-product Taylor series with functional-equation expansions to produce countably many three-term identities and finite decompositions for positive-integer secondary-zeta values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-sum identities connect the secondary-zeta coordinates to Li coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records additional sum rules and a transformation linking the zero sums to Li coefficients, hence to a positivity formulation of the Riemann Hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Translation covariance separates polynomial polar data from transcendental special values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that shifting the squared spectrum preserves admissibility and makes asymptotic coefficients, pole parts, and trace identities polynomial in the shift, while finite-point Taylor data and positive values vary transcendentally.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial zeros plus a ghost eigenvalue form a shadow spectrum

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Difference-conjugated Hamiltonian as a conditional zero spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states its central construction and separates several consequences: the origin boundary condition maps spectral parameters to nontrivial zeta zeros, the commuting limit is 2xp, modified PT symmetry supplies a possible reality route, a new inner product is proposed, and off-critical zeros would produce degeneracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite difference, its kernel, and a decay-qualified inverse
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Writing the proposed Hamiltonian as a similarity transform through Delta exposes the key structural issue: Delta is a unit shift difference, annihilates unit-periodic functions, and therefore has no inverse on all smooth functions. The authors restrict attention to functions vanishing at infinity and give a Bernoulli/Borel prescription whose right-inverse property is tied to that boundary choice.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunctions and boundary selection of zeta zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Borel-summed inverse applied to a power is recognized as a Hurwitz-zeta representation. The resulting eigenfunction is minus the Hurwitz zeta, and imposing its value at the origin to vanish makes the spectral parameter a zero of the Riemann zeta function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Asymptotics separate trivial-zero states from the proposed domain
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts polynomially growing Bernoulli-polynomial states at trivial zeros with sublinear nontrivial-zero states, and correspondingly distinguishes whether Delta applied to the state vanishes at infinity. Together with the later orthogonality behavior, this is used to exclude trivial-zero states from the Hamiltonian domain while retaining a discrete spectrum indexed by nontrivial zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reality of the spectrum is left to a heuristic symmetry analysis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors explicitly distinguish their complex extension of the Berry-Keating idea from the missing proof that the eigenvalues are real, and announce the limited route they pursue: modified PT symmetry, pseudo-Hermiticity, an isospectral Berry-Keating representative, and a biorthogonal inner product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modified parity-time reflection gives a conditional spectral-reality route
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After interchanging the usual roles assigned to coordinate and momentum, the source defines PT to fix x and reverse p, making iH invariant. It then uses the broken/unbroken PT eigenvalue alternatives to state that maximal breaking for iH would make the spectrum of H real, while distinguishing the behavior asserted for nontrivial and trivial zero states.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditional metric and formally Hermitian representatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming the momentum operator is symmetric on the eventual domain, the source computes an adjoint relation with a nonnegative metric based on sin-squared of half the momentum, then discusses similarity transforms yielding a Hamiltonian with a quantum-anomaly momentum term or the Berry-Keating dilation Hamiltonian. It also records the decisive obstruction that the inverse metric is unbounded.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary transport to a Berry-Keating quantization condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A similarity representative with Berry-Keating Hamiltonian has power-law eigenstates, and the source transports the original origin boundary condition through a sine-of-momentum relation to an explicit limiting quantization condition involving the Hurwitz zeta function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adjoint eigenstates define a metric pairing for the non-Hermitian eigenbasis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source replaces ordinary orthogonality by eigenstates of the formal adjoint, gives their forward-difference form, and defines an associated-state map and inner product on the span of the original eigenstates. This makes the metric operator the bridge between non-Hermitian spectral data and a symmetry claim.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Distributional pairing distinguishes nontrivial from trivial states
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The biorthogonal pairing is reduced to a scale-invariant power integral. Under the source's RH-conditioned conjugacy relation it is interpreted as a Dirac delta, giving off-diagonal biorthogonality, whereas the analogous integral for trivial-zero states diverges too strongly even as a tempered distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The origin boundary condition is reused to suppress integration-by-parts terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the metric commutes with momentum, the source reduces momentum symmetry to vanishing boundary terms in paired original and adjoint states. The adjoint state diverges at the origin, so sufficient vanishing of the original state is needed; the already imposed condition at zero is said to suffice. Under that assumption, a formal integral rearrangement makes H symmetric in the new inner product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Off-critical zeros are represented as exceptional-point degeneracies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source claims that if RH is false, eigenstates associated with off-critical nontrivial zeros coalesce into Jordan-block structures and satisfy self-orthogonality. It then connects spectral nondegeneracy to simplicity of zeros, but explicitly makes the strongest simplicity conclusion depend on a one-to-one correspondence between eigenstate boundary conditions and the secular equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infinite norms motivate a finite-window regularization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separates its formal Hamiltonian analysis from ordinary quantum mechanics because the states are not normalizable, then proposes a symmetric multiplicative cutoff, logarithmic state renormalization, and a limit. It reports that the transformed-position expectation has the same leading scale as prime counting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Domain and completeness remain the unresolved self-adjointness bottleneck
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The discussion identifies the domain of H and establishment of self-adjointness as difficult open problems. The boundary-condition revisit further notes that finite-dimensional biorthogonality logic does not automatically pass to the infinite-dimensional setting: completeness of the proposed eigenstates is needed to identify the displayed operator as the Hermitian adjoint.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An epsilon-family interpolates the finite difference toward a power-law representative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A substantive note embedded among the references replaces the unit difference by an epsilon-scaled difference, gives Hurwitz-zeta eigenstates with rescaled argument and unchanged spectral parameter, and states that the zero-epsilon limit yields a momentum-conjugated dilation Hamiltonian with a power-law eigenstate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why critical-line functional statistics require a change of scale or regularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts pointwise limits away from the critical line with Selberg normalization and the failure of continuous functional limits on the line, isolating three possible repairs: normalization, shrinking neighborhoods, or generalized-function limits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random matrices, log-correlated fields, and multiplicative chaos as a shared statistical picture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This passage connects zero statistics and characteristic polynomials to the claim that log zeta is log-correlated, then explains why exponentiating such rough fields leads to multiplicative chaos and potentially universal fractal statistics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The random-shift field on the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper turns vertical statistics into a random function by shifting zeta with a uniform height parameter and states the exact large-height object whose law is studied.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Renormalized exponentials of log-correlated fields and the subcritical-critical transition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text constructs Gaussian multiplicative chaos as a weak-star martingale limit, explains why it can collapse to zero, and identifies the logarithmic covariance and extra normalization at criticality as the decisive features.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dependent complex chaos: nonintegrable covariance repaired by a singular-integral kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unlike standard complex-chaos models, the real and imaginary parts have a sign-kernel dependence. The resulting two-point singularity is not absolutely integrable, yet its Hilbert-transform form restores an L2 route and reflects analytic boundary structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global random shifts converge to a smooth factor times complex chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1.1 places the critical-line shifts in negative Sobolev space and identifies the limit as a randomized zeta boundary distribution factored into a nonvanishing smooth random function and a complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mesoscopic dilation separates a divergent zero mode from a universal log field
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Scaling a translation-invariant log-correlated field produces an exploding constant Gaussian component plus a residual covariance of strictly logarithmic form, motivating the later mesoscopic factorization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta and Haar-unitary characteristic polynomials share the mesoscopic chaos component
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 compare the two models in Wasserstein-Sobolev topology and show that their spatial chaos agrees while their divergent scalar factors differ only in bounded details.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quotienting by nonzero scalars exposes a proper mesoscopic limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Passing to a projectivized negative Sobolev space removes the divergent multiplicative zero mode and leaves a scale-invariant chaos defined only modulo constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two-point functions and randomized truncated Euler products bridge zeta to its limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof outline isolates the Hilbert-transform main kernel, obtains Sobolev tightness, approximates zeta by finite Euler products, equidistributes prime phases, and then lets the randomized product converge as a generalized boundary value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The randomized boundary value is neither a function nor a complex measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The non-measure theorem explains why continuous-function limits fail and why generalized functions are not merely a convenient proof space but the correct limiting category.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Log randomized zeta equals a Gaussian prime field plus an exponentially controlled smooth error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1.7 supplies the structural decomposition that later transfers Gaussian-chaos results to randomized zeta, with almost-sure smooth convergence and exponential derivative bounds for the error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subcritical and critical real chaos from normalized absolute zeta powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states almost-sure subcritical convergence, zero collapse at and above the naive critical threshold, moment ranges, and a separately renormalized nontrivial critical measure, each differing from Gaussian chaos by a positive smooth factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real-chaos limits for actual zeta are blocked by unavailable moment and correlation asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conjectured zeta measures are motivated by the proved randomized model, but their normalization and convergence require precise absolute moments and multipoint correlations beyond current unconditional results in the source.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The imaginary log-zeta field is tied to zeros and is harder than the real-chaos problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source identifies zero locations as an added obstruction for imaginary-part chaos while pointing to mesoscopic zero linear statistics as partial log-correlated evidence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Fourier-sampling norm on logarithms of integers controlled by weighted L2 decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Z norm samples a test function's Fourier transform at log-integer frequencies, matching Dirichlet-series structure; a Sobolev estimate embeds it into a weighted L2 space and supplies the test-function control needed later.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta kernels realize the Fourier-sampling norm and expose the oscillatory Hilbert-transform term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A distributional Fourier-transform computation converts zeta on the one-line into the Z inner product and shows how the shifted second-moment kernel converges after an oscillatory singular-integral cancellation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform two-point asymptotics for full, mixed, and truncated zeta fields
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2.8 identifies the full shifted two-point function, the mixed truncation kernel, and the fully truncated limit with errors that are uniform in spatial variables at fixed truncation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second moments turn Euler truncation into a fixed-test-function L2 approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combining the kernel asymptotics makes the variance of full minus truncated zeta equal the omitted part of the Z norm, so choosing truncation before height yields arbitrary accuracy for each admissible test function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier testing lifts scalar variance control to negative-Sobolev Wasserstein approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Testing against exponentials and integrating with the Sobolev weight converts the fixed-test estimate into mean-square approximation of whole generalized functions, hence a Wasserstein bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-phase equidistribution and Hilbert-valued martingales construct randomized zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unique prime factorization yields joint equidistribution of vertical prime phases; the randomized Euler products form an L2-bounded negative-Sobolev martingale and therefore converge almost surely and in Wasserstein distance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three matched approximations prove the global functional limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof closes a triangle among shifted zeta, a fixed truncated shift, the matching randomized truncation, and the randomized infinite limit, choosing truncation and height in the necessary nested order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite Dirichlet polynomials bypass mixed two-point estimates at the cost of quantitative truncation control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A second proof route approximates both zeta and randomized Euler products through finite Dirichlet polynomials using easier cross-moment estimates, but loses the good errors available for Euler-product truncations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sobolev boundary convergence forces an analytic randomized Euler product beyond the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poisson extension transfers boundary convergence into local uniform convergence in the half-plane, establishing the infinite randomized Euler product there and its nonvanishing by Hurwitz's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Radial blow-up rules out any local measure representation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first prime-harmonic term has divergent variance and a zero-one-law blow-up, while higher harmonics remain bounded; finite radial limits for Poisson extensions of measures then contradict this behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Square-summable random function series converge smoothly with exponential supremum bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Banach-valued random-series lemma upgrades derivative square summability to uniform smooth convergence and exponential control, providing the reusable engine for all later smooth-error estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher prime powers contribute only a smooth random remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding log Euler products separates the first prime harmonic from all higher powers; absolute convergence for powers at least three and the random-series lemma for the square term show the latter are smooth with exponential bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Block freezing converts prime phases into Gaussian blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Primes are grouped into slowly varying blocks, their spatial phases are frozen at a block representative, and a quantitative Gaussian coupling replaces each two-dimensional phase sum with a Gaussian block of matching covariance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Coupling and freezing errors become a smooth field under summable block conditions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separately bounds Gaussian-coupling error and phase-freezing error, showing each converges in every C-derivative norm with exponential maximal bounds when explicit block sums converge.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A sparse block schedule satisfies both errors and controls partial blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Prime-number estimates justify a concrete block sequence, and concentration inside incomplete blocks extends convergence from block endpoints to every truncation, completing the Gaussian-plus-smooth approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Gaussian exponential is an L2-bounded generalized-function martingale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The complex Gaussian exponential has expectation one without a real variance renormalization, and its two-point series is bounded through the Z norm, producing a nontrivial negative-Sobolev martingale limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smooth-error convergence passes multiplicative factorization to the generalized limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Testing on compactly supported smooth functions and using Sobolev multiplier continuity lets the identity at finite truncation pass to randomized zeta equals a smooth exponential times complex chaos.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complex Brownian Fourier fields turn exponential second moments into convolution expansions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A spectral stochastic-integral representation gives a clean covariance formula, while a Fatou comparison on spectral amplitudes provides a lower-semicontinuity tool for exponential-field second moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic one-sided spectrum restores an L2 estimate for complex chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the high-frequency u^{-1/2} field, analytic continuation of the covariance exponential produces a Cauchy-kernel boundary value; the Plemelj formula and Hilbert-transform boundedness control the chaos action by weighted L2 norm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two spectral cutoffs construct the mesoscopic complex chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uniform Sobolev second moments make the low- and high-frequency cutoff exponentials a two-parameter martingale, yielding the full chaos as cutoffs go to zero and infinity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime Gaussian sums are successively regularized into a Brownian spectral integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Prime locations are replaced by inverse logarithmic-integral locations, Gaussian coefficients by Brownian increments, and the resulting Riemann sum by a stochastic integral; each replacement contributes only a smooth exponentially controlled error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dilation yields a universal chaos, a divergent scalar, and a vanishing smooth distortion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After scaling, the randomized zeta boundary value factors as h_delta times exp(Y_delta) times a chaos whose law is independent of delta; h_delta tends smoothly to one and Y_delta splits into a Gaussian of variance log(1/delta) plus a controlled remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A diagonal scale choice transfers randomized mesoscopic limits back to zeta and to the scalar quotient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The global approximation is combined with the dilation estimate through a piecewise-constant diagonal sequence, while projectivization removes the divergent scalar and yields convergence to the universal chaos class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Covariance bounds and martingale uniform integrability govern real Gaussian chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states the precise covariance convergence and upper-bound conditions under which Gaussian exponential measures converge, remain nontrivial below criticality, collapse above it, and possess controlled moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The prime Gaussian covariance is one-half logarithmic plus a smooth arithmetic remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Successive comparison of primes with j log j, sums with integrals, and the cosine integral identifies the diagonal log singularity uniformly and proves smoothness away from it via the Euler product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local Euler-factor expansion matches zeta and Gaussian exponential normalizations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Independence and a small-parameter expansion show that expected absolute randomized-zeta powers are uniformly comparable to the Gaussian exponential normalization and grow with the predicted log-power.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform integrability transfers subcritical and supercritical behavior through the smooth error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Gaussian chaos convergence is multiplied by the smooth error from Theorem 1.7; exponential error moments and Holder bounds make the zeta martingale uniformly integrable below criticality and preserve zero collapse above.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical chaos is transferred by matching covariance approximations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A covariance-comparison theorem says that uniformly close Gaussian approximations with off-diagonal convergence share the same non-atomic critical limit, and the source supplies a reference white-noise field with known critical normalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A spectral weight with exact logarithmic covariance is matched to the prime field
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The prime Gaussian field is rewritten as a Brownian integral, its u^{-1/2} weight is replaced by the Fourier transform of a compact logarithmic covariance, and variance matching selects the critical time scale before applying covariance comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Independence of early and late scales identifies the critical randomized-zeta measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After the reference critical measure converges, fixed initial Gaussian scales and the smooth error are separated from the tail; conditioning and uniform convergence pass the critical limit to the normalized randomized-zeta density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mesoscopic real chaos separates a growing scalar Gaussian from strict logarithmic chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The covariance asymptotics imply that a slowly shrinking randomized-zeta density factors into an exploding scalar mode, a bounded random correction, and a standard real Gaussian chaos approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line growth implies quantitative mean one for long zeta averages
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A subconvex growth estimate and contour shift to the absolutely convergent line show that the average of zeta over any long critical-line interval is one with endpoint-dependent error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted products become divisor sums whose Perron contours reveal two main terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Encoding zeta times a shifted zeta or truncated Euler product by generalized divisor sums allows an effective Perron formula and contour shift to derive the needed uniform summatory asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The functional equation converts shifted critical-line moments into divisor-sum asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Titchmarsh integral lemma, truncation of the Dirichlet series, residue calculus, and contour error estimates reduce both full and mixed shifted moments to the divisor sums of the previous unit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large-shift bounds and range symmetrization complete the two-point theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof first recovers the classical mean square as the zero-shift limit, then partitions spatial shifts, symmetrizes the time interval, applies the functional equation, and uses finite phase equidistribution for the fully truncated kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier discrepancy and tail mass bound Wasserstein distance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A shared diagonal coupling removes common mass, and truncating to a ball turns total-variation control into an L1 Fourier-density bound plus tail integrals, yielding a reusable quantitative coupling inequality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothing characteristic functions couples normalized sums to covariance-matched Gaussians
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A small auxiliary Gaussian regularizes the normalized sum, Taylor expansion controls its characteristic function on the main region, tail estimates control the complement, and low-rank covariance cases are split off to obtain a polynomial Wasserstein error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean coupling error plus concentration yields exponential and Gaussian-tail moment bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bernstein or Azuma concentration and a cutoff decomposition upgrade the first-moment coupling estimate to exponential control, which is what the smooth-error series requires.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Toeplitz asymptotics control characteristic-polynomial truncation in negative Sobolev space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Exact determinant correlations, Fisher-Hartwig asymptotics for cross terms, and strong Szego asymptotics for truncated terms show that Haar-unitary characteristic polynomials are approximated in mean square by exponential trace truncations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian trace limits become an H-valued multiplicative-chaos martingale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Diaconis-Shahshahani finite-trace convergence passes through a continuous exponential map, and the resulting Gaussian exponential truncations form an L2-bounded negative-Sobolev martingale, identifying the global random-matrix chaos limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local Sobolev dilation transfers the global CUE limit to a slowly shrinking arc
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A lattice Fourier-sampling estimate proves the circle-to-line dilation bound, allowing a scale sequence on which the coupled global characteristic-polynomial error remains negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Block Brownian coupling identifies the mesoscopic CUE chaos and controls regularization uniformly
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Trace Gaussians are coupled to Brownian increments so discrete exponential covariances become spectral-integral covariances; an epsilon regularization separates limits, with uniform L2 bounds and Fourier sampling justifying its removal.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The failure of continuous functional limits is resolved not by hiding roughness but by identifying a randomized Euler-product boundary distribution whose radial blow-up precludes even a local measure representation.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This synthesis concerns the randomized/global statistical limit and does not settle microscopic zeta behavior.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Why the critical-line limit is distribution-valued

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The special real-imaginary dependence generates a Cauchy or Hilbert-transform singularity; analytic one-sided spectral structure turns the apparently nonintegrable two-point function into an L2-bounded generalized-function martingale.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The argument is specific to this covariance and analytic boundary structure, not a universality theorem for arbitrary complex chaos.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: The Hilbert-transform rescue of dependent complex chaos

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: After the first prime harmonic is coupled to a log-correlated Gaussian field, higher prime powers, prime-location irregularity, phase freezing, and coupling errors all converge smoothly, so the singular universal component separates from an arithmetic smooth multiplier.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The decomposition is proved for the randomized Euler-product model; transfer to actual zeta uses the separate global-limit theorem.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Arithmetic is compressed into a smooth factor

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Fourier-sampled test norms and uniform two-point asymptotics control truncation, prime-phase equidistribution identifies each finite randomized product, and Hilbert-valued martingale convergence closes the function-space limit in a fixed order.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The method establishes existence and convergence under the stated Sobolev regularization, not sharp rates or optimal test spaces.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Nested approximation triangle from zeta shifts to randomized Euler products

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Dilation separates an exploding scalar Gaussian mode from a delta-independent strict log chaos; quotienting generalized functions by nonzero scalars makes zeta and CUE converge to the same mesoscopic spatial law.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Only sufficiently slow deterministic shrinking scales are constructed, and equality is modulo scalar factors rather than pointwise equality.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Mesoscopic zero-mode separation and projective universality

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Once prime covariance is identified as one-half logarithmic plus smooth, subcritical uniform integrability and critical covariance comparison transfer Gaussian-chaos phase behavior to normalized absolute powers of randomized zeta.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: For actual zeta shifts the analogous measures remain conjectural because the required moment and correlation asymptotics are unavailable.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Real-chaos phase transition transferred through the smooth error

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The paper can prove the second shifted moment needed for generalized-function convergence, but real and imaginary chaos for actual zeta would demand substantially stronger absolute and multipoint correlations, with zeros adding an extra obstruction for the imaginary part.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: A proof-search failure or missing estimate would not refute the conjectured chaos picture; it identifies the present analytic bottleneck.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Moment asymptotics are the bridge still missing for actual zeta chaos

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Toeplitz determinant asymptotics replace zeta divisor-sum estimates, Gaussian trace limits replace prime-phase equidistribution, and dilation plus Brownian coupling then recover the same mesoscopic chaos component.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The global inputs are model-specific and the paper does not claim that all microscopic statistics coincide.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Random-matrix transfer uses different exact inputs but the same approximation architecture

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Euler-product truncation gives the strongest variance and function-space control through explicit two-point kernels, whereas finite Dirichlet polynomials bypass the hardest mixed estimate but provide weaker quantitative approximation.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These are alternative proofs of the same randomized limit, not independent validation of the limiting law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From spectral analogies to a Young-diagram phase space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects Hilbert-Polya and random-matrix analogies to the paper's concrete plan: model eigenangles as positions, Young-row lengths as momenta, and use their relation to draw a zero-sensitive phase space.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Inverse model design with divergences rather than a zero density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Precisely distinguishes the proposed observable: a no-gap eigenvalue density has logarithmic divergences at mapped zeros, but is not itself identified with the zero distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universality question for free-fermion large-N saddles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Frames the eigenvalue/Young duality as a universality problem and states that extremization, rather than an accidental identification, should produce the h-theta relation for generic plaquette phases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arbitrary-cycle characters block direct Young-density solution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the technical obstruction—no tractable exact arbitrary-cycle character—and the weaker but sufficient target of deriving a boundary relation between row lengths and eigenangles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generic Fourier-coupled unitary one-plaquette model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the parameterized action whose Fourier couplings control phases and later become Li-number coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eigenangle saddle equation with Haar repulsion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows the reusable move from a unitary integral to a continuum eigenvalue density governed by an external Fourier force and cotangent repulsion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resolvent analyticity, reciprocal symmetry, and Dyson-Schwinger closure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces a singular integral by an analytic function inside and outside the unit disk, with R(z)+R(1/z)=1 and a quadratic Dyson-Schwinger solution controlling phases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Density and force as resolvent boundary components
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the bridge from the analytic resolvent to eigenvalue density via its jump/real part and to the potential derivative via its imaginary part.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed zeta as an entire involution-symmetric input
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces xi(s), removes the pole/trivial-zero singularities, and supplies xi(s)=xi(1-s), the symmetry later translated into the resolvent reciprocal condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime product and zero product representations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Places the prime and nontrivial-zero factorizations side by side, enabling the later density calculation and prime-counting comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li coefficients as derivative data and a zero sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States RH equivalence to nonnegativity of all Li coefficients and supplies both the derivative definition and zero-based expression used as model couplings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mapping the critical line to the unit circle
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses s=1/(1-z) to map the critical line to |z|=1, separates the two half-planes by the circle, and transfers zero accumulation and xi symmetry into the unit-disk geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resolvent designed from log xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs inside/outside branches of R from log xi, fixes normalization at z=0, enforces reciprocal symmetry, and exposes logarithmic branch points at mapped zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalized no-gap density with zero-marked logarithmic spikes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the xi product into a density whose logarithmic divergences occur at mapped zero angles while remaining integrable and normalized across the full circle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li numbers as plaquette couplings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches Taylor coefficients of the designed no-gap resolvent to Cauchy representations of Li numbers, producing beta_n=-alpha*lambda_n/n and an explicit matrix action.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero crossings become jumps in the potential derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tracks the imaginary part of log xi across upper- and lower-half-plane zeros to obtain a step function and hence discrete force jumps at mapped zero positions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Resolvent boundary data yields a nonnegative Li cosine sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fourier extraction plus integration by parts converts Li coefficients into a sum of terms 1-cos(n theta_i), making positivity manifest inside the proposed unit-circle construction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From trace powers to a sum over Young diagrams
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the plaquette exponential by cycle counts, decomposes trace monomials into symmetric-group characters, uses U(N) character orthogonality, and recasts the partition function as a representation sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Young density and constant-density droplet marginals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the large-N row variable and Young density, then formulates eigenvalue and Young densities as marginals of one constant phase-space distribution whose boundary carries the phase information.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Frobenius coefficient formula for arbitrary cycle data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the available exact character representation for arbitrary conjugacy classes through power sums, a Vandermonde factor, and coefficient extraction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Frobenius auxiliary variables recover the eigenvalue saddle and boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Exponentiates the Frobenius contour integral, takes a large-N saddle on the unit circle, identifies its imaginary part with the eigenvalue equation, and obtains a real algebraic relation between h and theta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Even-function redundancy in the Young boundary equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the character action cannot distinguish h(theta) from h(theta)+f(theta) for even f, so different Young distributions can correspond to the same eigenvalue density.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partition-level identification of auxiliary variables with eigenvalues
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extremizes the full representation integral, obtains conjugate unit-circle saddle variables, fixes cycle counts by Fourier moments, and recovers the original eigenvalue partition function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: No-gap and multi-gap topology fix boundary separation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constrains the boundary redundancy by droplet topology: a no-gap phase has boundaries 0 and 2*pi*rho, while a multi-gap phase has two nonzero boundaries separated by 2*pi*rho.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complex phase-space distribution combines density and potential
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines Omega(h,theta) so its real marginal gives eigenvalue density, its imaginary marginal gives the potential derivative, and its theta marginal gives Young density; real topology varies by phase while imaginary topology is model-fixed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One spiky density supports multiple normalized Young representations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the no-gap boundary to the Riemann-zero density and explains how nonmonotonicity yields multiple monotone branches and hence multiple dominant representations for the same eigenvalue distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Broom-shaped zero phase space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets positive h radially and periodic theta angularly, turning density spikes into sticks positioned at mapped Riemann zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-counting fluctuation as an alternative phase-space variable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the prime-counting function and its Mellin relation to log zeta to rewrite the same resolvent through a distribution over the fluctuating prime-counting component J-tilde.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Non-injective Young/prime correspondence and canonical-transform suggestion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares the many inverse branches of J-tilde to the multiple Young branches, proposes h corresponding to J-tilde and u(h) to an inverse-x quantity, and suggests—but does not prove—a canonical relation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Limits of the free-fermion interpretation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the classical large-N droplet from a still-unknown quantum many-body theory, notes compact group-manifold and trigonometric-boundary differences, and explicitly says theta=pi*u(h) is unproved.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace logarithmic spikes by an exact zero-counting density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposes a sharper follow-up model whose density is the derivative of the zero-counting step function, to retest the Young/prime relation when eigenvalues are concentrated directly at zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Product formula to log-sine eigenvalue density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the xi product at conjugate unit-circle boundary points and reduces it to the log-sine expression used for zero-marked density spikes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Direct and contour normalization of the density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Checks that the proposed singular density integrates to the required total using zero symmetry and independently ties normalization to the resolvent contour integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lagrange-multiplier route to theta=pi*u(h)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adds a multiplier enforcing Young-density constraints, varies a positive-factor representation of h, and selects a sign-dependent multiplier to motivate the theta=pi*u(h) identification.

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The paper does not solve the full generic dominant Young density, and the theta=pi*u(h) step remains heuristic.

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source reports resemblance and a canonical-transform suggestion, not an established symplectic map or a proof that primes and zeros form conjugate variables.
