result_and_mechanism_map.title: Leading-order theorem and log-correlated comparison
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the typical short-interval maximum theorem and connects nearby zeta values to logarithmic covariance and random-matrix characteristic polynomials, motivating why extreme-value rather than independent-value heuristics apply.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic transfer and prime-block proof architecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the easy upper bound from the lower-bound pipeline: move right of the critical line, mollify zeta, approximate by short prime sums, and organize primes into near-equal-variance blocks.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second moment under multiscale correlation and the branching-tree model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how a mesh of candidate points, one- and two-point large deviations, and near/far pair separation overcome correlations; it then identifies the approximate rooted-tree dependence underlying the prime blocks.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sobolev and moment control of the short-interval upper bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows the reusable move of controlling a continuum supremum by endpoint values plus a derivative integral, then closing the probability estimate with second moments of zeta and its derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lower bound as a prime-block simultaneous exceedance problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the shifted line and scale-separated prime polynomials, isolates exceptional first/last blocks, and reduces the zeta maximum to finding one location where all retained blocks are high.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal mean values and Gaussian moments of prime polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the analytic bridge from averaging Dirichlet polynomials over height to diagonal combinatorics, Bessel-product moments, and high-moment bounds that later justify Gaussian transforms and tail control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson-kernel transfer from a shifted line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Carries the mechanism that represents shifted-line zeta values as a weighted average of critical-line values and uses it to make a nearby shifted large value force critical-line mass.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncated Möbius mollifier as a typical inverse to shifted zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs a finite reciprocal surrogate with controlled prime support and number of factors, then proves that its product with shifted zeta is close to one on average by separating diagonal Euler-product and error terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From mean-square mollification to uniform short-interval inversion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Upgrades pointwise-in-height mean-square control to simultaneous control over every point in a short interval by applying the same Sobolev, Chebyshev, and Cauchy-Schwarz pattern to the mollified product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Separating prime sums from von Mangoldt prime-power corrections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes the logarithmic polynomial into prime and prime-power pieces and proves uniform exceptional-set bounds using Sobolev plus high moments, preventing prime powers or rare block spikes from corrupting the exponential approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recovering the mollifier from the exponential of prime blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches the finite Möbius mollifier to a truncated exponential of logarithmic prime sums, bounds the Taylor tail on a typical set, and controls coefficient mismatches caused by excessive or oversized prime powers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Assembling shifted-line transfer, inversion, and prime blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Composes the three analytic approximations into a direct lower-bound comparison from the critical-line zeta maximum to the retained prime-block sum, including why the exceptional first and last blocks can be discarded.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Block moments encode variance and distance-dependent covariance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that joint moments of prime blocks at two nearby points match a Gaussian system over a wide range and quantifies when blocks remain correlated or decorrelate with separation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bessel Euler products yield the Gaussian main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how the prime-polynomial moment formula factorizes into Bessel terms, whose quadratic exponential is exactly the Gaussian moment-generating function while higher analytic factors are negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncating rare values before passing from moments to transforms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a high-probability cutoff so rare extremes cannot dominate Fourier-Laplace transforms, then uses Taylor truncation and restricted-to-unrestricted moment replacement to recover one- and two-point Gaussian transforms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair tails remember the last shared correlation scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses exponential tilting with the two-point transform to bound simultaneous exceedances, treating early shared blocks differently from later decorrelated blocks according to separation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothed contour inversion gives Gaussian tails and far-pair factorization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces a sharp indicator by a contour-represented smoothing, controls transform tails and cutoff errors, and shows that small cross-covariances make well-separated joint exceedances asymptotically factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fine-mesh high points via near/far pair decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Places logarithmically many candidate points on a short interval, estimates the first moment, splits pair contributions by separation scale, and uses Cauchy-Schwarz/Paley-Zygmund to show a high point exists with probability tending to one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gram and Riemann-Siegel formulas separate by cutoff scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper frames computational strength through the number of retained Dirichlet terms: Euler-Maclaurin asymptotics force a Gram-scale O(|t|) main sum, while the Riemann-Siegel formula uses about O(sqrt(t)) terms. This supplies the baseline criterion later used to classify smoothed expansions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complementary-error smoothing removes the discrete-cutoff discontinuity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two convergent/smoothed representations replace the sharp Riemann-Siegel upper limit by a complementary-error transition that is near one below the cutoff and decays above it. The text explicitly connects smoothing to continuity in t while retaining the Riemann-Siegel-scale cutoff.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simple smoothing forces a less efficient Gram-type cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This is the paper's governing negative result: although a free parameter permits exponential or real-error-function smoothing, asymptotic correction and remainder terms force the transition to occur after O(t) terms. It separates aesthetic simplicity of the smoothing rule from computational efficiency.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin-Perron construction of an incomplete-gamma-smoothed Dirichlet sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Mellin integral for the incomplete gamma function is inserted into an absolutely convergent sum, summation and integration are reversed, and contour displacement across the poles at zero and 1-s produces the basic smoothed zeta representation. This is the analytic bridge from a smoothing kernel to zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shifting yields the generalized expansion and its computational admissibility condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moving the remainder contour across gamma poles and applying the zeta functional relation yields a finite correction series plus a remainder, which combines with the smoothed main sum into the generalized expansion. The coefficients unusually contain zeta itself, so usefulness requires a parameter regime in which those zeta values are computable by a convergent Dirichlet series; the earlier formula appears as a special case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The remainder is reduced to a weighted gamma-ratio integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After fixing the remainder contour and applying the zeta functional relation, elementary gamma/hyperbolic estimates reduce |R_M| to an integral governed by a gamma-function ratio F. The appendix-supplied facts that F is even and increasing, while its scaled form G decreases in the relevant regime, create the monotone structure needed for a usable bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Monotonicity turns the remainder integral into an incomplete-gamma bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The integral is split at t, monotonic bounds on the scaled gamma ratio control the tails, and the remaining integral is evaluated as an incomplete gamma function. A standard incomplete-gamma inequality then gives a simpler explicit estimate when X exceeds N.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The final bound has a coefficient that loses moderate size beyond an M-scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The derived critical-strip bound isolates a computable coefficient G_p(M;t). The reported values agree with its fixed-M asymptotic behavior at low M but show that it ceases to be order one once M exceeds an approximate (t/2)^(2/3)/p scale, foreshadowing why the bound deteriorates well before optimal truncation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential smoothing inherits a forced Gram-scale cutoff
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Choosing a=1 converts the incomplete-gamma kernel to a real exponential and integer p simplifies the correction coefficients. Large-order behavior of those corrections imposes K > t/(2 pi), so the nominal switch-off near n approximately K necessarily retains O(t) terms and the formula is Gram-type.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Optimal truncation and sharper smoothing pull accuracy in opposite directions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The correction series initially decreases and then diverges, with an estimated optimal index depending sensitively on p and the scale ratio. Increasing p suppresses the main-sum tail and makes shifted zeta values easier, but eventually destroys asymptotic character and raises the least correction term, limiting attainable accuracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line specialization separates optimal from practically sufficient truncation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For p=1 and K=t/(2 pi), the paper specializes the expansion and remainder bound on the critical line, then shows numerically that optimal truncation can be enormous while much smaller, deliberately suboptimal truncations already deliver high accuracy for larger t. The t=10 case also shows that optimal truncation need not imply uniformly spectacular accuracy at modest height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The rigorous remainder bound is realistic only far below optimal truncation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Direct comparison of actual Z(t) error with the proved bound shows close tracking for modest M, followed by rapid deterioration around M proportional to t and uselessness at optimal truncation. This distinguishes true expansion accuracy from sharpness of the available proof technique.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Increasing K buys accuracy with more main-sum work, while increasing p can reduce accuracy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The controlled computation separates two knobs: increasing K raises attainable accuracy at the cost of moving the effective cutoff outward, whereas increasing p sharpens exponential tail decay but lowers the optimal correction-series truncation and worsens its least term. This is a concrete multi-objective design constraint.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Complementary-error-function smoothing is simple but remains Gram-type
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selecting a=1/2 changes the kernel from an exponential to erfc while leaving the correction-series asymptotic constraint intact. With p=1 on the critical line, K must again be of order t/(2 pi), so changing the simple smoothing function alone does not recover Riemann-Siegel efficiency.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The argument geometry of the smoothing kernel controls the cutoff class
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Berry-Keating error-function argument depends logarithmically on n/N_t and cuts off at Riemann-Siegel scale, whereas the paper's fixed-order incomplete-gamma choices yield Gram scale. The contrast motivates the proposed transition study between a=O(1) and the s-dependent choice a=s/2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Crude absolute bounds conceal possible optimal-truncation accuracy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper identifies the failure of its remainder estimate past moderate M as an artifact of crude inequalities and proposes analysis that retains integrand oscillation. It carefully separates an unproved assumption of asymptoticity from numerical indications of potentially enormous accuracy at optimal truncation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial-zero cancellation transforms the generalized formula into its symmetric special case
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Setting a=s/2 and p=1 leaves a single contour pole because other gamma poles cancel against zeta's trivial zeros. After the functional equation and a variable reversal, the residual integral matches the original Mellin form with transformed s and reciprocal scale, revealing a dual smoothed sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Absolute convergence and analytic continuation recover the critical-line expansion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The two-sum expansion is first justified in an angular domain by incomplete-gamma decay, extended by analytic continuation, and then specialized through a scale choice and conjugacy to obtain the earlier convergent formula on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A gamma-function ratio is even and increasing above a parameter threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A product representation makes F even, and logarithmic differentiation expresses its derivative with a sign that is positive for x>0 when the parameter exceeds one half. This supplies the monotonicity invoked when bounding the remainder integral.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scaling removes gamma-ratio growth and exposes the eventual monotonic sign
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The dominant power growth of F is factored out to define G tending to one. Its large-x expansion identifies a parameter regime with eventual decrease and records a closed boundary-case expression, providing the normalization used throughout the remainder analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An integral-sign argument proves global decrease of the scaled gamma ratio
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A gamma identity and product representation convert the logarithmic derivative of G into integral expressions. Two integrations by parts reduce its sign to positivity of a sine transform of a positive decreasing function, proving G decreases for x>0 when a>1; numerical computation suggests a lower threshold but is explicitly separate from the proof.

section_argument_map.label: 1. Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Compares Gram, Riemann-Siegel, and smoothed formulas; identifies cutoff scale, smoothing shape, discontinuity removal, and the paper's simple-smoothing-versus-efficiency tradeoff.

section_argument_map.label: 2. A generalised expansion for zeta(s)
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds the incomplete-gamma-smoothed representation from a Mellin/Perron integral, contour displacement, residues, and the zeta functional relation, then states its computational admissibility condition and special case.

section_argument_map.label: 3. A bound on R_M when a > 0
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Reduces the remainder integral to gamma-ratio estimates, uses monotonicity and incomplete-gamma bounds, and diagnoses the parameter range in which the bound coefficient remains moderate.

section_argument_map.label: 4. An exponentially-smoothed main sum
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Specializes to exponential smoothing, derives the forced Gram-scale cutoff and optimal truncation, analyzes the free smoothing parameter, and compares actual numerical error with the rigorous remainder bound.

section_argument_map.label: 5. Concluding remarks
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Contrasts the complementary-error-function specialization with Berry-Keating smoothing, identifies a possible transition in the free parameter, and isolates the non-sharp remainder analysis as the main unresolved bottleneck.

section_argument_map.label: Appendix B. Monotonicity of F and G
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves evenness and monotonicity of an unscaled gamma ratio and a sufficient monotone-decrease regime for its scaled form, supporting the remainder estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short-interval moments split into four sigma regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper defines its common moment functional and explains why integer moments and the functional equation reduce the study to four qualitatively different regions, with the critical line singled out as the hard case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Absolute convergence turns moments into a diagonal main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expanding zeta^k as a divisor-coefficient Dirichlet series separates equal indices from oscillatory unequal indices; absolute convergence makes the latter bounded and yields a short-interval main term proportional to H.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: At sigma=1, global error control yields short-interval asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates the pole-adjacent mean-square error, connects its pointwise bound to zeta on the 1-line, and records complex-k, logarithmic-derivative, and log-zeta mean values that imply a linear short-interval asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Secondary terms and error scales inside the critical strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The mean square and fourth moment develop additional main terms away from sigma=1, and comparison of the spectral fourth-moment error with those terms identifies where the nominal expansion ceases to be informative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher-moment remainders are parameterized by sigma-star
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: general-moment control by a critical abscissa
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After special low moments stop generalizing, the source expresses a general 2k-th moment remainder in terms of the least line on which a T^(1+epsilon) moment bound is available and shows how this produces explicit but nonuniform exponents.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two controls dominate in complementary parts of the strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source compares a divisor-problem mean-square parameter with the moment-abscissa parameter, explaining that one controls remainders near sigma=1 while the other is better near its threshold, then instantiates the comparison for several moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramachandra's kernel transports a lower bound across sigma
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A lower bound in the absolutely convergent region is carried to the critical strip by a residue representation with double-exponential horizontal decay, followed by two parameter choices that first prevent the target integral from being tiny and then close the bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Atkinson represents the mean-square error by dual oscillatory sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The critical-line mean-square error is converted into two explicit oscillatory sums with complementary ranges, making the error term accessible to cancellation estimates rather than only integral identities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-Siegel sums and error increments control local zeta size
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A structurally different Riemann-Siegel-based formula estimates the same error term, and a local averaging inequality turns increments of E into pointwise control of zeta, exposing how global error exponents set short-interval asymptotic thresholds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian smoothing opens a spectral route to the fourth-moment error
result_and_mechanism_map.unit_type: spectral representation of a smoothed fourth moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Motohashi's Gaussian-smoothed fourth moment is expressed through spectral data via trace formulas; resulting upper, omega, and mean-square bounds for E2 translate into a concrete short-interval length at which a fourth-moment asymptotic is unconditional.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line higher moments expose both equivalences and bottlenecks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey contrasts the lone strong twelfth-moment bound with absent asymptotics for k>=3, identifies all-moment T^(1+epsilon) bounds as equivalent to Lindelof, and links the sixth moment to a ternary additive divisor conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line moments have the conjectured logarithmic lower scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 strengthens the general lower bound on the critical line to H times a k-squared logarithmic power and records the arithmetic Euler-product constant and the log-log interval threshold.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large values replace pointwise RH bounds in moment control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explains why known unconditional upper bounds are sparse, distinguishes RH from Lindelof, and contrasts a weak pointwise RH consequence with Soundararajan's essentially sharp full-interval moment bound based on the distribution of log|zeta|.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The full-interval large-values method localizes to H=T^theta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 gives an RH-conditional upper bound matching the lower-bound logarithmic scale up to a vanishing exponent loss, while explicitly recording the fixed-power interval restriction and known exceptional low-moment ranges.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Log|zeta| tails have Gaussian and V log V regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 4 partitions the admissible large-value range into two near-Gaussian decay regimes and a far-tail V log V regime, with explicit theta-dependent losses suited to a short interval.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discretized tails reduce the moment bound to a quadratic maximum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Small and very large values are disposed of directly, the middle range is discretized, and multiplying its measure by exp(2kU) reduces the problem to maximizing a concave quadratic, recovering the k-squared logarithmic exponent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH turns large log|zeta| into a large prime polynomial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Three lemmas upper-bound log|zeta| by a smoothed Dirichlet polynomial, show prime powers contribute only a small error, and control high moments of prime polynomials on a short interval under the length-budget condition x^r<=H.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-range splitting converts moment estimates into tail decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof chooses a V-dependent polynomial length, splits primes at a secondary cutoff, forces one piece to be large, and applies high moments with optimized integer orders to obtain Gaussian or V log V decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The second prime range is bounded and the three tail regimes close
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A parallel high-moment bound controls the longer-prime piece, case-specific choices verify the short-interval length constraint, and comparison with the first-piece bounds yields each of Theorem 4's three stated estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Type II off-diagonal terms as a multidimensional circle-method problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the paper's reusable strategic reframing: moments of long Dirichlet polynomials require systematic treatment of Type II off-diagonal terms, viewed as a multidimensional Hardy-Littlewood circle method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole-subtracted long Dirichlet polynomials for shifted moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the shifted coefficient family tau_A, the smoothed moment, Perron truncation, and residue subtraction that lets a finite polynomial represent the intended shifted-zeta average at large length.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Recipe terms encoded as equal-cardinality signed swaps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the moment recipe into a combinatorial transformation on shift sets: remove equal-sized subsets, negate them across the two sides, and track the resulting arithmetic factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet-polynomial length selects the maximum swap depth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how the factor (X/T^{|U|})^{w+z} suppresses terms beyond a threshold, so T^ell<=X<T^{ell+1} determines which swap cardinalities survive.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Convolution partition of the off-diagonal mean square
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the smoothed mean square term-by-term, decomposes tau_A and tau_B into ell convolutions, and explains why ordered pairings of the component sets become relevant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rational-direction stratification prevents missing delta-method main terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the central obstruction to a naive delta-method application: solutions must be stratified by rational directions M_j/N_j under a coupled product constraint, with discrepancies h_j measuring distance from each direction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Refined Type II sum and weighted partition conjecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the rationally stratified sum O^dagger, averages it over decompositions with a later-justified weight, and states that this reconstructs the pole-subtracted shifted moment up to power saving.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Delta-method averaging with all discrepancies nonzero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces coupled shifted-divisor sums by local averages expressed through Ramanujan sums and additive twists, converting discrete correlation data into contour integrals over continuous size variables.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rescaling discrepancies and enforcing the product range by Perron inversion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The variables v_j=T|h_j|/(2pi u_jN_j) isolate the oscillatory scale, while a Perron integral detects the coupled product bound and gathers the result into the common LHS_ell expression.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theorem 1: analytic Type II expression equals the ell-swap recipe contribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the key rigorous identity that identifies the transformed all-nonzero correlation expression with recipe terms choosing one shifted element from every paired block.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sign-summed Fourier integrals collapse through contour rotation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Generalizes the one-dimensional Fourier identity by integrating variables from the inside out, rotating positive and negative sign contours, and producing gamma/chi factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shift poles cancel truncation residues and trigger the zeta functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands additive-twist averages at poles near one, sums discrepancies into zeta factors, identifies residues that cancel the earlier R_A,R_B subtraction, and then converts remaining factors with the functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global identity reduced to a primewise Euler-factor identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reorganizes the transformed integrand so equality with the recipe is reduced, for each chosen swap, to equality of two Euler products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Formal power-series encoding and Theorem 2
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Suppresses the prime and divisor notation to work in X=1/p, introduces cumulative coefficient identities and C(A,B), and states the local identity whose right side is precisely a swapped Euler factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three local lemmas separate boundary kernels, convolution, and inclusion-exclusion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Decomposes Theorem 2 into explicit formulas for Sigma(M,0) and Sigma(0,N), a diagonal convolution identity F=C, and an inclusion-exclusion expansion of the swapped Euler factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Assembly of the local identity from the three lemmas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that expanding each local Sigma term yields the same disjoint-subset inclusion-exclusion expression as the swapped Euler factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary splitting makes the local Sigma kernel telescope
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the d-sum at d=M, telescopes the finite and infinite pieces, recognizes a convolution, and obtains the three-term boundary formula, with the N case by symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal convolution identity via the minimum of paired indices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves F=C for arbitrary coefficient sequences by Fourier-enforcing equal totals and uniquely decomposing each pair (R,S) by K=min(R,S).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local swapped product expands over disjoint subset choices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies a one-pair three-term identity independently across blocks and integrates equal total degree, yielding the signed sum over disjoint choices J1,J2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero discrepancies become exact rational directions and lower the active dimension
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When h_j=0, coprimality forces m_j=kappa_jM_j and n_j=kappa_jN_j; factoring these exact directions changes the length cutoff and leaves a lower-dimensional nonzero correlation problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mixed-stratum Perron expression and Theorem 3

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Active poles plus diagonal factors reduce to a hybrid local identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the earlier pole/functional-equation mechanism on active blocks with untouched diagonal divisor factors, then reduces the residue at s'=0 to an Euler-product equality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theorem 4: hybrid Euler factor for active and diagonal blocks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the local identity that combines Sigma factors for active blocks with ordinary shifted-divisor coefficients for zero-discrepancy blocks, producing the corresponding partial-swap Euler factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Earlier local lemmas extend to the hybrid identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substitutes the boundary Sigma formula, then uses the same convolution and inclusion-exclusion identities with all blocks in C but only active blocks in the swap factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Every fixed ell-swap is repeated by block decompositions with one marked element each

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same multiplicity counts representations by direction-discrepancy systems

result_and_mechanism_map.title: All discrepancy strata collectively reproduce all surviving swap terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Summarizes the causal correspondence: all nonzero h_j give ell swaps, exactly ell-prime nonzero h_j give ell-prime swaps, and summing weighted partitions makes the delta-method and recipe evaluations agree.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how even a suboptimal tail bound can control parameter-dependent interval lengths by first handling impossible extreme lengths and then applying a grid union bound with the zeta second moment.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small primes are nearly rigid across a negative-theta interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Refines the generic prime-polynomial maximum bound by decomposing a short-interval process into its value at one point and a small increment, then proving exponential tails for both via moments and discretization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncating the removed-prime exponential makes mollified zeta discretizable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On a high-probability event, approximates the exponential cutoff by a finite Dirichlet polynomial, combines it with the smoothed zeta approximation, and invokes the general grid inequality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive-theta upper bounds optimize moment order and high-point entropy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses the moment exponent matched to the predicted maximum, then handles supercritical beta by stratifying the integral into high-point levels, making the linear frozen exponent emerge from endpoint domination.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Negative-theta upper bounds repeat the variational argument after deleting common scales
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits zeta into a mollified field and its small-prime factor, uses concentration to discard the latter, and optimizes moments with the reduced effective variance to recover both subcritical and frozen exponents.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The lower bound is organized as approximation followed by a multiscale second moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the moment and maximum lower targets and makes explicit that the maximum will follow from moments after off-axis approximation, mollification, and high-point analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gabriel log-convexity makes an interior vertical-line norm no larger than the boundary norm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages analyticity and decay into a strip interpolation inequality and derives a monotonic domination from the critical boundary into the half-plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An entire Fourier localizer approximates a rectangle while decaying outside it
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs an entire function from a rescaled smooth transform, proves interior approximation, exterior decay, controlled off-axis growth, and decay in the real direction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic localization transfers an off-axis moment to a slightly enlarged critical-line interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the entire localizer and Gabriel convexity to a finite zeta approximation, then unsmooths by controlling the central window and summing rapidly decaying exterior annuli.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A theta-sensitive finite mollifier uniformly inverts zeta on the whole interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adapts pointwise L2 mollification to a growing grid by increasing the allowed factor count with theta, then upgrades the mean-square estimate to uniform interval control through discretization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The mollifier equals an exponential prime-power field up to a rare high-factor tail
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the Euler product logarithm to convert a multiplicative inverse into an additive prime-power polynomial and controls the truncation discrepancy uniformly by Rankin weighting, a mean-value estimate, and discretization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime scales are chosen for nearly equal variance while endpoint blocks are removed to enforce decorrelation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the scale increments, explains equal variance, and identifies why the first and last blocks are omitted: one would preserve unwanted long-range correlation and the other would distort variance balance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: High-point volume converts into the piecewise free-energy exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a high-point entropy function, lower-bounds the moment integral by level-set volume, and optimizes beta times height plus entropy, yielding an interior quadratic optimizer below criticality and endpoint domination above it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theta-dependent removal of early blocks reduces high-point abundance to Paley-Zygmund
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For negative theta, discards the shared early scales, chooses slightly elevated per-block barriers, defines the high-point volume, and reduces the desired entropy lower bound to concentration of that volume.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-point Gaussian tails and separation-dependent two-point bounds encode branching
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the local probabilistic inputs: a product Gaussian-tail asymptotic, asymptotic independence beyond the branching scale, and an exponential bound when two points share early increments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partitioning pairs by distance isolates the independent bulk and suppresses correlated diagonals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the first moment, applies Paley-Zygmund, divides the pair integral by branching distance, and shows only the far-separated region contributes at leading order while every near-diagonal band is negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Off-axis transfer, mollifier replacement, and block trimming assemble the moment lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chains the previously isolated reductions in their precise order and shows that prime powers and endpoint blocks can each be removed with negligible loss before invoking the multiscale lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A sufficiently high moment lower bound forces the predicted maximum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the frozen linear branch of the moment exponent and the elementary L-beta-to-L-infinity comparison to derive the maximum lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime number theorem sums give both variance growth and logarithmic covariance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records the prime-sum asymptotics that repeatedly convert Euler products into log powers and cosine sums into correlation lengths.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short Dirichlet polynomials are orthogonal on average up to an explicit length error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Supplies the diagonal-dominance principle used to evaluate polynomial L2 norms and truncation errors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-sum moments are approximately Gaussian and yield covariance and tail estimates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects exact moment generating products to a Gaussian variance, permits removal of early primes, and derives the large-deviation scale used in the multiscale argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A crude factorial moment estimate provides rapid exceptional-set control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives the flexible upper-moment inequality repeatedly used for maximum tails, prime-power errors, and discarded events when sharp Gaussian asymptotics are unnecessary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH as simultaneous hyperbolicity of completed-zeta Jensen polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span converts a statement about all nontrivial zeta zeros into real-rootedness of a two-parameter family built from Taylor coefficients at the symmetry point, and notes that differentiation makes the unshifted family sufficient. It is the paper's exact conceptual entry point from RH to finite polynomials.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Locally quadratic log-growth forces a Hermite Jensen limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 isolates a reusable mechanism: after centering and scaling, fixed-degree Jensen polynomials converge to Hermite polynomials when short coefficient ratios have an asymptotically linear-minus-quadratic logarithm. Stability of simple real roots then turns convergence into eventual hyperbolicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative-aspect Hermite limits as a GUE-compatible normal form
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors separate two limiting aspects and argue that Hermite roots supply the derivative-aspect random-matrix prediction, while degree growth connects unshifted Jensen roots to completed-zeta zeros. This is a conceptual bridge between local coefficient geometry and global zero-statistics heuristics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolicity asymptotics as a criterion for partition log-concavity phenomena
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This span explains why the general Hermite criterion matters beyond zeta: real-rooted Jensen polynomials control higher log-concavity in enumerative sequences, and the partition function supplies a concrete eventual-hyperbolicity conjecture with finite threshold evidence and an effective-but-large bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weakly holomorphic modular-form coefficients inherit eventual Jensen hyperbolicity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The partition sequence is reframed as a modular-form coefficient sequence, leading to a general theorem for real Fourier coefficients of weakly holomorphic modular forms. The span also identifies a common proof architecture: verify one universal asymptotic criterion separately for each sequence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-difference cancellation selects the limiting polynomial family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 6 shows that a general local ratio expansion produces a polynomial family determined by a formal generating series. Its proof exposes the reusable algebraic engine: the relevant finite difference kills all powers below the required order and retains exactly the matching coefficient, with the Hermite case arising from a Gaussian generating series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bessel coefficient asymptotics verify the Hermite criterion for modular forms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof turns a classical Bessel asymptotic for modular-form coefficients into an all-orders short-shift log-ratio expansion, explicitly identifying the linear and quadratic scales required by Theorem 3. It is a clean transfer from global coefficient growth to local polynomial geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed-zeta derivatives become moments of a theta-kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span replaces high central derivatives of the completed zeta function by moments of a positive theta-kernel and then expresses the Jensen coefficient sequence through neighboring even moments. This representation change makes saddle-point localization available.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: All-orders saddle parameterization and an effective two-term coefficient approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 7 parameterizes the dominant region by the unique positive saddle L and supplies an expansion to arbitrary algebraic order. The accompanying two-term approximation is explicitly strong enough for the eventual zeta hyperbolicity proof and demonstrates why leading-order asymptotics alone are insufficient for the required ratio control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Saddle localization plus exponentially small theta-tail control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof identifies a unique maximum, expands multiplicatively around it, integrates Gaussian moments to generate successive corrections, and justifies replacing the full theta kernel by its leading exponential because the discarded terms are smaller than every algebraic order near the saddle. This is the analytic engine behind Theorem 7.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short-shift expansion verifies eventual fixed-degree hyperbolicity for zeta coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This span applies the universal criterion to gamma(n): analytic control of the implicit saddle and correction factors yields a Taylor expansion of log gamma(n+j)/gamma(n), identifies a positive vanishing quadratic scale, and bounds higher coefficients strongly enough for every fixed degree. Theorem 1 then follows from Hermite convergence and root stability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite verification plus a certified asymptotic tail proves degrees at most eight
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof of the all-shift finite-degree result is a hybrid certificate: direct Hermite-criterion checks cover n up to one million, while coefficient neighborhoods around the limiting Hermite polynomial and explicit uniform ratio bounds cover the infinite tail. The d=4 inequalities illustrate how a stability neighborhood is made effective.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher-order normalization accelerates visible Hermite convergence but may fail at small shifts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The example explains why a two-term local normalization is chosen even though a one-term normalization suffices asymptotically: it converges faster and makes the Hermite model visible earlier. The footnote that delta(6) is not real records a concrete small-index limitation of the asymptotic coordinates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orthogonal symmetry produces the k(k-1)/2 moment exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects a concrete class of self-dual L-function families to the orthogonal moment exponent, central-value parity behavior, and functional-equation scaling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Characteristic-polynomial limits predict the universal constants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps each symmetry type to a large-rank Gamma-product limit and explains why the Gamma(1+B(lambda)) normalization is retained to preserve arithmetic meaning and integral special values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic continuation at lambda=1/2 predicts a constrained zeta moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a nonintegral random-matrix constant to make a numerical first-moment prediction and compares it with an RH-conditional bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A common reciprocal-polynomial mollifier and the unitary response
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a family-independent mollifier from coefficients of L(s)^{-1}, then gives the unitary quadratic functional that exposes how mollifier length enters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The orthogonal short-mollifier limit is anomalous
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the orthogonal mollified mean square has a qualitatively unexpected limit as mollifier length shrinks, suggesting sensitivity to low-lying zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Differentiation interchanges symplectic and orthogonal mollified responses
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies M_Sp(P,Q',theta) with M_O(P,Q,theta), turning previously observed coincidences between distinct nonvanishing arguments into a symmetry-level operator relation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole data and growth identify normalized g_lambda with double Gamma expressions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages nonvanishing, order, pole multiplicities, Barnes double-Gamma representations, and cross-symmetry identities into an analytic continuation of the universal constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A second Gamma difference controls meromorphic order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the logarithm of the unitary product as a second finite difference of log Gamma, bounds it through a second-derivative estimate, and reads exact order from pole convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite factorial products expose integrality and prime support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States integrality and prime-divisor restrictions, gives finite factorial/double-factorial formulas for all symmetry types, and derives the unitary product from the random-matrix limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Floor-sum valuations prove integrality term by term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Regroups nested factorial products, derives exact p-adic floor-sum expressions, and proves every scale contribution is a nonnegative integer via a two-case residue analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime valuations converge to a scale-invariant distance series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines c_p by a bilateral distance-to-nearest-integer series, identifies it as the scaling limit of valuations, and classifies local behavior at rational points as self-similarity, cusp, or vertical tangent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A periodic seed generates a continuous discrete-scale covariant function

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Split negative, intermediate, and tail scales to analyze local behavior

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Floor-valued p-adic sums converge to distance-to-integer energy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unifies two valuation cases, rescales k=[p^j x], controls the infinite tails uniformly, and converts the limiting floor expression to ||p^ell x||^2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry-dependent constants have explicit large-k expansions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives distinct large-k expansions for unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic g_k and explains that their combination with Gamma asymptotics fixes the Barnes double-Gamma representations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factorial products reduce the asymptotics to four Euler-Maclaurin sums

section_argument_map.label: 4. Meromorphicity of g_lambda

section_argument_map.label: 5. Integrality results

section_argument_map.label: 7. Asymptotics
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives large-k expansions for all three symmetry constants from factorial products and Euler-Maclaurin summation, closing the double-Gamma identification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three conductor-ordered families and their symmetry classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes large-weight GL2, large-level GL2, and symmetric-square GL3 families, then uses self-duality and functional-equation signs to predict O/SO parity types versus Sp.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scaled low-lying zero density as a symmetry observable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the conductor-scaled one-level statistic and states the density conjecture that identifies its family limit with a random-matrix symmetry kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Density theorem across three families and why support past one matters
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the conditional support ranges for parity-split GL2 and symmetric-square densities and explains that crossing Fourier support one activates genuinely new Kloosterman off-diagonal main terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positive band-limited tests convert density into central nonvanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces constrained positive test-function optimization, states the resulting nonvanishing and mean-rank-style bounds, and explains that support extension is what beats diagonal-only thresholds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime exponential-sum cancellation would force a GL2 zero-free region
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Pairs an unconditional parity-mixed weighted density with a stronger prime-progressions hypothesis, then derives extended support and a quasi-Riemann-hypothesis consequence for large-weight GL2 forms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bessel summation, Petersson averaging, and the explicit formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assembles the three transformations used repeatedly: averaging Bessel kernels over weight, replacing form averages by diagonal plus Kloosterman sums, and replacing zeros by prime-power coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit-formula decomposition in the diagonal support regime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how the zero statistic splits into archimedean, prime-square, prime, and higher terms; compact support bounds prime ranges so Petersson plus Weil makes the non-diagonal pieces negligible and leaves the O-density main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extended support turns density positivity into individual zero exclusion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tracks the new oscillatory Bessel term past the diagonal range, controls it by the prime-progressions hypothesis, and uses a nonnegative squared-sinc test to turn the averaged estimate into a bound on each real off-line zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Removing harmonic weights before parity-sensitive averaging
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses GRH to approximate the symmetric-square value by a short Dirichlet series, multiplies it into the explicit formula, and separates diagonal, negligible, and potentially main off-diagonal pieces.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kloosterman-to-character conversion yields the SO parity split
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the surviving prime-linear Petersson term by Bessel averaging, character orthogonality, GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, and a principal-character main term, producing opposite Fourier-tail corrections for the two signs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric-square explicit formula and identification of its exceptional term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the prime coefficients for symmetric squares, introduces the corresponding uniform average, and isolates the prime-square term that becomes a main term only beyond support one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson analysis of the symmetric-square term produces symplectic density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the exceptional Petersson term into arithmetic sums, evaluates a multiplicative Kloosterman aggregate, applies Poisson summation, extracts the zero-frequency main term, and proves the remaining frequencies negligible.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large-level newform normalization and Petersson weights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the level-N functional-equation sign, unfolds an Eisenstein series to identify the first Fourier coefficient and natural harmonic weight, then obtains usable Petersson estimates including a special coefficient involving N.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From harmonic level averages to uniform sign subfamilies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines uniform and sign-projected sums, removes the inverse symmetric-square harmonic weight with a short series, establishes equal leading sizes for the two signs, and states the level-aspect explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Large-level density isolates a single non-diagonal prime term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splits the sign-restricted density average, evaluates the universal and prime-square pieces, and identifies the remaining prime-linear contribution as the only order-N source of symmetry separation beyond support one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The parity-blind large-level off-diagonal term cancels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies Petersson, truncates the modulus, expands primes by residue-class characters, and uses Dirichlet GRH to show both principal and nonprincipal portions of the parity-blind contribution are lower order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The level coefficient creates the orthogonal Fourier-tail correction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inserts the functional-equation sign as a level-N coefficient, factors the Kloosterman sum, removes nonprincipal characters, and evaluates the principal contribution to obtain opposite tail terms and hence SO(even)/SO(odd) densities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nonconstant Fourier-side density makes the standard sinc test suboptimal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the constrained nonnegative band-limited density infimum and observes that a nonconstant Fourier-side correction—created by off-diagonal analysis—prevents the familiar squared-sinc function from attaining it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Density bounds, parity of vanishing, and strict nonvanishing gains
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses positivity and parity of central vanishing order to turn extremal density values into explicit nonvanishing proportions, and shows why splitting signs gives a strict mean-order gain that the parity-mixed O-kernel cannot provide.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Band-limited positivity becomes a Fredholm quadratic minimization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factors admissible positive test functions as squared entire functions, transfers the problem by Plancherel to a convolution quotient, and identifies the minimizer through the equation (I+K)f=1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A projection argument characterizes when squared sinc is optimal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves the Fredholm minimizer by decomposing any normalized competitor into the solution plus an orthogonal remainder, then shows the constant Fourier factor—and hence squared sinc—is optimal exactly when the kernel average is constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Solving the symmetry-kernel Fredholm equations sharpens nonvanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses evenness to reduce the SO kernels to integral equations, solves them by trigonometric functions, and feeds the resulting minimum values back into improved nonvanishing and mean-order bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional zeta as a shifted-convergence Dirichlet series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span distinguishes a complex-plane Caputo construction from the resulting log-weighted Dirichlet series and shows that fractional order shifts the pointwise convergence boundary from Re(s)>1 to Re(s)>1+alpha while recovering integer derivatives.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Asymmetric reflection, symmetric completion, and Xi invariance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The same zeta reflection law is reframed from asymmetric formulas to a completed symmetric form and then compressed into xi(s)=xi(1-s), providing the classical representation target for the fractional construction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Operator replacement exposes a generalized-Leibniz functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source rejects the integral fractional derivative for this derivation, installs the forward Grünwald–Letnikov difference limit because it satisfies generalized Leibniz, and states the resulting triple-infinite-series functional equation and its overflow bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The alpha-translated strip from mismatched zeta and eta convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source combines the Euler-product zero-free baseline with convergence of zeta^(alpha) on Re(s)>1+alpha and eta^(alpha) on Re(s)>alpha to motivate (alpha,1+alpha) as a translated analogue of the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integer-derivative functional equations as the fractional template
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite higher-derivative reflection formulas and Apostol exponential form establish the representation that the paper later extends by replacing finite Leibniz expansion with its fractional infinite counterpart.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential repackaging reduces the fractional equation to one infinite series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span rewrites the classical sine factor as a difference of exponentials, differentiates the packaged product, proves the exponential factor's fractional response, and states Theorem 3.3 with one rather than three infinite sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential packaging turns reflection differentiation into product differentiation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introducing psi isolates the completed zeta factor from a pair of exponentials, so repeated differentiation becomes a finite Leibniz sum whose exponential derivatives are simple powers of w; this is the structural bridge used in the fractional generalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponentials are eigenfunctions of the forward fractional difference operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 3.2 evaluates the Grünwald–Letnikov binomial series on exp((1-s)w), converting the fractional difference limit into multiplication by a phase and w^alpha under Re(w)<0.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A sine-cosine alternative to the compressed fractional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3.4 reorganizes the costly equation by expanding sin(pi(s+j)/2), collecting coefficient series, and expressing the fractional functional equation as sine and cosine components relevant to harmonic analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A completed fractional expression invariant under reflection up to phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The span derives the reflection phase for fractional zeta derivatives, fractionally differentiates the completed classical equation, expands gamma and pi factors, and constructs T_alpha satisfying reflection symmetry up to a multiplicative constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional differentiation under s-to-1-s introduces a phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the forward difference definition to zeta(1-s), followed by a binomial-series limit, yields D^alpha zeta(1-s)=exp(-i*pi*alpha) zeta^(alpha)(1-s), isolating the precise obstruction to exact symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generalized Leibniz expansion links eta^(alpha) to zeta derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Differentiating eta=(1-2^(1-s))zeta with the generalized Leibniz rule expresses eta^(alpha) and the even-index log-weighted series as an infinite combination of lower fractional derivatives of zeta, with finite truncation at integer order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional eta-zeta expansion truncates to finite Leibniz sums at integer order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The alpha-to-zero comparison and explicit first-, second-, and m-th-order identities show how the infinite fractional series reduces to ordinary finite Leibniz expansions, furnishing a structural consistency check rather than numerical evidence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nonmultiplicativity and unknown derivative zeros block the direct prime route
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source states why differentiating the Euler product is unavailable for log^alpha weights and why known information about zeros of integer zeta derivatives is insufficient to justify a fractional critical-line analogue, motivating a weaker left-half-plane link.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A convergence-equivalent prime-power series for zeta^(alpha)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The section moves from the failure of a direct Euler-product derivative to Theorem 4.3, which replaces equality by joint convergence or divergence with a double prime-power series in Re(s)<0 and begins deriving it through the Grünwald–Letnikov limit and product-to-series comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For degrees one through three, reflected convergence regions have convex hull C^2 and local correction factors are uniquely forced; at degree four and above the group becomes infinite, uniqueness fails, and an essential-singularity boundary appears.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cubic moment theorem and the higher-moment continuation gap
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The main cubic asymptotics are paired with a diagnosis of the higher-moment barrier: many corrected series satisfy the same functional equations, yet the desired central point lies beyond the region generated from absolute convergence and before the expected essential-singularity curve.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Polar divisors provide a non-Euler-product route to zeta moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source proposes calculating all polar divisors through the central point, applies the program to an integral of shifted zeta factors, and stresses that functional equations plus continuation—not an Euler product—are the essential inputs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic and geometric factors meet at a multiple-series pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The historical moment problem is reframed by separating an Euler-product arithmetic factor from a random-matrix geometric factor and asserting that both occur in the residue structure at w=1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An oscillatory integral family isolates the unique w=1 pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The generalized integral series includes an oscillatory phase naturally produced by Stirling's formula; Proposition 2.1 gives initial continuation and singles out the zero-frequency case as the source of the simple w=1 pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Oscillation continues Mellin kernels while zero frequency retains the pole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A model kernel is continued by integration by parts; nonzero logarithmic frequency gains holomorphy for Re(w)>0, whereas frequency zero and ratio one produce exactly the w=1 pole. Expanding zeta factors then transfers this dichotomy to the multiple series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Near-diagonal multiplicative ratios are controlled by logarithmic separation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof handles the delicate nonresonant sum by splitting product ratios near and far from one and converting logarithmic denominators into divisor-sum estimates, completing continuation in the full stated si-region.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The w=1 residue factors into zeta diagonals and an arithmetic Euler product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The resonant condition is expressed multiplicatively, factored prime by prime, and separated into universal zeta singularities and a holomorphic remainder whose central specialization is the arithmetic moment factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quasi-functional involutions reflect the initial polar hyperplane
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Affine involutions simultaneously reflect a zeta variable, shift w, flip a sign, and alter frequency. Their finite abelian group yields quasi-functional equations, while the frequency-zero stabilizer identifies precisely which reflections transport the w=1 pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A polar-orbit continuation conjecture is sufficient for all even zeta moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conjecture specifies continuation to a tube containing the central point, no additional local polar components beyond the reflected w=1 hyperplane, and boundary holomorphy; a Tauberian theorem then reduces the moment conjecture to the leading Laurent coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Group symmetrization cancels lower Taylor data and selects the geometric constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Summing a model principal part over the reflection group produces divisibility cancellations that make the central limit exist; positive-degree Taylor terms vanish after scaling, leaving the constant term and the random-matrix geometric factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic-family symmetry predicts a different pole order and geometric factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Known first through third moments and a conjectured fourth are organized into the general symplectic-family moment law, with pole degree m(m+1)/2 and a family-specific arithmetic factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic moment series expose the m>=4 shortage of usable functional equations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The fundamental-discriminant series directly encodes products of quadratic L-values, but the known continuation proof breaks at m>=4 because its functional equations do not reach beyond the first significant polar divisor near the central point.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Congruence splitting and gamma completion convert the raw family series into a finite-group invariant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The raw discriminant sum is split by sign and residue class, then completed by gamma factors so each coordinate functional equation becomes an affine involution and the resulting pair of series is invariant under a finite abelian group.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic reciprocity makes square products the sole contributors to the w=1 residue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After expanding the L-functions and imposing squarefreeness, reciprocity rewrites the inner discriminant sum as ordinary character series. Only the principal-character case—equivalently a square product of indices—has a w=1 pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-product separation recovers the quadratic-family arithmetic factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The square-product residue is factored into singular zeta factors and a holomorphic Euler product, then specialized at the center to identify exactly the arithmetic constant in the family moment conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: All reflected hyperplanes through the central point are posited as the local polar divisor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Finite-group invariance forces a family of 2^m candidate polar hyperplanes; Conjecture 3.6 asserts these are exactly the local divisor and that no w>1 obstruction remains, which is sufficient by a Tauberian theorem for even family moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Divisibility cancellation evaluates the quadratic-family geometric factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reflection-orbit sum is rewritten with a common denominator; symmetry and invariance force the numerator to contain all apparent singular factors, proving the central limit exists and reducing it to the constant Taylor term, which yields the geometric coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The cubic family is realized as a GL(3) Eisenstein twist with imprimitive completions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The cube of a quadratic L-function is realized as a twisted GL(3) Eisenstein L-series. For nonsquarefree parameters, a Dirichlet polynomial repairs the twist so it obeys the same functional equation as a primitive character.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equations, squarefree invariance, and interchange determine local correction polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Three functional identities plus a summation-interchange law characterize the P and Q correction polynomials uniquely in degrees one through three; simultaneous loss of uniqueness and finiteness at degree four explains the structural boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reciprocity closes the w-functional equation on a finite character vector
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The corrected building blocks are indexed by finitely many bad-prime characters. Interchanging summation, applying the character functional equation, and sieving residue classes expresses w reflection as a meromorphic matrix acting on this finite vector.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The s-functional equation also closes after bad-prime bookkeeping
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the GL(3) twist functional equation and expanding omitted Euler factors yields a second finite-dimensional matrix relation reflecting s and shifting w. Together the two vector equations generate the continuation machinery.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two involutions generate a dihedral group whose region hulls fill C^2
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tube-domain convexity converts overlapping analytic regions into their convex hulls. The two functional-equation involutions generate D12, and the staged hulls R1 to R2 to R3 to C^2 give a geometric continuation plan.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Alternating reflections and polar cancellation produce an entire corrected series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Initial convergence estimates from both summation orders overlap to give R1; applying s, w, then s reflections and repeatedly taking tube convex hulls extends an explicitly pole-cancelled product to all C^2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Several-variable holomorphy converts boundary polynomial bounds into finite order
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Vector functional equations transfer polynomial bounds around a reflected annular tube; a domain-of-holomorphy argument fills the central hole, proving the specialized entire function has order one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mean-value input and reflection chains bound the corrected series across the critical strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A fourth-moment estimate for quadratic twists yields absolute convergence on one boundary, while Proposition 4.12 states the reflected vertical-strip bound and limits possible poles to w=1 and w=3/4.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reflection paths eliminate spurious bad-prime poles but preserve a structural w=3/4 candidate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Alternating the two functional equations moves a difficult boundary point into absolute convergence and yields a convexity bound. Analyticity in two variables then rules out apparent poles from finite Euler factors by approaching along reflected hyperplanes; the orbit of w=1 leaves w=3/4 as a genuine possible pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius inversion turns corrected building blocks into the fundamental-discriminant series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Auxiliary divisibility parameters are introduced so Möbius summation forces the square multiplier to one. The target cubic moment series thereby inherits analytic continuation and vertical growth from the corrected Z_M family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite linear combinations restore bad Euler factors and isolate all fundamental-discriminant classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each divisibility-sieved series is expressed as a finite combination of previously continued Z_M blocks; a second Möbius sum removes imprimitive terms, and sign/congruence linear combinations reconstruct the full family while retaining the desired bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Shifted continuation imports the general residue calculation and a Mellin shift yields the smoothed asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rather than recompute a seventh-order residue, the cubic construction is extended to nearby shifted Eisenstein parameters and matched to the general Section 3 calculation. A Mellin inversion and contour shift then turn the pole at one into the full logarithmic polynomial with a power-saving error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An unweighted signed sum requires a separate short-interval moment estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Removing smoothing cannot rely on positivity of cubic central values, so the proof imports a short-interval second-moment bound obtained from a degree-two corrected double series with nonnegative coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short intervals control the truncation error by combining fourth and second moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A truncated Perron integral approximates divisibility-restricted partial sums. The near-cutoff error is partitioned into short intervals and bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz using fourth-moment and short-interval second-moment estimates, while far terms use absolute convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The functional equation converts the left contour into an oscillatory integral with a square-root saving
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After contour shifting, a possible reflected-pole residue and three contour integrals appear. Reflecting the left edge into absolute convergence yields gamma-ratio phases; a second-derivative estimate saves a half-power of the height parameter.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A divisor-sum lemma and parameter equalization determine the final error exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A dyadic divisor-sum bound feeds all contour and truncation errors; splitting small and large sieve moduli, choosing distinct heights, and equalizing the four dominant powers yields the stated unweighted error exponent.
