result_and_mechanism_map.title: Full and natural Beurling spans in the common Hilbert space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separates the classical span generated by all real dilation parameters from the smaller span generated only by natural parameters, making the strengthening precise relative to the classical closure criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann hypothesis via the natural Beurling subspace
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem replaces membership in the full Beurling span by membership in the much thinner natural-parameter span, which is the paper's central strengthening.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why direct natural approximants motivate regularization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The unsmoothed Möbius approximants have partial convergence but diverge in the ambient Hilbert space, proposed subsequences remain problematic, Selberg smoothing is an alternative, and a universal lower bound explains intrinsically slow convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius-weighted analytic family as a correction of reciprocal zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weighting natural Beurling functions by a complex exponent creates a meromorphic family tied to 1/ζ and decomposes the proof into conditional membership fε∈Bnat followed by an unconditional Hilbert-space limit fε→−χ.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free half-plane controls finite Möbius Dirichlet sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The quoted Balazard–Saias lemma turns a zero-free region for ζ into a uniform finite-sum approximation to 1/ζ with an explicit cutoff and vertical-growth error, enabling later norm domination.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation bounds the symmetric zeta ratio
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A ratio comparing ζ on opposite sides of the critical line is bounded by a mild vertical power independently of RH, separating an unconditional control from the conditional Möbius-sum estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite regularized natural sums and their two pointwise limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Finite Möbius-weighted natural sums converge pointwise to fε, and the fundamental Möbius identity then sends fε pointwise to −χ as ε decreases, isolating the remaining task as promotion to Hilbert norm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier–Mellin isometry converts Hilbert norm to transform norm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Plancherel identifies an invertible isometry from the original L2 space to a vertical-line space, and the Mellin transform of a fractional-part function converts regularized Beurling sums into zeta times a Dirichlet polynomial.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH supplies transform-side domination for the finite cutoff limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Littlewood convergence identifies the transform-side pointwise limit, while the conditional finite-sum estimate, the zeta-ratio bound, and Lindelöf growth combine into an integrable uniform majorant, upgrading convergence to the Hilbert norm.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From weighted convergence to natural-span membership and the χ limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separate estimates on (0,1) and (1,∞) remove the auxiliary x-power, proving fε as an H-limit of finite natural sums; the identified transform limit and the unconditional ratio estimate then yield fε→−χ and complete the strengthened implication.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regularized finite sums give a direct convergence criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof yields an RH-equivalent condition phrased as H-convergence of the finite regularized sums for every sufficiently small positive ε and is presented as avoiding the earlier Hardy-space machinery.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subsequence sufficiency, Cesàro smoothing, and cutoff-sensitive regularization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source reframes the proof as a summability method, notes that suitable subsequences in both cutoff and regularization remain sufficient, proposes Cesàro smoothing, and identifies unused cutoff dependence as the route to quantitative control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Inverse-log-log error for an explicit natural approximant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH the source selects a cutoff-dependent regularization scale and states a finite natural Beurling approximant whose H-distance from χ is bounded by an inverse one-third power of log log n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Balance zero-sensitive shift error against finite-sum truncation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Plancherel splits the approximation error into a finite Dirichlet-sum discrepancy and a shifted-zeta ratio discrepancy; zero-near and zero-far estimates give the latter an ε^(2/3) scale, a cutoff-sensitive Balazard–Saias estimate controls the former, and choosing ε proportional to 1/log log n balances the bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Farey sequence construction and discrepancy coordinates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the ordered reduced fractions, mediant insertion, cardinality scale, and the pointwise discrepancy delta_nu from uniform spacing that the later criteria measure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mertens and Chebyshev formulations of RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records the two arithmetic error estimates that later Farey and Kubert identities reduce to, making explicit the downstream equivalence target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform distribution reframed as a discrepancy-error program
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves from equidistribution of Farey points to the stronger question of estimating test-function errors, explicitly proposing broad function classes as a route to RH criteria.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parity-guided short-interval and Kubert criteria
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects reflection parity to cancellation or interval reduction and states the paper's third- and quarter-interval and even-Kubert RH-equivalent estimates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius-convolution sums as a zero-free-region detector
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines S_s as a Dirichlet convolution and shows that square-root cancellation in S_s is equivalent to RH through the quotient zeta(z+s)/zeta(z) and its analytic continuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Farey sums converted to Möbius convolutions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the central reusable transform: a function summed over reduced fractions in an interval becomes a Möbius convolution with unrestricted numerator sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bernoulli decomposition of short-interval power moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the Farey-to-convolution transform with the Bernoulli power-sum formula to decompose every power moment into a uniform main term and structured arithmetic errors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic and cubic moments collapse to the same RH signal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that distinct whole-interval power-moment deviations are affine multiples of S(x), hence equivalent to RH by a common hidden arithmetic statistic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Centering a partial Farey sum by its local count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces a fixed uniform center with h(xi)/(2 Phi(x)) and isolates the Bernoulli and S(x) terms that govern short-interval criteria.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residue extraction and telescoping preserve cancellation exponents
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that removing multiples of a modulus and comparing scaled arguments can be inverted by a finite telescoping series, so the transformed bound is equivalent to the original S_s or Chebyshev bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional-part kernel for centered short-interval Farey sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the centered partial sum through a bounded fractional-part kernel weighted by the Mertens function, exposing the arithmetic channel behind all subsequent special intervals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local centering differs from cumulative Farey discrepancy only by bounded error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the explicit centering error, notes why it likely cannot be improved to o(1), and bridges the new centered sum to Landau's maximal-discrepancy RH criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Half- and third-interval RH criteria
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the fractional-part kernel at rational endpoints, turning centered Farey sums on one-half and one-third intervals into transformed S(x) expressions equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modulo-three decomposition of the one-third kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Demonstrates how a rational interval endpoint converts the fractional-part kernel into a nonzero-residue sum and then uses the telescoping lemma to recover an RH-equivalent bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quarter-interval RH criterion via odd residue classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives a still shorter interval criterion by decomposing the kernel modulo four and reducing it to odd-part S sums whose estimate is equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why fixed endpoint centering leaves uncontrolled residue sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that replacing the adaptive count h(xi) by naive constants at one-third or one-quarter introduces single-residue Mertens sums the authors do not know how to control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kubert functions form a parity-split two-dimensional space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the distribution identity, records the even/odd basis structure, identifies polylogarithm and Hurwitz-zeta realizations, and explains extension to the circle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kubert identities turn Farey averages into gcd-weighted sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms single and pairwise Farey averages of a Kubert function into Mertens-weighted gcd sums, combining distribution identities with the Farey Möbius transform.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The logarithmic Kubert function recovers Chebyshev's function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a roots-of-unity product and divisor expansion of log m to identify the Farey sum of log|2 sin(pi x)| with psi(x), directly connecting a semantic function identity to a classical RH error term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bernoulli and polylogarithm averages share the S_s channel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes the Kubert transform to Bernoulli polynomials and polylogarithms and relates a pairwise polylogarithm average to squared Farey discrepancy, foreshadowing Franel's identity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Non-odd Kubert components yield RH-equivalent Farey sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that a Kubert sum is a nonzero scalar multiple of S_{s-1}(x) precisely when the function has a surviving even component, making odd cancellation an explicit obstruction rather than a failure of the arithmetic criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier decomposition transfers Kubert criteria to Bernoulli and Clausen functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses real and imaginary parts of polylogarithms to express the same RH signal in Bernoulli-polynomial and Clausen-function representations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Half-interval tangent sums encode a Chebyshev scale difference
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Converts a half-interval Farey sum of log tan into psi(x)-psi(x/2), whose square-root error is equivalent to RH by the estimate-preserving telescoping principle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Generalized Dedekind correlations and their cyclic three-term law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the Bernoulli correlation needed for Farey discrepancies and states the cyclic three-term relation whose gcd terms ultimately collapse to Franel's formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bernoulli identities and congruence counting prove the three-term law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adapts a pointwise Bernoulli identity, sums it over congruence classes, and evaluates exceptional integral cases to turn analytic-looking correlations into gcd data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Farey discrepancy squares become Bernoulli correlation sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites each discrepancy using the fractional-part Bernoulli function, expands its square, and isolates a double Mertens-weighted Bernoulli correlation to which Lemma 7 applies.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cyclic averaging exposes the Dedekind three-term relation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a triple sum, observes its invariance under cyclic permutation, and averages the three presentations so Lemma 8 can replace Dedekind terms by symmetric gcd expressions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gcd and Möbius convolutions collapse the symmetrized expression
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates the remaining symmetric gcd terms and a primitive-triple sum, reducing the three-variable expression to Phi(x) and completing Franel's exact identity.

section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identification and title only.

section_argument_map.label: 1. Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines Farey series and discrepancies, recalls classical RH criteria, motivates Farey error sums, explains parity, and announces the paper's three contributions.

section_argument_map.label: 2. Preliminaries
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces Bernoulli power-sum machinery, Möbius-convolution sums S_s, their RH equivalence, and the transform from Farey sums to arithmetic convolutions.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Power moments
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives general Bernoulli expansions for Farey power moments and reduces quadratic and cubic whole-interval moment criteria to S(x).

section_argument_map.label: 4. Short interval results
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Centers partial Farey sums, develops telescoping residue-class criteria, proves half-, third-, and quarter-interval RH equivalents, and records a centering obstruction.

section_argument_map.label: 5. Kubert functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses the Kubert distribution identity and parity structure to turn Farey averages of polylogarithmic, Bernoulli, Clausen, and logarithmic functions into RH-equivalent arithmetic sums.

section_argument_map.label: 6. Franel's theorem
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Relates Bernoulli correlations to generalized Dedekind sums, proves their three-term relation, and derives Franel's discrepancy-square identity.

section_argument_map.label: References and author matter
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Bibliography, affiliations, and receipt date; no new mathematical argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why the microscopic object must be a normalized analytic function

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalized microscopic characteristic-polynomial process and functional limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines ξ_n as a ratio that cancels the nonconvergent common magnitude, records its functional equation, and states convergence as an entire function rather than merely convergence of zero processes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Virtual-isometry coupling across matrix dimensions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs Haar unitary matrices on one probability space via rank-one extensions and turns marginal convergence into pointwise eigenangle convergence with a quantitative central-window error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical paired infinite product with sine-kernel zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the almost-sure compact-uniform convergence to an entire function whose symmetrically paired product is absolutely convergent and whose zeros are exactly the limiting sine process.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional convergence transfers directly to ratios and derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how convergence in the holomorphic-function topology simultaneously yields almost-sure limits for arbitrary finite ratios and derivatives, while flagging expectation convergence as a separate integrability problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithms and eigenvalue counts from a pathwise analytic limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a zero-avoiding contour to pass convergence from entire functions to chosen logarithm branches, then turns the imaginary logarithm into microscopic eigenvalue counts.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic derivative as a symmetrically summed resolvent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the microscopic characteristic-polynomial logarithmic derivative with a meromorphic sum over limiting sine-kernel zeros, giving the basic resolvent representation used throughout the paper.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform ratio moments, determinant identity, and zeta-ratio transfer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages the uniform integrability needed to pass ratio expectations to the limit, states the limiting determinant identity, and isolates its conditional zeta analogue.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Argument variation converts spectral counting into eigenangle error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates the number of zeros on an arc to the change in the characteristic-polynomial argument, yielding an exact bridge between argument control and deviation of renormalized eigenangles from their indices.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From one-point subgaussian control to a uniform circle bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives a Chernoff bound from the Gamma-product moment generating function, applies rotational invariance and Borel-Cantelli on a regular grid, and fills grid gaps using the deterministic sawtooth behavior of the argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Determinantal count variance, Bernstein tails, and exponential moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Obtains uniform finite/infinite sine-process counting estimates from Fourier variance formulas and the Bernoulli decomposition of determinantal counts, furnishing the tail control needed for rigidity and analytic tails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Global logarithmic rigidity by patching count tails and coupling
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns interval-count concentration into y_k=k+O(log|k|) for the infinite sine process and combines global finite-n argument bounds with central-window coupling to obtain the uniform finite-level estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite ratio rewritten as a symmetric product over periodic eigenangles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the sine product and periodic eigenangle indexing to transform the normalized characteristic polynomial from a finite matrix product into the same symmetric zero-product representation used at the limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Paired tail control plus pointwise convergence yields compact functional convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses logarithmic rigidity to pair positive and negative factors, obtains uniform O(log A/A) product-tail errors, and combines finite-factor convergence with Montel's theorem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Order-one growth of the canonical entire function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions product factors into three regimes to prove an exp(O(|z|log|z|)) upper bound and uses the imaginary axis product to obtain exponential lower growth, identifying order one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Microscopic linear-statistic convergence for all integrable tests
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extends compactly supported bounded-test convergence by truncating the test function and controlling the discarded part solely through the unit one-point intensity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Centered linear statistics as an integral of the boundary argument
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses summation by parts against the counting function to express a centered linear statistic as the integral of Im log ξ against f', linking point configurations to analytic boundary data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta functional-limit conjecture supported by paired Hadamard zero sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States process-level convergence of a locally normalized zeta function and its logarithmic derivative, then shows the zeta logarithmic derivative decomposes into the same paired zero-resolvent plus the same iπ archimedean term as ξ∞.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Index-symmetric and spatial-window truncations agree
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the paired logarithmic-derivative sum can equivalently be truncated by spectral location |y_k|<A, with rigidity making the boundary discrepancy only O(log A) terms of size O(1/A).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform exponential control of logarithmic-derivative tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions the far spectrum into growing blocks, separates deterministic mean cancellation from centered count fluctuations, and combines Jensen with determinantal exponential moments to control tails uniformly over finite and infinite n.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lp tail decay licenses moment passage through infinite zero sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Converts exponential tail control into quantitative Lp decay, proves the logarithmic derivative has moments of every order off the real axis, and justifies computing moments by bounded-window correlation functions followed by A→∞.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Low logarithmic-derivative moments from sine-kernel correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the first and second moments by splitting diagonal and off-diagonal point contributions, evaluating kernel integrals, and extending by L2 continuity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta logarithmic-derivative moments as a pair-correlation criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers the computed ξ∞ covariance to a two-point zeta logarithmic-derivative conjecture and records that its diagonal specialization is equivalent, under RH, to the pair-correlation conjecture.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Balanced off-real ratios are uniformly integrable and converge in expectation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses zero-free paths and exponential logarithmic-derivative bounds to prove uniform ratio moments, then combines almost-sure compact convergence with uniform integrability to pass arbitrary balanced ratio expectations to ξ∞.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Giambelli determinant identity transported from polynomial ensembles to CUE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes a formal determinant identity for Vandermonde polynomial ensembles to CUE characteristic polynomials and carefully upgrades formal-series validity to analytic domains by absolute convergence, holomorphic continuation, arc removal, and dominated convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Limiting determinant formula for ratios and its zeta conjecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the finite-n determinant with expectation convergence to obtain an explicit ξ∞ ratio-moment formula, handles coincident points by cancellation or continuity, and states the matching randomized-zeta limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: General logarithmic-derivative moments by differentiating ratio determinants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses uniform ratio bounds to differentiate expectations, expands the Cauchy determinant, and reduces a large derivative expansion through fixed points, involutions, and cycle cancellation to a closed permutation formula for arbitrary joint moments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Centered logarithmic derivative as a resolvent linear statistic and blue-noise target
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets ξ∞'/ξ∞−iπ as a conditionally convergent resolvent trace of the operator with sine-process spectrum and defines blue noise through its H^{1/2} spectral covariance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mesoscopic sine-process fluctuations converge to blue noise
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Adapts cumulant bounds from finite CUE, passes them to the sine process, extends the statistic continuously to H^{1/2}, and proves that dilation kills higher cumulants while preserving the |k|-weighted variance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stieltjes statistic equals the centered logarithmic derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Approximates 1/(z−t) by compactly supported H^{1/2} tests and identifies the resulting centered sine-process statistic with ξ∞'/ξ∞ minus its half-plane deterministic term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian scaling limit and covariance of the logarithmic-derivative field
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies blue-noise convergence to Stieltjes tests, obtaining a centered Gaussian field under large-scale dilation and computing its same-/opposite-half-plane covariance explicitly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From finite-dimensional Gaussian limits to a holomorphic process
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses increment bounds for continuity, contour covariance plus Morera-type reasoning for holomorphicity, and uniform Kolmogorov estimates for tightness, upgrading finite-dimensional convergence to compact-uniform convergence on C\R.

section_argument_map.label: 1 Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Motivates the functional microscopic limit, explains why almost-sure coupling replaces moment methods, and separates ratio, linear-statistic, and zeta-value applications.

section_argument_map.label: 1.1 The characteristic polynomial of random unitary matrices and the number theory connections
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines sine-kernel scaling, the normalized characteristic-polynomial process, and its functional limiting problem.

section_argument_map.label: 1.2 Virtual isometries and almost sure convergence
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Constructs the cross-dimensional Haar coupling, states eigenangle rigidity input and the canonical infinite-product limit, and records functional consequences.

section_argument_map.label: 1.3 Outline of the paper
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States uniform ratio-integrability and determinantal expectation results, the corresponding zeta-ratio conjecture, and the mesoscopic endpoint.

section_argument_map.label: 2.1 On the argument of the characteristic polynomial
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Converts argument variation into eigenvalue counts and proves a uniform logarithmic bound by concentration and discretization.

section_argument_map.label: 2.2 Precise estimates for the eigenvalues of virtual isometries
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Derives determinantal count variance and tail bounds and upgrades them to finite- and infinite-level eigenangle rigidity.

section_argument_map.label: 2.3 Infinite product representation of the ratio and its convergence
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Rewrites finite characteristic-polynomial ratios as symmetric zero products and proves compact convergence by paired-tail control.

section_argument_map.label: 3.1 The order of ξ∞ as an entire function
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Bounds the canonical limit above and below to identify its entire-function order.

section_argument_map.label: 3.2 Convergence of linear statistics
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Extends microscopic linear-statistic convergence to integrable tests and represents centered statistics through the boundary argument of the limiting function.

section_argument_map.label: 4 Fine estimates for the logarithmic derivative and related zeta conjectures
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Relates paired zero sums to logarithmic derivatives, proves uniform tail integrability, computes low moments, and states solver-conditional zeta analogues.

section_argument_map.label: 5.1 Expectation of ratios
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Proves ratio integrability and expectation convergence, transports a Giambelli determinant identity to CUE, and passes it to the limiting function and zeta conjecture.

section_argument_map.label: 5.2 Moments of the logarithmic derivative
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Differentiates the ratio determinant and organizes the resulting combinatorics into a general logarithmic-derivative moment formula.

section_argument_map.label: 6 Mesoscopic fluctuations and blue noise
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Reframes the logarithmic derivative as a renormalized resolvent linear statistic and defines the blue-noise target.

section_argument_map.label: 6.1 The sine kernel from afar
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses cumulant estimates and Sobolev completion to prove mesoscopic sine-process fluctuations converge to blue noise.

section_argument_map.label: 6.2 Application to the Stieltjes transform of the sine kernel
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Identifies the Stieltjes statistic with the centered logarithmic derivative and upgrades its Gaussian limit to a holomorphic-process limit.

source_identity.title: The circular unitary ensemble and the Riemann zeta function: the microscopic landscape and a new approach to ratios

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The virtual-isometry coupling supplies pointwise spectral control, the finite product is recoded in the limiting zero representation, and paired rigidity tails upgrade those ingredients to an almost-sure compact-uniform entire-function limit.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This mechanism is established for the coupled CUE construction; it does not by itself construct an analogous coupling for zeta.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Coupling produces a canonical analytic object rather than only a local zero limit

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The same canonical product turns zeros into logarithmic derivatives, arguments, counts, centered linear statistics, and a cutoff-justified Stieltjes transform, providing several interchangeable views of the sine process.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Equivalence requires the stated branch, decay, off-real, and symmetric-truncation conditions.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Zero configurations become analytic, counting, and linear-statistic observables

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Argument concentration and determinantal count tails yield logarithmic rigidity, which in turn controls paired products and, after blockwise fluctuation estimates, licenses Lp manipulation of infinite logarithmic-derivative sums.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The strongest uniform tail bounds use determinantal-specific count estimates and should not be presumed for an arbitrary zero process.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Rigidity is the common control layer for global analytic tails

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Uniform off-real exponential control supplies the analytic integrability gate; this permits finite-n Giambelli identities to pass to ξ∞ and permits differentiation of ratio moments into general logarithmic-derivative moment formulas.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Exact formulas depend on balanced ratios, off-real compact sets, and extraction-sensitive determinant/combinatorial notation.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Ratio integrability unlocks determinant identities and arbitrary derivative moments

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Unit-spacing normalization and paired Hadamard sums motivate a single process-level hypothesis whose ratio and logarithmic-derivative consequences agree with GUE/pair-correlation predictions while conceptually suppressing prime-driven longer-range structure.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: All transfers from ξ∞ to zeta are conjectural or conditional; CUE agreement is not independent evidence for RH or for a zeta functional limit.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: The zeta bridge isolates a zero-driven microscopic process hypothesis

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The resolvent belongs to the H^{1/2} statistic space, dilation preserves the blue-noise variance while suppressing higher cumulants, and covariance plus tightness upgrades the resulting Gaussian limit to compact-uniform holomorphic convergence off the real axis.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The theorem concerns the sine-kernel process and the centered field away from the real line; it does not establish boundary convergence or the conjectural zeta analogue.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Mesoscopic dilation turns the sine resolvent into a holomorphic blue-noise field

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin transform turns fractional-part dilation into zeta-weighted approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The displayed Mellin identity makes dilation multiplicative in the transform variable and turns density of fractional-part dilates in L2 into an RH-equivalent closure problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reciprocal-integer dilates strengthen the criterion and expose quantitative distance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The move from arbitrary dilations to reciprocal integers yields the Baez-Duarte criterion, an orthogonal-projection distance formulation, conjectural rate information, and a link from approximation error to zero-free regions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Muntz-transform criterion isolates compact support as the obstruction to analytic kernels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The general strong criterion reframes RH through approximation by dilated Muntz transforms and pinpoints why the known converse excludes noncompact analytic kernels, setting up the paper's controlled-tail repair.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two inequivalent placements of expectation define pNB and gNB
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Placing expectation outside the squared Hilbert error versus inside each random fractional-part function creates distinct criteria, with Jensen's inequality giving pNB implies gNB.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random Beurling functions embed in a product Hilbert space with norm linear in the mean dilation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The product-space formulation turns random dilates into Hilbert vectors, suggests Gram-determinant structure, and proves that integrability of X suffices with an exact norm proportional to E[X].

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moment interpolation controls the L2 tail of a random Beurling function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposition converts an L2 moment of Z into a uniform decay estimate beyond a cutoff M, the reusable device later used for noncompact random dilates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A positive-probability bounded-support event derandomizes pNB into NB
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assumption P ensures a uniform positive chance that every sampled dilation lies in the classical interval; intersecting that event with a small-error event realizes one deterministic NB approximant and hence RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The smallest sampled dilation limits probabilistic approximation quality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A deterministic lower bound at minimum scale transfers through the support event and Cauchy-Schwarz to show that pNB error cannot decay faster than permitted by the logarithmic size of the minimum dilation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Concentration near reciprocal integers yields pNB equivalent to RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem packages mean matching, rapidly shrinking variance, and a nondegeneracy condition into a two-way criterion, explicitly connecting random perturbations to quantitative deterministic approximants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Variance concentration recovers the positive-probability support condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A union bound plus Chebyshev converts uniform small variance around reciprocal means into Assumption P, closing the easy direction from pNB to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin-Plancherel frequency splitting stabilizes Mobius approximants under random perturbation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof compares randomized and deterministic fractional-part approximants, transfers their difference to the critical line, bounds low frequencies using concentration plus Lindelof, bounds high frequencies using integrability, and tunes the cutoff so both vanish.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vanishing L2 approximation excludes off-critical zeta zeros via a Mellin contradiction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming an off-critical zero makes the Mellin transform of every approximation error equal a fixed nonzero target term, while splitting at t=1 and using L2 convergence forces that same integral to zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Admissible targets plus moment and coefficient-tail control suffice for gNB to imply RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 8 replaces the indicator target by any function with nonvanishing Mellin transform and controlled L2 tail, while explicitly states the moment and coefficient condition that compensate for unbounded random dilations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A moving Mellin cutoff separates approximation error from noncompact tails
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At a hypothetical zeta zero the averaged approximation has a fixed nonzero Mellin value; choosing a threshold growing slowly enough makes the lower-range integral vanish by gNB error, reducing the contradiction to tail control.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rare large dilations are controlled by coefficient-weighted tail probability and moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Splitting each expected fractional part according to whether Z exceeds the moving cutoff isolates a large-dilation term; Cauchy-Schwarz factors it into precisely condition C and the summable moment budget.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded dilations are closed by target decay, gNB error, and the random-Beurling tail estimate
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For dilations below the cutoff, the fractional part linearizes on the tail, reducing the remaining integral to a coefficient-weighted first moment; gNB, admissible-target decay, Proposition 2.2, and condition C then force it to zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Expected fractional parts are negative Muntz transforms of survival functions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Writing the survival function of X turns expectation of the random fractional part into a deterministic Muntz transform, furnishing a direct bridge between probability and the general strong criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Deterministic strong approximation transfers RH to gNB for dilated random variables
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH, bounded deterministic Baez-Duarte coefficients approximate the indicator; the Muntz bridge transfers this to survival-function approximation by X/k, while a q-moment gives condition C through polynomial tail decay.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential dilation and Gamma concentration instantiate different criterion routes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The examples separate a fixed-law dilation family handled through gNB/Muntz transfer from a triangular Gamma family handled through pNB concentration, and the implication map highlights that pNB can imply RH without condition C.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the full final transfer architecture: combine the prime variance and pair-correlation energy identities, localize by averaging, separate diagonal from off-diagonal contributions, discard remote prime ranges with a sieve bound, and infer existence from positivity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why zero statistics should improve classical prime-gap bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts classical RH bounds and short-interval results with Gallagher-Mueller and Mueller hypotheses, then frames the paper's task as weakening or sharpening the pair-correlation assumptions needed for prime consequences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reduce short-interval prime variance to a weighted zero sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 2 supplies the reusable analytic reduction on the prime side: smooth a short increment, insert the explicit-formula decomposition, split the error contributions, and control prime-pair terms by a uniform sieve estimate and remaining terms by mean-square bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair correlation as weighted L2 energy of a zero exponential sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 3 makes the central representation change exact: the pair-correlation weight is the Fourier transform of a positive kernel, so the two-zero statistic equals an integrated squared exponential sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Control a pointwise zero sum by nearby pair-correlation energy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 4 combines a one-dimensional smoothing inequality, partial summation, and the positive-kernel identity to bound a pointwise exponential sum by a local maximum of pair correlation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair-correlation decay implies a sharper prime-counting error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows a clean transfer pattern: truncate the explicit formula at two scales, use the hypothesis and Lemma 4 on the long range, use a trivial bound on the short range, then choose the scale after fixing the target error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Encode large prime gaps inside short-interval variance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns each sufficiently large consecutive-prime gap into a region where the short-interval counting error is forced, sums those nonnegative contributions, and invokes Lemma 2 to reduce the desired gap bound to a zero-sum estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bound low zero frequencies through partial summation and pair-correlation energy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Handles the low-ordinate portion of the zero sum by crude weight bounds, partial summation, Cauchy-Schwarz, and Lemma 3, producing a pair-correlation bound at the short-interval scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Control high zero frequencies by scale decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites the high-frequency weight as a difference of scaled factors, applies partial summation and Cauchy-Schwarz, and integrates the resulting energies to obtain a maximum over pair-correlation scales, completing Theorem 2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Express a weighted zero-sum energy through pair correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands a weighted exponential-sum energy into pairs of zeros, replaces asymmetric weights with a controlled symmetric form, and uses partial summation to rewrite the result as a transform of the pair-correlation function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncate the energy integral and isolate the Lemma 5 kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Obtains a uniform global energy bound, chooses a logarithmic cutoff to suppress tails, and differentiates the weight into a kernel that yields Lemma 5 with a controlled error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Combine prime variance and zero energy after a logarithmic change of variables
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Aligns Lemmas 2 and 5 by an exponential change of variables and a sum over translated windows, converting the smoothed prime-counting variance into an integral of pair correlation against a derived kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Average the interval scale to localize the pair-correlation hypothesis
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces a compact triangular average in the short-interval parameter, thereby restricting the transform to the theorem's usable pair-correlation range and separating the main term from endpoint and hypothesis errors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extract a close prime pair from diagonal and off-diagonal mass
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses continuity to choose a good scale, expands the nonnegative variance into background, linear, and prime-pair terms, evaluates the diagonal, bounds remote off-diagonal ranges by the sieve estimate, and forces positive mass from nearby distinct primes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gauged CPT as an effective low-energy boundary condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source turns a general no-global-symmetries expectation into a concrete modeling move: microscopic gauging may survive semiclassically as a boundary condition rather than as a new visible degree of freedom.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert-Polya ambiguity reframed as a boundary-condition problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage cleanly separates three missing ingredients in spectral approaches to zeta zeros—the self-adjoint operator, its function space/boundary condition, and the physical origin of that choice—then identifies gauged CPT as the proposed source of discretization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two phase-space normalizations with one scattering matrix
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source exhibits two Hamiltonian descriptions—one with partial-wave-dependent commutators and one with a common phase-space cell plus an l-dependent shift—that are asserted to yield the same scattering matrix. This separates representation choices from the scattering observable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Black-hole coordinates turn the dilation algebra into near-horizon scattering data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage maps the abstract Hamiltonians to Schwarzschild partial waves, relates Kruskal and asymptotic-observer coordinates, and interprets the U-V commutator as both a gravitational back-reaction effect and a minimal phase-space/causal-diamond uncertainty.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dilation dynamics decomposes into SL(2,R) weight and parity sectors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source identifies Hamiltonian evolution with dilation, places the generators in an SL(2,R) algebra, converts energy into conformal weight, and resolves the twofold degeneracy into even and odd eigenfunction branches. This parity split later determines which L-function enters the quantization condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discrete conformal inversions act automorphically on energy eigenfunctions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The inversion V maps to plus or minus 1/V is lifted to a weighted action on functions, under which the parity eigenfunctions have fixed eigenvalues. This supplies the symmetry template for the later canonical phase-space maps.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical global CPT identification cannot be imposed on quantum conjugate coordinates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After deriving the partial-wave CPT identification and its antipodal classical consequence, the source pinpoints the obstruction: a pointwise condition on both U and V is not a valid wavefunction condition when those variables are canonically conjugate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uncertainty forces CPT identification from spacetime points to phase-space states
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This passage reframes a geometric identification as a quantum phase-space condition and states that it must constrain both ingoing and outgoing wavefunctions because they use conjugate representations. It is the key bridge from the classical obstruction to the canonical construction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical inversion extensions generate a D4 central phase-space diamond
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source enlarges coordinate inversion into area-preserving transformations of conjugate variables, observes their Hamiltonian action, and shows that at fixed UV they generate an eight-element dihedral action on four phase-space cells. This replaces an inadmissible point identification with a finite canonical symmetry structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A central involution induces the local CPT boundary on UV hyperbolae
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The central element T2+ is chosen as the light-cone CPT identification; edge identification gives an RP2 topology, and commutation with dilation transports the condition from the central diamond to every paired point on UV=plus or minus h. The homotopy note explains the resulting two path classes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier scattering separates even and odd dilation channels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The in/out partial-wave expansion and Fourier transform convert near-horizon scattering into coefficient relations with distinct gamma-function factors for even and odd eigenfunctions. This is the analytic bridge between phase-space symmetry and the two later L-function conditions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum CPT acts on in/out wavefunctions along Planckian hyperbolae
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source combines the canonical map with conjugation and spherical parity to formulate CPT directly on both scattering representations, then restricts the identification to the dilation orbit |UV|=h. This is the quantum replacement for the rejected global pointwise condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Even-sector boundary plus zeta functional equation yields a zero condition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combining the even scattering relation, CPT identification, and zeta functional equation produces an equivalence relation asserted to hold over the full one-parameter locus |UV|=h; the source argues nonzero eigenfunctions then require paired zeta zeros, with real energy placing s on the critical line.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Odd parity changes the spectral condition from zeta to Dirichlet beta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The sign carried by odd eigenfunctions modifies the equivalence relation, and the Dirichlet beta functional equation supplies the corresponding discrete odd-wave spectrum. This exposes how a representation-theoretic branch choice changes the arithmetic spectral object.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The boundary condition regularizes dilation while breaking parity degeneracy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source interprets the local phase-space boundary as a symmetry-respecting alternative to a naive cutoff, decomposes the complete shifted Hamiltonian into partial-wave contributions, and explains that zeta/beta branches break the original even/odd degeneracy while retaining m-degeneracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trivial zeros are mapped to imaginary-energy resonances
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes nontrivial real-energy spectral conditions from trivial zeros and interprets the latter through poles and zeros of the scattering matrix on imaginary energy axes as unstable resonances.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same identification leaves light-cone momentum spectra continuous
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the boundary map to Kruskal momentum eigenfunctions constrains coefficients but does not discretize momentum. This is a valuable counterpoint: the boundary condition is observable-selective rather than a universal discretizer, and the source reads that invariance as evidence for horizon smoothness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same zero relations may encode missing spectral lines rather than emitted levels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The conclusion records a materially different Connes-style interpretation: equations (16)-(17) could describe absorption gaps in a continuum rather than a discrete emission spectrum, and deciding among absorption, emission, or both requires comparison of trace formulas with zeta density of states.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Entropy, multiparticle observables, and the missing ground state remain open tests
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source identifies concrete ways the proposal could fail or be sharpened: a density/partition-function calculation must test black-hole entropy and state completeness, multiparticle observables remain unchecked, and the discrete spectrum is still unbounded below despite gauging CPT.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Auditing reasons rather than assigning belief
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates refuting evidence for skepticism from proving RH and makes perspective switching and scale-sensitive randomness the paper's method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A snapshot fixes shape but hides scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that normalized local gaps determine a scale-free graph while Selberg-scale magnitude can differ by orders of magnitude, defeating inference from visible shape to size.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation, real Z-function, and sign normalization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects several functional-equation forms to a real graphable function and distinguishes immaterial global sign from the nonzero mean bias of zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: RH symmetry and Turing-style zero certification
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates critical-line symmetry, real zeros of Z, sign-change counting, the N(T) error term, and S(t) into a formal interval-verification mechanism while warning that graph extrema alone are not equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unfolding zeros and separating typical from extreme size
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Normalizes variable zero density, links large gaps to S(t), contrasts conjectural extremes with Selberg-typical values, and explains why a conspicuous computed peak is atypical.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-height Riemann-Siegel bias can mimic asymptotic scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how the dominant first term and Gram-point sampling create an order-one bias indistinguishable from the extraordinarily slow asymptotic scale in feasible computations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three large-value inferences and Gram's-law intuition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States four recurring extrapolations to be tested and distinguishes usefulness at moderate height from validity as asymptotic intuition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nearby zeros determine shape; distant zeros supply a slow scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a polynomial product to isolate local zero geometry from a locally constant contribution of distant zeros, giving the foundational three-factor decomposition for Z(t).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Carrier waves govern bulk value distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the slow scale factor and shows why persistence across many zeros, not a pointwise CLT alone, lets one L-function dominate a linear combination through most zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial-Hadamard measurement of a carrier wave
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs a local approximation by moving equally spaced cosine zeros to observed zeros, isolates the scale factor, and records its window dependence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The functional equation supplies the highest tone
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Interprets the Riemann-Siegel expansion as an approximately band-limited signal whose gamma-factor fixes the leading frequency and whose Dirichlet coefficients perturb zero locations, explaining low-conductor Gram bias.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zeta model must preserve self-reciprocity and unitary zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the involution/real-locus analogy and rejects coefficient-random ensembles because they fail either unitary zeros or the observed kind of spacing randomness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repulsion parameter selects the CUE Goldilocks regime
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how beta controls gas-to-crystal behavior and why quadratic repulsion fits observed zero gaps and values better than the too-flexible COE or too-rigid CSE.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random matrices are generators, not the essential content
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lists distinct generators of the same CUE zero law and compresses the model to beta-two repulsion rather than a matrix ontology.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From local GUE statistics to value recipes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates three stages of RMT influence: limiting local statistics, finite-conductor compact-group value models, and arithmetic recipes with full main terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local statistics forget global ensemble geometry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines local statistics and uses determinantal kernels converging to the sine kernel to explain why GUE and CUE share limiting neighbor behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: GUE zero statistics predict gaps but not values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the Montgomery-Odlyzko law and consequences for simple, small, and large gaps, then identifies primes, finite-height corrections, and value distribution as missing channels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Keating-Snaith matches zero density and value distributions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches zeta near height T to characteristic polynomials of size log(T/2pi), explains finite-height value skew and moment constants, and specifies an ensemble of independent windows for global extremes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic lower-order corrections damp random-matrix extremes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why a naive independent prime-times-zero refinement cannot generally reproduce lower terms and records systematic damping relative to unitary matrices.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Map real Z to rotated polynomials and zeta half-planes to disks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes modeling a real Z-function from modeling complex zeta and justifies the half-plane-to-disk map using normalization and derivative-zero geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Statistical sampling excludes pathological unitary counterexamples
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Classifies leading agreement, arithmetic-factor agreement, and pointwise analogy failure, then shows why rare polynomials violating a Lindelof analogue do not invalidate an ensemble prediction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Carrier waves inside one degree-1000 unitary polynomial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Demonstrates a factor-500 scale change within one fixed polynomial, measures it by local zero matching, and shows that a smaller individual gap can host the global maximum when its carrier is larger.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Density wave as weighted neighbor discrepancy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces individual gaps with a multiscale density measure, derives a weighted sum of distant-neighbor discrepancies, and matches it to the logarithmic carrier wave.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: S(t) slope reveals an emergent density wave
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects increasing or decreasing averaged S(t) to dense or sparse regions and explains carrier waves as collective behavior suppressed at computable heights by rigidity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Matching mean spacing does not determine matrix size
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Exposes a hidden scaling choice in Keating-Snaith and uses carrier-wave amplitude to reject a larger rescaled system with the same local mean gap.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral rigidity separates universal from arithmetic regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses neighbor-spacing variance and S(t) to show where local universal statistics give way to prime-sensitive long-range constraints that limit density waves.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small gaps are universal; large gaps inherit rigidity uncertainty
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the robust one-third smallest-gap exponent from quadratic repulsion, notes consequences for derivative moments, and limits large-gap transfer because zeta is more rigid than CUE beyond the universal regime.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An individual gap is lower order than the carrier wave
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates two independent contributions to log magnitude and shows that conjectural maximal gaps contribute only a lower-order square-root-log amount.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A large gap compresses neighbors over a proportional range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Finds the likely neighboring-zero configuration, gives a charge-splitting scaling argument for proportional influence range, and uses moved zeros plus Stirling to bound the gap's log-value contribution by O(g).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg-typical large and small values require many-gap coordination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that attributing a positive mass of typical extremes to single very large or very small gaps contradicts both gap tails and total gap mass.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: For self-reciprocal polynomials, large values have two distinct zero mechanisms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Backlund's criterion to reframe Lindelof away from unitary-only models, proves one polynomial implication, and distinguishes radial off-circle zeros from angular gap irregularity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mollifiers must cancel the slow wave, not merely local zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recasts zeta locally as a slow random amplitude times a unit-spaced polynomial and explains why normalized linear combinations of derivatives share a viable reciprocal mollifier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primes and zero density are dual explanations of the same wave
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rejects a literal causal choice between Euler and Hadamard products, sketches the prime-sum CLT mechanism, and assigns universal local behavior to zeros and long-range behavior to primes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An adjustable Euler-Hadamard product splits prime and zero scales
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a parameterized product whose cutoff trades nearby zeros against small primes and records leading-order splitting and maximum invariance alongside lower-order limitations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime phases and matrix traces produce log-correlated fields
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Maps prime sums to trace sums, identifies logarithmic covariance, and imports clustered/cascading maxima intuition that explains carrier-wave persistence and depressed extremes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Log-correlation invalidates independent sampling of local maxima
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts the FHK coefficient and tail with naive independent Gaussian samples, then blocks an invalid inference to global extremes by identifying a nonuniform tail factor and switched limits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Carrier-wave width is suggested by clustered effective sample size
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines theorem lower bounds, FHK effective sampling, and shifted moments to suggest a log-log span while explaining why fixed moments cannot identify bulk-wave width.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small waves suggest valleys within valleys
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extends the carrier concept symmetrically to small values, compares positive and negative shifted moments, and identifies hierarchical wave generation as a currently inaccessible modeling target.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moments of moments and GMC encode log-correlated hierarchy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records freezing transitions and the convergence of a shifted random zeta function to a randomized Euler product factored into universal GMC and a smooth nonvanishing perturbation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Transfer to a system where RH is built in blocks skeptical inference
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines two controls: a fact shared by unitary polynomials or arising only from finite verified computation cannot itself count as evidence against RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lehmer pairs show fragility, not evidence of failure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows arbitrarily close gaps are expected in unitary models where RH is true, broadens 'barely true' through carrier perturbations and the de Bruijn-Newman constant, and separates analytic stability from the sought number-theoretic mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tightly packed spikes are an axis-choice, not an RH contradiction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Refutes a visual implausibility argument by separating amplitude, horizontal compression, and the already-known existence of many critical-line oscillations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Blanc's interpolation identity targets derivatives near an isolated maximum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the exact setup in which low odd derivatives make one side large while a zeta-specific high-derivative bound may make the integral side small, avoiding immediate dismissal by unitary analogy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repeated differentiation drives zeros toward cosine spacing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains lower and upper derivative thresholds through zero equalization, derives the functional-equation frequency scale, and constructs self-reciprocal/unitary examples that approach the universal cosine attractor too slowly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A failed Blanc contradiction may bound gaps rather than refute RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Enumerates cancellation escape routes, tests the mechanism on likely unitary configurations, and extracts a parameterized polynomial problem whose solution could improve zeta gap bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two moment error terms cannot determine RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reconstructs the k/4 extrapolation from two known cases, exposes it as pattern matching by equally simple alternatives, and distinguishes the genuine k=4 structural transition in main-term methods from unsupported error growth.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Linear combinations lose Euler products and fail RH systematically
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses carrier-wave dominance to explain why most zeros can remain critical while crossings create off-line zeros, then identifies loss of Euler product and zeros in absolute convergence as the structural distinction from L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wrong large-value notions can still be productive filters
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates asymptotically false causal stories from finite-height algorithms that successfully locate records, while showing why truncated initial terms cannot capture the true extreme scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A search for off-line zeros needs a failure model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Runs the large-gap story backward, notes distant off-line zeros need not create visible anomalies, and argues that computational search should be conditioned on an explicit failure mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Precise Gram law fails under zero sloshing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Restores Gram's original indexed interlacing, gives an S(t) necessary condition showing its asymptotic rarity, and reframes long coherent displacements as the same density wave that controls carrier amplitude.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random-matrix controls make Gram-point effects transient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives sign/reversal conjectures from CUE symmetries, matches zeta data at the prescribed finite matrix size, and uses increasing N plus lower-order damping to explain both similarities and statistically significant differences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-first skepticism versus zero-first explanation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts accidental-zero and structural-zero worldviews and summarizes how density waves let the zeros determine both scale and local corrections.

within_source_synthesis_map.title: One carrier wave, three representations

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The conclusion is based on the source's stated asymptotic conjectures and model transfer; it is not a direct computation beyond the accessible range.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Why finite computation reverses the hierarchy of causes

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Quadratic repulsion robustly transfers finite normalized local statistics and the smallest-gap exponent, while long-range rigidity, large gaps, values, and lower terms retain arithmetic information.

within_source_synthesis_map.title: Universality has a scale boundary

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: An observation is not skeptical evidence if it occurs in unitary models where the RH analogue is built in or only inside verified computation; a credible failure claim needs an L-function-specific mechanism and a model for off-line zeros.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Passing this filter would make evidence relevant, not prove RH false; random-matrix transfer itself remains statistical and approximate.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: A disciplined filter for evidence against RH
