result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scalar projection turns modular bootstrap into a spin-sensitive RH interface
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage explains why projecting to U(1)c scalar primaries is more informative than spinless energy grading and states the two distinct targets: scalar-gap bounds and a zeta-zero/RH reformulation, with a more difficult Virasoro generalization.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Roelcke-Selberg decomposition separates constant, continuous, and cusp spectra
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This is the structural harmonic-analysis basis that later lets a partition function be separated into a constant mode, Eisenstein continuum, and discrete Maass data with unique coefficients.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eisenstein analytic continuation survives scalar averaging while Maass cusp forms vanish
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The contrast between Eisenstein constant terms and the zero scalar piece of every Maass cusp form is the reusable projection mechanism that removes sporadic cusp data from the scalar crossing equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Subtracting an Eisenstein series makes the reduced U(1)c partition function spectrally decomposable
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factoring out U(1)c characters produces a primary-counting partition function, and subtracting Ec/2 cures its cusp growth so the unique harmonic decomposition can be applied without assuming the theory is Narain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Constrained Epstein zeta series encode the scalar spectrum and inherit a functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The scalar dimensions are compressed into a Dirichlet series that is simultaneously an Eisenstein overlap; this dual representation supplies analytic continuation and the functional equation used in contour shifting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The shifted contour becomes an explicit arithmetic scalar crossing kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After the zeta-zero residues are isolated, the remainder is converted using the constrained-Epstein functional equation, a convergent scalar sum, and the ratio ζ(2s)/ζ(2s-1), yielding the final crossing equation with Möbius-derived coefficients and a hypergeometric kernel.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson-Mellin factorization forces the functional action on powers to contain ζ(s)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poisson resummation makes the test sum rapidly decaying at both endpoints, so its Mellin action analytically continues as ζ(s)Mφ(s); evaluating at nontrivial zeros deletes the otherwise sign-indefinite residue terms and produces a usable sum rule.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Width constraints can be replaced by derivatives at the self-dual Gaussian
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The argument identifies the only unconstrained width dependence, shows its first derivative vanishes at k=1, and obtains even-derivative sum rules whose vacuum term is the ∆→0 limit, forming the numerical basis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fixed derivative order yields a scalar-gap bound with apparent quadratic large-c growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first numerical regime shows a qualitative mismatch between the scalar bound and familiar linear scales: at four derivatives the fitted leading behavior is near c²/(4π²), while the authors explicitly flag the order-of-limits caveat.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discretized positivity search requires adversarial resampling and exposes two scaling bottlenecks
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the functional is not polynomial-times-positive, the calculation samples dimensions, solves a linear program, checks positivity globally, and resamples negative regions; convergence slows with c while kernel evaluation grows as c^4.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bootstrap scalar-gap bounds and the averaged Narain scale probe different extrema
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source derives the averaged Narain scalar-gap scale from the integrated average density, contrasts its near-linear growth with much larger bootstrap upper bounds, and warns that an average need not resemble the optimum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-annihilating Virasoro functionals lose both convergence and sign control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two independent failures are isolated: integration weakens dimension decay from exponential to exponential-in-square-root, which can lose against Cardy growth, and character coefficients vary in sign across spin, defeating a uniformly positive functional.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A conjectural scalar-only Virasoro sum rule works below a sharp convergence threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplying by the c=1 cusp factor suggests a scalar-only rule for general Virasoro spectra; high-dimension decay implies c<1+6 min(k,k^-1), hence c<7, and numerical tests support the rule while derivation and analytic continuation remain open.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The SU(3)1 scalar spectrum turns zeta zeros into high-temperature log-oscillations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An explicit c=2 model shows how subtracting the leading terms and rescaling isolates oscillations whose envelope distinguishes critical-line zeros; fitting finite-temperature data recovers early known zeros, while exponential residue decay and truncation limit the test to finite height.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Virasoro scalar crossing requires harmonic analysis beyond square-integrable cusp subtraction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors identify the cusp multiplication that introduced all spins and propose that a genuinely scalar Virasoro equation may require harmonic analysis accommodating exponential cusp divergence, with the c<7 guessed rule as a boundary case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A fixed-spin crossing equation couples target-spin data to scalar and Maass-cusp sectors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Keeping a nonzero Fourier spin restores Maass cusp contributions: the Eisenstein contour can still be evaluated using scalar data and the same zeta-zero poles, but sporadic cusp eigenvalues block a comparably clean analytic equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stronger scalar bounds may require intersecting crossing systems or retaining zero residues
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The large gap between current bounds and the averaged Narain scale motivates three concrete changes: combine scalar with traditional or four-point crossing, broaden the functional family beyond Gaussians, or incorporate rather than annihilate zeta-zero residues.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian action reduces every crossing term to Bessel and hypergeometric kernels
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The appendix computes a reusable transform library for powers, exponentials, and confluent hypergeometric terms, then assembles the exact functional action subject to the two Gaussian-width constraints.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: At c=3 the infinite arithmetic kernel collapses to a closed hyperbolic expression
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source shows that odd central charge can make the general functional action elementary; for c=3 the divisor-weighted infinite sum is evaluated exactly, enabling faster and more transparent positivity analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Odd c≥5 admits a finite auxiliary-function kernel after exact divisor resummation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Auxiliary finite sums convert the general special-function action into an odd-c closed form, and the remaining arithmetic sum can also be evaluated exactly; this explains both numerical tractability and the c^4 growth noted in the main text.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: k↔k^-1 antisymmetry yields an equivalent scalar crossing equation for every c
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying k^(3/2)∂k reveals an inversion-antisymmetric form that converges for arbitrary c, not merely odd c, and shows the vacuum term is the ∆→0 member of the same kernel family.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: At c=1 the spectral decomposition loses cusp forms and crossing reduces to theta modularity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Exceptional poles change the generic decomposition: the radius-parametrized free boson has no Maass sector, its scalar spectrum makes all zeta-zero residues vanish, and the resulting arithmetic identity is checked by a Möbius divisor identity and Jacobi-theta modular transformation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Mellin zero cancels the apparent ζ(1) divergence in the general c=1 functional
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For a general U(1) c=1 theory the zero-residue simplification cannot be assumed. The same functional seems to hit ζ(1), but Mφ(1)=0 cancels the pole; after removing a formally divergent constant the arithmetic sum is exactly evaluated into convergent even-derivative rules.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The c=2 Narain partition function factorizes into three completed Eisenstein factors plus triple cusp products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Repackaging the four moduli as two upper-half-plane variables exposes a special spectral factorization with a regularized Eisenstein constant and parity-matched triple Maass products, explaining why c=2 needs a separate contour analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: At c=2 a pole at s=1 and zeta-zero poles produce logarithmic leading behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Scalar projection removes the triple cusp products; shifting the special contour crosses s=1 and (1+z)/2 poles, producing a log(y)/y leading term, explicit zeta-zero residues, and a convergent hypergeometric remainder.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The c=2 mechanism extends from Narain models to any gapped U(1)2 CFT
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source identifies the minimal ingredients that survive beyond the explicit moduli factorization: subtract the regularized Eisenstein series, use the scalar gap to constrain allowed poles, and evaluate the same nonperturbative correction kernel.

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The obstruction is for the documented functional family; the source explicitly leaves open a different annihilator that preserves faster decay.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Zero annihilation trades sign control for weaker spectral localization

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The gap bounds are solver- and discretization-conditioned, and finite-temperature recovery only reproduces already known low zeros rather than independently testing RH.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Empirical checks probe different links of the construction

within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The scalar-only rule is numerically observed rather than derived, and neither analytic continuation to high c nor control of Maass data is supplied.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Virasoro extension has three separable bottlenecks

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Gaussian transforms exist for general c, odd c permits exact arithmetic simplification, and k↔k^-1 antisymmetrization produces an equivalent equation for every c; closed forms improve computation but are not the source of the crossing identity's validity.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: All-c convergence of the kernel does not by itself provide positivity, efficient derivatives, or sharp numerical bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source makes kernel choice a two-constraint design problem: residues must reproduce the n-dependent power in the alternating zeta term, while the resulting rational function of n must still have a usable series sum. result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The evaluated residue integral replaces each alternating-series term by an integral, after which the source interchanges sum and integral and applies a closed alternating rational-series formula to produce Eq. result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starting from Eq. (2.6), the source uses evenness to restrict the integral to the positive half-line and writes b=b'+iq so that s=1/2+ib has real part 1/2-q. result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pole abundance and gap control beyond the earlier explicit-formula restrictions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The abstract and introduction identify the target phenomenon: a good quotient of products of zeta translates has infinitely many poles to the right of every fixed vertical threshold, with control of gaps between pole ordinates. They also say the treatment subsumes the earlier section without assuming RH and covers more functions, locating the paper's actual advance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A good Dirichlet series combines right-half-plane convergence with recurrent non-small coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The definition couples convergence in a far right half-plane to a lower-bound condition asserting that sufficiently large multiplicative ranges contain a coefficient that is not too small. That coefficient condition is later the bridge from analytic mean values back to the Dirichlet series, while Remark 2 identifies it with the earlier paper's working hypothesis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Good shifted-zeta quotients and finite sums have poles in every logarithmic ordinate window
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 turns the abstract goodness condition into a pole theorem for a Dirichlet polynomial times a quotient of finite products of shifted zeta functions. Besides infinitely many poles beyond each fixed ordinate threshold, it asserts a pole in an interval beginning at every sufficiently large Y and having logarithmic length, and preserves the conclusion for finite sums when the sum itself is good.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The pole mechanism extends across derivatives, ordinary and number-field L-functions, and localized shifts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remarks separate what the proof actually needs from the initial zeta notation: bounded-order derivatives may replace numerator factors, ordinary L-functions and arithmetic-progression series may be used, number-field and ray-class zeta functions are admitted under a degree comparison, and shifts can vary under localization. This exposes a reusable analytic mechanism rather than a one-function accident.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic control plus goodness forces a pole in a prescribed short vertical window
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 abstracts the concrete zeta quotient into F=F1/F2. Under analytic continuation, boundedness, a zero-free denominator, growth control, and scale conditions on H and auxiliary parameters, goodness rules out analyticity throughout the window T-H to T+H. This is the engine from which Theorem 1 is said to follow.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local zero counts produce zero-separated Ingham lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Step I first bounds the number of denominator zeros in unit-height intervals and then applies pigeonhole separation to choose a horizontal line a controlled distance from every such zero. This converts a discrete zero count into a contour on which later analytic estimates can safely run.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero separation controls the logarithmic derivative and then the quotient on horizontal boundaries
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemmas 4.3-4.4 use an Ingham line to bound F2'/F2, integrate that information into a bound for log F2 and its reciprocal, and combine it with the numerator bound to control F. This is the analytic transfer that makes the selected horizontal contours usable in maximum-modulus rectangles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A doubly decaying sine kernel turns contour bounds into an interior strip bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first maximum-modulus step multiplies F by an exponential of a squared sine. On a rectangle whose horizontal sides are Ingham lines, the kernel suppresses the potentially large horizontal-boundary contribution, while the two vertical sides have controlled values. The result is a uniform bound after trimming controlled neighborhoods of the vertical window's ends.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A second kernel and a balancing monomial transport the upper bound to a left vertical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The second maximum-modulus step introduces Y(s)=F(s) times a power weight and another decaying sine kernel on a rectangle extending from a left line to the convergence half-plane. The power base is chosen to balance the two vertical-boundary contributions, and a sufficiently tall rectangle makes the horizontal contributions negligible, yielding a left-line upper bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic continuation and endpoint control yield a coefficient-sensitive mean-square lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Step III quotes a Balasubramanian-Ramachandra theorem whose operational role is to lower-bound a vertical mean square of a Dirichlet series by a weighted sum of squared coefficients, provided analytic continuation, endpoint bounds, and scale conditions hold. The paper then selects the ordinary Dirichlet frequencies needed for its application.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Goodness converts the mean-value theorem into a large value on the left line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors apply the quoted theorem to the mean square of F(-A+it), using boundary lines supplied by the preceding maximum-modulus work. The coefficient lower bound in goodness guarantees a non-small term in the coefficient sum, which forces a lower bound for the mean square and hence a point where F is large.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The propagated upper bound and coefficient-forced lower bound forbid a long pole-free interval
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Step IV compares Lemma 5.3's left-line upper bound with Step III's pointwise lower bound. Choosing the auxiliary constant large forces an upper restriction on H incompatible with H exceeding a constant multiple of the two logarithmic trimming scales, completing the contradiction and Theorem 2.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Degree dominance marks the proposed reach of the quotient method
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The concluding remarks propose replacing individual zeta translates by products of ray-class zeta functions or bounded-order derivatives over arbitrary number fields. They identify a comparison between maximal associated field degrees, together with normalization of the denominator at positive infinity, as the kind of condition needed for the method, and flag the need for usable sufficient conditions for goodness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A distinguished pole in a purely imaginary shift quotient forces recurrent poles nearby
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 3 states a concrete specialization for purely imaginary shifts: if the quotient has the designated pole at s=1 minus the first numerator shift, then it has infinitely many poles above every fixed ordinate and, near each sufficiently large Y, a pole whose ordinate differs from Y by at most a constant times log log Y.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mellin integral converted to a keyhole-contour continuation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A Mellin integral for the Dirichlet series is re-expressed through a contour around the origin with an explicit branch convention, producing a continuation that the source says is one-valued and finite except at 1 and vanishes at negative even integers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour reversal and residues expose the s to 1-s symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For negative real part the source reverses the contour to enclose the other singularities, sums the contributions at integer multiples of 2 pi i, and concludes that a completed zeta expression is invariant under replacing s by 1-s.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gamma insertion turns the completed zeta into a theta Mellin transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Motivated by the functional symmetry, the source inserts a half-argument gamma integral termwise, defines a theta-like sum psi, and rewrites the completed zeta as its Mellin integral. This is the bridge that makes reciprocal-variable symmetry available.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Jacobi reciprocity symmetrizes the theta integral at x equals 1
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reciprocal-variable relation for psi is used to split and transform the Mellin integral, yielding a form with an elementary pole term and an integral whose paired powers display the functional symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Centering the completed function yields even cosine-integral representations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The substitution s equals one half plus t i defines xi(t), and the source gives cosine-integral forms that make dependence on t through an even kernel visible and support the subsequent statements that xi is finite and expandable in powers of t squared.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero count, real-zero conjecture, failed proof search, and product from roots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source confines possible zeros to a strip, gives an asymptotic count, reports finding approximately that many real roots, calls it very probable that all roots are real while explicitly wishing for a stricter proof and recording futile attempts, then uses zero density and growth to justify a logarithmic product representation up to a constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted prime-power counting as the inverse transform of log zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source defines a midpoint convention for the prime count, forms a weighted sum over prime powers, identifies log zeta divided by s as its Mellin transform, derives a vertical-line inverse using Fourier theory including the mean value at jumps, and identifies why direct integration of separated zero and gamma terms fails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integration by parts repairs an invalid termwise explicit-formula route
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After proposing substitution of the root-and-gamma expansion into the inverse transform, the source observes that the individual term integrals do not converge to infinity and changes the representation by integration by parts before evaluating factors separately.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gamma and zero contributions are compressed to one inverse-transform kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A limiting product expansion for the gamma factor is differentiated, after which the source states that every nonconstant term in the expression for the smoothed count has a common factor-parameter integral form. This converts a heterogeneous decomposition into one reusable contour calculation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factor inversion splits by the sign of the parameter real part and fixes branches by limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source evaluates the generic factor contribution differently according as the factor parameter has negative or positive real part, obtains logarithmic-integral forms with different endpoints, and uses limiting imaginary or real directions to determine paths, branches, and integration constants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zero-based explicit formula requires magnitude ordering
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The factor evaluations are combined into a formula for the smoothed prime-power count with a main logarithmic-integral term, paired zero contributions, an additional integral, and a constant; the source then specifies ordering zeros by magnitude and warns that reordering the series can produce an arbitrary real value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Squarefree alternating inversion recovers the prime count from the smoothed count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source inverts the weighted prime-power relation by summing over integers not divisible by any nontrivial square, with sign determined by the number of prime factors, thereby recovering F from values of f at fractional powers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite zero sums model oscillatory prime-density corrections around nonperiodic terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: With finitely many zero terms, differentiating the smoothed explicit formula gives an approximate density whose cosine terms encode local oscillation; the source contrasts these with nonperiodic logarithmic-integral corrections from prime powers and states an order-scale limitation for the Li approximation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Historical counts motivate tracking individual periodic terms and the smoother function f
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source compares Li with counts reported by Gauss and Goldschmidt, notes fluctuations and the absence of an observed law, proposes monitoring individual periodic terms in future counts, and suggests that the weighted function f behaves more regularly than F and agrees on average with the stated main expression in the observed range.

section_argument_map.label: Opening and prime-encoding point of departure
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Frames prime accumulation and identifies the Euler product and integer Dirichlet series as two convergent representations of zeta.

section_argument_map.label: Mellin continuation and functional symmetry
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Passes from a positive-real Mellin integral to a keyhole contour, continues zeta, identifies the pole and negative-even zeros, and obtains the s to 1-s symmetry by reversing the contour and summing singular contributions.

section_argument_map.label: Theta reformulation and centered xi transform
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces a theta series, applies Jacobi's reciprocal-variable identity, symmetrizes the integral, and centers the completed function as xi(t) with cosine-integral representations.

section_argument_map.label: Zeros, conjectural location, and product representation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Bounds the zero region, estimates zero count, distinguishes observed real zeros from the unproved all-real conjecture, records abandoned proof attempts, and represents log xi through its roots using a growth argument.

section_argument_map.label: Prime-power counting and transform inversion
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Defines midpoint prime counting and its weighted prime-power smoothing, derives the log-zeta Mellin relation, inverts it via Fourier theory, and repairs a nonconvergent termwise substitution by integration by parts.

section_argument_map.label: Common factor kernels and branch-sensitive contour evaluation
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Reduces gamma and zero factors to a common inverse-transform form, evaluates the kernel in cases determined by the real part of a factor parameter, and fixes branches and constants through limiting paths.

section_argument_map.label: Explicit formula and ordering condition
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Combines pole, zeros, remaining integral, and constant into an explicit formula for the smoothed count while warning that the zero terms require magnitude ordering and are reorder-sensitive.

section_argument_map.label: Recovery, truncated density, and empirical diagnostics
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Recovers the prime-counting function by squarefree alternating inversion, interprets finitely many zero terms as oscillatory density corrections, separates nonperiodic prime-power effects, and proposes empirical tracking of individual periodic terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 7 replaces direct Laplace analysis by Gaussian averaging and a Gamma integral, with a bulk-tail split that gives a uniform stationary asymptotic for complex b.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repulsive zero dynamics predicts the exact accessible relaxation scale

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetric infinite products turn zero geometry into coefficient identities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The sine product shows how convergence-respecting symmetry converts a known divisor into Newton-sum identities, while the DL definition isolates the geometric prerequisite and links a one-line divisor to reflection symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gamma turns factorial interpolation into divisor factorization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gamma simultaneously interpolates factorials, supplies a prescribed pole divisor, factors the sine complement, and illustrates why low-order symmetric holomorphic interpolation can be rigid across scalar domains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Divisor-preserving exponential factors limit naive Newton reconstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplying by an exponential changes Taylor data without changing zeros, showing why divisor information alone does not determine coefficient identities; finite-order/minimality constraints motivate the source's transalgebraic heuristic for otherwise unsafe limiting algebra.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler factors are rescaled sine divisors, but infinite products need arithmetic control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unique factorization creates the Euler product; each local factor has a vertical divisor and sine-like form, motivating a local-to-global DL conjecture while the text explicitly warns that arbitrary infinite products do not preserve it and cites a non-Eulerian failure case.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithms isolate the prime-frequency term from a controlled remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Taking logs of the Euler product separates the prime sum from higher powers whose remainder stays bounded near one, so the zeta pole transfers divergence to the reciprocal-prime sum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Hankel contour removes the Mellin integral's half-plane restriction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Mellin representation is converted into a contour integral entire in the parameter; contour deformation reconnects it to the original integral, gamma reflection exposes the candidate poles, and monodromy/Cauchy cancellation leaves only the simple pole at one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local expansion at zero converts continuation into Bernoulli values and trivial zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Bernoulli generating series inserted into the contour representation makes negative-integer values coefficient extractions, separating rational special values from forced real trivial zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Residues at the contour lattice produce the first functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Closing the contour in a region of decay converts the Hankel integral into residues at a regularly spaced lattice, whose sum is zeta at the reflected argument; gamma normalization then yields the functional equation and transports special values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completion converts a meromorphic equation into an entire zero symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gamma duplication/reflection and a symmetric pole-killing factor define the order-one entire xi function, turning the functional equation into an involution and forcing nonreal zeros into conjugate/reflected orbits within the critical strip.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theta modularity transfers through Mellin splitting to zeta symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poisson summation gives theta inversion; splitting the Mellin integral at the self-dual point and changing variables creates an expression invariant under parameter reflection, providing a second route to the same completion and a Fourier-cosine representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-count asymptotics and sampled real zeros do not supply the missing critical-line proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separates Riemann's zero-count asymptotic, finite computations, partial later lower bounds, and the stronger assertion that every zero is on the line, preserving the gap between density evidence and totality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional symmetry makes the critical line the minimal DL configuration
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Once completion and Euler factors live in a divisor-on-lines setting, reflection symmetry permits paired vertical lines, while the strongest one-line configuration is forced to be the critical line; this compresses RH into a minimal-divisor heuristic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero real parts control prime-counting oscillation size
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each nontrivial zero contributes an oscillatory prime-counting term whose magnitude is governed by its real part, yielding an error estimate equivalent to RH and tying zero-free regions to asymptotic accuracy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic differentiation equates prime powers with the completed zero divisor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Euler-product differentiation produces von Mangoldt weights, while Hadamard factorization of the completed function produces reciprocal distances to zeros; equating them yields the prime-zero identity that powers later explicit formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Möbius sign cancellation reformulates RH but resists half-plane improvement
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The reciprocal Euler product encodes square-free parity in Möbius coefficients, suggesting cancellation strong enough for continuation to the half-plane, but the source records that even a weaker convergence improvement remains unavailable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime powers become a positive step measure adapted to Mellin inversion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Log zeta naturally weights prime powers by reciprocal multiplicity; the resulting step function has a Mellin/Fourier-Laplace transform, and Möbius inversion recovers ordinary prime counting.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integration by parts makes zero-factorization compatible with transform inversion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Direct substitution of the logarithmic zero product is divergent, so an integration-by-parts regularization permits termwise inversion and decomposes prime counting into a smooth term, trivial corrections, and zero-driven oscillations; controlling the latter is the unresolved step.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A smooth prime approximation can be striking yet fail as an exact predictor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Ramanujan's Möbius-corrected logarithmic-integral approximation is reported as numerically false in its strongest reading, motivating a weaker recurrence/density question and illustrating how impressive local accuracy can coexist with unmodeled zero oscillations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero exponentials distinguish prime-power frequencies from generic frequencies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Riemann/Landau explicit formulas show enhanced noncancellation exactly at prime-power frequencies; Cramer's exponential sum packages the same resonance into meromorphic continuation with singularities tied to logarithms of primes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A symmetric contour becomes a Fourier-Poisson distribution and positivity criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluating a log-derivative contour by residues and by Euler/functional-equation boundary terms yields explicit formulas; distributional test functions unify them, and Weil's reformulation converts RH into positivity on a suitable function class.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit and trace formulas share a divisor-frequency architecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selberg, noncommutative, and zeta-regularized trace viewpoints are presented as instances of a common transformation between spectral/divisor data and geometric or Dirichlet frequencies, motivating Poisson-Newton rather than a literal physical identification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson-Newton interpolates between Newton identities and Poisson summation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For a finite-order meromorphic Dirichlet series, the Newton-Cramer distribution of its divisor is equated with atoms generated by logarithmic Dirichlet frequencies; one-frequency and polynomial specializations recover Poisson and Newton, while zeta and Selberg specializations recover explicit and trace formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Inverse Laplace of the logarithmic derivative extends Newton relations beyond Dirichlet series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing discrete Dirichlet data by the inverse Laplace transform of f'/f extends the divisor identity to finite-order meromorphic functions and reinterprets Gauss's gamma integral as continuous-exponent Newton relations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pair correlation agreement underdetermines a Hilbert-Polya mechanism
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Montgomery's normalized spacing law and GUE agreement are separated from the much stronger existence of a Hermitian operator; the source offers a shared Fourier kernel as an alternative explanation and treats numerical confirmation as statistical, not causal, evidence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-orbit trace matching exposes both a shared formalism and a sign obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substituting a formally divergent Euler product into the zero-count fluctuation aligns prime logarithms with periodic-orbit periods and amplitudes, yet a divergent sign and absence of a natural system block literal identification; Poisson-Newton offers a broader common explanation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unnormalized zero differences encode low zeros as repulsion deficits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Histograms of all zero differences, rather than only normalized neighbors, are reported to show a hierarchy of uniformity, Montgomery behavior, and deficits at existing zero locations, suggesting translation-invariant global rigidity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mating distinct L-function zeros points to product-character divisors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Cross-differences between zeros of distinct Dirichlet L-functions place deficits at zeros of the product character and local-factor pairings recover local poles, a pattern the source argues is algebraic-arithmetic rather than same-spectrum quantum correlation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The eñe-product turns local root multiplication into global divisor convolution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A second product on rational Euler factors forms a commutative ring and extends primewise to arithmetic Dirichlet series; its divisor behavior predicts why cross-L-function zero differences locate the divisor of a product-character L-function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A unit equation converts an off-line zero into a forbidden product zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source uses the eñe-product unit equation to argue heuristically that an off-critical zero would induce a zero in a half-plane where the product identity has none, illustrating how a new algebra on L-functions could constrain divisors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adelic Fourier-Mellin analysis puts finite and infinite primes on one footing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Ostrowski's places, restricted idèles, factorized test functions, and local Fourier-Mellin transforms reconstruct finite Euler factors and the archimedean gamma factor uniformly; global Fourier duality then explains the completed functional equation and the need for the infinite place.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Greater L-function generality tends to reduce available analytic control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The survey explicitly organizes the zeta universe as increasing structural scope paired with diminishing knowledge of continuation and other analytic properties, and hypothesizes that a successful mechanism should extend beyond one function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conjugate pairing restores a self-functional equation for complex characters
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Character multiplicativity yields the Euler product, parity fixes the gamma factor, and a non-real character's L-function is paired with its conjugate so the product has self-duality and a union divisor, allowing the generalized critical-line statement without pretending each factor is individually real analytic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dedekind zeta packages ideal factorization and global invariants into analytic data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Unique ideal factorization gives local Euler factors; completion reflects real/complex embeddings, while the residue at one encodes class number, regulator, roots of unity, and discriminant, showing how a zeta singularity carries arithmetic structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Artin local factors are natural algebraically but analytically unusable without transfer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Frobenius actions define characteristic-polynomial local factors in arbitrary representations, but continuation and functional equation are recovered only by reducing characters to one-dimensional/known zeta cases, demonstrating bridge construction as a substitute for direct Euler-product analysis.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-field point counts become rational cohomological zeta data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Frobenius-periodic point counts define a generating zeta function; the Weil package links rationality, duality, absolute-value bounds, and Betti degrees, and cohomology turns the polynomials into Frobenius actions so geometric positivity can prove the local RH bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local rational RH does not resolve global transcendental Euler products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplying finite-field local factors across rationally independent prime frequencies creates a genuinely transcendental Hasse-Weil function; the source sharply distinguishes success on rational/periodic local models from the analytic continuation and divisor problem of the global product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Automorphic local representations propose a universal L-function package but not its analytic proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Finite-place polynomial factors, archimedean gamma parameters, contragredient symmetry, and Langlands generation give a broad structural container, while the source emphasizes that an Euler-product definition alone does not deliver continuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke eigenvectors turn modular transformation laws into Euler products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Modular symmetry supplies analytic continuation and reflection, while simultaneous Hecke eigenstructure enforces coefficient multiplicativity and hence an Euler product, exhibiting the dual analytic-arithmetic input missing from bare Euler-product definitions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maass and higher-rank forms replace holomorphy with invariant spectral data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Laplacian eigenfunctions, Fourier-Bessel coefficients, and commuting Hecke operators reproduce Euler products and functional equations without holomorphic modular forms, then Iwasawa/higher-rank structure generalizes the same pipeline to degree-n local factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symbolic dynamics makes periodic-orbit zeta rational by trace enumeration
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Fixed-point counts define dynamical zeta; a finite Markov transition matrix gives counts as traces of powers and sums them to a determinant, while hyperbolic Markov partitions extend the combinatorial mechanism up to boundary redundancy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Selberg class packages four recurring constraints without explaining their origin
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Analyticity, Ramanujan coefficient growth, completed reflection, and controlled Euler factors are isolated as a compact interface for a conjectural RH domain, summarizing recurring requirements across prior families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kummer-compatible special values define p-adic zeta branches
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Congruences among Bernoulli special values make residue-class-restricted sequences converge p-adically; removing the local Euler factor yields analytic branches interpolating complex zeta values in a new scalar domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Current evidence types support plausibility but not total zero control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separately discounts finite computation, partial critical-line proportions, weak off-line density, algebraic/dynamical toy models, and spectral analogy as insufficient for the universal claim, offering a reusable audit against overinterpreting proxy success.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The central bottleneck couples continuation beyond convergence with rigid prime frequencies

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta as the prototypical Dirichlet series

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sum-integral tail replacement for zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how to replace the tail of a Dirichlet series by an integral with a controlled error, then choose the truncation length from the imaginary frequency to obtain a logarithmic bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product converts integer sums into prime-local factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses geometric series, absolute convergence, and unique factorization to establish the sum/product duality that drives later zero-free arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Von Mangoldt weighting exposes the logarithmic derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why the technically natural prime-counting weight is the one whose Dirichlet series equals -zeta'/zeta, making zeros and poles directly relevant to prime distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet series as a Fourier transform in log n
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reframes n^{-it} as an oscillatory frequency on logarithmic scale and motivates coefficient recovery as Fourier-like inversion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A truncated contour kernel approximates a threshold indicator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the step-function kernel by shifting contours toward the half-plane where y^s decays, with separate behavior for y below, at, and above one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncated Perron formula recovers coefficient sums
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the scalar threshold kernel into a general coefficient-sum inversion, with absolute convergence justifying exchange of sum and contour integral and truncation frequency controlling error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothing trades a sharp cutoff for faster transform decay
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies slow 1/|t| decay as the transform-side cost of a sharp interval and proposes smooth physical-space weights as the reusable remedy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Perron inversion turns Psi into a movable contour integral
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializes Perron to -zeta'/zeta, controls the truncation error, chooses c near one, and contrasts direct boundary evaluation with analytic continuation plus contour deformation and residues.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional-part correction continues zeta to Re(s)>0
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a sum-plus-integral expression with a simple pole at one, proves independence of the arbitrary cutoff, and matches the original series where both apply.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Continuation formula controls zeta and its derivative near the 1-line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that choosing the cutoff at the frequency scale yields logarithmic and squared-logarithmic bounds slightly left of Re(s)=1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hardy-Littlewood approximation reduces the tail error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the need for an approximation useful left of the 1-line and isolates slow oscillation as the new ingredient that improves the error from a frequency-sized term to x^{-sigma}.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Slow phases make sums track integrals
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a special van der Corput estimate by separating the zero Fourier mode from faster nonzero modes and controlling the latter via integration by parts and monotonicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic phase converts slow oscillation into a short zeta approximation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies the oscillatory lemma to f(w)=-(t/2pi)log w, showing the sum-integral discrepancy is small when x is at least the frequency scale and interpreting polynomial length as analytic complexity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weighted PNT yields the ordinary prime-counting asymptotic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the quantitative weighted theorem, explains passage from Psi to pi by summation by parts, and situates the zeta route as the source of the asymptotic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A positive trigonometric combination prevents zeta from becoming too small
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the Euler product to form a nonnegative 3-4-1 frequency combination, converts that positivity into a lower bound to the right of one, and transports it slightly left using a derivative bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A weak zero-free strip produces a quantitative PNT
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves the Perron contour left without crossing zeros, extracts the pole residue x, separately bounds horizontal and vertical edges, and balances height against strip width.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Logarithmic losses can be absorbed into stretched-exponential savings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes explicit the common proof move of weakening an exponential constant to suppress fixed logarithmic factors and warns that recycled constants have changed value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Short-interval failure diagnoses the need for a wider zero-free region
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses subtraction of PNT estimates to show that the weak error can swamp a shorter-interval main term, then traces improvement back to how far the contour may move before zeros intervene.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic size bounds transfer to zero-free width
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Landau's general mechanism: a size bound in a strip of width 1/w yields a zero-free strip narrowed by phi times w, then instantiates it to obtain the classical logarithmic zero-free region.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity plus local growth control widens the zero-free region

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-free region bounds the logarithmic derivative inside it

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical zero-free width yields the square-root-log PNT error

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation reflects zeta across the critical line

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta control becomes a short oscillatory-sum problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It identifies the causal entry point of the method: a bound left of the one-line feeds Landau's theorem, while partial summation reduces the needed zeta estimate to sums of n^{-it} even at scales much shorter than t, where integral approximation fails.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Small bilinear shifts polynomialize the logarithmic phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Averaging n by shifts xy creates a small ratio xy/n, so a controlled Taylor truncation converts the unstructured logarithmic phase into a polynomial in xy. The required degree grows like log t/log N, explicitly exposing the method's later capacity bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two independent shifts create reorderable bilinear structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source isolates a reusable design principle: introduce two independent variables even when one suffices for Taylor expansion, because later inequalities can alternately complete and move either variable family inside absolute values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bilinear completion trades a sparse prime sum for an integer correlation sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The toy proposition exhibits the basic move: complete one side of a bilinear sum, apply Cauchy–Schwarz, expand a square into differences, and bound the resulting geometric progressions by distance to the nearest integer.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rational approximation distributes phases into controlled spacing bins
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Coprimality permutes residue classes, and a small perturbation from a/q places only O(1) phases in each interval of width 1/q; isolating the near-zero bin and harmonically summing the rest yields the key min(U,1/||·||) bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repeated Hölder duplication regularizes sparse polynomial-curve vectors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The sparse vectors (x,x²,…,x^r) cannot simply be completed to a box. Two Hölder steps duplicate each variable family, turn sums of curve points into difference coordinates, dominate shifted counts by the central Vinogradov mean value, and finally factor the phase into estimable one-dimensional sums.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal and volume counts predict the Vinogradov mean-value threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two structurally different lower bounds—diagonal solutions and average occupancy of difference boxes—motivate a two-term conjecture. Their crossover explains why k at least about r(r+1)/2 is the regime needed for near-uniform behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A quantitative mean-value bound is organized as induction through congruences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The theorem gives the explicit loss parameter governing the application, and the proof preview identifies the core architecture: fix degree, induct in variable count, reduce modulo a scale-matched prime, and invoke Linnik's lemma.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Power sums plus distinct residues rigidify a tuple modulo a prime power
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Congruences at different powers are first lifted to a common modulus. Newton identities convert power sums into elementary symmetric data, so the associated monic polynomials agree modulo p; distinct roots then force tuples to agree up to permutation modulo p^r.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The power-sum system is translation invariant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Subtracting a common center preserves every balanced power-sum equation because each binomial coefficient term is itself a lower-degree balanced equation. This permits residue classes to be normalized before scale reduction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The nonsingular residue branch freezes a class and applies Linnik at the matched scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Choosing p approximately Z^{1/r} matches Linnik's p^r range to the variable scale. Solutions with enough distinct residues are symmetrized, most residue classes are frozen using an integral/Hölder argument, translated to zero, and bounded by Linnik times a lower-variable mean value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The singular residue branch gains by occupying too few classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: When either half lacks r distinct residues, the number of admissible residue patterns drops. Hölder bounds each pattern by a common-class moment, and translation followed by division by p turns that moment into a smaller-scale Vinogradov count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Iterating scale descent proves the quantitative mean-value theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The induction separates the trivial small-scale regime from the scale-reduction regime and tracks how the loss parameter changes when k is reduced by r and Z is replaced by a power of Z.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three reductions define the final zeta-sum pipeline
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explicitly composes the argument: Taylor reduction produces U(n), Hölder duplication reduces U(n) to a mean value plus spacing sums, and the mean-value theorem supplies control when k is sufficiently large relative to r.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A rational-approximation degree window converts mean-value savings into zeta-sum cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After setting k proportional to r², the mean-value theorem supplies a global negative exponent. For degrees in a selected window, the explicit Taylor coefficients admit rational approximants with denominators in a favorable range, giving extra spacing savings; choosing the proportionality constant controls delta and makes the negative term dominate losses.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta-sum bound's strength is diagnosed by the N-versus-t scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For N=t^theta the estimate gives a power saving, while below every fixed power it remains nontrivial only down to an exponential-in-log(t) threshold. The source contrasts this with the square-root cancellation heuristic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Block decomposition transfers short-sum cancellation to a near-one-line zeta bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Hardy–Littlewood approximation is split into exponentially sized blocks; Abel summation imports the zeta-sum estimate into each weighted block, and a second grouping makes the block series summable. A different splitting point handles sigma farther from one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A controlled growth strip feeds Landau's theorem to widen the zero-free region
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The zeta bound is rewritten in exponential form on a restricted strip, matched to Landau's phi and width functions, and converted into the Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free boundary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour truncation is balanced against the zero-free decay to optimize the PNT error
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shifting the prime-number-theorem contour into the new zero-free region creates two competing error contributions; choosing the truncation height T to balance them yields the characteristic 3/5 and 1/5 exponents.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The error term encodes deep cancellation yet remains far from the RH scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The closing discussion separates qualitative applications of sharper errors from mere numerical refinement, identifies the zeta-sum estimate as the Fourier-analytic content transported to primes, and states that wider cancellation ranges would widen zero-free regions without providing a route to the critical line.

section_argument_map.label: 8. Bilinear forms
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Develops completion, rational-spacing bounds, and repeated Hölder duplication as a way to turn sparse polynomial-curve sums into mean-value counts and one-dimensional geometric sums.

section_argument_map.label: 11. Some spectacular (?) consequences
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Transfers zeta-sum cancellation to a near-one-line zeta bound, a zero-free region, and the optimized prime-number-theorem error term, then explains the remaining gap to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maximum modulus from powering and Cauchy estimates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Raises the function to high powers so fixed contour constants disappear after taking nth roots, then repeats the device on derivatives to force constancy at an interior maximum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local circular maximum principle globalized without a regular contour boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the circle-mean equality case and propagates it through connectedness to obtain the interior strict maximum principle on an arbitrary domain, then locates maxima on the boundary of bounded domains.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Boundary limsup control by compact exhaustion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses nested compact subsets and boundary-approaching maximizing points to convert sequential boundary limsup bounds into interior bounds, then derives minimum and boundary-value principles via reciprocals and exponentials.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded-strip Phragmen-Lindelof and multiplicative interpolation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Controls an infinite strip by multiplying by a Gaussian-type damping factor, applying the finite maximum principle, and removing the perturbation; normalization yields the three-lines geometric interpolation bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Half-strip Phragmen-Lindelof below the critical exponential growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a tailored exponential barrier whose decay dominates subcritical growth, and identifies a critical-growth counterexample showing why the threshold and barrier shape are natural.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Interpolation of polynomial and limiting boundary growth across a strip
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms unequal boundary powers by a single-valued complex power and transforms asymptotic boundary bounds by an auxiliary rational factor, producing interior exponents as linear interpolants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Schwarz contraction and rigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Divides out the forced zero, applies the maximum principle on expanding circles, and obtains both contraction and the rigid rotation equality case, including scaling to a general disk.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Caratheodory inequality via a half-plane-to-disk transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Encodes a real-part bound as a disk-valued Möbius transform, applies Schwarz's lemma, and inverts the transform to bound the original function and identify equality cases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Borel coefficient bounds by root-of-unity filtering
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: First controls the linear coefficient from a real-part bound, then averages rotations to isolate any chosen coefficient, a reusable symmetry-projection technique.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One positive-real-part integral yields coefficient, increment, and derivative bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reverses the preceding dependency chain: Fourier extraction of the nonnegative real part gives coefficient bounds directly, from which function and all-derivative estimates follow.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-free entire functions are exponentials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Integrates the entire logarithmic derivative to show a zero-free entire function is an exponential, then factors finitely many zeros before addressing infinite products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weierstrass canonical product with adaptive primary factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Cancels enough terms of each logarithm to make an infinite product converge locally uniformly, choosing fixed genus when a reciprocal-power sum converges and adaptive genus otherwise.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite order limits zero density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines order through maximum modulus and converts growth into a quantitative zero-count bound by dividing out enclosed zeros and applying the maximum principle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponent of convergence and genus of the zero set
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives convergence of reciprocal powers from the zero-count estimate and positions canonical-product genus between the exponent of convergence and the entire-function order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard factorization from logarithmic derivatives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Controls the logarithmic derivative after removing enclosed zeros, integrates it around expanding circles, and recovers an exponential polynomial times a canonical product for finite-order entire functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Order equals the maximum of exponential-polynomial degree and zero exponent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Bounds primary factors using an exponent arbitrarily close to the zero exponent, proving that total order is exactly the larger of the polynomial factor's degree and the zero-set exponent, with consequences for nonintegral order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gamma as a Mellin integral and factorial interpolation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Establishes convergence and analyticity of the Mellin integral and obtains the recurrence by integration by parts, explaining Gamma's interpolation role.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Beta integral and Gamma reflection formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Changes variables in a double Mellin integral to derive the beta quotient, then specializes it to the half-value and the reflection identity that later drives zeta continuation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hankel-contour continuation of Gamma and reciprocal entireness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses a keyed branch around the positive axis to express Gamma through an entire contour integral and cosecant, locating poles and residues and deducing that the reciprocal is entire.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reciprocal Gamma as an order-one canonical product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines the contour estimate, zero exponent, and Hadamard theorem to factor reciprocal Gamma, determine Euler's constant, recover Gauss's limiting product, and obtain logarithmic convexity from the log derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bohr-Mollerup-Artin characterization of Gamma
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that recurrence alone admits periodic ambiguity, while positivity, normalization, and log convexity squeeze any candidate between adjacent Gauss approximants and force uniqueness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gauss multiplication formula from Gamma uniqueness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs a product of shifted Gamma factors satisfying the same recurrence and log convexity, invokes uniqueness up to scale, and determines the scale asymptotically.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform complex Stirling formula from a bounded periodic remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites log Gamma as a main term plus an integral of the bounded sawtooth remainder, integrates by parts, and obtains uniform sectorial asymptotics and log-derivative consequences.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product and zero-freeness for Re(s)>1
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Justifies the prime-factor product by finite truncation and unique factorization, making the prime connection exact and proving nonvanishing in the absolute-convergence half-plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime data encoded by log zeta and its logarithmic derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the Euler product into a prime-counting integral, prime-power logarithmic series, von Mangoldt logarithmic derivative, and Möbius reciprocal series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta products generate divisor and shifted-divisor coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses multiplication of absolutely convergent Dirichlet series and Euler factors to derive divisor-count, divisor-sum, and squared shifted-divisor identities later reused in a zero-free-line proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial summation and half-planes of Dirichlet-series convergence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the summation-by-parts integral, uses it to prove angular uniform convergence, and thereby explains why convergence regions are half-planes supporting analytic termwise differentiation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniqueness of Dirichlet coefficients from remote zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplies by the leading exponential and lets the real part tend to infinity in a controlled angle, forcing the first coefficient to vanish and then iterating.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Absolute abscissa and singularity forced by nonnegative coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates ordinary and absolute convergence, bounds their gap for ordinary Dirichlet series, and shows positivity prevents analytic continuation through the convergence boundary by a Taylor-series contradiction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Perron coefficient-sum recovery via contour truncation and growth control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proves the Mellin step-function kernel, controls Dirichlet partial sums uniformly, and moves a contour for the tail to rigorously recover a sharp partial sum from the generating series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Order-free alternative proof of Perron's formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Avoids a global order estimate by splitting finite and tail series, applying partial summation at an intermediate line, and obtaining a tail bound that vanishes as the split moves outward.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hankel-contour continuation of zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin-transforms the geometric series, wraps the kernel around its branch point, and expresses zeta as Gamma times an entire contour integral, exposing the pole at one and special values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First functional equation by summing contour residues
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expands the Hankel contour across the lattice of kernel poles, lets a square contour escape, and packages the result into the symmetric completed zeta and xi function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second functional equation from the fractional-part Fourier series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Continues zeta using the bounded sawtooth error, repeatedly integrates its primitive to extend the domain, and inserts its Fourier series to derive the functional equation through sine Mellin transforms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vertical-strip bounds for zeta by optimized truncation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares zeta with a finite Dirichlet sum plus an integral remainder and chooses the truncation at the height, yielding logarithmic growth on Re(s)>=1 and polynomial bounds further left.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation yields theta reciprocity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives Poisson summation from Fourier coefficients and Fejer summation under explicit convergence conditions, then applies it to the Gaussian to obtain the theta transformation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theta-Mellin splitting gives continuation and symmetry in one formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Mellin-transforms the theta tail, splits at one, uses theta reciprocity on the small-x piece, and obtains an entire symmetric remainder that simultaneously continues zeta and proves its functional equation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Completed zeta symmetry localizes and classifies zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses xi's entireness, reflection and conjugation symmetries, Euler-product nonvanishing, Gamma poles, and an alternating-series sign argument to isolate nontrivial zeros in the critical strip and trivial zeros at negative evens.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Xi growth forces infinitely many zeros and a canonical product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines Stirling and zeta bounds to identify xi's order-one but non-minimal growth, then invokes the earlier entire-function theory to force infinitely many zeros and derive product and logarithmic-derivative expansions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-freeness on Re(s)=1 from positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives two distinct positivity mechanisms: a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial applied to log zeta, and a positive-coefficient Dirichlet series whose convergence boundary must be singular.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Riemann-von Mangoldt formula by symmetry and argument variation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Counts xi zeros with the argument principle, reduces the contour by completed-function symmetries, evaluates Gamma's phase with Stirling, and bounds zeta's remaining phase by counting real-part crossings.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local zero density and asymptotics of ordered zero ordinates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extracts O(log T) zeros in fixed-height windows, reciprocal-ordinate sum bounds, and gamma_n asymptotics from the global counting law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Disk zero bound and argument principle
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factors zeros through disk automorphisms to compare zero count with maximum modulus, then states the logarithmic-derivative argument principle used in the zero-count proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hardy's Fourier-transform contradiction for infinitely many critical-line zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Represents the real critical-line xi function as a cosine transform, inverts it, and shows that eventual constant sign would force high even moments and derivatives to have one sign, contradicting boundary decay inherited from theta reciprocity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hamburger characterization from a zeta-type functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Mellin inversion to turn paired Dirichlet series and their functional equation into a theta-like transformation, shifts contours across finitely many poles, and exploits imaginary periodicity and residue equality to force constant coefficients and hence a scalar zeta function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Chebyshev functions transfer the prime number theorem among three normalizations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the prime-counting, theta, and psi encodings, proves their upper and lower limiting behavior agrees, and connects psi to the logarithmic derivative of zeta.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wiener-Ikehara from triangular Fourier smoothing and monotonicity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Subtracts the pole, smooths the boundary Fourier transform with a triangular kernel, passes to a positive convolution, and uses monotonicity to squeeze the normalized counting function to one.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime number theorem from zero-freeness, and zero-freeness back from PNT
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applies Wiener-Ikehara to the von Mangoldt transform using zeta's sole boundary pole and zero-free line, then reverses the logic by showing a PNT error transform cannot have a pole at 1+it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-counting asymptotics are equivalent to nth-prime asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers between a monotone counting function and its generalized inverse using logarithmic equivalence and adjacent-prime squeezing.

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The source progressively turns local maximum control into stripwise and asymptotic interpolation by introducing barriers whose boundary effect vanishes while their growth effect persists.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This is a within-source methodological relation, not a claim that all later strip estimates reduce to one identical theorem.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Maximum principles as growth-transport devices

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Disk/half-plane transforms and coefficient estimates control logarithms of zero-removed functions, supplying the derivative bounds used in Hadamard factorization.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Exact constants and some displayed formulas are OCR-sensitive and require scan verification before training use.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Real-part control feeds entire-function factorization

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The monograph reuses one architecture: zero locations determine a canonical product, growth bounds restrict the residual exponential polynomial, and logarithmic differentiation converts zeros into analytic identities.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The functions have different normalizations and growth evidence; this synthesis does not identify their products term by term.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Canonical products recur from arbitrary zeros to Gamma and xi

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Contour residues expose the pole lattice, fractional-part Fourier analysis exposes periodic error, and theta-Mellin splitting exposes self-reciprocity; each reaches the same completed symmetry through a different representation.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Equivalence is only at the final zeta identity; intermediate hypotheses and analytic continuations differ materially.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Three functional-equation routes expose complementary structure

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Partial summation establishes analytic half-planes and uniqueness, while Perron kernels recover sharp coefficient sums; the second proof shows the recovery can avoid a global order estimate.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source's sharp cutoff convention and convergence hypotheses remain essential and should not be generalized silently.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Dirichlet-series inversion connects analytic functions back to coefficients

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Completion converts the zeta functional equation into an entire symmetry; Stirling growth then enables canonical products and argument-principle counting, which in turn yields local zero-density information.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These results establish location symmetry and density, not the Riemann hypothesis.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Completed zeta links symmetry, growth, products, and zero counts

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Euler-product positivity excludes boundary zeros, positive-coefficient singularity principles diagnose forbidden continuation, and Tauberian positivity turns the surviving pole into prime-counting asymptotics.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The Tauberian conclusion also uses monotonicity and exact analytic boundary hypotheses, not positivity alone.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Positivity at the boundary is the bridge to primes

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The source repeatedly changes representation: Mellin inversion recovers multiplicative-scale data, Fourier inversion detects sign and periodicity, and smoothed Fourier kernels convert boundary analyticity into Tauberian asymptotics.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These transforms are not interchangeable; each unit carries its own convergence and local regularity conditions.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Fourier and Mellin transforms serve distinct inversion roles
