result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three responses to analytical intractability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates difficult models by tractable analogues, replaces singular exact quantities by smoothed observables, and organizes spectra into ensembles whose shared statistics define universality.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation turns quantum lattice labels into periodic orbits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The rectangular billiard makes explicit how Fourier duality separates a smooth density term from oscillatory terms indexed by classical periodic-orbit lengths.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Density of states as the imaginary trace of the resolvent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replaces dependence on explicit eigenvalue formulas by a Green-function representation that becomes the general starting point for trace formulas.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quotient geometry implemented by summing Green-function images
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that a fundamental-domain Green function is produced from the covering-space kernel by summing group images, with the identity image furnishing the local singularity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trace-formula divergence is repaired by test-function smoothing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why naive orbit sums are not mathematical objects and how rapid decay of Fourier harmonics makes the smoothed trace convergent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolic invariants under fractional-linear transformations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds the geometry-preserving PSL(2,R) action together with invariant measure, geodesics, and Laplace-Beltrami operator needed to transfer quotient and trace ideas from the plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Discrete-group quotient and fundamental domain
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects discreteness to separated images and defines the fundamental region by coverage plus uniqueness, illustrated by modular generators and side identifications.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Periodic geodesics are hyperbolic conjugacy classes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives the invariant geodesic, relates its length to the matrix trace, and explains why conjugate matrices represent the same closed orbit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Automorphic spectrum from the hyperbolic Green function and images
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the invariant Laplace-Beltrami eigenproblem, computes a distance-only covering-space resolvent, and enforces automorphy by summing its group images.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Identity group element determines the smooth hyperbolic density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the identity image from nontrivial classes and shows it produces the area-dependent mean density, approaching the planar Weyl term at high momentum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Centralizers remove double counting in a conjugacy-class sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Rewrites a group-element integral as a sum over conjugacy classes and replaces summation over conjugates by integration over the centralizer's fundamental domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exact Selberg trace formula from primitive geodesics and repetitions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Evaluates each hyperbolic conjugacy-class contribution and obtains an exact spectral/test-function identity whose orbit weights depend on primitive lengths and repetitions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trace formula forces exponential periodic-orbit proliferation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A heat-kernel test function converts the spectral zero mode into a large-time constraint that identifies orbit-density growth as e^l/l.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg zeta packages the primitive-orbit spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transforms the primitive-orbit product by logarithmic differentiation and matches its poles and zeros to spectral and smooth terms in the trace formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg spectral zeros and functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates nontrivial Laplace-spectrum zeros from topology-controlled trivial zeros and obtains analytic continuation through the s to 1-s symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrable spectra arise from periodic-orbit families
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Action quantization plus Poisson summation yields the Thomas-Fermi mean term, while saddle conditions select commensurable frequencies and hence continuous periodic-orbit families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical trajectories build the semiclassical Green function
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Hamilton-Jacobi phase and transport amplitude turn the resolvent into a sum over classical paths, setting up isolated-orbit tracing for chaotic systems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gutzwiller trace formula selects isolated periodic saddles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Tracing the semiclassical Green function makes stationary closed paths into periodic orbits and weights them by period, action, Maslov index, and monodromy stability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theta duality yields the Riemann functional equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses Mellin transformation and Poisson summation to continue the completed zeta function, expose the s to 1-s symmetry, and locate trivial versus critical-strip zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weil explicit formula makes primes the orbit-like dual of Riemann zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contour shifting and the logarithmic Euler-product derivative transform a smoothed sum over nontrivial zeros into gamma/smooth terms plus prime-power oscillations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime/periodic-orbit dictionary and the sign obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Matches primes with primitive orbits and log primes with periods while preserving the opposite oscillatory sign, motivating an absorption-spectrum interpretation rather than claiming a conventional self-adjoint spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unfolding separates local fluctuations from mean density
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines symmetry-indexed random-matrix ensembles, unfolds spectra to unit local density, and distinguishes level repulsion, form factors, and nearest-neighbor statistics from Poisson behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Energy smoothing turns one spectrum into a local ensemble
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines n-point correlations as smoothed products of densities and constrains the averaging window between quantum spacing and classical variation scales.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diagonal orbit pairing reproduces only the short-time universal form factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Keeps equal-action pairs, applies the Hannay-Ozorio sum rule, and recovers the symmetry-dependent small-time random-matrix slope before conflicting with long-time saturation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orbit proliferation bounds diagonal approximation by interference time scales
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates smoothing resolution to exponentially shrinking action gaps, deriving an Ehrenfest-scale limit for chaotic systems and a longer, Heisenberg-scale window for the Riemann prime spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Off-diagonal Riemann correlations reduce to shifted von Mangoldt averages
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Near-diagonal prime-power pairs survive energy smoothing, so the spectral problem becomes estimation of the arithmetic correlation alpha(r)=average Lambda(n)Lambda(n+r).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Circle-method singularities produce the Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Approximates a generating function near every rational point of the unit circle using primes in arithmetic progressions, then extracts the shifted correlation as a singular series.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local divisibility ratios repair naive prime-pair probabilities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows why multiplying infinitely many local prime-avoidance probabilities gives a wrong constant, then forms a convergent relative probability whose local corrections yield the Hardy-Littlewood product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-pair input supplies the missing oscillatory GUE correlation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Substituting the Hardy-Littlewood series into the off-diagonal trace product yields an arithmetic correction whose small-separation limit exactly matches the oscillating GUE two-point term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-height arithmetic corrections explain Odlyzko residual structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The finite-height diagonal plus off-diagonal formula is compared with a large numerical zero sample, and the residual after the arithmetic correction is reported as consistent with statistical error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical chaos can coexist with Poisson spectra through exact orbit-length degeneracy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poses arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces as a counterexample to generic chaos-to-RMT expectations and identifies coherent interference among exponentially many equal-length orbits as the mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integral modular traces imply exponential length multiplicity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compares only e^(L/2) possible integral trace values with e^L/L periodic orbits to derive mean degeneracy proportional to e^(L/2)/L.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic groups as groups with integral representations up to commensurability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Generalizes beyond 2x2 integral matrices by requiring a multiplicative higher-dimensional integral representation and closes the class under finite-index commensurability.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Algebraic integers act by integral matrices across embeddings
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how finite field extensions, their integral bases, and conjugate embeddings support faithful multiplication representations with integer matrices.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Division quaternion algebras generate compact arithmetic groups
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects norm/determinant multiplicativity, the absence of zero-norm field solutions, algebra orders, and unit-norm elements into discrete integral matrix groups.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded nonidentity embeddings enforce arithmetic discreteness
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why algebraic integers alone are nondiscrete and states Takeuchi's criterion: traces lie in a totally real field while every relevant nontrivial embedding stays bounded by two.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic trace lattice yields universal exponential orbit degeneracy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Counts trace values in one growing embedding coordinate with all conjugates bounded, obtaining linear trace growth and hence e^(L/2)/L mean length multiplicity for every arithmetic group.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Degeneracy accelerates the arithmetic form factor to Poisson scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Inserts length-dependent multiplicity into the diagonal orbit sum and shows exponential growth reaches the saturation scale around the Ehrenfest time, unlike generic chaotic RMT behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modular spectral correlations reduce to multiplicity correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the Selberg trace formula and integral traces to normalize conjugacy-class multiplicities, then expresses the two-point form factor entirely through their shifted correlation and Fourier transform.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A modular Hardy-Littlewood method computes multiplicity correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Averages multiplicities in residue classes via finite modular matrix groups, analyzes generating-function poles at rational phases, and reconstructs the two-point multiplicity correlation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Kloosterman and Euler factors make modular correlations explicit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses rational-phase weights through Kloosterman sums and factors the shifted correlation multiplicatively into prime-power contributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Smoothed modular form factor tends to the Poisson value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the dense arithmetic delta peaks, after the fixed-time high-energy limit and smoothing, collectively approach the constant Poisson form factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke correspondences provide arithmetic integrability
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extends determinant-one modular transformations to finite determinant-p correspondences, symmetrizes automorphic functions over their cosets, and obtains a commuting algebra that also commutes with the Laplacian.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic spectral transfer and the non-arithmetic degeneracy threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Links Hecke eigenvalues to Fourier coefficients and trace formulas, states Jacquet-Langlands spectral transfer, then shows non-arithmetic triangles can have subcritical exponential length degeneracy without leaving GOE statistics.

source_identity.title: Quantum and Arithmetical Chaos

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Across a torus, hyperbolic quotient, generic integrable/chaotic system, and the Riemann zeta function, a smoothed spectral side is dual to classical or arithmetic primitive data, while exactness and orbit organization change with the regime.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This is a structural comparison, not evidence that Riemann zeros are eigenvalues of a known Hamiltonian; formula conventions differ and require PDF checking.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: One dual architecture, four trace-formula regimes

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Equal-action pairing supplies only short-time behavior; longer-range spectral information depends on correlations among nearby prime powers or among modular length multiplicities, which can be attacked by rational-phase generating-function singularities.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Both Hardy-Littlewood uses are heuristic/conditional in these lectures, and dynamical transfer beyond the arithmetic cases is not established.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Off-diagonal information is a correlation problem in the dual data

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Bounded algebraic conjugates make trace values sparse, forcing exponentially many periodic geodesics to share lengths; their coherent contributions drive a classically chaotic arithmetic surface toward Poisson spectral statistics and coexist with a commuting Hecke algebra.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source presents degeneracy and Hecke structure as complementary explanations but explicitly denies a precise equivalence; the exact correlation calculation is modular-group-specific.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Arithmeticity changes quantum statistics through exact phase coincidences

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Arithmetic mean multiplicity grows at the critical exponent one half, allowing the form factor to reach order one within the diagonal approximation's validity, whereas subcritical exponential degeneracy in non-arithmetic triangles can remain compatible with GOE statistics.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The non-arithmetic exponents come from short-range numerical fits and the threshold argument is semiclassical and diagonal, not a theorem about all spectral statistics.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: The degeneracy exponent is a boundary between harmless and order-one interference

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Canonical semi-local operators and the normalization obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction distinguishes the artificial global Sobolev realization from canonical semi-local Hilbert-space operators, then identifies local principal-value normalization and the global Poisson formula as the likely missing ingredient in a positivity proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantization of PQ as the scaling generator and the need for two cutoffs
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It identifies the symmetric quantization of PQ with the unitary scaling generator and explains why unboundedness prevents a discrete spectrum until matched position and momentum cutoffs are imposed.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symplectic conversion of white light to scaling phase space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The exponential-coordinate symplectomorphism turns a cutoff regular representation into a hyperbolic PQ region, providing the representation bridge needed to compare background white light with the spectral model.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two finite phase-space discrepancies and the one-state rectangle
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The comparison isolates a high-momentum excess and a unit-area rectangle, clarifying exactly what differs between the cutoff absorption region and cutoff white light before rescaling.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Area-preserving rescaling recovers the Berry-Keating missing region
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A symplectic rescaling preserving PQ and area converts the excess white-light region into the Berry-Keating semiclassical picture, showing equality of the zero-count asymptotics without asserting model equivalence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The absorption sign survives in Maslov phases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text separates semiclassical count agreement from quantum fluctuations: the emission description must encode the absorption minus sign through a uniform Maslov-phase choice.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantized differential as a graded commutator calculus
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It replaces ordinary differentiation by commutation with a self-adjoint involution and shows how graded forms retain nilpotence, furnishing the reusable operator-calculus abstraction used later.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One-variable Hilbert-transform commutator kernel
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The abstract differential is realized by the Hilbert transform, with a difference-quotient kernel that converts regularity of functions into operator properties.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantized calculus on modulated groups
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The one-variable construction is generalized to any locally compact abelian group with a proper modulus, replacing the Hilbert transform by a Fourier-conjugated modulus projection.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semi-local adèle-class quotient and scaling action
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It removes the additive/multiplicative Haar singularity by restricting to finitely many places, forms the quotient XS by S-units, and equips it with the natural multiplicative action and self-dual additive pairing.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unitary Fourier and regular-representation models of L2(XS)
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The additive Fourier transform descends unitarily to L2(XS), while a second unitary identification converts the nonunitary scaling action into the regular representation with an explicit modulus factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier transform factors through inversion and local L-factor ratios
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It packages each local additive Fourier transform as inversion plus multiplicative convolution by a unitary local-factor ratio, then tensors these into the semi-local operator factorization of Lemma 2.3.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dual infrared and ultraviolet cutoffs become a truncated quantized differential
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The physical-space cutoff and its Fourier conjugate are combined, and Lemma 2.4 converts their sandwiched scaling action into truncated projections around the quantized logarithmic derivative of the local-factor product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Product-rule decomposition yields a sum of local trace terms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The quantized logarithmic derivative obeys a product decomposition, turning a single operator trace into the sum of placewise principal-value contributions used in the explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semi-local trace formula with logarithmic main term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2.5 identifies the asymptotic trace of the cutoff scaling action with a universal logarithmic term plus normalized local explicit-formula distributions, and then rewrites them symmetrically in the test function h.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li's positive-operator strategy from finite-place localization
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Compact support reduces the explicit formula to finitely many places, while positivity of trace-class products suggests proving Weil's inequality through a balanced near-zero cutoff in the semi-local model.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The cutoff proposal reduces positivity to the sign of a logarithmic derivative
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The convolution test function gives a positive multiplication operator, and Li's replacement cutoff would prove the desired inequality precisely if its positive compression equaled minus one half of the quantized logarithmic derivative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Negative quantized logarithmic derivative iff Hardy-subspace invariance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 3.4 proves equivalence among the cutoff identity, negativity of the logarithmic derivative, and invariance of the projected subspace; Corollary 3.5 identifies the one-variable condition with innerness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local-factor ratios have boundary modulus one but are not inner
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Both finite-prime and archimedean local-factor ratios are unimodular on the critical line yet fail Hardy innerness through poles or unbounded growth, directly invalidating the criterion needed by the cutoff proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The desired inequality would force false monotonicity of the Riemann-Siegel phase
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Beyond failure of the proof mechanism, Fact 3.6 shows the inequality itself fails generally: in the archimedean case it would force a constant-sign logarithmic derivative and hence monotonicity of the Riemann-Siegel angle.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Support-restricted Weil positivity as a finite semi-local problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's criterion is rewritten as a convolution square with two moment constraints, motivating the conjecture that places below a support-determined threshold suffice for the corresponding test functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation produces the archimedean local-factor ratio
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The scaling-equivariant theta-like map E becomes multiplication by zeta in multiplicative Fourier variables, while Poisson conjugacy of additive Fourier transform with inversion forces their quotient, explaining the local-factor ratio conceptually.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semi-local Poisson summation fixes character normalization on the quotient
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing integers by QS decomposes the sum into S-units and a complementary monoid, removes selected Euler factors, and shows why different self-dual character choices become equivalent after quotienting by S-units.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson distributions and the scaling Hamiltonian generate Sonine elements
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A differential operator enforcing simultaneous value and Fourier-value constraints transforms the Poisson comb into distributions supported away from zero; smoothing gives Schwartz Sonine functions, and a Fourier-symmetric polynomial in the scaling generator supplies a canonical choice.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta zeros are naturally times in the function-field analogue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The function-field model turns zeros into periodic arithmetic progressions in the imaginary coordinate, supporting the scaling approach's dual interpretation of zeros as times rather than energy levels.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic support exploitation versus global geometric structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The closing comparison identifies a plausible analytic next step and its vulnerability to principal-value normalization errors, while explaining what the global geometric model adds: an interpretation of scaling as Frobenius on the Scaling Site.

section_argument_map.label: Front matter and abstract
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: States the absorption/emission comparison, Li-attempt audit, and proposed semi-local operator-theoretic RH program.

section_argument_map.label: Introduction
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Motivates a return from global geometric methods to canonical semi-local Hilbert-space operators and previews the normalization obstruction.

section_argument_map.label: 1. The Scaling Hamiltonian
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Relates the PQ scaling generator and its cutoffs to white-light subtraction and the Berry-Keating phase-space count, while locating the residual sign in quantum phases.

section_argument_map.label: 2. Semi-local Trace Formula
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds quantized differentials, the semi-local quotient Hilbert space, Fourier factorization by local factors, dual cutoffs, and the resulting local trace decomposition.

section_argument_map.label: 3. Sonine Spaces and the Attempt of X.-J. Li
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Turns the proposed positive cutoff into an operator-sign and inner-function criterion, then proves the local factors fail that criterion and the desired inequality fails generally.

section_argument_map.label: 4. An Operator Theoretic Problem
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Translates Weil positivity into constrained convolution form, states the semi-local conjecture, explains Poisson normalization and Sonine witnesses, and compares time/energy and analytic/geometric viewpoints.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semiclassical geodesic dictionary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies quantum chaos as the semiclassical study of a quantized chaotic Hamiltonian and, for geodesic flow, turns the limit of Planck scale into the high-Laplacian-eigenvalue limit. This is the source's governing representation change between dynamics and spectral geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integrable torus quantization produces localized quasimodes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how invariant tori yield quantization conditions and quasimodes localized on the torus, then makes the mechanism geometric through the whispering-gallery example. It gives the comparison class against which chaotic localization is judged.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stable periodic orbits organize spectrum; unstable ones pose the chaos problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts the failure of integrable quantization in chaotic negative curvature with the strong spectral and quasimode influence of a stable closed geodesic. The unresolved influence of unstable periodic orbits is isolated as a central quantum-chaos obstruction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantum ergodicity constrains most states but leaves exceptional quantum limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines eigenfunction probability measures and quantum limits, states full-density equidistribution, and records geodesic-flow invariance of any limit. It sharply separates an almost-everywhere theorem from the unresolved possibility of exceptional localization or scarring.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random-wave behavior yields Gaussian and extreme-value diagnostics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns the random-wave proposal for individual chaotic eigenfunctions into falsifiable distributional and sup-norm expectations rather than leaving it as a visual analogy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Number variance separates Poisson from random-matrix rigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a local spectral statistic and compares its scale under Poisson, Gaussian orthogonal, and Gaussian unitary models. It supplies the quantitative language of clustering versus rigidity used throughout the source.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universal statistics have a finite spectral window
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records the integrable-Poisson and chaotic-GOE heuristic only within a universal range, beyond which system-specific periodic-orbit oscillations take over. This guards against treating random-matrix behavior as scale-free.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Stadium dynamics separates visual scars from persistent strong scarring
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The stadium combines global ergodicity with measure-zero bouncing-ball families that influence the spectrum. The source then distinguishes finite-energy enhancement near unstable orbits from strong scarring defined through singular support of a limiting measure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolic quotients provide controlled chaotic models
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Realizes constant-negative-curvature systems as discrete-group quotients in upper-half-plane or disk models and introduces compact/orbifold and Hecke-triangle examples. This is the geometric substrate for the later arithmetic/nonarithmetic comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compact and modular hyperbolic spectra test the random-wave picture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reports nonlocalized, approximately Gaussian eigenstates on a compact hyperbolic surface, then distinguishes the modular surface's continuous Eisenstein spectrum from its embedded discrete cusp forms. The same chaotic geometry thus supports different spectral representations that must not be conflated.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Modular cusp forms motivate a Gaussian distribution conjecture
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Converts repeated numerical observations of no localization and Gaussian amplitude behavior into a limiting distribution conjecture for modular eigenfunctions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simplicity and number variance test distinct spectral features
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the conjectural simplicity of the modular spectrum from number-variance comparisons: an integrable billiard follows Poisson while the chaotic stadium follows GOE in the universal range, with bouncing-ball effects predicted later.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmeticity is encoded by trace fields and bounded conjugates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Presents Takeuchi's trace-based characterization of arithmetic lattices and a stronger condition for quaternion-algebra origin, then classifies the arithmetic Hecke triangles. It recasts a geometric group property into algebraic data used later for spectral clustering.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic chaos violates the naive GOE universality rule
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Numerical number variance is Poisson-like for arithmetic hyperbolic triangles but GOE-like for nonarithmetic ones, despite both being chaotic. This is the source's central counterexample to identifying classical chaos with one universal spectral ensemble.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Families of periodic trajectories force long-range spectral nonrigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why a measure-zero positive-dimensional family of equal-period trajectories can force a variance lower bound outside the GOE window. The stadium, Sinai billiard, and integrable examples connect the trace mechanism to concrete systems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Length multiplicity and bounded clustering drive arithmetic nonrigidity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States arithmetic number-variance lower bounds and identifies high multiplicity of the length spectrum, compressed into a bounded-clustering property of traces, as their cause. It also records the important asymmetry that useful lower bounds exist while upper bounds remain unavailable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic manifolds carry nonlocal correspondences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs arithmetic hyperbolic three-manifolds from quadratic forms, then abstracts a correspondence as a multivalued local-isometry relation and associates a Laplacian-commuting operator. Margulis's commensurator dichotomy makes an infinite correspondence family equivalent to arithmeticity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A commuting self-adjoint Hecke algebra refines Laplace eigenstates
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how classical and quaternionic correspondences form commuting self-adjoint Hecke operators, allowing simultaneous eigenbases. This extra spectral labeling is the arithmetic resource used to study individual eigenfunctions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke structure rules out geodesic strong scars and motivates QUE
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States that quantum limits for congruence arithmetic manifolds cannot have singular support confined to proper geodesic submanifolds, then formulates individual equidistribution as quantum unique ergodicity. It also highlights the counterfactual contrast: quantum uniqueness is expected although chaotic classical flow has many invariant measures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local eigenfunction bounds are too geometry-blind for quantum chaos
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines extremal eigenfunction norms, contrasts general local bounds with improved torus behavior, and ties that improvement to absolute continuity of quantum limits. The discussion isolates the need for global geometry or arithmetic to improve on local restriction-theoretic barriers.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The chaotic sup-norm conjecture links random waves to Lindelof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Formulates subpolynomial sup-norm growth for negatively curved surfaces, derives it heuristically from random waves, and identifies it as an eigenfunction analogue of Ramanujan whose arithmetic cases would imply Lindelof-type bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke amplification beats the local sup-norm barrier
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records an arithmetic improvement over the general convexity-like sup-norm bound and a lower-growth result showing eigenfunctions are not uniformly bounded. Weighted Hecke spectral sums access individual states and reveal large values at a dense set of CM points.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sup-norm control would constrain spectral multiplicity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives an inequality from eigenvalue multiplicity to extremal sup norm, so the chaotic norm conjecture would imply subpolynomial multiplicity. The gap between this and known bounds exposes a major bottleneck despite numerical simplicity.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Theta lifts delimit random-wave universality in dimension three
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An infinite subsequence of arithmetic three-dimensional eigenfunctions violates random-wave norm expectations. A special-point vanishing law explains the mechanism: most states vanish there, forcing the surviving states to be exceptionally large.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Special L-values govern dissolution of cusp forms under deformation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects persistence of bound states on noncompact hyperbolic surfaces to arithmeticity and explains generic dissolution through nonvanishing Rankin-Selberg values, interpreted as a Fermi-golden-rule condition. A conditional finiteness theorem exposes spectral simplicity/multiplicity as the controlling unresolved input.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Random-matrix ideas move from Laplace spectra to Hecke spectra
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Reverses the failed random-matrix model for arithmetic Laplace eigenvalues by applying it to Hecke operators, relating semicircle and expansion behavior to Sato-Tate and Ramanujan conjectures and then to explicit pseudorandom graphs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta growth organizes RH, Lindelof, convexity, and subconvexity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Introduces the Euler product, functional equation, RH, and Lindelof growth on the critical line, then distinguishes convexity from genuine improvements. This establishes the analytic hierarchy later mirrored by eigenfunction bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: General L-functions expose several convexity aspects
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Abstracts degree, Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation into a general L-function template, then distinguishes spectral-height, conductor, and archimedean-parameter aspects of Lindelof and convexity. It provides the common language for the later bridges.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eisenstein series realize the continuous spectrum beside Hecke cusp forms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Constructs Eisenstein Laplace eigenfunctions, uses their Fourier expansion to identify near-square-integrability on the critical line, and decomposes the modular spectrum into continuous Eisenstein and discrete cuspidal parts. Both families can then test the same eigenfunction conjectures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CM evaluation converts an Eisenstein sup norm into an L-value problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Handles non-square-integrability by truncating Eisenstein series on a compact region, then evaluates at a CM point to factor the value through a quadratic-field zeta function. The eigenfunction sup-norm conjecture therefore implies a Lindelof bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Cusp-form values at CM points encode twisted central L-values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines Hecke Euler products, a special-value identity, half-integral-weight correspondence, and central-value formulas to equate pointwise eigenfunction control at a CM point with Lindelof in the spectral-parameter aspect.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rankin-Selberg subconvexity is the threshold for individual equidistribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Associates a degree-four Rankin-Selberg L-function to pairs of cusp forms, uses its integral representation to translate Lindelof-type control into decay of eigenfunction observables, and contrasts individual, mean, and quantum-ergodic estimates. Beating convexity in the spectral aspect is isolated as sufficient for individual equidistribution against the continuous spectrum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Trace singularities turn periodic families into counting variance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Outlines how a clean positive-dimensional fixed set of the geodesic flow creates a trace-formula singularity, which a calculus lemma converts into an averaged lower bound for the Weyl counting remainder and hence number variance.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bounded trace clustering makes Selberg smoothing yield arithmetic variance lower bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses the Selberg trace formula to approximate a strongly smoothed spectral counting fluctuation by a length-side Dirichlet polynomial. Arithmetic spacing or bounded clustering controls its mean square and diagonal contribution, while off-diagonal ignorance blocks both the nonarithmetic analogue and useful upper bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Hecke correspondence separates singular support and forbids geodesic scars
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A separation lemma chooses a correspondence whose inverse image meets a proposed geodesic singular support in exactly one point. Applying the Hecke eigenrelation and Cauchy inequality to shrinking neighborhoods forces zero mass at that support point, contradicting singular support.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hecke amplification breaks the local pretrace barrier
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The pretrace formula gives the local sup-norm bound from a unit-width spectral window; shortening the window makes the geometric side exponentially nonlocal. Applying Hecke operators and counting near-return correspondences creates weighted inequalities that can isolate an individual eigenfunction and beat that barrier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CM fixed points create an arithmetic resonance for large eigenfunctions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Chooses a point fixed by many Hecke correspondences so the geometric side receives an enhanced contribution for selected arithmetic indices. Comparing that enhancement with a general upper bound forces large values of some eigenfunctions at CM points.

section_argument_map.label: Front matter
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Title, date, and author metadata only.

section_argument_map.label: Section 1. Background
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Sets the semiclassical geodesic model, contrasts integrable localization with chaotic quantum limits, and introduces random-wave and spectral-statistics diagnostics.

section_argument_map.label: Section 2.1. The Stadium
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Uses a chaotic billiard with bouncing-ball families to distinguish finite-energy visual scarring from persistent strong scarring.

section_argument_map.label: Section 2.2. Hyperbolic Surfaces
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Introduces hyperbolic quotient models and numerical evidence for Gaussian, nonlocalized eigenfunctions on compact and modular examples.

section_argument_map.label: Section 2.3. Fine structure of the spectrum
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Compares simplicity and number variance across integrable, nonarithmetic chaotic, and arithmetic chaotic spectra, including the arithmetic trace criterion.

section_argument_map.label: Section 3. Arithmetic Manifolds
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Develops length-spectrum multiplicity, Hecke correspondences, scarring and norm conjectures, exceptional theta lifts, cusp-form deformation, and the shifted role of random-matrix ideas.

section_argument_map.label: Section 4. L-functions
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Builds the zeta/general-L-function framework and connects sup norms and equidistribution to central values, Rankin-Selberg products, Lindelof bounds, and subconvexity.

section_argument_map.label: Section 5. Outline of some proofs
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Exhibits trace-formula, bounded-clustering, Hecke-separation, pretrace-amplification, and CM-point mechanisms behind the earlier results.

section_argument_map.label: Section 6. Conclusion and acknowledgements
section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Recapitulates the represented mechanisms and records author acknowledgements.

section_argument_map.mathematical_role: Bibliographic apparatus; inspected for boundary completeness but not semantic-unit content.

source_identity.title: Arithmetic Quantum Chaos

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Arithmetic surfaces can display random-wave-like eigenfunctions while their Laplace eigenvalues are Poisson-like rather than GOE; arithmetic length multiplicities explain the spectral exception, and random-matrix structure reappears for Hecke operators.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The eigenfunction side is partly numerical/conjectural and the claims are dimension- and operator-specific.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Arithmetic chaos splits eigenvalue and eigenfunction universality

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The progression from full-density quantum ergodicity to exclusion of geodesic singular supports and finally individual equidistribution uses two complementary arithmetic routes: nonlocal correspondence separation and subconvex control of Rankin-Selberg periods.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The no-scarring theorem is restricted to Hecke arithmetic settings, while full QUE remains conjectural in this source.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Quantum unique ergodicity as a correspondence-to-subconvexity program

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The same nonlocal arithmetic correspondences refine the eigenbasis, move singular support away from itself, overcome local pretrace barriers, and create resonances at CM points, unifying upper, lower, and delocalization arguments.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Each use requires different algebraic input; correspondence abundance alone does not automatically supply every lemma or optimal bound.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Hecke correspondences are both separators and amplifiers

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: General local sup-norm bounds play the role of convexity, while CM evaluation identities translate improved pointwise eigenfunction control into Lindelof-type central-value bounds; Hecke amplification supplies a partial subconvex analogue.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The identities are special to arithmetic eigenfunctions and selected evaluation points, so the analogy is not a general equivalence for all chaotic manifolds.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Eigenfunction size and L-function growth share a convexity barrier

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Positive-dimensional periodic families create trace singularities, while repeated arithmetic lengths create large diagonal mass in a smoothed Selberg trace analysis; both mechanisms force variance lower bounds through different sources of coherent recurrence.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The resulting arguments are lower-bound mechanisms and do not provide the missing upper bounds or unsmoothed control.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Trace formulas expose both dynamical and arithmetic nonrigidity

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Gaussian numerical behavior and no-geodesic-scar results do not imply universal random-wave norms: in dimension three, theta-lift subsequences are forced large by arithmetic vanishing even without classical focusing.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The exceptional construction is arithmetic and three-dimensional; it does not refute the stated surface conjectures.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Theta lifts are an adversarial boundary for random-wave heuristics

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Arithmetic symmetries provide Hecke labels for bound states, whereas under deformation the nonvanishing of Rankin-Selberg values can dissolve cusp forms; spectral persistence is therefore controlled by both operator symmetry and special-value obstructions.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The deformation conclusions include simplicity or multiplicity hypotheses and generic statements, not a classification of every surface.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Arithmeticity can stabilize or dissolve spectral states through different L-data

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why individual L-functions are deformed inside families
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects family averaging to density theorems, subconvexity, and function-field deformation, and frames low-zero statistics as a family-level phenomenon distinct from high-zero GUE behavior.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic conductor, functional equation, and duality type
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the ordering/complexity variable and the orthogonal-versus-symplectic distinction via poles of symmetric- and exterior-square factors, which later drive family symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Individual Sato–Tate measures and non-unique group realizations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Moves from local components to a limiting measure and observes that different compact-group embeddings can yield the same measure, making the measure rather than a uniquely named group the stable invariant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Harmonic families from trace-formula-isolable spectral sets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines a reusable spectral construction: isolate a large automorphic set on H, then transfer it through an L-group representation to GL(n).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric families from specialized cohomology
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines the geometric route from a smooth proper family over an affine base to specialized étale-cohomology L-functions and, conditionally, automorphic representations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gauge ordering, family operations, and the Diophantine boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why discriminant gauges can stand in for conductor, how unions/products preserve parametrization, and why intersections can introduce uncontrolled Diophantine sets.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finiteness, infinitude, and vertical coefficient limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specifies the nondegeneracy conditions that make asymptotic family statistics meaningful and expresses averaged Dirichlet coefficients through local-density main terms with power-saving error.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Family Sato–Tate equidistribution as a vertical local measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Conjecture 1 makes the family a probability distribution on local representations, permits a finite convex product decomposition, and defines the horizontal Sato–Tate limit over primes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three trace indicators recover cuspidal, self-dual, and sign type
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how three low-order trace moments classify generic cuspidality, self-duality, and orthogonal/symplectic type and uniquely recover their mixture proportions even when group decomposition is nonunique.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From product measures to homogeneous subfamilies, but not canonical groups
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Suggests a density-weighted decomposition into irreducible homogeneous pieces while explaining why a general family Sato–Tate group is neither uniquely determined nor tractable for thin families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Family rank measures persistent central zeros through a secondary local term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Relates generic rational cycles to a next-order prime average and explains why universal fluctuations should be studied only after removing family-persistent central zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Root-number splitting requires Möbius-type cancellation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates local Sato–Tate type from the functional-equation sign and identifies polynomial Möbius cancellation as the extra arithmetic input needed to split a symplectic family by root number.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conductor-scaled low zeros and the universality dictionary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines universal zero scaling by analytic conductor and maps unitary, orthogonal, and sign-refined symplectic families to the four limiting compact-group laws and r-level densities.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local equidistribution is shallower than low-zero universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes the comparatively accessible local Sato–Tate theorem from universality, which needs analytic continuation and deeper cancellation, and uses function-field cohomology to explain the apparent duality reversal of symmetry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic characters as a fully explicit orthogonal family
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Realizes the same family both spectrally and geometrically and computes its local measure, rank, indicators, and predicted symplectic low-zero law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Function-field averaging certifies number-field density identities
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines r-level density for quadratic characters and explains how matching function-field calculations plus uniformity in q force difficult combinatorial identities in the number-field limit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hilbert specialization and Chebotarev determine Artin-family type
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds a family from generic polynomial specializations and shows how finite-field counting yields vertical local limits converging to the Haar measure of the fixed Galois image.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prehomogeneous parametrizations turn field counting into family statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses orbit parametrizations and geometry of numbers to count cubic through quintic fields by discriminant, then reads symplectic low-zero symmetry from orthogonal standard representations of symmetric groups.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elliptic-family invariants depend on the ordering interface
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows geometric monodromy gives a pure symplectic family, while moving from height to conductor introduces square-free-sieve and average-conductor questions; family rank is independently geometric.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric rank and root-number bias vary independently
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Exhibits constant negative root number at different family ranks and relates average signs to the nodal factor of the discriminant and Möbius cancellation, preventing conflation of two central-zero mechanisms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dwork invariant cohomology converts parity of monodromy into symmetry
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Extracts an H0-invariant middle-cohomology summand, controls ramification by the discriminant, and uses symplectic versus orthogonal monodromy according to parity to predict low-zero classes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quantitative Plancherel equidistribution from the trace formula
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the harmonic route: Weyl-law counting, a uniform trace-formula estimate for local test functions, and pushforward of unramified Plancherel measure to obtain the family local distributions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Eisenstein and residual spectra obstruct higher-rank Maass equidistribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the known Weyl law from the stronger quantitative local equidistribution and identifies continuous/residual spectrum control as the bottleneck.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dual-group representation determines harmonic-family invariants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies the family Sato–Tate group with the image of the dual group, equates irreducibility and self-duality properties with the three indicators, proves rank zero from Plancherel decay, and leaves root-number splitting as the subtle residue.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Partial L-functions make universality robust to ramified-factor uncertainty
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Argues that Ramanujan bounds prevent ramified local poles from cancelling relevant zeros, so low-zero universality can be formulated using partial L-functions and support is controlled by the quality of equidistribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Classical modular forms separate sign equidistribution from detectable support
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Computes the SU(2) Sato–Tate law and symplectic family type, splits root signs through ramified Plancherel mass, and shows why Fourier support beyond one is needed to distinguish three orthogonal/symplectic density laws.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Quadratic twisting pushes forward the individual Sato–Tate measure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Expresses the thin twist-family measure as the average of an individual measure and its negative, revealing why local family equidistribution can remain as hard as the individual Sato–Tate conjecture while coarse indicators are easier.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Averaging over all characters forces unitary universality
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing quadratic scalars by the full unit circle annihilates the self-duality indicators, making the family unitary independently of the fixed cuspform and relating this to an infinite-center Sato–Tate group.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Frobenius–Schur signs multiply under Rankin–Selberg products
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows a self-dual product family can have fixed even functional equation without symmetry being reducible to root signs, and proposes multiplicativity of the third indicator under family tensor product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adjoint and spin families expose the danger of natural weights
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Derives orthogonal adjoint and symplectic spin types from invariant bilinear forms, then shows central-L-value weights introduced by a trace formula can distort observed symmetry and must be removed for interpretation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vertical Sato–Tate limits can fail along arithmetic exhaustions while universality survives
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Models universal local measures by conductor strata of Plancherel measure but records level sequences for which coefficient-limit equidistribution fails even though low-zero universality is still expected or proved.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric averages localize to residue classes away from the discriminant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows local factors depend only on parameters modulo p, making the family measure atomic; Lang–Weil makes ramification negligible and lattice equidistribution reduces the vertical average to a finite-field problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Deligne–Katz turns geometric monodromy into the family Sato–Tate law
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Packages fiber cohomology as a lisse sheaf, separates arithmetic and geometric monodromy, normalizes Frobenius by purity, and obtains Haar equidistribution on a maximal compact group independent of large p.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scheme Sato–Tate tolerates bases that family statistics do not
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts prime-power averaging for a fixed scheme with parameter-family averaging, warning that mild geometric base hypotheses for one do not guarantee meaningful arithmetic statistics for the other.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Diophantine parameter sets can encode arbitrary recursive behavior
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why general bases and intersections cease to be analyzable and constructs a quadratic-character image whose real subfamily realizes an arbitrary recursive subset, defeating universal asymptotics.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Field-of-rationality cuts may be finite or secretly geometric
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines bounded-rationality subfamilies, asks whether the two conjectures hold when they are infinite, and develops evidence and obstructions for realizing them through motives or geometric moduli.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Measure-zero local constraints defeat trace-formula isolation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies families with fixed cohomological or algebraic archimedean type as natural but outside positive-Plancherel-volume methods, making even their growth hard before local or zero statistics can be tested.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universal H-type classes versus constructible geometric subfamilies
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts the inaccessible class of all cuspforms with a prescribed hypothetical Sato–Tate group against Hilbert-specialized geometric subfamilies and class-field cases where type and symmetry are computable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hybrid field/spectral variation and arithmetic restrictions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines varying number fields with functorial lift and automorphic induction, permits removal of common factors, and records how conductor shells, prime conductors, and mixed Galois types complicate otherwise natural families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weil–Deligne data and local Langlands preserve L-factors and conductors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Provides the local bridge used throughout geometric families: a Weil–Deligne representation with monodromy maps bijectively to an irreducible smooth GL(n) representation while preserving local analytic invariants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric Galois representations are conjecturally exactly algebraic automorphic data
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Builds global L-functions from local Weil–Deligne realizations, defines coming from geometry, states geometric automorphy, and reformulates it as a unique L-algebraic automorphic/algebraic l-adic correspondence with local-global compatibility.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The unitary normalization is unconditional only at good reduction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why twisting degree-d cohomology by |det|^(d/2) places good-reduction Satake parameters on the unit circle, while bad-reduction unitarity remains conditional on weight-monodromy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Regular algebraic orthogonal representations have noncritical center
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under the stated motivic and correspondence conjectures, translates central criticality into even motive rank and then uses the Galois sign theorem to force symplectic type, contradicting orthogonality; examples distinguish Dirichlet and elliptic cases.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Moments as an average-to-pointwise bridge
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defines shifted and critical-line moments and explains that the full family of near-linear moment bounds is equivalent to Lindelof, while RH supplies a stronger zero-location premise with prime-distribution consequences. This fixes why moment growth is an informative proxy for extreme values rather than merely an integral statistic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Conditional, convexity, and subconvex pointwise regimes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Places RH-implied subexponential control, unconditional convexity, and successive subconvexity exponents in one hierarchy. The comparison exposes how analytic continuation and functional symmetry give a baseline and how improvement below that baseline becomes a distinct structural problem.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From known moments to the sharp-order moment problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows the historical shift from using moments to control extremes, through exact low moments and a high-moment bound, to the general target T(log T)^(k^2). It distinguishes inaccessible full asymptotics from the weaker but structurally sharp upper and lower order-of-magnitude goals.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fractional moments despite the nonregularity of zeta powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States Heath-Brown's rational/unconditional and real/conditional ranges and identifies the central obstruction: fractional powers of zeta need not be regular, so ordinary Cauchy contour deformation is unavailable. Gabriel convexity is introduced as the replacement move.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet surrogate, discrepancy, and smoothed convexity comparison
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Approximates zeta^k through a finite divisor Dirichlet polynomial S, packages the mismatch as g=zeta^u-S^v, and compares smoothed functionals J, K, and L. Mean-value control of L plus Gabriel convexity transfers estimates between the critical line and a shifted line, turning the nonregular fractional-power problem into tractable surrogate and error terms.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Convexity machinery transfers beyond the original global moments
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Documents that the reusable contribution was not only a larger theorem range but a convexity method subsequently adapted to short intervals, uniformity in the moment parameter, derivative inequalities, Dirichlet L-functions, value distribution, and other L-function families.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Truncated Dirichlet coefficients predict the moment exponent and arithmetic factor
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starts from a convergent shifted-moment mean value, moves it toward the critical line by truncating at the analytic conductor scale, and obtains the k-squared logarithmic exponent together with an Euler-product factor a_k. It isolates prime arithmetic as one component of the conjectural constant.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Selberg Gaussian fluctuations independently predict k-squared growth
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Treats log|zeta| as approximately Gaussian and applies its exponential moment, converting variance proportional to log log T into the same T(log T)^(k^2) scale. This supplies a probabilistic representation of the exponent independent of the coefficient truncation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Keating-Snaith completes the moment constant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the conjectural leading constant into the arithmetic factor a_k and a second factor g_k, then states the Barnes-G formula valid for positive real k and its factorial specialization for integer k. This upgrades isolated guessed constants into a uniform law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero statistics select a unitary characteristic-polynomial model
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers Montgomery's local zero-statistics analogy to unitary eigenphases, matches mean densities to choose matrix size N approximately log(T/2pi), and replaces zeta by det(I-U). Evaluating characteristic-polynomial moments then produces the g_k factor and the k-squared polynomial degree.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Reconciling universal matrix statistics with prime arithmetic
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies a limitation of the pure matrix model—a_k has to be inserted—and records hybrid Euler-Hadamard and full moment-polynomial approaches that recombine primes and zeros or predict lower-order structure beyond the leading coefficient.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Symmetry type transfers the moment model across L-function families
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains how zero distributions in families select unitary, symplectic, or orthogonal compact groups, allowing the characteristic-polynomial recipe to generalize by symmetry type. It also records distinct multiple-Dirichlet-series and long-Dirichlet-approximation routes to the same family of conjectures.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Three routes toward sharp moment bounds
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Organizes progress into conditional high-moment upper bounds, unconditional small-moment upper bounds, and unconditional all-moment lower bounds, then locates Soundararajan's almost-sharp and Radziwill's sharp-range conditional results within that map.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime-sum majorants and asymmetric control of small and large primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under RH, upper-bounds log|zeta| by a prime-supported Dirichlet polynomial plus a truncation penalty, splits primes into two scales, and trades computable high moments of small-prime sums against variance control for large primes. Markov bounds on large values convert these controls into an almost-sharp zeta moment estimate.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Harper's multiscale Taylor and exceptional-set iteration
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Refines the two-range method into many prime blocks, assigns decreasing powers as prime size grows, approximates exponentials by truncated Taylor polynomials on good sets, and shows bad blocks occur on sets too small to matter. Flexible truncation and length choices keep each resulting Dirichlet polynomial inside available mean-value theorems.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twisted anchor moments propagate unconditional upper bounds downward
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Formulates the principle that computing a moment with room to spare—equivalently with a short Dirichlet-polynomial twist—can yield sharp upper bounds for smaller moments. The zeta implementation combines an iterative scheme with a twisted fourth-moment input to reach the full interval from zero to two.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Twisted mean values propagate lower bounds on both sides of the first moment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Summarizes how short Dirichlet-polynomial twists turn a computable mean value into sharp lower bounds above an anchor and how a twisted second moment also reaches below the first moment. It contrasts this interpolation-like route with an independent route through lower bounds for large deviations in Selberg's central limit theorem.
