result_and_mechanism_map.title: Historical rooting through pRH avatars
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates the unresolved classical RH from its finite-field avatar and frames analogous statements and proof methods as evidence about mathematical placement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From autonomous polynomial arithmetic to an analytic zeta component
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows how polynomial arithmetic modulo a prime was made structurally parallel to integer arithmetic, while algebraic number theory retained a distinct analytic zeta-function layer.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Artin's quadratic function-field zeta polynomial and pRH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers quadratic number-field organization to quadratic function fields, compresses the zeta problem into a finite polynomial, removes trivial zeros, and expresses pRH as a common modulus condition on its roots.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: One Euler-product definition across rings and its RH questions
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Presents maximal-ideal Euler products as a common representation for classical, Dedekind, polynomial-ring, and curve cases, then separates continuation, functional equation, and zero-location questions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extension-field point counts as a zeta generating series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Encodes the entire sequence of point counts over finite extensions into one formal power series, exposing zeta data as compressed dynamical information about Frobenius iterates.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Curve-zeta rationality, Frobenius factors, and pRH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Connects the Euler product of a smooth complete curve to a rational generating function whose numerator factors into Frobenius terms, making pRH a modulus constraint and point counts over extensions a power-sum readout.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Affine versus complete zeta functions and trace determination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes the places-at-infinity convention explicit and shows that, for a complete elliptic curve, one point count fixes the Frobenius trace and hence its quadratic zeta numerator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Schmidt's coordinate-free arithmetic of function fields
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing Artin's chosen variable by all places of the function field incorporates infinity uniformly and lets Riemann–Roch support the functional equation in arbitrary genus.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Functional equation, rationality, and pRH as three separate targets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Factorizes the early curve-zeta program into three logically distinct properties and records that Schmidt established the first two while Hasse handled pRH only for elliptic curves.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gauss's Last Entry as a bridge from congruences to elliptic point counts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Records an early empirical rule connecting biquadratic residues and lemniscatic functions through a congruence whose solution count later becomes an elliptic-curve count.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Normalize Gauss's curve and read its count as Frobenius norm
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Turns Gauss's singular plane model into an elliptic normalization and identifies the counted quantity with the norm of Frobenius minus identity, yielding its characteristic polynomial.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Point counting, Frobenius norm, and CM reduction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States pRH as a norm/point-count equivalence and explains characteristic-p point counting by reducing a controlled CM curve and its division points from characteristic zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hasse's first proof via a chosen CM lift
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains the strategic move of realizing a finite-field elliptic curve as the reduction of a suitably chosen CM curve so explicit class-field theory can control its points.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CM lattice setup, ray-class reduction, and the odd-degree obstruction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Details how a lattice, factorization of a field power, congruent invariants, and division-point coordinates reduce counting to class-field theory, then isolates the j-invariant restriction as technical rather than intrinsic.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The Hasse point-count bound as elliptic pRH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Makes the elliptic pRH operational as a square-root error bound for rational-point counts and records its extension from Artin's examples to all elliptic curves.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Elliptic curve versus genus-one curve without a rational point
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Separates genus one from elliptic-curve structure by the rational-point/group-law requirement and notes why the distinction collapses over finite fields but not over arbitrary fields.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves through endomorphisms
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives equivalent group-theoretic, endomorphism-ring, splitting, and abelian-variety characterizations of ordinary versus supersingular behavior, including the quaternionic endomorphism algebra.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Supersingular parameters from a Hasse polynomial and symmetry orbits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Combines a polynomial criterion in Legendre form with an S3 action to count isomorphism classes as orbits, illustrating how parameter-space symmetry converts roots into moduli information.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: CM, finite-field definability, descent, and isogeny
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Distinguishes being definable over a smaller field from descending a given model, and shows how base extension changes isomorphism classes even at fixed j-invariant; it also tracks the elliptic insight into higher-dimensional CM results.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Frobenius cases expose a base-field conflation in Hasse's criterion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Classifies ordinary and two supersingular Frobenius regimes, then diagnoses a historical false equivalence caused by mixing an algebraically closed curve with a Frobenius attached to a fixed finite field.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From Deuring's elliptic endomorphisms to Tate's homomorphism theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows a reusable generalization pattern: an elliptic-curve isomorphism between geometric homomorphisms and Galois-equivariant Tate-module maps motivates the corresponding theorem and conjectures for abelian varieties.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Supersingular curves away from Hasse's claimed boundary cases
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uses explicit Frobenius polynomials to falsify the claim that supersingularity occurs only at boundary trace values, and includes a nearby polynomial satisfying a naive bound but not realizable as elliptic Frobenius.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Honda–Tate existence test for elliptic Frobenius polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Partitions trace valuations and field degrees into ordinary existence, several supersingular existence regimes, and a forbidden regime, turning a magnitude bound into a realizability criterion.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hasse's second proof from Frobenius norm and positive involution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recasts elliptic pRH as the identity between Frobenius and its adjoint under the endomorphism-algebra involution, avoiding the chosen CM-lift restrictions of the first proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A structural function-field framework as a research commitment
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Explains why Hasse preferred his second proof: it embedded pRH in an intrinsic arithmetic theory of function fields and thereby shaped which higher-genus routes appeared natural.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Competing higher-genus routes: abelian uniformization or algebraic methods
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Transfers a principle from Siegel's function/value relations to congruence counting, forecasts higher-genus abelian uniformization, and explicitly keeps Weil's algebraic route as an alternative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Replace elliptic endomorphisms by self-correspondences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Identifies Deuring's key higher-genus abstraction: the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve should become the ring of correspondences of a curve with itself, within Hasse's arithmetic function-field program.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Analytic, geometric, and arithmetic languages for correspondences
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that the same object had analytic, Italian-geometric, and function-field presentations, with algebraization over arbitrary characteristic as the contested bridge.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Algebraize correspondences, then supply differentials, norm, and positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Gives a concrete higher-genus program: form a ring of correspondences, develop its action on differentials, generalize norm by extension degree, and reduce pRH to positivity; it also records that the norm step was never supplied.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weil's quotient ring and warning against discarding prior gauges
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Recognizes Deuring's ring as correspondences modulo the ideal of valence zero and argues that translation into modern algebra should preserve older theories as diagnostic gauges.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dialect fragmentation blocks a collective proof program
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Documents how mathematically related approaches failed to coordinate because their practitioners used incompatible algebraic-geometric languages, while also separating that bottleneck from later proof priority disputes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Intrinsic characteristic-p proof versus lifting and a later language shift
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts Hasse's allegiance to an intrinsic function-field proof with lifting to characteristic zero, then notes that eventual success required a newly consolidated algebraic-geometric language.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lift an elliptic curve together with an endomorphism
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: States the exact repair to Hasse's first proof: every finite-field elliptic curve and chosen endomorphism admit a compatible characteristic-zero lift.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Higher-dimensional lifting failures and isogeny-level CM repair
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Shows that pair lifting generalizes to ordinary/almost-ordinary cases but fails for many higher-dimensional pairs, while CM lifting can be restored after a suitable isogeny and sometimes base extension.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A proof would mathematically root RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Argues that superficial classification as special-function theory is inadequate because RH has many equivalent formulations and avatars; the eventual proof mechanism would provide its first non-provisional mathematical placement.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Disciplinary labels do not determine RH's proof route
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Contrasts Weil, Riemann's title and possible Dirichlet/Eisenstein influences, the breakup of arithmetic algebraic analysis, Kronecker's assessment, and later classification shifts to show that disciplinary placement is historically unstable.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Real and imaginary zero curves as a meromorphic X ray
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source's central representation change replaces a hard-to-see meromorphic map by the preimages of the real and imaginary axes, whose intersections expose zeros and poles and whose combined picture organizes scattered knowledge.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeros, critical points, and monotonic motion on level curves
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: This span identifies curve intersections with zeta zeros, curve branching with derivative zeros, and monotonic variation of the remaining component along a regular real- or imaginary-value curve.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Topological numbering of real- and imaginary-value lines
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The author gives persistent integer identities to curves using their real-axis intersections and continuation, encoding parity as real versus imaginary value and allowing later geometric counting arguments.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Why imaginary-value curves disappear far to the right
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Uniform convergence of zeta to 1 as real part grows gives a positive-real-part half-plane and therefore excludes purely imaginary values there.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Parallel line spacing and alternating zero carriage
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Dominance of the first Dirichlet-series oscillation predicts nearly equally spaced real-value curves, while monotonic direction alternates so that every other regular parallel line is forced through zero.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Orienting curve crossings by image quadrants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Following a real-value curve away from a zero determines the sign and limiting range of zeta and thereby assigns neighboring source-plane sectors to image-plane quadrants.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Curve boundaries partition the plane by image quadrant
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The real- and imaginary-value curves form region boundaries, and crossing one boundary changes exactly one sign, enabling quadrant labels to propagate across the source plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Counting solutions of zeta(s)=a from a region boundary
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A region known to map into one quadrant is traversed on its curve boundary; the image winds twice around that quadrant, giving two preimages of any interior value and implying a derivative zero in the region.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Computed curve tracing is not automatically proof
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source explains its numerical line-tracing construction and explicitly distinguishes proved exterior behavior from near-critical-strip paths accepted only after dense computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From asymptotic line numbers to nontrivial-zero counts
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Stirling's expansion and the functional equation number incoming curves, after which an argument-principle contour converts curve crossings into the classical main-term count of nontrivial zeros and a mod-four distinction between parallel-line types.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-MacLaurin continuation with controllable remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The expansion represents zeta by a finite Dirichlet sum plus analytic correction terms and a bounded remainder, with tunable cutoffs yielding arbitrary precision throughout the plane.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hardy's real transform and the Riemann-Siegel speedup
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Multiplying critical-line zeta by a phase produces real Hardy Z, turning sign changes into certified critical-line zeros, while Riemann-Siegel reduces the dominant term count from order t to order square-root t.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Escape constraints force line pairing into sheets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A horizontal crossing bound prevents the many right-originating lines from escaping vertically through the strip; the much denser left family must pair and return, producing Speiser's sheets and increasingly nested configurations.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Maintaining monotonicity through derivative zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At derivative zeros several level-curve branches meet; choosing an outgoing branch with the appropriate angle continues monotone function values, while non-polar curves must escape every compact set.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: First Speiser criterion via sheets meeting the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Each real sheet carries exactly one zero by monotonicity and growth; the source uses how such a sheet intersects the critical line to formulate an RH-equivalent geometric condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gram points turn phase regularity into sign brackets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defining Gram points by integer phase makes zeta real there; the typical sign rule makes neighboring Hardy-Z values opposite and brackets critical-line zeros, while the mean-sign version still proves infinitely many such zeros without pointwise Gram's law.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Second Speiser criterion: derivative-zero separatrices
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source sketches how a left-of-line zeta zero forces a returning constant-argument separatrix through a derivative zero, and conversely how descending branches from a derivative zero set up a trapped region.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The trapped-region contradiction in the reverse Speiser direction
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The increasing-modulus branch cannot cross either decreasing-modulus boundary or the critical-line segment, so assuming no left-side zeta zero leaves it unable to exit a bounded region.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Derivative zeros organize near-intersections and sheet motion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Observed attraction of real curves toward derivative zeros explains sheet trajectories and abrupt near-crossings, including the distinction between exact perpendicular meeting at a real critical value and an almost-real near miss.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sheet counts predict the number of derivative zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Subtracting alternating non-sheet zeros from the total zero count yields an asymptotic sheet count; under the one-critical-point-per-sheet interpretation this becomes the asymptotic count for zeros of zeta-prime.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gram failures compensate in pairs and sheets restore correspondence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The first failure of Gram's law leaves one interval empty and the next doubly occupied, motivating a sheet-based bijection between Gram points and zeros rather than interval-by-interval order.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Lehmer's close zeros expose cancellation and certification limits
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A pair of extremely close zeros produces a tiny positive local maximum of Hardy Z through cancellation among Riemann-Siegel terms; changing its sign would signal an RH counterexample, and higher-precision Euler-MacLaurin evaluation is needed to separate the roots.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Near-double-zero geometry and reconnection off the critical line
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Two close zeros look like a double zero at coarse scale; the actual curves turn sharply near a derivative zero, and a small counterfactual reconnection would create a symmetric pair of off-line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Rosser blocks and S(t) quantify stronger failures of zero separation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Good and bad Gram points form blocks whose expected zero count is Rosser's law; the discrepancy S(t) measures departure from the smooth zero count, with thresholds explaining when Gram's and Rosser's rules can fail.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Horizontal X-ray crossings encode the argument discrepancy
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A large value of S is read as repeated real/imaginary curve crossings along a horizontal segment; tracking quadrant transitions reconstructs an argument change consistent with the numerical discrepancy.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Unbounded S predicts arbitrarily many-line coils
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source converts Selberg's unbounded discrepancy result into a qualitative prediction that higher X rays contain coils involving arbitrarily many level curves.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Equivalent formulations as a strategic black hole
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source distinguishes mathematically exact equivalence from proof-fertile reformulation and warns that a large catalog of equivalents can redirect effort without exposing a mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-prime Weil forms joined to infrared and ultraviolet prolate models
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction isolates the paper's central proposed synthesis: finite-prime extremizers approximate low zeros, while a prolate operator also models high-energy zero behavior, with the trace formula connecting both roles.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: From prime-counting error to phase-doubling nonvanishing
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage relates the strength of prime-counting error terms to zero location and gives the reusable phase-doubling contradiction behind nonvanishing on the line Re(s)=1.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Tauberian mediation and the elementary PNT contrast
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: It explains how Tauberian theorems expose the analytic-input-to-arithmetic-output bridge and contrasts that conceptual reorganization with the later proof that complex analysis is not logically necessary.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The correct variable in Riemann's conditionally convergent zero sum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The text shows why Li(x^rho) suppresses branch data and why Ei(rho log x) preserves the variable needed for a meaningful conditionally convergent explicit formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Explicit formula as a zeros-versus-places distribution identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Guinand-Weil form replaces a pointwise prime-counting expression by a test-function identity whose Mellin transforms sample zeros and whose local distributions decompose over all places.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Gaussian smoothing reveals hidden prime-counting sign changes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage identifies Gaussian averaging of the explicit formula as the mechanism that converted an enormous ineffective-looking crossing scale into tractable localization of sign changes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hardy's real Z-function converts critical-line zeros into sign changes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Choosing the phase so Z(t) is real turns critical-line zero detection into a real-variable sign-change problem, with the approximate functional equation supplying analyzable oscillatory structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Mollification upgrades infinitude to a positive proportion
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selberg's mollifier controls zeta on average and changes the target from isolated sign changes to a quantitative lower bound N0(T) comparable with T log T; later refinements optimize the same mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zero-density control versus Lindelöf convexity control
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source contrasts counting zeros in right half-strips with controlling zeta growth on vertical lines, and shows how the functional equation plus convexity propagates the Lindelöf boundary value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Evenness compresses the Hadamard product for Xi
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Completing zeta produces an order-one entire function, and the functional equation makes Xi even so paired zeros cancel exponential factors and yield a product in squared zero parameters.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Jensen's boundary average becomes Nevanlinna value distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage reframes Jensen's balance between boundary growth and interior zeros/poles as the prototype for Nevanlinna characteristic and a-point distribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Critical-line alignment is unstable under nonzero additive perturbation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Borchsenius-Jessen is used as an adversarial contrast: for every nonzero x, solutions of zeta(s)=x crowd the strip immediately to the right of the critical line, making x=0 exceptional.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Universality from phase choices in a Hilbert-space dense-series theorem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Voronin approximation is reduced to a reusable functional-analytic mechanism: square-summable vectors with divergent projections admit dense convergent unit-phase sums, applied to logarithms of Euler factors.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Self-adjoint eigenvalues and scattering resonances as competing zero models
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source separates the direct Hilbert-Polya template, where reality follows from self-adjointness, from scattering models where zeros appear as resonances and boundary conditions remain unresolved.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric RH from intersection pairing to Frobenius cohomology
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The function-field analogue shows two successive representations of RH-type control: positivity of an intersection pairing and absolute values of Frobenius eigenvalues in etale cohomology.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Primes as knots through the etale fundamental group
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Mumford-Mazur analogy reframes prime interaction as linking data in covers, with the etale fundamental group supplying the covering-space language.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Motives as a universal carrier for zeta and L-function structure
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Motives are presented as a compression across cohomology theories that would make analytic properties consequences of geometric structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adeles connect global-field arithmetic, harmonic analysis, and Langlands transfer
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Passing from a discrete global field to its locally compact adele ring creates harmonic-analytic structure; Langlands then proposes equality between motivic and automorphic L-functions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramanujan-Petersson as RH at Euler-factor scale
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Modular-form L-functions provide concrete analytic continuation and functional equations, while the bound on local coefficients realizes an RH-like constraint at each Euler factor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The sign mismatch between Selberg and Riemann explicit formulas
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Selberg trace formula gives a complete geometric-spectral interpretation, yet its prime/geodesic terms occur with the opposite sign from the Riemann explicit formula, isolating a structural obstruction to naive transfer.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Local unfolding enables GUE comparison but obstructs a fixed global operator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Zero spacings agree with GUE only after a height-dependent rescaling that compensates for logarithmically increasing density; the source infers that the correspondence is inherently local rather than the spectrum of a simple fixed ensemble.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Family symmetry selects unitary, orthogonal, or symplectic zero statistics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Katz-Sarnak turns one numerical analogy into a family-level classification where arithmetic structure determines the random-matrix symmetry type, proved in finite-field families via Frobenius equidistribution.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Zeta moments split into universal matrix and arithmetic Euler factors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Keating-Snaith model separates the moment constant into a universal determinant-moment factor and a zeta-specific Euler product, a reusable universal-versus-arithmetic decomposition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adele-class zeros as an absorption spectrum
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The noncommutative adele-class quotient realizes zeros through a trace formula whose spectral side is an absorption spectrum, accounting for the negative sign absent from Selberg's model.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime linking encoded by periodic-orbit mapping tori
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A prime's periodic orbit in the adele-class sector lifts to a mapping torus whose monodromy records its linking with other primes, concretizing the primes-as-knots analogy in class-field-theoretic data.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Numerical zero verification couples fast evaluation with rigorous counting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The computational history culminates in the reusable distinction between approximating zeros with the Riemann-Siegel/Odlyzko-Schonhage machinery and certifying completeness with error bounds and Turing's method.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Compact support localizes Weil positivity to finitely many primes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Weil's criterion turns RH into positivity of convolution test functions; compact multiplicative support forces all but finitely many local prime distributions to vanish at each scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Beurling-Nyman turns RH into an L2 density problem
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The criterion changes a zero-location statement into completeness of constrained fractional-part functions, with approximation rate reflecting off-line zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Li coefficients turn RH into positivity of a sequence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Li's criterion compresses the zero multiset into scalar coefficients whose positivity for every index is equivalent to RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Arithmetic equivalences expose decidability without supplying feasible proof search
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Robin and Lagarias translate RH into universal divisor-sum inequalities, after which the source contrasts decidable instances with the cost of direct verification and speculates about provability limits.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-prime Weil quadratic form produces a real-zero Mellin transform
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For functions supported in a finite multiplicative interval, only finitely many prime powers enter the explicit-formula quadratic form; a normalized minimizer is then mapped by Mellin transform to an entire function whose zeros lie on the critical line under a simplicity/evenness condition.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Extreme finite-prime agreement still leaves the convergence theorem open
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The computed first fifty zeros from primes at most 13 closely match zeta zeros, motivating a limit in which minimizers converge and Hurwitz preserves line-supported zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Decompose the finite-to-infinite limit through Hermite and prolate approximants
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposed route recenters the minimizer, represents Xi through a Hermite summation map, localizes the Hermite functions by prolate eigenfunctions, and separates approximant convergence from approximation of the true minimizer.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Simple even extremizers have Fourier transforms with only real zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 6.1 supplies the rigorous rigidity engine: a lower-bounded convolution-kernel operator with a simple isolated minimum and even eigenfunction yields an entire Fourier transform with all zeros real.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Xi as the Fourier transform of a summed Hermite combination
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Poisson summation and the map E express Riemann's Xi as the Fourier transform of E(h), where h is the unique zero-integral combination of two Fourier-invariant Hermite modes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prolate eigenfunctions jointly diagonalize time and band limitation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The commuting prolate differential operator resolves the angle between time-support and frequency-support projections, providing localized analogues of Hermite functions whose first relevant eigenvalues approach one exponentially.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The smallest restricted-Weil eigenvalue tracks a prolate leakage eigenvalue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The restricted Weil form is represented by a compact-resolvent self-adjoint operator; numerics motivate E applied to a zero-integral combination of the first prolate modes as the smallest-eigenvector ansatz.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Poisson summation turns near time-frequency intersection into a near Weil radical
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because the global E-range lies in the Weil radical, simultaneous approximate time and band limitation creates compactly supported near-radical vectors; prolate modes quantify the failure of the two projection ranges to intersect exactly.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prolate-Hermite approximants converge to Xi on closed substrips
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Classical prolate-to-Hermite estimates yield uniform-on-closed-substrip convergence of the Fourier transforms of k_lambda to Xi, providing the analytic convergence side needed for a Hurwitz argument.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Two unresolved gates separate the program from RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source names the exact remaining obligations: prove the restricted Weil minimum is simple with an even eigenvector, and prove the prolate ansatz sufficiently approximates that eigenvector.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Scaling kernels realize Frobenius correspondences as divisors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: In the adelic scaling-site picture, Schwartz kernels mediate between operators and geometric correspondences, with the delta kernel of scaling representing the Frobenius divisor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Time and frequency cutoffs rewrite the archimedean local term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The archimedean trace formula uses independent support and bandwidth projections, turning the local Weil distribution into a trace identity in exactly the operators used in information theory.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Sonin space supplies an archimedean positivity lower bound
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Functions vanishing with their Fourier transforms on a common interval define the orthogonal complement of the two projection ranges, and compression to this Sonin space yields a positive trace lower bound for the archimedean Weil functional.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Semilocal adele quotients assemble into a cross-product sheaf
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Finite sets of places define quotients A_S/Gamma_S whose Bruhat-Schwartz cross products form a sheaf over Spec Z; its generic stalk and global sections connect semilocal and global arithmetic geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The semilocal trace formula inserts finite-prime contributions into the projection identity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Equation (22) extends the archimedean time-band trace representation to a finite set of places, giving an operator-theoretic form of the restricted Weil quadratic form used in the minimizer comparison.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infrared determinant convergence and ultraviolet heat asymptotics are distinct targets
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The spectral-triple viewpoint separates low eigenvalues, modeled by rank-one perturbations whose normalized determinants are intended to approach Xi, from high eigenvalues, modeled through heat asymptotics and a prolate operator.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The zeta-zero heat expansion is asymptotic and factorially divergent
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Assuming RH and a self-adjoint operator with zeta ordinates as spectrum, the explicit formula gives a heat-trace expansion whose coefficient growth proves it is not convergent.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A self-adjoint prolate extension matches ultraviolet zero asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Restricting the natural self-adjoint prolate extension to Sonin space yields discrete negative spectrum, and a Darboux-built Dirac square root has the same ultraviolet behavior as zeta zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Wiener-Ikehara converts boundary regularity into the PNT
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The note makes the Tauberian bridge explicit: nonnegativity plus extension after pole subtraction converts analytic control of the logarithmic derivative into psi(x) asymptotic to x.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Nevanlinna growth and Borchsenius-Jessen limiting distribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The notes define proximity and pole-counting terms, report zeta's characteristic growth, and state that the limiting distribution of log zeta has full complex support in the inner strip without assuming RH.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Expanded Ei formula preserves branch-sensitive zero dependence
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The note demonstrates the periodicity defect in x^beta and writes the corrected zero sum using Ei(rho log x), making the earlier representation repair explicit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Angles between projections classify near intersections
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The note explains that a pair of closed subspaces is classified componentwise by an angle satisfying P cos^2(alpha)=PQP, the abstraction used by the prolate construction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The module identifies the semilocal quotient with the trace-formula Hilbert space
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The semilocal module descends through the quotient, identifies additive and multiplicative L2 spaces, and reduces the general trace formula to the kernel-invariant component used in equation (22).

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Compact support makes each Weil test depend on finitely many primes, and extremization yields line-rigid approximants; the global problem is displaced into controlling the scale limit rather than eliminated.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Neither finite-prime positivity nor the observed zero match proves simplicity or convergence as the support grows.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Finite localization without finite sufficiency

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Time-frequency concentration constructs a near-radical vector whose Fourier transform has a proved Xi limit, while the real-zero theorem would transfer rigidity if it were identified with the true Weil minimizer.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The required minimizer simplicity/evenness and quantitative k_lambda-to-theta_x comparison remain open.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: From prolate concentration to a candidate RH limit

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The same pair of support and bandwidth projections governs prolate concentration, Sonin-space positivity, and the archimedean-to-semilocal trace formulas.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: A shared operator vocabulary does not yet provide the finite-prime positivity or eigenvector bound needed for RH.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Information theory as the common operator language

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Low-lying finite-prime approximants and high-energy prolate asymptotics probe different ends of a proposed zeta spectral geometry.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The source does not construct one operator with the exact full zeta spectrum; the heat expansion is conditional and the UV match is asymptotic.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Infrared and ultraviolet are complementary but nonidentical spectral evidence

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The negative prime-side sign obstructing a direct Selberg analogy is reinterpreted by the adele-class trace formula as an absorption rather than emission spectrum.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This interpretation organizes the sign but does not establish Weil positivity.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Why the Riemann trace formula needs absorption

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Intersection positivity, Frobenius cohomology, adeles, and Schwartz kernels outline successive representation changes by which a geometric RH proof might be imitated over Spec Z.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Each bridge remains analogical in the classical case; no arithmetic cohomology with the required positivity is produced.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Function-field transfer map and its arithmetic gap

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Zeta's nonzero value behavior is extremely flexible, whereas Fourier transforms of simple even extremizers form a deliberately rigid class with real zeros.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: These concern different function classes, so the contrast supplies design intuition rather than a direct implication about zeta.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Universality versus engineered zero rigidity

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Random matrices explain unfolded local statistics and universal moment factors, while the prolate construction targets an operator-level ultraviolet asymptotic.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Local statistics, moment predictions, and ultraviolet matching are all weaker than equality with the exact zeta zero set.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Statistical universality separated from exact spectral realization

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Explicit formulas must retain rho log x rather than only x^rho because conditional summation depends on branch-sensitive information lost by exponentiation.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This repairs notation and interpretation but does not alter the unresolved zero-location problem.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Branch-aware representations as a correctness prerequisite

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The source itself supports a hierarchy from certified finite computation, through reported numerical approximation and asymptotic matching, to a proved analytic limit for a surrogate, with two proof-critical gates still open.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: No independent recomputation or verification of cited experiments was performed in this semantic source audit.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Alternation and a generating function turn a divergent power sum into a finite boundary value
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The passage isolates Euler's two-step move: first pass from zeta to a less divergent alternating series, then encode powers by repeatedly applying an Euler-type differential operator to a geometric series whose rational form can be evaluated at the boundary. It explicitly distinguishes the formal historical move from its later Abel-summability justification.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A second parameter separates convergence control from the zeta argument
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors construct f_q(s,t) by combining q-integers with an independent exponential damping parameter. Keeping t independent makes the initial series absolutely convergent in a clear half-plane and postpones the structurally important choice of how t should depend on s.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Binomial expansion converts the q-series into an explicit meromorphic pole decomposition
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 1 expands each denominator binomially, interchanges the two sums, and evaluates the inner geometric series. result_and_mechanism_map.title: The same two-parameter deformation admits a beta-like Jackson-integral representation

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The diagonal t=s-1 is selected because singular loci cancel without creating persistent extra poles
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Specializing the two-variable family along t=s-1 turns intersections with the pole divisor at non-positive integers into finite indeterminacies and gives the desired full classical limit. Nearby choices reveal the design constraint: t=s lacks the cancellation, while t=s-k introduces extra finite-q poles even when their residues vanish classically.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler's alternating simplification does not transfer cleanly because it couples q and q squared
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The natural q-analogue of the alternating series satisfies a relation involving both zeta_q and zeta at q squared. The extra scale coupling destroys the simple one-function reduction that made alternation useful classically, so the paper explicitly rejects this otherwise plausible route.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Vanishing binomial factors and a singular denominator combine to produce finite values on the pole diagonal
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Proposition 2 reads the pole set from the continued series and then evaluates zeta_q at non-positive integers. Most terms vanish because generalized binomial coefficients truncate, while the single singular term is resolved by a first-order limit, yielding a finite closed formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite-difference annihilation isolates the Bernoulli coefficient in the classical limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 1 rewrites the negative-integer formula as a finite alternating binomial sum, inserts the Bernoulli generating series, and uses a derivative/finite-difference identity that kills every intermediate degree. Only the constant and degree m+1 contributions survive, producing the classical Bernoulli value.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Negative q-zeta values generate q-Bernoulli numbers with both a binomial recursion and a dilation equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source packages the negative-integer values into q-Bernoulli numbers, derives a closed formula including the r=0 limiting convention, and shows that the coefficient recursion is equivalently encoded by F_q(qt)=e^t F_q(t)-t e^t.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Pointwise convergence to zeta can coexist with severe finite-sum instability near a zero
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Theorem 2 asserts convergence for every complex s except the pole. The numerical examples contrast benign convergence at s=1/2 with enormous truncation sensitivity near the first non-trivial zero, preserving an important distinction between analytic convergence and practical numerical conditioning.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Adding a shift parameter transports the q-limit and Bernoulli-value mechanism to Hurwitz zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The remark shows that the same construction extends from n to n+a, with the classical limit becoming Hurwitz zeta and the negative-integer limit becoming a Bernoulli polynomial. It also records the deliberate scope boundary: the paper does not develop the resulting q-Bernoulli polynomials.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Integer specialization turns the q-zeta limit into a hierarchy of Lambert-series asymptotics
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: At positive integer s=k, the continued expansion reorganizes as a Lambert series with a binomial polynomial weight. Comparing its leading degree with lower-degree terms and using induction transfers zeta_q convergence into the stated asymptotic involving zeta(k).

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Lambert series becomes an Eisenstein Fourier expansion whose constant term is fixed by the zeta limit
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For even weight, the divisor-sum expansion identifies the Lambert series with the nonconstant part of an Eisenstein series. Modularity and the q-to-1 asymptotic then provide an alternative route to the constant term, linking positive zeta values with Bernoulli data; the odd-weight failure is explicitly stated.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler-Maclaurin continuation separates a polar part, finite Bernoulli corrections, and a movable remainder
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof first records the classical mechanism: repeated integration by parts yields Euler-Maclaurin, and choosing an arbitrarily high remainder order moves the valid half-plane leftward until the whole zeta plane is covered, leaving only the simple pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Increasing Euler-Maclaurin order cannot continue the q-sum because the exponential factor preserves the same half-plane constraint
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying Euler-Maclaurin directly to the q-summand produces an explicit formula, but higher derivative order does not improve convergence: q^{x(s-1)} forces Re(s)>1 regardless of M. The source thereby identifies the exact failure that necessitates a different representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Fourier expansion converts the blocked periodic remainder into uniformly controlled incomplete-beta modes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Replacing the periodic Bernoulli polynomial by its uniformly convergent Fourier series permits interchange of sum and integral. The substitution q^x=u then packages each Fourier mode as an incomplete beta integral with a uniform-in-mode bound, creating a continuation route unavailable in the original x-representation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Repeated integration by parts moves incomplete-beta parameters and exposes an arbitrarily extendable half-plane
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The incomplete beta integral is recursively decomposed into finitely many boundary terms plus a shifted remainder. Applying this to each Fourier mode extends the expression to Re(s)>2-M, so increasing M now genuinely enlarges the continuation domain.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The q-limit reproduces the classical Euler-Maclaurin continuation term by term
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: After taking the elementary q-to-1 limits, Fourier identities turn the beta-mode boundary terms into Bernoulli corrections and the surviving remainder into the periodic-Bernoulli integral. The resulting expression is exactly the classical formula for zeta, and arbitrary M covers the entire plane except the pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Occupancy caps compress an infinite multiplicative support to at most N integers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Primes are partitioned into scale blocks, numbers with excessive occupancy in any block are removed, and factorial/binomial estimates show that the remaining square-free support is divisor closed and has cardinality at most N.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An exponential tilt proves the discarded multiplicative mass is negligible
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A union bound reduces discarded mass to blockwise tails; inserting a tilt b>1, factorizing over primes, and balancing its gain against the occupancy penalty yields a negative exponent and proves the truncation preserves the Euler-product main term.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Spectral comparison transfers a weighted extremizer to unweighted GCD configurations

result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The paper fixes the branch and jump convention for the argument of zeta, places S directly in the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula, and contrasts unconditional and RH-conditional upper and lower bounds. Theorem 2 then states improved conditional extremes for both S and S1 on a movable interval.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A Cauchy-kernel formula transfers large log-zeta values into lower bounds for the primitive S1
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Starting from a conditional integral representation of log absolute zeta in terms of S, integration by parts replaces S with S1 and an explicit signed kernel. Choosing sigma just to the right of the critical line then imports an earlier large-value result to obtain a preliminary conditional S1 bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Longer positive resonators improve amplitude but enlarge the location interval and lose sign flexibility
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors contrast resonance with high moments and with earlier shorter resonators. Larger primes and a longer Dirichlet polynomial improve the detectable maximum, but currently yield a much larger interval and no comparable measure estimate. Because all coefficients are nonnegative, the construction detects large positive real parts and cannot symmetrically force both signs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Contour shifting turns a smoothed zeta value into a weighted Dirichlet series plus an explicit pole residue
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 1 shifts a contour from the critical strip to an absolutely convergent line, expands zeta there, and shifts each kernel integral back. The result cleanly separates Fourier-selected Dirichlet coefficients from the residue of the zeta pole.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The smoothed logarithm equals a prime series plus an explicit correction from zeros to the right
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Selberg's convolution formula writes log zeta as a von-Mangoldt Dirichlet series plus integrals over any zeros with real part beyond sigma. RH removes that correction at the critical line. Taking imaginary parts yields the S formula, while a bounded correction and an extra logarithmic denominator yield the S1 formula.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Prime bands and square-free multiplicative weights build a large but cardinality-controlled resonator
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The resonator uses a multiplicative weight supported on square-free products of primes in carefully chosen logarithmic bands. Removing integers with too many factors in any band produces a divisor-closed set M whose cardinality stays below N while preserving the desired multiplicative structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Exponential tail estimates show that truncation preserves the weighted prime contribution
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 4 proves a lower bound for a normalized weighted divisor sum. It introduces a narrower typical set, reduces the claim to showing exceptional multiplicative mass is negligible, factorizes each prime band, and chooses an exponential tilt b so the tail exponent is negative.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Geometric binning compresses the support while preserving near-multiplicative correlations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The construction chooses one representative from each narrow multiplicative interval and assigns it the square root of nearby f-mass. Gaussian Fourier decay then controls off-diagonal pairs in the L2 norm, while Cauchy-Schwarz transfers exact relations mk=n on M to approximate relations on the thinned set M-prime.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Positivity lets a resonator retain a favorable finite subcollection of any Dirichlet series
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 6 abstracts the resonance step for an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients. Expanding the weighted integral makes every term nonnegative, so a selected finite portion indexed by the resonator's multiplicative relations yields an exponential lower bound.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Restricting the von-Mangoldt series to selected primes converts combinatorial divisor mass into the S-scale gain
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Lemma 7 adapts positivity to coefficients Lambda(n)a_n/log n. Keeping only primes in the designated set transforms the weighted integral into the divisor sum controlled by Lemma 4, producing the square-root log T log3 T over log2 T scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A compact-frequency even kernel combines pole control, interval localization, and positive resonance
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proof selects a sinc-squared kernel whose Fourier transform is nonnegative and compactly supported. Moment bounds control the central interval, Gaussian decay removes the far tail, kappa below 1-beta suppresses errors, Lemma 1 supplies the positive Dirichlet series, and Lemmas 5-6 convert the weighted mean into the claimed maximum.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An odd kernel turns the imaginary prime series into a lower bound for the absolute size of S
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For S, the proof differentiates a Gaussian to obtain a real odd kernel with purely imaginary Fourier transform. The conditional convolution formula, second-moment localization, and Lemma 7 then select the imaginary part of the prime series and yield a lower bound for max absolute S.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: An even positive-frequency kernel yields a one-sided positive extreme for S1
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For S1, an even Gaussian kernel has a real positive Fourier transform. The same localization and resonance architecture now extracts the real prime series with an additional log denominator, explaining both the positive sign and the extra powers of log log in the final scale.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Commutativity versus zero divisors in choosing a hypercomplex zeta setting
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The introduction identifies the structural tradeoff behind the construction: quaternions avoid zero divisors but are noncommutative, whereas bicomplex numbers are commutative but have zero divisors. This predicts both the ease of defining powers/products and the later need to track a singular divisor.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bicomplex algebra and its noninvertible locus
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The four-dimensional commutative algebra is represented as z1+z2 i2 over C(i1), and noninvertibility is characterized by two component conditions. This is the algebraic obstruction governing differentiation, poles, and product convergence later in the source.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bicomplex differentiability as coupled complex holomorphicity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The source turns a difference-quotient notion that excludes noninvertible increments into ordinary holomorphicity of two complex-variable components plus complexified Cauchy-Riemann equations. This is a reusable bridge from an algebra-valued analytic notion to familiar component conditions.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Idempotent splitting and componentwise reconstruction of holomorphic maps
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Every bicomplex number splits uniquely into two orthogonal idempotent components, making addition, multiplication, division, invertibility, and holomorphic maps componentwise. Theorems 2 and 3 establish both synthesis from two complex holomorphic functions and decomposition of every bicomplex holomorphic function.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bicomplex exponentiation reduced to idempotent complex powers
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Defining n^w through the bicomplex exponential makes the Dirichlet series meaningful and immediately exposes its two ordinary complex-power components. This is the construction that connects algebraic representation to analytic convergence.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Dirichlet series convergence as intersection of two complex half-planes
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The bicomplex series is exactly the idempotent sum of two classical zeta Dirichlet series. Its convergence domain is therefore the simultaneous pair of complex half-plane conditions, equivalently a wedge in the original coordinates. This illustrates how componentwise semantics turns a multivariable convergence question into an intersection of scalar constraints.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Componentwise continuation on the complement of the translated zero-divisor set
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The continued bicomplex zeta is assembled from two classical continuations. Identifying the domain as a product of punctured complex planes proves openness and connectedness, componentwise holomorphic reconstruction proves T-holomorphicity, and the several-variable identity theorem yields uniqueness.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The complex pole lifts to an entire translated zero-divisor polar set
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Approaching any point where either idempotent coordinate equals the classical pole forces the bicomplex norm to diverge. Thus the excluded set is not an arbitrary technical domain restriction but the maximal obstruction inherited componentwise.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Bicomplex zeros require simultaneous component zeros
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Orthogonal idempotent components force zeta(w)=0 precisely when both scalar zeta values vanish. Applying the classical trivial-zero set then produces a two-parameter lattice of trivial bicomplex zeros.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A bicomplex zero-coordinate condition equivalent to classical RH
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The proposed bicomplex condition encodes the possibilities in which both idempotent coordinates are zeta zeros, allowing trivial/nontrivial mixtures as well as two nontrivial components. Classical RH implies the listed coordinate loci; conversely a hypothetical off-critical classical zero embeds diagonally as a bicomplex zero that violates them.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Infinite-product convergence adjusted for zero divisors
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The usual nonzero-factor condition is replaced by invertibility of all but finitely many factors and an invertible limiting product. Lemma 1 then proves equivalence with convergence of the two ordinary complex component products.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Euler product inherited independently by the two idempotent components
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: On the common absolute-convergence domain, the two scalar Dirichlet series admit their classical Euler products; Lemma 1 recombines them into a bicomplex Euler product. The unit demonstrates factorization transfer through a representation that preserves multiplication.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolic zeta as a real-component restriction of bicomplex zeta
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Restricting to the hyperbolic subalgebra turns the idempotent coordinates into the real values c+d and c-d. The bicomplex construction therefore supplies powers, convergence, Euler product, differentiability, continuation, and a polar set for a hyperbolic zeta without creating a separate analytic mechanism.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hyperbolic holomorphicity does not force unique continuation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A piecewise real scalar extension is applied separately to c+d and c-d, producing a second D-holomorphic function that agrees with the Dirichlet series on its initial domain and has the same polar behavior. This exposes a sharp limit of importing complex analytic-continuation intuition into a zero-divisor algebra with real components.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Every zero of the hyperbolic restriction is trivial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Because both idempotent arguments are real, a hyperbolic zero requires two real zeta zeros, which are negative even integers. The rich nontrivial-zero geometry of the bicomplex setting collapses to the previously identified trivial lattice, so no analogous RH remains in this restriction.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Period polynomials encode critical L-values as coefficients
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The period integral and binomial expansion turn the critical values of a modular-form L-function into the coefficients of one polynomial. This is the foundational compression that lets a statement about a list of L-values become a statement about polynomial zero geometry.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The L-function functional equation becomes reciprocal symmetry of polynomial roots
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Applying the functional equation coefficientwise yields a self-inversive relation: every root is paired with its reciprocal transform. This identifies the symmetry circle and motivates the polynomial ‘Riemann hypothesis’ that all roots lie on it.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A half-polynomial converts circle zeros into a sign-change count
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors package half of the critical values into an auxiliary polynomial, reconstruct the period polynomial by reciprocal reflection, and observe that its unit-circle restriction is a cosine or sine polynomial according to the functional-equation sign. The circle-zero theorem is thereby reduced to producing exactly the required number of real sign changes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A root-count sign condition becomes an inequality among critical L-values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For even functional-equation sign, evaluating the auxiliary trigonometric polynomial at a distinguished boundary point forces a nontrivial alternating inequality among critical values. The paper then flags two explanations—unconditional low-weight Hadamard arguments and a conditional argument from the L-function RH—linking polynomial root geometry back to L-value structure.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Hadamard zero pairing forces monotonicity of completed critical values
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Hadamard factorization pairs real and conjugate zeros, and the known zero strip makes each factor grow to the right of the critical region. This yields monotonicity of the completed L-function at successive critical arguments, with a refined normalized chain for odd functional-equation sign.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Ramanujan bounds control ratios of L-values in the absolute-convergence range
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The logarithmic derivative of the Euler product, together with bounds on prime-power coefficients, is integrated between two real arguments to dominate a modular-form L-value ratio by an explicit zeta-function ratio. This converts form-dependent coefficients into uniform analytic error bounds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weight four reduces exactly to one sine or cosine equation
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For the degree-two case, functional-equation sign makes the transformed polynomial either a multiple of z−z⁻¹ or a two-term cosine expression. Monotonicity of adjacent completed L-values gives the exact unit-circle root count, while a ratio estimate locates the roots for large level.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Weight six is reduced to two product inequalities at trigonometric extrema
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: For weight six, differentiating the unit-circle trigonometric polynomial identifies all relevant extrema. The required four roots are equivalent to prescribed signs at those extrema, which in turn become two multiplicative inequalities among three adjacent completed L-values.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Factorwise inequalities propagate through the Hadamard product
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: An elementary product lemma lifts an additive inequality satisfied by each aligned factor triple to an inequality for products. The proof groups L-function zeros by functional-equation and conjugation symmetries, checks the needed inequality separately for real, critical-line, and off-line groups, and passes to the full Hadamard product.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: The L-function RH gives the boundary sign through Taylor-coefficient positivity
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: Under the usual RH for the completed modular L-function, the derivatives also have the required zero geometry; symmetry kills odd derivatives and nonnegativity of even central derivatives makes a Taylor comparison prove the boundary inequality. This supplies an illuminating conditional explanation distinct from the unconditional Hadamard proof.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Monotone coefficients transfer Pólya–Szegő zero counts to period polynomials
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: A classical theorem forces simple, interlacing zeros of sine and cosine polynomials when their coefficients increase. Completed-L monotonicity handles the first comparison, the Euler-product ratio bound makes the remaining comparisons explicit in level and weight, and computation is reserved for the finite set below those thresholds.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: A zero-transparent exponential model controls the large-weight polynomial
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The normalized auxiliary polynomial is decomposed into a dominant truncated-exponential model plus three errors. On the unit circle the dominant model has an explicitly monotone phase and alternating extrema, so a uniform error smaller than its minimum amplitude preserves all required real- and imaginary-part sign changes.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Uniform coefficient bounds reduce the large-weight proof to an explicit finite threshold
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The Euler-product ratio estimate bounds the first error, the exponential tail bounds the second, and central-value monotonicity bounds the third. Combining them gives a single explicit inequality in weight and level, a threshold table, and a finite collection of residual forms delegated to computation.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Phase perturbation upgrades circle membership to quantitative root locations
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The same exponential approximation yields an explicit leading phase whose regularly spaced zero locations persist under a uniform small error. Evaluating on either side of each predicted phase zero traps one true root, producing the asymptotic location and equidistribution result for both functional-equation signs.

result_and_mechanism_map.title: Finite residual cases are closed by L-value evaluation and direct sign-change tests
result_and_mechanism_map.why_material: The authors identify exactly which weights and levels escape the analytic criteria, enumerate newforms in Sage, compute critical L-values at high precision, test the monotone-coefficient inequality when possible, and otherwise verify the needed number of trigonometric sign changes directly. This records the logical role of computation in completing the theorem.

source_identity.title: Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials of modular forms

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Encoding critical L-values in a period polynomial transports the L-function functional equation into reciprocal root symmetry; factoring that symmetry through a half-polynomial then turns the desired circle-zero statement into a count of sine or cosine sign changes.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: This mechanism establishes the paper’s polynomial analogue only; it supplies no implication for the zero locations of the Riemann zeta function or the underlying modular L-function.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Functional symmetry becomes a real-variable root-count problem

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Known confinement and symmetry of L-function zeros yield monotonic critical values through Hadamard factors, while Euler-product bounds make coefficient ratios uniform; those coefficient constraints are precisely what classical trigonometric zero-counting criteria need.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: Some low-weight inequalities require more specialized grouped-factor arguments, and the general coefficient criterion fails for specific small cases.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: L-function zero geometry constrains polynomial coefficient geometry

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: The same critical-value inequality is proved unconditionally by multiplying inequalities over symmetric zero groups and explained conditionally by positivity of even Taylor coefficients under the L-function RH, separating proof from conceptual interpretation.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The conditional Taylor route cannot be used as unconditional evidence for the L-function RH; exact factor and derivative identities remain formula-dependent.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Two complementary explanations of the weight-six sign invariant

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Once a normalized polynomial is uniformly close on the circle to a model with monotone phase and alternating extrema, a strict amplitude-versus-error inequality preserves the full zero count and also traps each root near a predicted phase location.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The preserved count depends on the strict numerical bound; the extracted constants and finite threshold table must be verified before transferring the argument.
within_source_synthesis_map.title: Stable zero counts from a dominant phase plus a uniform error budget

within_source_synthesis_map.claim: Two analytic criteria cover complementary weight-level regions and explicitly expose a finite remainder, after which direct high-precision sign-change evaluation is used instead of silently extrapolating the estimates.
within_source_synthesis_map.limit: The paper text does not preserve enough computational provenance or error certification to reproduce the finite closure as an exact audit artifact.
